Source: docs/guide/user/editor.md

# Editor

Forge's editor is built on CodeMirror 6. Markdown, SVG, image and CSV/TSV files open in
editors of their own with a preview, zoom or a table view: see
[Markdown, images and CSV](docs/guide/user/markdown-images-csv.md). Language intelligence (completion, hover, diagnostics,
Go to Declaration, formatting) comes from [language servers](docs/guide/user/language-servers.md) and from
Forge's own indexes for PHP, Lua and the frameworks. Shortcuts below are the Windows/Linux
defaults with macOS in parentheses; the full list is in the
[keymap reference](docs/guide/reference/keymap.md).

## Code completion

- Completion pops up while you type, from the language server(s) of the file and, in
  framework projects, from Forge's framework sources (Laravel routes and views, Symfony
  services, Twig, DQL, …). Each item has a kind icon (class, method, property, variable,
  keyword, …).
- **Basic Completion** `Ctrl+Space` (also `Shift+Space`) opens it explicitly. Then words
  that already occur in the document are offered as well; this works in every file, even
  without a language server.
- `Enter` or `Tab` accepts. Functions are inserted with parentheses and the caret between
  them; snippet placeholders from the server can be filled in with `Tab`.
- Brackets and quotes are closed automatically.

![Completion](docs/screenshots/lsp-completion.png)

### Postfix completion

Postfix templates wrap the expression you just typed: type a dot and the template key after
an expression, as in PHPStorm. In PHP, `$user->isAdmin().if` becomes

```php
if ($user->isAdmin()) {
    |
}
```

- The templates appear in the completion popup after `expr.` (below the members of the
  expression), with their description. Typing the full key and pressing `Tab` expands the
  template directly.
- Templates such as `.if`, `.return`, `.var` or `.foreach` take the whole statement before
  the dot (`$a > 0.if` → `if ($a > 0)`); `.not`, `.par`, `.isset` or `.await` take the
  closest expression (`$x = $valid.not` → `$x = !$valid`).
- `.var`, `.foreach` and the other templates that introduce a name suggest one from the
  expression and select it (`$this->getUsers().foreach` → `foreach ($this->getUsers() as
  $user)`), so you can type over it.
- Templates are not offered in strings and comments.

| Language | Templates |
| --- | --- |
| PHP | `.echo`, `.else`, `.empty`, `.for`, `.forek`, `.foreach`, `.forr`, `.if`, `.isset`, `.new`, `.not`, `.notnull`, `.null`, `.par`, `.return`, `.sprintf`, `.switch`, `.throw`, `.try`, `.unset`, `.var`, `.while` |
| JavaScript and TypeScript | `.await`, `.const`, `.else`, `.for`, `.fori`, `.forin`, `.forof`, `.if`, `.let`, `.log`, `.new`, `.not`, `.notnull`, `.null`, `.par`, `.return`, `.switch`, `.throw`, `.typeof`, `.undefined`, `.var`, `.while` |
| Lua | `.else`, `.for`, `.if`, `.ipairs`, `.local`, `.nil`, `.not`, `.notnil`, `.pairs`, `.par`, `.print`, `.return`, `.while` |

**Settings | Editor | General | Postfix Completion** switches postfix completion on and off,
hides the templates from the completion autopopup, chooses the expand key (`Tab`, `Space`
or `Enter`) and switches single templates off. Selecting a template shows its description
and a before/after example.

![Postfix completion](docs/screenshots/postfix-completion.png)

![Settings | Editor | General | Postfix Completion](docs/screenshots/settings-postfix.png)

### Complete Current Statement

**Complete Current Statement** (`Ctrl+Shift+Enter`, macOS `Cmd+Shift+Enter`) finishes the
statement at the caret and puts the caret where you continue typing:

- closes the parentheses and brackets the line left open and adds the missing `;` in PHP,
  JavaScript and TypeScript (`$a = foo(bar(1` → `$a = foo(bar(1));`). Inside multi-line
  arrays, calls and object literals, and before a chained `->where(…)` line, no `;` is
  added;
- opens the block of `if`, `elseif`, `else`, `for`, `foreach`, `while`, `switch`, `try`,
  `catch` and function or class declarations and moves the caret into it. PHP functions and
  classes get their brace on the next line (PSR-12); an existing block is entered instead
  of adding a second one;
- in Lua adds `then` / `do` and the matching `end` (`if ready` → `if ready then … end`),
  and closes `function … end` and `repeat … until`;
- starts a new line when the statement is already complete.

![Complete Current Statement](docs/screenshots/complete-statement.png)

### Cyclic Expand Word

**Cyclic Expand Word** (`Alt+/`) completes the word at the caret with a word that already
occurs in the file, the nearest one above the caret first, then the ones below, then the
words of the other open files. Press `Alt+/` again to cycle through the other matches;
**Cyclic Expand Word (Backward)** (`Alt+Shift+/`) cycles the other way and, when it starts,
looks below the caret first. It works in every file type, without a language server.

## Quick documentation on hover

Hold the mouse over a symbol to see its documentation: signature, description, parameters
and return value, deprecation notes and links, rendered PHPStorm-style. Problems at that
position are shown in the same popup.

For PHP, Forge merges the language server's answer with its own index (PHPDoc, attributes,
inherited documentation) and falls back to the index when no server runs. Lua uses LuaForge's
index until lua-language-server answers.

![Hover documentation](docs/screenshots/lsp-hover.png)

## Quick Documentation

**View | Quick Documentation** (`Ctrl+Q`, macOS `F1` or `Ctrl+J`) shows the same documentation
for the symbol at the caret, without the mouse. The popup closes when you move the caret, type
or press `Escape`. Its toolbar has three buttons:

- **Open in Documentation Tool Window** (pin; or press `Ctrl+Q` a second time) moves the
  documentation to the Documentation tool window.
- **External Documentation** (`Shift+F1`) opens the symbol's page in the browser.
- **Edit Source** (`F4`) jumps to the declaration.

When there is nothing to show, a hint says "No documentation found".

![Quick Documentation](docs/screenshots/quick-documentation.png)

### Documentation tool window

The **Documentation** tool window (right stripe, View | Tool Windows | Documentation) keeps the
documentation open while you work. With **Auto-Update from Source** (the crosshair button,
on by default) it follows the caret and shows the documentation of each symbol you move to;
while it is open, `Ctrl+Q` updates it instead of opening the popup. Its toolbar also has
External Documentation and Edit Source.

![Documentation tool window](docs/screenshots/documentation-tool-window.png)

## External Documentation

**View | External Documentation** (`Shift+F1`) opens the online documentation of the symbol at
the caret in your browser:

| Symbol | Page |
| --- | --- |
| PHP functions, classes, methods and keywords of PHP itself | php.net manual |
| Laravel framework classes and methods (`Illuminate\…`) | Laravel API reference |
| JavaScript built-ins (`Array`, `JSON.parse`, `Promise`), DOM and Web APIs (`document`, `fetch`, `console.log`), keywords | MDN |
| HTML tags, CSS properties, at-rules and pseudo-classes | MDN |
| Vue Composition API (`ref`, `computed`, `onMounted`, `defineProps`) in files that import `vue` | vuejs.org API |
| React hooks and APIs (`useState`, `memo`, `createRoot`) in files that import `react` | react.dev reference |
| Lua standard functions and libraries (`print`, `string.format`, `table`) | Lua 5.4 reference manual |

Your own project's classes have no external page; the hint "No external documentation
found" appears instead. PHP symbols are resolved like Go to Declaration (language server,
PHP index, PHP stubs), so `$date->format()` opens `DateTime::format`.

## Quick Definition

**View | Quick Definition** (`Ctrl+Shift+I`, macOS `Alt+Space` or `Cmd+Y`) shows the source of
the declaration at the caret in a popup, with its docblock and attributes, up to the closing
brace (Lua: `end`), without leaving the file. The header names the symbol and its file and
line; **Edit Source** (pencil) opens it. When there are several declarations (an interface
method, a class declared twice), the arrows switch between them. On a declaration itself,
the popup shows that declaration. Declarations in the PHP stubs and other library files work
too. Long declarations are cut after 80 lines.

![Quick Definition](docs/screenshots/quick-definition.png)

## Type Info, Context Info and Error Description

- **Type Info** (`Ctrl+Shift+P`) shows the type of the expression at the caret in a small hint:
  a variable's or property's type, a method's return type, a class's name. It comes from the
  language server's hover, in PHP also from the PHP index.

  ![Type Info](docs/screenshots/type-info.png)

- **Context Info** (`Alt+Q`, macOS `Ctrl+Shift+Q`) shows, at the top of the editor, the
  headers of the class, function or method (in CSS: the rules and `@media` blocks) that
  enclose the caret, with their line numbers. Useful when they are scrolled out of view.

  ![Context Info](docs/screenshots/context-info.png)

- **Error Description** (`Ctrl+F1`, macOS `Cmd+F1`) shows the full text of the problems at
  the caret, with their severity and the inspection or language server that reported them.

  ![Error Description](docs/screenshots/error-description.png)

## Parameter Info

**Parameter Info** (`Ctrl+P`, macOS `Cmd+P`) shows the parameters of the call at the caret,
the current one in bold, with its documentation. It also opens automatically after you type
`(` and follows you as you type `,`.

![Parameter Info](docs/screenshots/lsp-parameter-info.png)

## Go to Declaration

**Go to Declaration or Usages** (`Ctrl+B`, macOS `Cmd+B`), `Ctrl+Click` (macOS `Cmd+Click`)
or a middle click jumps to the declaration of the symbol at the caret. While `Ctrl` is held,
the symbol under the mouse is underlined like a link, with a small tooltip that shows where it
is declared (in PHP: the namespace or class and the declaration).

Forge first asks its framework providers, which know things a language server cannot
resolve: Laravel route names, views, config keys and Eloquent attributes; Symfony service ids,
routes and Twig templates; Doctrine entities and DQL fields; React/Vue/Angular components and
props; Lua modules. Then it asks the language server and, in PHP files, Forge's PHP index and
the PHP stubs (see [PHP navigation](docs/guide/user/php.md#navigation)).

On a declaration itself (a class, method or function name), Go to Declaration shows its
**usages** instead, as in PHPStorm; a single usage opens directly.

When there are several targets — from a framework provider (a view that exists in two places, a
component used in many templates) or from the language server — the **Choose Declaration**
popup lists them at the caret with file, line and the code of each target (or the symbol name
and its namespace), as in PHPStorm. Pick one with the arrow keys and `Enter`, or `Escape` to
cancel. The same popup is used by line markers with several targets, in every language pack
(PHP and its frameworks, WebForge, LuaForge).

![Choose Declaration in React](docs/screenshots/editor-polish-choose-declaration-react.png)

![Choose Declaration in Lua](docs/screenshots/editor-polish-choose-declaration-lua.png)

If nothing is found, a hint "Cannot find declaration to go to" appears at the caret.

Declarations outside the project (PHP's own classes in the PHP stubs, files a language server
points to outside the project) open in a **read-only** tab with a "Read-only library file"
banner and breadcrumbs such as `PHP Runtime › Core › Core_c.php › Throwable`.

**Back** / **Forward** (`Ctrl+Alt+Left` / `Ctrl+Alt+Right`, macOS `Cmd+[` / `Cmd+]`) return
to where you were.

### Implementation, Type Declaration, Super Method

| Action | Shortcut | macOS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Implementation(s) | `Ctrl+Alt+B`, `Ctrl+Alt+Click` | `Cmd+Alt+B`, `Cmd+Alt+Click` |
| Type Declaration | `Ctrl+Shift+B` | `Cmd+Shift+B` |
| Super Method | `Ctrl+U` | `Cmd+U` |

They ask the language servers (`textDocument/implementation`, `typeDefinition`) and fall back
to the PHP index in PHP files. When a server lacks the feature and the index finds
nothing, the hint says so.

> **Note:** Go to Test (`Ctrl+Shift+T`) is not available yet. In React and Vue projects, Go to
> Declaration on a component's own name lists its usages through the framework provider.

## Find Usages and Show Usages

**Show Usages** (`Ctrl+Alt+F7`, macOS `Cmd+Alt+F7`) opens a popup at the caret with every
usage of the symbol: its code line with the reference highlighted, the file and the line,
grouped by usage type (import, new instance, method call, static access, extends/implements,
type declaration, PHPDoc, …). `Up`/`Down` select, `Enter` opens, `Escape` closes, the pin
button opens the result in the Find tool window.

**Find Usages** (`Alt+F7`) shows the usages in the **Find** tool window (`Alt+3`, macOS
`Cmd+3`), one tab per search, as a tree by usage type and file; **Group by Usage Type**,
**Expand All** and **Collapse All** are on its toolbar. The Find stripe button appears once
there is a result.

Usages come from the language servers (`textDocument/references`); in PHP files without a
server answer, from the PHP index. Unsaved changes in open editors are taken into account.

![Show Usages](docs/screenshots/php-nav-show-usages.png)

![Find tool window](docs/screenshots/php-nav-find-window.png)

### Find Usages settings

**Find Usages Settings…** (`Ctrl+Alt+Shift+F7`, macOS `Cmd+Alt+Shift+F7`, or the **Settings**
button of the Find tool window and the Show Usages popup) opens the **Find Usages** dialog for
the element at the caret. What it offers depends on the element, like in PHPStorm:

| Element | Find | Options |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Class, trait, enum | Usages, Usages of methods, Usages of fields, Derived classes (classes) | Search in comments and strings, Search for text occurrences |
| Interface | Usages, Usages of methods, Implementing classes, Derived interfaces | Search in comments and strings, Search for text occurrences |
| Method | Usages, Overriding methods (implementing methods of interfaces and abstract methods) | Search in comments and strings, Search for text occurrences |
| Property | Read access, Write access | Search in comments and strings, Search for text occurrences |
| Variable | Read access, Write access | — (searched in its file) |
| Function, constant, other symbols | Usages | Search in comments and strings, Search for text occurrences |

**Scope** is one of Project Files (the default; `vendor/` and `node_modules/` left out),
Project and Libraries, Open Files, Current File, Recently Changed Files (the working tree's
changes and unsaved editors), Directory (with **Include subdirectories**) or Custom (a pattern
in PHPStorm's scope language such as `file:app//*.php&&!test:*..*`, or file globs separated by
`;` where `!` excludes, e.g. `app/**/*.php; !app/Legacy/**`). Below them the list offers
Project Production Files, Project Test Files and your named scopes from Settings | Appearance &
Behavior | Scopes (`findUsages.scope.name`; see [Scopes and file colors](docs/guide/user/scopes-and-file-colors.md)),
and **…** opens that page. **Open in new tab** off
replaces the active usages tab of the Find tool window instead of adding one.

**Find** saves the choices as settings (`findUsages.*`, see the
[settings reference](docs/guide/reference/settings.md)), so later Find Usages (`Alt+F7`) and Show
Usages (`Ctrl+Alt+F7`) runs use them too, and searches. **Search for text occurrences** adds
the name in files of other languages (configuration, templates, Markdown) as **Non-code
usages**; **Search in comments and strings** adds it in comments and string literals. The
filtering and the extra occurrences are computed in Rust next to the files, so remote projects
work the same.

![Find Usages dialog](docs/screenshots/find-usages-dialog.png)

### Find Usages in File

**Find Usages in File** (`Ctrl+F7`, macOS `Cmd+F7`) finds the usages of the element at the
caret in the current file and shows them in the Find tool window, like Find Usages with the
scope Current File ("Usages of Order in File 'PriceCalculator.php'").

![Find Usages in File](docs/screenshots/find-usages-in-file.png)

## Highlight usages

When the caret rests on a symbol, its usages in the file are highlighted: reads in blue, writes
(assignments, declarations, parameters) in red, also as marks on the right edge of the editor
(the error stripe; a click moves the caret there). Turn it off with **Settings | Editor |
General | Highlight on Caret Movement | Highlight usages of element at caret**
(`editor.highlightUsagesAtCaret`).

**Highlight Usages in File** (`Ctrl+Shift+F7`, macOS `Cmd+Shift+F7`) keeps the highlighting
until you press `Escape`; `F3` / `Shift+F3` jump to the next / previous usage, and the status
bar says "4 usages of '$price' found (Press Escape to remove the highlighting)". Pressing it
again on the same element removes the highlighting. Like PHPStorm it also highlights:

- the **exit points** of a function or method (every `return` and `throw`, closures left out)
  when the caret is on `return` or `throw`;
- the **implementing methods** when the caret is on `implements`, and the overriding methods on
  `extends` (PHP).

The usages come from the language servers (`textDocument/documentHighlight`), in PHP files
without a server answer from the PHP index (read and write access of properties and
variables), else from a lexical search for the identifier in its scope (variables in their
function; comments and strings left out).

![Usages of the element at the caret](docs/screenshots/highlight-usages-at-caret.png)

![Highlight Usages in File](docs/screenshots/highlight-usages-in-file.png)

![Exit points](docs/screenshots/highlight-exit-points.png)

## Problems

Diagnostics from language servers (and Forge's own syntax checks for YAML, JSON, INI, dotenv,
Bash, Python, Postfix and similar files) appear as:

- squiggles: red for errors, yellow for warnings, a weaker underline for weak warnings; unused
  code is grayed, deprecated usages are struck through;
- markers in the gutter;
- the **inspection widget** in the top-right corner of the editor: a ✓ when the file is clean,
  otherwise the number of errors and warnings. Click it to open the Problems tool window.

Typos and grammar problems in comments, strings, names, text files and commit messages are
inspections of their own (green and blue underlines, `Alt+Enter` for suggestions and the
dictionaries); see [Spelling and grammar](docs/guide/user/spelling-and-grammar.md).

JSON and YAML files with a JSON schema (`composer.json`, `package.json`, Compose files, CI
pipelines, your own mappings) are checked against it, with schema-driven completion and hover;
see [JSON Schema](docs/guide/user/json-schema.md).

**Next Highlighted Error** `F2` and **Previous Highlighted Error** `Shift+F2` move the caret
between problems.

The **Problems** tool window (`Alt+6`, macOS `Cmd+6`) has two tabs: **Current File** and
**Project Errors**, each a file → problem tree. Click a problem to open it.

![Problems tool window](docs/screenshots/lsp-problems.png)

## Rename

**Rename…** (`Shift+F6`) renames the symbol at the caret everywhere, like PHPStorm's in-place
rename:

1. The name gets an edit box and every occurrence in the file is highlighted. Type the new name;
   the occurrences change as you type.
2. **Enter** (or `Tab`, or moving the caret out of the box) renames it in the whole project,
   including files that are not open. **Escape** puts the old name back.
3. `Shift+F6` again opens the **Rename** dialog: the new name, **Rename file** for classes and
   **Preview**, which lists every change before anything is written.

![In-place rename](docs/screenshots/rename-in-place.png)

When the rename would break something, the **Problems Detected** dialog lists the problems
first (a class or member with the new name already exists, a file with the new name is in the
way) together with every occurrence; **Continue** renames anyway, **Cancel** keeps the old name
and **Show in View** cancels and lists the problems in the Find tool window. In PHP files the
check also runs when a language server computes the rename.

![Problems Detected](docs/screenshots/rename-refactoring-preview.png)

![Rename conflicts in the Find tool window](docs/screenshots/rename-conflicts-in-find.png)

![Rename dialog](docs/screenshots/rename-dialog.png)

- The language server computes the rename where it can (TypeScript, Vue, Lua, php-lsp,
  …); PHP files fall back to Forge's PHP index, see [PHP](docs/guide/user/php.md#rename).
- Renaming a class whose file is named after it (`Order.php` declaring `class Order`) also
  renames the file, like PHPStorm; untick **Rename file** in the hint below the edit box or in
  the dialog to keep the name. Open tabs follow the file.
- An invalid name ("'2fa' is not a valid identifier") keeps the edit box open.
- **Undo:** the whole rename is one step. `Ctrl+Z` (macOS `Cmd+Z`) in any editor the rename
  changed undoes it in every file: open editors, files that were not open (written back
  through the project, also on remote hosts) and a renamed file. `Ctrl+Shift+Z` redoes it.
  Files edited after the rename are left alone and a balloon names them. Redo is not
  available in a tab that undo reopened under its old name.
- Open files keep the change as unsaved edits; files that were not open are saved directly.
- In the **Project** view, `Shift+F6` renames the selected file or folder.
  **Refactor | Rename File…** renames the file of the current editor.

## Show Context Actions

**Show Context Actions** (`Alt+Enter`) opens PHPStorm's intention popup at the caret:

- **Quick fixes** (red bulb) from the language servers, for example "Remove unused import" or
  "Add method 'markAsPaid()' to class 'Order'";
- **Intentions** (yellow bulb) from the language servers and Forge's own PHP intentions;
- refactorings and source actions, and links like **Generate…** (`Alt+Insert`) last.

In strings, the popup also offers **Inject language or reference**, **Edit &lt;language&gt;
Fragment** and **Un-inject Language** (see [Language injections](docs/guide/user/language-injections.md)).

On an undeclared PHP name, the quick fixes include **Create method / field / constant /
function / class**, see [PHP: Create from usage](docs/guide/user/php.md#create-from-usage).

![Context actions](docs/screenshots/context-actions.png)

Use `Up` / `Down` and `Enter`, or click. An entry with `›` has more options ("Fix all '…'
problems in file"): open them with `Right`, go back with `Left`. Typing filters the list.
`Escape` closes it. A chosen fix is applied as one undo step, also when it changes other files.

When actions are available at the caret line, a **light bulb** appears at the start of the line
after a short pause (red when a quick fix is available); click it to open the popup.

![Light bulb](docs/screenshots/light-bulb.png)

## Reformat Code

**Reformat Code** (`Ctrl+Alt+L`, macOS `Cmd+Alt+L`) formats the file with the language
server's document formatting. Lua files use StyLua when it is installed (see
[LuaForge](docs/guide/user/luaforge.md)). The server gets the [code style](#code-style) of the file's
language, and Forge then applies the options the server does not know (see
[Code style](#code-style)).

| Scroll Up / Down | `Ctrl+Up` / `Ctrl+Down` | — |
| Go to Line/Column | `Ctrl+G` | `Cmd+L` |
| Undo / Redo | `Ctrl+Z` / `Ctrl+Shift+Z` | `Cmd+Z` / `Cmd+Shift+Z` |
| Copy Absolute Path | `Ctrl+Shift+C` | `Cmd+Shift+C` |
| Copy Reference (`path:line`) | `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+C` | `Cmd+Alt+Shift+C` |

Without a selection, **Copy** and **Cut** take the whole line, as in PHPStorm.

## Multiple carets and column selection

![Clone Caret Below on the imports of User.php](docs/screenshots/clone-carets.png)

Everything you type, delete, copy or paste applies at every caret. The status bar shows
`3 carets` instead of the caret position while there are several; `Escape` returns to one caret.

| Action | Windows/Linux | macOS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Clone Caret Above / Below | `Ctrl` twice, hold, then `Up` / `Down` | `Alt` twice, hold, then `Up` / `Down` |
| Add or remove a caret | `Alt+Shift`+click | `Alt+Shift`+click |
| Add Carets to Ends of Selected Lines | `Alt+Shift+G` | `Alt+Shift+G` |
| Add Selection for Next Occurrence | `Alt+J` | `Ctrl+G` |
| Unselect Occurrence | `Alt+Shift+J` | `Ctrl+Shift+G` |
| Select All Occurrences | `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+J` | `Ctrl+Cmd+G` |
| Rectangular selection | `Alt`+drag or middle-button drag | `Alt`+drag or middle-button drag |
| Column Selection Mode | `Alt+Shift+Insert` | `Cmd+Shift+8` |

- **Clone Caret Above / Below** adds a caret on the line above or below every caret, in the same
  column (short lines get the caret at their end, the column is kept for longer lines further
  on). Keep `Ctrl` down and press the arrow again for more carets; the other arrow takes the
  last clones back. The actions are also in Settings | Keymap | Editor Actions, where you can
  give them ordinary shortcuts.
- **Alt+Shift+click** adds a caret, or removes the caret you click on; `Alt+Shift`+drag adds a
  selection.
- **Add Selection for Next Occurrence** selects the word at the caret first, then adds the next
  occurrence as another selection. **Select All Occurrences** works without a selection too.
- **Column Selection Mode** (Edit | Column Selection Mode, also in the editor context menu) makes
  `Shift`+arrow keys and mouse drags select rectangles, one selection per line, until you turn it
  off again. It is per editor; the status bar shows **Column** while it is on (click it to turn
  the mode off). In this mode `Alt`+drag makes an ordinary selection.
- A middle-button **click** still goes to the declaration; only a drag selects a rectangle.

![Column Selection Mode with a rectangle over the @property tags](docs/screenshots/column-selection-mode.png)

### Copy and paste with multiple carets

Copying with several carets remembers the text of each caret. Pasting with the same number of
carets puts one part at each caret, like PHPStorm, even when the parts span several lines; with
another number of carets the whole text is pasted at every caret. Text with as many lines as
there are carets is spread one line per caret.

## Paste from History

![Paste from History](docs/screenshots/paste-from-history.png)

**Edit | Paste Special | Paste from History…** (`Ctrl+Shift+V`, macOS `Cmd+Shift+V`) lists the
texts copied or cut in Forge during this session, newest first, with a preview of the selected
entry. Type to filter the list, `Enter` (or a click) pastes, `Delete` removes the entry, `Escape`
closes the popup. The pasted entry moves to the top and becomes the clipboard content again. An
entry copied with several carets shows the number of carets and pastes one part per caret.

The history lives in memory until Forge closes; it is never written to disk. Its size is
**Maximum number of contents to keep in clipboard** in Settings | Editor | General | Limits
(default 20). Paste from History also works in text fields such as the commit message.

**Paste as Plain Text** (`Ctrl+Alt+Shift+V`) pastes the clipboard text unchanged. Forge does not
reformat pasted code or add imports on paste, so it behaves like **Paste**, including the
one-part-per-caret rule.

## Folding

Click the fold markers in the gutter, or use:

| Action | Windows/Linux | macOS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Expand / Collapse | `Ctrl+=` / `Ctrl+-` | `Cmd+=` / `Cmd+-` |
| Expand / Collapse Recursively | `Ctrl+Alt+=` / `Ctrl+Alt+-` | `Cmd+Alt+=` / `Cmd+Alt+-` |
| Expand All / Collapse All | `Ctrl+Shift+=` / `Ctrl+Shift+-` | `Cmd+Shift+=` / `Cmd+Shift+-` |

Custom folding regions (`// region Name` … `// endregion`, `#region`, `<!-- region -->`,
`// <editor-fold desc="…">`) fold too and show their name. Sticky lines, breadcrumbs, rendered
doc comments and Reader mode are described in
[Sticky lines, breadcrumbs and Reader mode](docs/guide/user/code-structure.md).

## Find and replace in a file

**Find** (`Ctrl+F`, macOS `Cmd+F`) and **Replace** (`Ctrl+R`, macOS `Cmd+R`) open the search
panel of the editor (CodeMirror's search panel) with match case, regular expression and
whole word options. **Find Next**
`F3` and **Find Previous** `Shift+F3` (macOS `Cmd+G` / `Cmd+Shift+G`) move between matches.
Other occurrences of the selected text are highlighted automatically.

To search the whole project, use [Find in Files](docs/guide/user/search-everywhere.md#find-in-files)
(`Ctrl+Shift+F`, macOS `Cmd+Shift+F`).

Replace in Files (`Ctrl+Shift+R`, macOS `Cmd+Shift+R`) opens the Find tool window with a
**Replace with** field (see [Search](docs/guide/user/search-everywhere.md)). The Find tool window also shows
[usages](#find-usages-and-show-usages) and the Find in Files results you open there (see
[Find tool window](docs/guide/user/workbench.md#find-tool-window)).

## Gutter

Left of the text, from outside in: line numbers, feature icons, Git change markers, fold
markers.

- **Git change markers** show added, modified and deleted lines compared with `HEAD`. Click
  one to see the change, roll it back or open the diff. See [Git](docs/guide/user/git.md#in-the-editor).
- **Line markers** of plugins: routes on controller actions, "go to template", entity ⇄
  repository, Angular component ⇄ template, compose services, and more. Click to navigate.
- **Implemented / overridden markers** in PHP: ↓ on classes with subclasses, interfaces and
  methods with implementations or overrides, ↑ on methods that implement or override one. See
  [PHP](docs/guide/user/php.md#gutter-icons).
- **Run icons** ▶ next to PHPUnit tests, `package.json` scripts, Lua main chunks, scratch
  files, `.http` requests, compose services and Dockerfiles.
- **Breakpoints**: click a line number in a PHP file to toggle a breakpoint (drawn over the
  number, as in the New UI), or press `Ctrl+F8` (macOS `Cmd+F8`). Right-click it to edit its
  condition. See [Debugging](docs/guide/user/debugging.md).
- **Bookmarks**: a bookmark icon, or the bookmark's mnemonic, on bookmarked lines (`F11`,
  `Ctrl+F11`). See [Bookmarks](docs/guide/user/workbench.md#bookmarks).
- **Annotate with Git Blame**: right-click the gutter. See [Git](docs/guide/user/git.md#blame).
- **Color swatches** next to colors in CSS, markup and scripts; click one to open the color
  picker. See [Emmet and color previews](docs/guide/user/emmet-and-colors.md#color-previews).

## Context menu

Right-click in the editor (or press the `Menu` key on Windows/Linux keyboards) to open the
editor context menu:

![Editor context menu](docs/screenshots/context-menu-editor.png)

| Entry | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Show Context Actions | works, see [Show Context Actions](#show-context-actions) |
| Paste from History… | not available yet |
| Cut, Copy, Paste | works |
| Copy / Paste Special > Copy Absolute Path, Copy Reference, Paste as Plain Text | works |
| Select All | works |
| Column Selection Mode | not available yet (use `Alt`+drag) |
| Find Usages | works |
| Refactor > Rename… | works, see [Rename](#rename) |
| Refactor > Refactor This… | works, see [Refactoring shortcuts](docs/guide/user/shortcuts/refactoring.md#refactor-this) |
| Refactor > Extract/Introduce > Variable…, Constant…, Field…, Parameter…, Method… | works, see [PHP](docs/guide/user/php.md#extract-introduce-and-inline) |
| Refactor > Inline… | works, see [PHP](docs/guide/user/php.md#extract-introduce-and-inline) |
| Refactor > Extract/Introduce > Interface…, Superclass…, Pull Members Up…, Push Members Down… | works in PHP classes, see [PHP](docs/guide/user/php.md#extract-interface-and-superclass-pull-members-up-and-push-members-down) |
| Go To > Declaration or Usages, Line/Column | works |
| Go To > Implementation(s) | works |
| Generate… | works in PHP files, see [PHP](docs/guide/user/php.md#generate) |
| Reformat Code | works |
| Optimize Imports | works, see [Optimize Imports and Auto Import](docs/guide/user/imports.md) |
| Comment with Line Comment | works |
| Git > Annotate with Git Blame | works |

Right-clicking outside the current selection moves the caret there first, like PHPStorm.

## Files changed on disk

When a file changes on disk (a checkout, a pull, a rollback, an AI agent's edit, a change in
another editor), the open tab is reloaded with the new content. The reload is not an undo
step: `Ctrl+Z` does not go back across it.

Line endings and encodings are preserved: a file with Windows line endings (CRLF) stays CRLF
when you save it, a Windows-1252 file stays Windows-1252. Forge detects both when it opens a
file (UTF-8 with or without BOM, UTF-16 LE/BE, ISO-8859-1, Windows-1252). Change them in the
status bar, see [Line separator, encoding and indent](#line-separator-encoding-and-indent).

## Saving

Files are saved with `Ctrl+S` (Save All) and automatically (Settings | Appearance & Behavior |
System Settings | Autosave): when Forge loses the focus (`system.autosave.onFrameDeactivation`,
on by default) and, if enabled, after `system.autosave.idleSeconds` seconds without typing or
clicking (`system.autosave.onIdle`).

Saving applies Settings | Editor | General | On Save, like PHPStorm:

| Option | Setting | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Remove trailing spaces on: None / Modified lines / All lines | `editor.stripTrailingSpaces` | Modified lines |
| Ensure every saved file ends with a line break | `editor.ensureNewlineAtEof` | on |

"Modified lines" are the lines changed since the file was opened or last saved. Lines with a
caret keep their spaces, so saving never moves what you are typing. An `.editorconfig` with
`trim_trailing_whitespace` or `insert_final_newline` overrides both options for its files.

Settings | Tools | [Actions on Save](docs/guide/user/actions-on-save.md) adds Reformat code, Optimize
imports, Rearrange code, code cleanup and external tools (ESLint, Prettier, PHP CS Fixer,
Laravel Pint) to an explicit save (`Ctrl+S`), and optionally to autosave.

When Forge gets the focus back it re-reads the open files that changed on disk and refreshes
the Project view and Git status (`system.syncExternalChanges`).

## Code style

![Code style of PHP](docs/screenshots/code-style-php-spaces.png)

Settings | Editor | Code Style works like PHPStorm's: a **scheme** holds every option, the
**Code Style** page sets the general ones and each language has a page of its own (PHP,
HTML, CSS/SCSS/Less, JavaScript, TypeScript, JSON, YAML, Lua, Blade, Twig, SQL, XML,
Markdown).

### Schemes

The **Scheme** box at the top of every page selects the scheme the project uses, and the
pages edit the selected scheme:

- **Default** (stored in the IDE, in your user settings) applies to projects that have no
  scheme of their own.
- **Project** (stored in the project, `.forge/settings.toml`, so it can be committed) is the
  project's own scheme. Options it does not set come from Default.
- More IDE schemes come from **Duplicate…**, **Copy to IDE…** and **Import Scheme**.

The ⚙ button next to the box opens the scheme actions: **Copy to Project…** (the current IDE
scheme becomes the Project scheme), **Copy to IDE…**, **Duplicate…**, **Rename…** and
**Delete** (for your own IDE schemes), **Reset** (the built-in defaults; the Project scheme
goes back to Default's values), **Export** and **Import Scheme**. Schemes are exported as
**IntelliJ IDEA code style XML** (the `<code_scheme>` format of PHPStorm's
`.idea/codeStyles/*.xml`; options PHPStorm has no name for are kept in a
`<ForgeCodeStyleSettings>` element) or as **Forge code style JSON** with every option.
Importing reads either format, also a PHPStorm `Project.xml`, into the current scheme or a new
one. Like every page of the Settings dialog, the changes apply with **Apply** or **OK**.

![Scheme actions](docs/screenshots/code-style-scheme-menu.png)

The settings keys did not change: the Default scheme is stored under `<language>.codeStyle.*`
(`php.codeStyle.indent`) and `editor.codeStyle.*` in the user settings, the Project scheme
under the same keys in the project settings, other IDE schemes under
`editor.codeStyle.schemes.<id>.*`, and `editor.codeStyle.scheme` names the project's scheme.
Settings files of older versions keep working; their single PHP brace option
(`php.codeStyle.braces`) becomes the three brace options of the PHP page.

### General

![Code Style General](docs/screenshots/code-style-general.png)

- **Line separator** for new files (LF, CRLF or the system's); existing files keep theirs.
- **Hard wrap at** (120) draws the right margin, **Visual guides** (e.g. `80, 120`) more
  vertical lines.
- **Detect and use existing file indents for editing** (`editor.codeStyle.detectIndents`): a
  file indented differently from the code style (2 spaces in a 4-space project, tabs) keeps
  its indent while you edit it.
- **Enable EditorConfig support** (`editor.codeStyle.useEditorConfig`): `.editorconfig` files
  from the project root down to the file set `indent_style`, `indent_size`, `tab_width`,
  `end_of_line` (for new files), `max_line_length`, `trim_trailing_whitespace` and
  `insert_final_newline`; they win over the scheme. A `charset` the file does not have is
  named in the encoding tooltip.
- The **Formatter** tab: **Turn formatter on/off with markers in code comments**. Lines
  between a comment with `@formatter:off` and one with `@formatter:on` (the markers can be
  changed) keep their text when you reformat; the preview shows it.

### Language pages

![Code style of JavaScript](docs/screenshots/code-style-javascript.png)

Each language page has PHPStorm's tabs, the options on the left and a preview on the right
that is formatted again as you change an option:

- **Tabs and Indents**: Use tab character, Tab size, Indent, Continuation indent and Keep
  indents on empty lines (YAML: Indent sequence value). Enter, `Tab`, the status bar's indent
  and Reformat Code use them.
- **Spaces**: before parentheses, around operators, within parentheses, brackets and braces,
  before and after commas and colons, … (as far as the language has them).
- **Wrapping and Braces**: brace placement (End of line / Next line), `else`/`catch`/`finally`
  on a new line (PHP), one selector per line (CSS), wrapping of objects and arrays (JSON),
  attributes (HTML, XML), long text (YAML), simple statements on one line (Lua).
- **Blank Lines**: Keep maximum blank lines in code, plus minimums (PHP: after namespace,
  after imports, around methods, before `return`; CSS: around rules; Markdown: around headers
  and block elements).
- Language tabs: **Code Conversion** (PHP: short or long array syntax, a comma after the last
  element of multi-line arrays, the case of `true`/`false`/`null`), **Punctuation**
  (JavaScript/TypeScript: semicolons, quotes), **Case** (SQL keywords), **Other** (CSS hex
  color case, YAML quotes, HTML "Do not indent children of", Lua quotes and call parentheses
  for StyLua and lua-language-server).

**Set from…** (top right) sets a language's options from a predefined style: PHP **PSR-12**,
**PER Coding Style 2.0**, **Symfony**, **Laravel**, **WordPress** and **Drupal**; JavaScript
and TypeScript **JavaScript Standard Style**, **Airbnb-like** and **Prettier defaults**;
CSS **stylelint-config-standard**; Lua **StyLua defaults** and **2 spaces, single quotes**;
SQL **Upper case keywords**.

![PHP set from WordPress](docs/screenshots/code-style-php-wordpress.png)

### What Reformat Code uses

Indents come from the scheme unless EditorConfig or the detected indent of the file wins
(see above). Then:

- The language server gets the options in its settings before it formats: php-lsp the
  brace placement, typescript-language-server the spaces, braces, semicolons and quote
  preference (`typescript.format` / `javascript.format`), the CSS, HTML, JSON, YAML and XML
  servers their `format` settings, lua-language-server its `Lua.format.defaultConfig`.
  StyLua gets indent, column width, quotes, call parentheses and simple statements on its
  command line when the project has no `stylua.toml`.
- Forge then applies what the formatter does not know, on the lines as they are: in PHP the
  spaces, brace and `else`/`catch`/`finally` placement and the code conversions (and the blank
  lines, see [PHP](docs/guide/user/php.md#code-style)); quotes in `.js`/`.ts` files without JSX; hex colors in
  CSS; SQL keyword case; Markdown's spaces and blank lines; the spaces inside Blade and Twig
  delimiters; Keep maximum blank lines; Keep indents on empty lines; and the formatter
  markers. Strings, heredocs, comments and code blocks keep their text.

## Line separator, encoding and indent

![Line separator popup](docs/screenshots/status-line-separator.png)

The status bar shows the active file's line separator, encoding and indent. Click them:

- **Line separator** (`LF`, `CRLF`, `CR`): pick another one; the file is converted and saved
  right away.
- **Encoding** (`UTF-8`, `UTF-8 BOM`, `UTF-16LE`, `ISO-8859-1`, `windows-1252`, …): pick
  another one and choose **Reload** (read the file again in that encoding, for a file that
  was detected wrongly; only without unsaved changes) or **Convert** (save the text in the
  new encoding). **Add BOM** / **Remove BOM** for UTF-8 files. Characters the encoding cannot
  hold stop the conversion with a message.
- **Indent** (`4 spaces`, `2 spaces*`, `Tab`): where it comes from is in the tooltip (code
  style, EditorConfig, or detected in the file, marked with `*`). The popup opens **Configure
  Indents for PHP…** or turns indent detection off for the project.

![Encoding popup](docs/screenshots/status-encoding.png)

## Inlay hints

![Inlay hints](docs/screenshots/editor-inlay-hints.png)

Language servers show parameter names at call sites (`precision: 2`) and inferred types
(`fn ($line): float`) inside the code. Settings | Editor | Inlay Hints:

| Option | Setting | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Parameter names (literal and null arguments) | `editor.inlayHints.parameterNames` | on |
| Inferred variable types | `editor.inlayHints.types` | off |
| Return types of closures and functions | `editor.inlayHints.returnTypes` | on |
| Implementations and inheritors (Code Vision) | `editor.inlayHints.implementations` | on |
| Per language: PHP, JavaScript and TypeScript, Lua, other languages | `editor.inlayHints.languages.<id>` | on |

Hints need a server that reports them: php-lsp, typescript-language-server / vtsls and
lua-language-server (Forge turns their hints on and filters them by these settings).

**Code Vision**: above PHP classes and methods with subclasses, implementations or overrides
Forge shows "4 inheritors", "2 implementations" or "1 override" (from the PHP index); click
it to go there.

![Code Vision](docs/screenshots/editor-code-vision.png)

## Soft wraps and appearance

Settings | Editor | General controls soft wrapping (`editor.softWraps` with the patterns in
`editor.softWrapFiles`, by default `*.md; *.txt; *.rst; *.adoc`), whitespace, line numbers,
the caret row highlight, caret blinking with its blink period (`editor.caret.blinkPeriod`) and
smooth scrolling. Settings | Editor | Font sets the font, size, line height and ligatures. See
the [settings reference](docs/guide/reference/settings.md).

# Sticky lines, breadcrumbs and Reader mode

These editor features show where you are in a file and make code you only read easier to
read. They work for PHP, Blade, Twig, HTML, XML, Vue, JavaScript, TypeScript (and JSX/TSX),
CSS, SCSS, Less and Lua, plus the brace languages Java, Kotlin, Go, Rust, C, C++ and C#.
Forge finds the classes, functions, blocks, rules and tags of a file itself, so they work
without a language server.

## Sticky lines

![Sticky lines](docs/screenshots/sticky-lines.png)

While you scroll, the first lines of the scopes around the top of the editor stay pinned
there: the namespace, class and method, `if` / `foreach` / `try` / `match` blocks, CSS rules
and at-rules, HTML parent elements and Lua functions and blocks. Each sticky line shows its
line number and keeps its syntax colors.

- **Click** a sticky line to jump to it.
- **Right-click** the sticky lines for **Configure Sticky Lines…** and **Disable Sticky Lines
  for** the file's language.
- **View | Active Editor | Show Sticky Lines** switches them for the current language.

Settings | Editor | General | **Sticky Lines**:

| Setting | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Show sticky lines while scrolling | on | `editor.stickyLines.enabled` |
| Limit sticky lines | 5 | `editor.stickyLines.maxLines`, 1–20 |
| Show sticky lines for | all languages | one checkbox per language (`editor.stickyLines.disabledLanguages`) |

![Sticky lines settings](docs/screenshots/sticky-lines-settings.png)

## Breadcrumbs

![Breadcrumbs and siblings](docs/screenshots/breadcrumbs-siblings.png)

The breadcrumbs at the bottom of the editor show the declarations around the caret, e.g.
`PriceCalculator › total()`, `@media (max-width: 600px) › .card` or
`html › body.antialiased › div#app`.

- **Click** a crumb to move the caret to that declaration.
- The small arrow next to a crumb (on hover) lists its **siblings**, e.g. the other methods of
  the class; pick one to go there.
- **View | Active Editor | Show Breadcrumbs** switches them for the current language.

The file path is in the [navigation bar](docs/guide/user/navigation-bar-and-file-structure.md#navigation-bar)
above the editor or in the status bar.

Settings | Editor | General | **Breadcrumbs**: *Show breadcrumbs* (`editor.breadcrumbs.show`),
*Placement* **Top** or **Bottom** (`editor.breadcrumbs.placement`, default Bottom) and one
checkbox per language (`editor.breadcrumbs.disabledLanguages`).

![Breadcrumbs at the top](docs/screenshots/breadcrumbs-top.png)

HTML, Vue and template files list elements as `tag#id.class`; `<script>` and `<style>`
blocks contain the functions and rules inside them.

![Breadcrumbs and Structure of an HTML file](docs/screenshots/breadcrumbs-web.png)

## Custom folding regions

![Folding regions](docs/screenshots/folding-regions.png)

Comments mark regions that fold like any other block and show their name when folded:

| Language | Start | End |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PHP, JavaScript, TypeScript, CSS preprocessors, C-like | `// region Name` or `//region Name` | `// endregion` |
| PHP, C# | `#region Name` | `#endregion` |
| HTML, Vue, Blade, Twig | `<!-- region Name -->`, `{{-- region Name --}}`, `{# region Name #}` | `<!-- endregion -->`, … |
| CSS | `/* region Name */` | `/* endregion */` |
| Lua | `-- region Name` or `--region Name` | `-- endregion` |
| NetBeans style, any language | `// <editor-fold desc="Name">` | `// </editor-fold>` |

- Regions can be nested. A region without a name folds to `...`.
- `<editor-fold desc="Name" defaultstate="collapsed">` regions start folded.
- **Code | Surround With** (`Ctrl+Alt+T`, macOS `Cmd+Alt+T`) › **region...endregion
  Comments** wraps the selected lines in a region (PHP, JavaScript, Lua, HTML and CSS); type
  its name at the caret. See [Live templates](docs/guide/user/live-templates.md).
- The **Structure** tool window (`Alt+7`, macOS `Cmd+7`) groups the members inside a region
  under the region's name.

![Structure view with regions](docs/screenshots/structure-regions.png)

## Rendered documentation comments

![Rendered doc comments](docs/screenshots/rendered-doc-comments.png)

PHPDoc, JSDoc / TSDoc and LuaDoc (LuaCATS `---@param`) comments can be shown as formatted
text, like Quick Documentation: the description with its Markdown, then the tags as a table
(**Params:**, **Returns:**, **Throws:**, **Properties:**, **Since:**, **See also:**,
**Author:** …) and `@deprecated` as a red note. `{@link https://… text}` becomes a link that
opens in the browser, `{@see Class::method()}` code.

| Action | Windows/Linux | macOS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Toggle Rendered View of the comment at (or above) the caret | `Ctrl+Alt+Q` | `Ctrl+Alt+Q` |
| Toggle with the mouse | book icon in the gutter; pencil icon on a rendered comment | |
| Render All Doc Comments of the file | Tools \| Render All Doc Comments | |
| Collapse Doc Comments | Code \| Folding \| Collapse Doc Comments | |

Settings | Editor | General | Appearance | **Render documentation comments**
(`editor.renderDocComments`, off by default) renders every comment of the files you open.

## Reader mode

![Reader mode](docs/screenshots/reader-mode.png)

Files you only read open in **Reader mode**: library files (under `vendor/` and
`node_modules/`, and the PHP stubs Go to Declaration opens) and read-only files. Reader mode
renders the documentation comments, turns on font ligatures and increases the line spacing.

The **Reader Mode** button at the top right of the editor switches it off (to read the
comments as code) and on again; **View | Active Editor | Reader Mode** does the same.

Settings | Editor | **Reader Mode**:

| Setting | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Use Reader mode | on | `editor.readerMode.enabled` |
| Use for | Library and read-only files | `editor.readerMode.applyTo`: library files, read-only files, or both |
| Rendered documentation comments | on | `editor.readerMode.renderDocs` |
| Ligatures | on | `editor.readerMode.ligatures` |
| Increased line spacing | on | `editor.readerMode.increaseLineSpacing` |

![Reader mode settings](docs/screenshots/reader-mode-settings.png)

Source: docs/guide/user/markdown-images-csv.md

# Markdown, images and CSV

Some files open in an editor made for them, like in PHPStorm: Markdown files and SVG images
get a preview next to the text, raster images open in the image editor, and CSV/TSV files can
be edited as a table. All of them work in remote projects too: files and images are read
through the project backend.

## Markdown

`.md` and `.markdown` files open in the Markdown editor: the text on the left, the rendered
preview on the right.

![Markdown editor and preview](docs/screenshots/markdown-preview.png)

### Layout

The three buttons in the top-right corner of the editor switch the layout of the file:

| Button | Action | Action id |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Editor Only | only the text | `TextEditorWithPreview.Layout.EditorOnly` |
| Editor and Preview | text and preview side by side; drag the divider to resize | `TextEditorWithPreview.Layout.EditorAndPreview` |
| Preview Only | only the preview | `TextEditorWithPreview.Layout.PreviewOnly` |

The actions have no default shortcut; find them with Find Action (`Ctrl+Shift+A`) or bind
keys in Settings | Keymap. The layout is remembered per file until Forge restarts; new files
open with the default layout from Settings | Languages & Frameworks | Markdown.

![Preview only, light theme](docs/screenshots/markdown-preview-only-light.png)

### What the preview shows

- **GitHub-flavored Markdown**: tables (with column alignment), task lists, strikethrough,
  footnotes (numbered in the order they are used, listed at the end), autolinks (`https://…`,
  `www.…` and e-mail addresses) and GitHub alerts (`> [!NOTE]`, `[!TIP]`, `[!IMPORTANT]`,
  `[!WARNING]`, `[!CAUTION]`).
- **Code blocks** with syntax colors for PHP, JavaScript, TypeScript, JSX/TSX, CSS, HTML,
  JSON, YAML, XML, Python and Rust (other languages get a simple highlighter).
- **Mermaid diagrams**: a ```` ```mermaid ```` block is drawn as a diagram (flowcharts,
  sequence, class, state, ER, Gantt, …). An invalid diagram shows Mermaid's error and the
  code. Turn it off in the settings to see the code instead.
- **Images**: relative paths (`![Logo](docs/guide/user/docs/logo.png)`, `<img src="logo.svg" width="120">`)
  are resolved against the Markdown file (`/…` against the project root) and loaded from the
  project; `https://` images are loaded from the web.
- **Front matter**: a YAML (`---`) or TOML (`+++`) block at the start of the file is shown as
  a table, or hidden (setting **Front matter**).
- **HTML in Markdown** is shown safely: `<img>`, `<a href>`, `<br>`, `<b>`/`<strong>`,
  `<i>`/`<em>` and `<s>`/`<del>` are rendered, HTML comments and all other tags (scripts,
  styles, event handlers) are dropped and only their text is kept.

The preview updates while you type.

### Links

| Link | Click opens |
| --- | --- |
| `#getting-started` | scrolls the preview to that heading (GitHub-style anchors) |
| `docs/setup.md`, `../app/Models/User.php` | the project file in Forge |
| `docs/setup.md#install` | the Markdown file at that heading |
| `src/app.ts#L42` | the file at line 42 |
| `https://…`, `mailto:…` | the system browser or mail client |

### Synchronized scrolling

With **Editor and Preview**, scrolling the editor scrolls the preview to the same block and
scrolling the preview moves the editor to its source. Turn it off with **Synchronize scrolling
between the editor and the preview**.

![Synchronized scrolling](docs/screenshots/markdown-preview-scrolled.png)

### Settings

| Setting | Key | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Default layout | `markdown.defaultLayout` | Editor and Preview |
| Synchronize scrolling between the editor and the preview | `markdown.syncScroll` | on |
| Front matter: Show as table / Hide | `markdown.frontMatter` | Show as table |
| Mermaid | `markdown.mermaid` | on |

![Markdown settings](docs/screenshots/markdown-settings.png)

## Images

PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, ICO and BMP files open in the image editor.

![Image editor](docs/screenshots/image-editor.png)

| Toolbar button | Action id | Windows / Linux | macOS |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Zoom In | `Images.Editor.ZoomIn` | `Ctrl+=`, `Ctrl+NumPad+` | `Cmd+=`, `Cmd+NumPad+` |
| Zoom Out | `Images.Editor.ZoomOut` | `Ctrl+-`, `Ctrl+NumPad-` | `Cmd+-`, `Cmd+NumPad-` |
| Actual Size (1:1) | `Images.Editor.ActualSize` | `Ctrl+/`, `Ctrl+NumPad/` | `Cmd+/`, `Cmd+NumPad/` |
| Fit Zoom to Window | `Images.Editor.FitZoomToWindow` | | |
| Show Grid | `Images.Editor.ToggleGrid` | | |
| Show Chessboard | `Images.ToggleTransparencyChessboard` | | |

- `Ctrl` + mouse wheel zooms as well. Images open at 100%, or smaller when they do not fit.
- The **chessboard** shows transparent areas; the **grid** draws pixel lines from 300% zoom.
- The toolbar shows the zoom and the image info, for example
  `128x128 PNG (32-bit color) 484 B`. Format, size and colour depth are read from the file
  header in Rust.
- The editor reloads the image when the file changes on disk.

> **Note:** in a code editor `Ctrl+=`, `Ctrl+-` and `Ctrl+/` keep their editor meaning
> (Expand, Collapse, Comment with Line Comment); the image shortcuts apply while the image
> editor has focus.

### SVG

SVG files are text: they open in an editor with an image preview (the same toolbar), which
follows your typing. The layout buttons work as for Markdown; the default is set in
Settings | Editor | Image | **SVG files open with**.

![SVG editor and preview](docs/screenshots/svg-preview.png)

| Setting | Key | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |

| Show grid | `images.showGrid` | off |
| SVG files open with | `images.svgDefaultLayout` | Editor and Preview |

## CSV and TSV: Edit as Table

`.csv`, `.tsv` and `.tab` files have two tabs at the bottom of the editor: **Text** and
**Table**. The actions **Edit as Table** (`Csv.EditAsTable`) and **Edit as Text**
(`Csv.EditAsText`) switch them from Find Action or a shortcut you assign.

![CSV file as a table](docs/screenshots/csv-table.png)

- The delimiter is detected: tab for `.tsv`/`.tab`, otherwise the most frequent of `,` `;`
  tab and `|` in the first line. The toolbar shows it with the row and column count.
- **First row is header** uses the first row as column titles (columns are named `C1`, `C2`,
  … otherwise).
- Click a column header to sort ascending, again for descending, a third time for the file
  order. Numbers sort by value, text case-insensitively, empty cells last. Sorting changes
  only the view, not the file.
- Double-click a cell, press `Enter` or `F2`, or just start typing to edit it; `Enter` saves
  and moves down, `Tab` moves right, `Escape` cancels.
- The toolbar and the context menu add rows (above/below) and columns (left/right) and delete
  the selected rows or columns.
- The table and the text are the same document: every table change is one undoable edit in
  the editor, `Ctrl+S` saves it. Cells you do not touch are written back exactly as they
  were: the delimiter, the quotes of quoted cells, the line separator and the final line break
  stay. New values are quoted only when they need it (delimiter, quote or line break inside).

Settings | Editor | CSV/TSV:

| Setting | Key | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Open CSV/TSV files as: Text / Table | `csv.defaultView` | Text |
| First row is header | `csv.firstRowIsHeader` | on |

# Optimize Imports and Auto Import

Forge keeps `use` statements and `import` declarations tidy like PHPStorm: **Optimize
Imports** removes unused ones and sorts the rest, and **Auto Import** adds them while you
write code. PHP imports are Forge's own (they follow the PHP code style's **Imports** tab);
JavaScript, TypeScript and Vue imports come from the TypeScript language server.

## Optimize Imports

**Code | Optimize Imports** (`Ctrl+Alt+O`, also in the editor's context menu) works on the
file in the editor:

- **PHP**: removes the `use` statements nothing in the file refers to (code, attributes,
  PHPDoc types and annotations such as `@ORM\Column` count) and arranges the rest as the
  code style says. Group uses (`use A\{B, C};`) become single statements. Files with syntax
  errors are left alone.
- **JavaScript, TypeScript, Vue**: the TypeScript server's "Organize Imports" (removes unused
  imports, sorts and merges them).

A hint above the caret says what happened: "Removed 2 imports, rearranged imports" or
"Imports are already optimized". The change is one undo step.

![Optimize Imports in the editor](docs/screenshots/optimize-imports-editor.png)

### Folders and the whole project

In the Project view, select folders or files and press `Ctrl+Alt+O`, or right-click and
choose **Optimize Imports…**. The **Optimize Imports** dialog shows what is optimized and
offers:

- **Include subdirectories**: also the files in subfolders (on by default).
- **Only VCS changed files**: only the files Git reports as changed or new.

**Run** optimizes every PHP, JavaScript, TypeScript and Vue file (Blade templates, minified
files, `vendor` and `node_modules` are skipped), applies the changes as one undoable step
(open editors included) and reports "Optimized imports in 3 files: removed 5 imports".

![Optimize Imports dialog](docs/screenshots/optimize-imports-dialog.png)

On save, **Settings | Tools | Actions on Save | Optimize imports** does the same for PHP
files, see [Actions on Save](docs/guide/user/actions-on-save.md).

## PHP code style: Imports

Settings | Editor | Code Style | PHP | **Imports** decides how Optimize Imports, Auto Import,
Actions on Save and every refactoring that adds imports (Import class, completion, Create
from usage, Move, Copy, Extract Interface, Pull Members Up) write `use` statements:

| Option | Values |
| --- | --- |
| Sort 'use' statements | **Alphabetically** (default), **By length** (shorter statements first), **Don't sort** (new imports go last) |
| Group 'use' statements | **By kind** (classes, then functions, then constants; default), **By kind and namespace** (also by the top-level namespace: `App`, `Illuminate`; global classes first), **Don't group** |
| Blank lines between groups | 0 (default) to 3 |
| Prefer fully qualified names (FQN) over imports | Completion and Import class write `\App\Models\User` instead of adding a `use` statement |

New imports are inserted in their group and in sort order among the existing ones; existing
imports are never reordered except by Optimize Imports.

![PHP code style Imports tab](docs/screenshots/code-style-php-imports.png)

## Auto Import settings

Settings | Editor | General | **Auto Import**:

![Auto Import settings](docs/screenshots/auto-import-settings.png)

### PHP

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Add unambiguous imports on the fly | off | After you stop typing, unresolved class names with exactly one candidate class get their `use` statement. The name you are still typing is left alone. |
| Optimize imports on the fly | off | Removes unused `use` statements while you edit, but not while the caret or your last edit is in the `use` block, and not an import whose name you are just typing (`Us` keeps `use App\Models\User;`). |
| Show import popup | on | The blue hint `? App\Models\User Alt+Enter` on an unresolved class name (`? Multiple choices… Alt+Enter` when several classes match). |
| Enable auto-import in namespace scope | on | Completing a class in a file with a namespace adds its `use` statement; off: the fully qualified name is inserted. |
| Enable auto-import in file scope | off | The same for files without a namespace. |
| Prefer FQN in PHPDoc | off | Classes completed or imported inside PHPDoc comments are written fully qualified. |
| Import classes from the global namespace | on | `use Exception;` for PHP's own classes in namespaced files; off: `\Exception`. |

A class with the same short name as an existing import or a class of the file is always
written fully qualified.

### JavaScript and TypeScript

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Add unambiguous imports on the fly | off | The TypeScript server's "add missing imports" after you stop typing, unless it would change the caret's line or the lines you just edited. |
| Optimize imports on the fly | off | The TypeScript server's "remove unused imports", with the same restriction. |
| Show import popup | on | `? Name from "module" Alt+Enter` on a name TypeScript cannot find; `Alt+Enter` lists the "Add import from" fixes. |
| Use paths relative to | Shortest path | How new import paths are written: shortest, project root (or `tsconfig` path mapping), current file, or module (non-relative). |
| Use type imports in TypeScript | off | `import type { … }` when only types are imported. |

Completion also adds the import of a completed name (the server's import edit), in PHP with
Forge's own rules above.

## Import class and the import popup

On an unresolved class name, **Alt+Enter** offers **Import class**. The candidates come from
the PHP index (project and `vendor` packages, also ones that are not indexed yet) and PHP's own
classes. With one candidate the import is added right away; with several, the **Class to
Import** chooser lists them with their namespaces.

While the import popup is shown, `Alt+Enter` imports its class directly (or opens the
chooser).

![Import popup](docs/screenshots/import-popup.png)

![Class to Import](docs/screenshots/import-class-chooser.png)

## Remote projects

Everything works in [remote projects](docs/guide/user/remote-development.md): the PHP index that finds the
candidates runs on the remote host, and folders are read and written there.

# Actions on Save

Settings | Tools | Actions on Save (`Ctrl+Alt+S`, then Tools) chooses what happens to a file
when you save it, like PHPStorm. Every action is off by default. The settings are stored per
project ("For current project"), so a team can share them in `.forge/settings.toml`.

![Actions on Save settings](docs/screenshots/actions-on-save-settings.png)

## Actions

| Action | Files | What it does | Configure… |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Reformat code** | the chosen file types (default: all) | Reformat Code (`Ctrl+Alt+L`): the language server's formatter, StyLua for Lua, plus the options of the [code style](docs/guide/user/editor.md#code-style) the formatter does not know. **Whole file** or **Changed lines** (only lines changed since the last commit; files that are not committed yet are reformatted completely). | Editor \| Code Style |
| **Optimize imports** | PHP | Removes unused `use` imports and arranges the rest as Settings \| Editor \| Code Style \| PHP \| Imports says (by default classes, then functions, then constants, each alphabetically), see [Optimize Imports](docs/guide/user/imports.md). Group uses (`use A\{B, C};`) are split into single imports. | |
| **Rearrange code** | PHP | Orders the members of classes, interfaces, traits and enums: trait `use`, enum cases, constants, properties, the constructor, the other methods. Members keep their order inside a group; docblocks, attributes and comments move with their member and blank lines stay where they were. | |
| **Run code cleanup** | PHP | Applies the safe quick fixes: removes unused imports, unnecessary semicolons (`;;`, `};`) and the redundant closing tag `?>` at the end of a pure PHP file. | |
| **Run biome check --write** | Biome's **Run for files** (default JavaScript, TypeScript, JSON and CSS) | `biome check --write <file>`: Biome's safe fixes and formatting. Where Biome applies, ESLint and Prettier are skipped (setting "Prefer Biome over ESLint and Prettier"). | Languages & Frameworks \| Code Quality Tools |
| **Run eslint --fix** | ESLint's **Run for files** (default `{**/*,*}.{js,ts,jsx,tsx,cjs,mjs,vue,html}`) | `eslint --fix <file>` with the project's ESLint configuration. | Languages & Frameworks \| Code Quality Tools |
| **Run stylelint --fix** | Stylelint's **Run for files** (default `{**/*,*}.{css,scss,less,vue}`) | `stylelint --fix <file>` with the project's Stylelint configuration. | Languages & Frameworks \| Code Quality Tools |
| **Run Prettier** | files matching **Run for files** (default `*.js; *.ts; *.jsx; *.tsx; *.cjs; *.cts; *.mjs; *.mts; *.vue; *.astro`) | `prettier --write <file>` with the project's Prettier configuration. | Languages & Frameworks \| Code Quality Tools |
| **Run Rector** | PHP | `rector process <file>` with the project's `rector.php`. | Languages & Frameworks \| PHP \| Quality Tools |
| **Run PHP CS Fixer** | PHP | `php-cs-fixer fix <file>` with the project's `.php-cs-fixer.dist.php`. | Languages & Frameworks \| PHP \| Quality Tools |
| **Run phpcbf** | PHP | PHP_CodeSniffer's fixer `phpcbf <file>` with the project's `phpcs.xml`. | Languages & Frameworks \| PHP \| Quality Tools |
| **Run Laravel Pint** | PHP | `pint <file>` with the project's `pint.json`. | Languages & Frameworks \| PHP \| Quality Tools |

The PHP actions are skipped for Blade templates and files with syntax errors; an import is
only removed when nothing in the file refers to it, including docblocks (`@var User`) and
annotations (`@ORM\Column`). The rows of a pack are shown only while its plugin is enabled.
"Update copyright notice" and "Upload to default server" are not offered because Forge has no
copyright profiles or deployment servers yet.

The "Reformat code" file types are picked from the **All file types** drop-down:

![Reformat code file types](docs/screenshots/actions-on-save-file-types.png)

## External tools

The web tools are the project's own packages, found and configured as on
[Web Code Quality Tools](docs/guide/user/web-quality-tools.md): the nearest `node_modules/eslint`,
`node_modules/prettier`, `node_modules/stylelint` or `node_modules/@biomejs/biome`, run with
the Node.js interpreter, and only for files below the tool's configuration file (automatic
configuration) or with the manual package, configuration file and options. A disabled tool
never runs on save. The PHP tools are the project's own installations: `vendor/bin/rector`,
`vendor/bin/php-cs-fixer`, `vendor/bin/phpcbf` and `vendor/bin/pint` (`.cmd` / `.bat` on
Windows). The page shows where each one was found, or "Not installed in the project". A
different executable can be set on the tool's settings page (`web.eslint.path`,
`web.prettier.path`, `web.stylelint.path`, `web.biome.path`, `php.tools.rector.path`, `php.tools.phpCsFixer.path`,
`php.tools.phpcs.phpcbfPath`, `php.tools.pint.path`); a relative path starts at the project
root. The PHP tools also take their configuration file, ruleset, other parameters and PHP
interpreter (Docker, Docker Compose, SSH, WSL) from
[PHP Quality Tools](docs/guide/user/php-quality-tools.md).

![PHP Quality Tools settings](docs/screenshots/php-quality-tools-settings.png)

The tools run on the saved file where the project lives, so they work in
[remote projects](docs/guide/user/remote-development.md) too. A missing tool is skipped with a balloon (once
per session); a failing tool shows its error in a balloon with a **Configure…** link, and the
file gets back the text it had before that tool ran. Balloons belong to the "Actions on Save"
notification group.

![A skipped tool](docs/screenshots/actions-on-save-run.png)

## When the actions run

- On **explicit save**: `Ctrl+S` (Save All, macOS `Cmd+S`).
- On **autosave** (when Forge loses the focus or after the idle time, see
  [Saving](docs/guide/user/editor.md#saving)) only with **Also run on autosave**
  (`actionsOnSave.runOnAutosave`), and then only Reformat code, Optimize imports, Rearrange
  code and Run code cleanup. External tools only run on explicit save.
- Saves that are part of another action (renaming, changing the encoding or line separator,
  Git operations) never run them.

The actions run in this order: Reformat code, Run code cleanup, Optimize imports, Rearrange
code, then the On Save cleanup of Settings | Editor | General (trailing spaces, final line
break), then the file is written and the external tools run on it (ESLint, Prettier,
Rector, PHP CS Fixer, phpcbf, Pint).

Everything the actions changed reaches the editor as **one edit**: a single `Ctrl+Z` undoes
all of it. If you keep typing while the actions run, your text wins: the actions' result is
dropped and what you typed is saved as it is.

## Settings

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actionsOnSave.reformat.enabled` | `false` | Reformat code |
| `actionsOnSave.reformat.scope` | `whole` | `whole` (Whole file) or `changed` (Changed lines) |
| `actionsOnSave.reformat.fileTypes` | `[]` | file type ids (`php`, `javascript`, …); empty: all file types |
| `actionsOnSave.optimizeImports` | `false` | Optimize imports |
| `actionsOnSave.rearrange` | `false` | Rearrange code |
| `actionsOnSave.codeCleanup` | `false` | Run code cleanup |
| `actionsOnSave.eslint` | `false` | Run eslint --fix |
| `actionsOnSave.prettier.enabled` | `false` | Run Prettier |
| `actionsOnSave.prettier.files` | `*.js; *.ts; …` | Prettier's "Run for files" patterns |
| `actionsOnSave.phpCsFixer` | `false` | Run PHP CS Fixer |
| `actionsOnSave.rector` | `false` | Run Rector |
| `actionsOnSave.phpcbf` | `false` | Run phpcbf |
| `actionsOnSave.pint` | `false` | Run Laravel Pint |
| `actionsOnSave.runOnAutosave` | `false` | Also run on autosave |

See the [settings reference](docs/guide/reference/settings.md#tools--actions-on-save) for all keys.

# Live templates

Live templates work as in PHPStorm: type an abbreviation such as `fore` and press `Tab`, and
Forge inserts the code it stands for. The variables of the template become tab stops: the
first one is selected, `Tab` moves to the next one (`Shift+Tab` back), and `Escape` or moving
the caret away finishes the template. Every occurrence of a variable is edited at once.

![A foreach expanded from fore](docs/screenshots/live-template-expand.png)

The template sets, the contexts a template applies in, the variable expressions and the
expansion are computed in Rust (`crates/forge-livetemplates`), so the desktop app and browser
mode behave the same.

## Expanding a template

- **By abbreviation:** type the abbreviation and press the expand key, `Tab` by default. The
  key keeps its usual meaning when no template applies (the word is not an abbreviation, or
  the template does not fit the place). Change the key in Settings | Editor | Live Templates
  ("By default expand with": `Tab`, `Space` or `Enter`).
- **From completion:** templates that apply at the caret are listed in code completion with
  their description; choosing one expands it.
- **Insert Live Template** (`Ctrl+J`, macOS `Cmd+J`, Code | Insert Live Template): a list of
  every template that applies at the caret. It is filtered by the word before the caret; type
  to narrow it further, `Enter` or `Tab` inserts the selected template and replaces the typed
  prefix.

![Insert Live Template](docs/screenshots/live-template-insert.png)

An abbreviation only expands as a whole word: `$fore`, `$x->fore` or `prefore` do not
expand, and neither do abbreviations inside comments or strings.

## Contexts

Each template says where it applies ("Applicable in"), with PHPStorm's contexts:

| Context | Where |
| --- | --- |
| PHP: Statement | where a statement can start (inside functions or at the top level of a PHP file) |
| PHP: Class Member | directly in a class, interface, trait or enum body |
| PHP: Expression | inside an expression, e.g. after `=` or `(` |
| PHP: Comment / String | inside comments or strings (only templates that ask for them) |
| PHP | all PHP code except comments and strings |
| JavaScript and TypeScript: Statement / Expression | JavaScript and TypeScript files and `<script>` blocks |
| TypeScript | TypeScript files and `<script lang="ts">` |
| HTML, CSS | markup (including the HTML parts of PHP files) and `<style>` blocks |
| Blade, Twig | Blade and Twig templates |
| Lua | Lua files |
| SQL | SQL files and query consoles, outside comments and strings |
| Other | every other file type |

## Variables and expressions

Template text uses `$NAME$` for a variable, `$END$` for the caret position after the last
variable and `$SELECTION$` for the text a template surrounds. `$$` is a literal dollar sign,
so PHP variables in template text are written `$$this`.

In "Edit Variables" each variable has an **expression**, a **default value** and
**Skip if defined**. The expression computes the initial value; when it is empty, the default
value (an expression too, usually a string such as `"value"`) is used. A variable with a value
and "Skip if defined" is filled in without a tab stop.

| Expression | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `className()`, `methodName()`, `functionName()`, `namespace()` | the class, method or function around the caret and the PHP namespace |
| `fileName()`, `fileNameWithoutExtension()` | the current file name |
| `date("yyyy-MM-dd")`, `time("HH:mm")` | the current date and time (Java `SimpleDateFormat` patterns) |
| `user()`, `clipboard()` | the system user name and the text last copied in Forge |
| `variableOfType("array")` | a variable used before the caret, preferring collections (`$orders`) |
| `suggestVariableName(ARRAY)` | a singular name for an element: `$orders` → `order` |
| `camelCase(s)`, `snakeCase(s)`, `capitalize(s)`, `decapitalize(s)`, `capitalizeAndUnderscore(s)`, `lowercaseAndDash(s)`, `spaceSeparated(s)`, `underscoresToCamelCase(s)`, `underscoresToSpaces(s)` | case conversions |
| `concat(a, b, …)`, `substringBefore(s, delimiter)`, `enum("a", "b")`, `complete()` | joining, cutting, the first of several values, an empty field |

## Built-in templates

| Group | Applies | Templates |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PHP | always | `fore`, `forek`, `fori`, `__c` (closure), `__fn` (arrow function), `eco`, `thr`, `inc`, `inco`, `rqr`, `rqro`, `pubf`, `prof`, `prif`, `pubsf`, `prosf`, `prisf`, `con`, `ctor`, `dc` |
| JavaScript | always (also TypeScript) | `fori`, `itar`, `ritar`, `iter`, `itin`, `log`, `anf`, `arf`, `imp`, `imd` |
| Lua | always | `fori`, `forp`, `forip`, `fun`, `lfun`, `req` |
| SQL | always (also consoles) | `sel`, `selc`, `selw`, `ins`, `upd`, `del`, `join`, `lj`, `rj`, `tab` (create table), `col` |
| Twig | always | `for`, `if`, `block`, `extends`, `include` |
| Laravel | Laravel projects | `rget`, `rpost`, `rres`, `rgroup`, `dd`, `validate`, `hasmany`, `belongsto`, `scope` |
| Blade | Laravel projects | `bif`, `bforeach`, `bforelse`, `bsection`, `bextends`, `binclude` |
| Symfony | Symfony projects | `action`, `route`, `render`, `redirect`, `json`, `flash`, `path`, `trans` |

The Laravel, Blade and Symfony groups apply only in projects that use the framework (and
while its plugin is enabled in Settings | Plugins).

## Surround With

**Code | Surround With** (`Ctrl+Alt+T`, macOS `Cmd+Alt+T`) wraps the selected lines, or the
caret line, in a statement. In PHP and JavaScript: `if`, `if / else`, `while`,
`do / while`, `for`, `foreach` (PHP), `try / catch`, `try / finally`,
`try / catch / finally`, `function`, `{ }`, `region...endregion Comments`, `(expr)` and
`!(expr)`; Lua, HTML, Blade and Twig have their own lists (`if … then … end`, `<tag></tag>`,
`@if`, `{% if %}`, …). Press the number or letter in front of an entry to pick it. The
selection is re-indented inside the new block and the caret lands in the condition.
`region...endregion Comments` (also in HTML and CSS) makes a
[custom folding region](docs/guide/user/code-structure.md#custom-folding-regions); type its name at the caret.

Below them, under "Live templates", the popup lists the templates that use `$SELECTION$`.
**Code | Surround with Live Template** (`Ctrl+Alt+J`, macOS `Cmd+Alt+J`) lists only those.

![Surround With](docs/screenshots/surround-with.png)

## Unwrap/Remove

**Code | Unwrap/Remove** (`Ctrl+Shift+Delete`, macOS `Cmd+Shift+Delete`) lists the
statements around the caret, innermost first. While an entry is selected, the editor shows
what goes away (struck through) and what stays (highlighted).

- **Unwrap 'if...'**, **'foreach...'**, **'for...'**, **'while...'**, **'do...'**,
  **'try...'**, **braces**: replaces the statement with the body the caret is in,
  re-indented.
- **Unwrap 'else...'** / **'elseif...'**: keeps that branch instead of the whole `if`.
- **Remove 'else...'**, **'elseif...'**, **'catch...'**, **'finally...'**: deletes only that
  branch.

It works in PHP, JavaScript and TypeScript (brace statements) and Lua (`if … then … end`,
`for`/`while … do … end`, `repeat … until`, `do … end`).

![Unwrap/Remove](docs/screenshots/unwrap-remove.png)

## Save as Live Template

Select code and choose **Tools | Save as Live Template** (also in the Code menu). Settings |
Editor | Live Templates opens with a new template in the `user` group: the selection is the
template text (dollar signs written as `$$`) and the contexts are those of the selection.
Enter an abbreviation and a description, turn parts of the text into `$VARIABLES$` and press
OK.

![Save as Live Template](docs/screenshots/save-as-live-template.png)

## Settings | Editor | Live Templates

![Live Templates settings](docs/screenshots/settings-live-templates.png)

- **By default expand with:** the expand key (`editor.liveTemplates.expandKey`).
- **Template groups:** check boxes enable or disable a template or a whole group; a disabled
  template neither expands nor shows in completion. Framework groups are marked with the
  projects they apply to. Use the search field to filter by abbreviation or description.
- **Toolbar:** `+` adds a template to the selected group (`user` when none is selected), `−`
  removes the selected template, and the restore button brings a changed built-in template
  (or all built-ins of the selected group, including removed ones) back to its shipped state.
  Changed built-in templates are shown in blue.
- **Editor:** abbreviation, description, template text, "Edit Variables" (name, expression,
  default value, skip if defined) and "Applicable in" with **Change** to pick the contexts.

User templates and changes to built-in ones are stored in the user settings
(`editor.liveTemplates.custom`), disabled templates in `editor.liveTemplates.disabled`;
Apply, Cancel and Reset work as on every other settings page.
