Source: docs/guide/user/emmet-and-colors.md

# Emmet and color previews

Emmet works as in PHPStorm: type an abbreviation such as `ul.nav>li*3>a` and press `Tab`, and
Forge writes the markup it stands for. Colors in stylesheets, markup and scripts get a swatch
in the gutter; click it to change the color with the color picker.

![An Emmet abbreviation expanded in a Blade view](docs/screenshots/emmet-expand.png)

Parsing and expanding abbreviations is done in Rust (`crates/forge-emmet`), and so is finding,
parsing and writing colors (`crates/forge-colors`); the desktop app and browser mode behave the
same.

## Where Emmet works

| Files | What expands |
| --- | --- |
| HTML, Blade, Twig, Smarty, Latte, Jinja, Handlebars, Vue templates | markup abbreviations in text (not inside a tag, a comment, `{{ }}` / `{% %}` / `@php` code or `<script>`) |
| PHP | markup abbreviations in the HTML outside `<?php … ?>` |
| JSX and TSX (also `.js` files with JSX) | markup abbreviations where an element can start: after `(`, `>`, `return`, `=>`, `&&`, `\|\|`, `?` or `:`; `.class` becomes `className` |
| CSS, SCSS, Less, Sass, Stylus and `<style>` blocks | property abbreviations where a declaration starts |

The expand key is `Tab` by default (Settings | Editor | Emmet: `Tab`, `Enter` or `Space`). When
no abbreviation ends at the caret the key does what it always does. Live templates and postfix
templates come first: `fore` + `Tab` in a Blade view still expands the live template.

After an expansion, empty attribute values and empty elements are tab stops: `Tab` and
`Shift+Tab` move between them, `Escape` leaves them.

## Markup abbreviations

| Syntax | Example | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Child `>` | `nav>ul>li` | `<nav><ul><li></li></ul></nav>` (formatted on lines) |
| Sibling `+` | `header+main+footer` | three siblings |
| Climb up `^` | `div>p^span` | `span` next to `div`, not inside it (`^^` climbs two levels) |
| Multiplication `*N` | `li*3` | three `li` elements |
| Grouping `( )` | `(dt+dd)*2` | the group twice |
| Id and class `#` `.` | `section#main.page.dark` | `<section id="main" class="page dark">` |
| Attributes `[ ]` | `a[href=/home title="Go home" data-x]` | values in quotes may contain spaces; an attribute without value becomes a tab stop; `[disabled.]` writes a boolean attribute |
| Text `{ }` | `button{Save}` | `<button>Save</button>`; `{Click }+a` puts text next to an element |
| Numbering `$` | `li.item$*3`, `h$*2` | `item1`, `item2`, `item3`; `$$` pads to `01`; `$@-` counts down; `$@3` starts at 3 |
| Implicit tags | `ul>.item`, `table>.row>.cell`, `em>.x` | `li`, `tr`/`td`, `span`; `div` elsewhere |
| Lorem ipsum | `lorem`, `lorem10`, `p*3>lorem5` | placeholder text (30 words by default) |

Snippets give elements their usual attributes and shortcuts: `a` → `<a href="">`, `img` →
`<img src="" alt="">`, `input:checkbox` (or `input:c`), `link:css`, `meta:vp`, `script:src`,
`btn:s`, `form:post`, `bq`, `ul+` (a list with an item), `table+` and `!` for an HTML5 document.
In JSX, `img` and other void elements close with ` />` and `label[for=x]` becomes `htmlFor`.

### Abbreviation preview

With Settings | Editor | Emmet | HTML | **Enable abbreviation preview**, a popup below the
abbreviation shows the markup while you type. It only appears for abbreviations that are clearly
Emmet (an operator, attributes, text, a known element or snippet).

![The abbreviation preview](docs/screenshots/emmet-preview.png)

## CSS abbreviations

| Abbreviation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `m10`, `p10-20`, `m10-20-30-40` | `margin: 10px;`, `padding: 10px 20px;`, four values |
| `m-10`, `m10--20` | negative values: `margin: -10px;`, `margin: 10px -20px;` |
| `w100p`, `m2e`, `p1r`, `h50vh`, `m1.5`, `lh1.5`, `z10` | `%`, `em`, `rem`, any unit; decimals are `em`; unitless properties stay unitless |
| `df`, `dib`, `dn`, `pos:a`, `posr`, `tac`, `fwb`, `ovh`, `jcsb` | `display: flex;` … `justify-content: space-between;` (keyword by first letters or initials) |
| `c#f`, `bgc#fff`, `bd1-s#f00` | `color: #fff;`, `background-color: #fff;`, `border: 1px solid #f00;` |
| `c#3!` | `color: #333 !important;` |
| `m10+p5` | several declarations at once |
| `pos`, `d`, `bd` | the property with its default value selected as a tab stop |
| `@m`, `@kf`, `@f`, `@i` | `@media`, `@keyframes`, `@font-face`, `@import` |

Full property names expand too (`color` → `color: #000;`), and unknown abbreviations are matched
fuzzily against property names (`bxsz` → `box-sizing`). In Sass and Stylus no `;` is written.

![CSS abbreviations](docs/screenshots/emmet-css.png)

## Surround with Emmet

Select some text (or put the caret on a line) and run **Surround with Emmet** (Find Action, or
`Ctrl+Alt+J` Surround with Live Template and choose **Emmet**, the first entry in markup
files). Enter an abbreviation; the popup previews the result and `Enter` applies it. `Up` and
`Down` bring back abbreviations used before.

- The selection goes into the innermost last element: `div.card>.body` wraps it in both.
- An element repeated with a bare `*` repeats once per selected line: `ul>li*` turns lines into
  list items.
- `$#` places the text explicitly: `a[title=$#]{$#}`.
- Wrapping a URL or an e-mail address with `a` fills its `href` (Settings | Editor | Emmet |
  HTML | Enable automatic URL recognition while wrapping text with `<a>` tag).

![Surround with Emmet](docs/screenshots/emmet-surround.png)

## Update Tag, Remove Tag and edit points

- **Update Tag with Emmet** (Find Action, action id `EmmetUpdateTag`): enter an abbreviation for
  the tag around the caret. A name renames the opening and closing tag, `#id` sets the id,
  `.class` adds classes and `[a=b]` sets attributes: `section.hero[role=banner]`.
- **Remove Tag** (Find Action, action id `EmmetRemoveTag`): removes the tag around the caret and
  keeps its content. Tags on lines of their own remove the line, and the content moves one
  indentation level out.
- **Next Emmet Edit Point** (`Alt+Shift+]`, macOS `Ctrl+Alt+]`) and **Previous Emmet Edit
  Point** (`Alt+Shift+[`, macOS `Ctrl+Alt+[`): move the caret to the next empty attribute value
  (`href="|"`), empty element (`<p>|</p>`) or empty line.

## Settings | Editor | Emmet

| Page | Setting | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Emmet | Expand abbreviation with: `Tab`, `Enter`, `Space` | `Tab` |
| Emmet \| HTML | Enable Emmet | on |
| Emmet \| HTML | Enable abbreviation preview | off |
| Emmet \| HTML | Enable automatic URL recognition while wrapping text with `<a>` tag | on |
| Emmet \| CSS | Enable Emmet | on |
| Emmet \| JSX | Enable Emmet in JSX | on |
| Emmet \| JSX | Class attribute: `className` or `class` | `className` |

![Settings | Editor | Emmet | HTML](docs/screenshots/emmet-settings.png)

## Color previews

Forge shows a swatch in the gutter next to each color (up to two per line):

- in CSS, SCSS, Less, Sass, Stylus, `<style>` blocks and `style="…"` attributes: hex colors
  (`#fff`, `#ffffff80`), `rgb()`/`rgba()`, `hsl()`/`hsla()` and `hwb()` in the legacy comma and
  the modern space syntax (`rgb(0 0 255 / 50%)`, `hsl(240deg 100% 50%)`) and the CSS color names
  (`tomato`, `transparent`), in declarations and custom properties (`--brand: #6d28d9`);
- in JavaScript, TypeScript, JSX, TSX and Vue scripts: colors in strings (`'#1e90ff'`,
  `"rgba(0,0,0,.5)"`, `'tomato'`, CSS in template literals);
- Tailwind CSS color classes in `class` / `className` attributes and strings: `bg-blue-500`,
  `text-white/50`, `hover:border-red-600` (read-only swatches).

Selectors (`#main {`), `var(--x)` and colors in comments are left alone. Settings | Editor |
General | Appearance has **Show color preview in the gutter** (on) and **Show color preview
inline** (off), which draws the swatch in front of the color in the text.

![Color swatches in the gutter](docs/screenshots/color-preview.png)

## Color picker

Click a swatch (or run **Show Color Picker** from Find Action with the caret in a color) to
open the color picker:

- the saturation/brightness square, the hue slider and the opacity slider;
- `RGB` or `HSB` fields and the opacity in percent, the hex field;
- **Recently used** colors (kept in the setting `editor.colorPicker.recentColors`).

Every change is written into the document at once in the notation the color was written in:
`#abc` stays short while the color allows it, `rgba(…)` keeps its separators, `hsl()` stays
`hsl()`, a color name becomes another name or hex, and an alpha below 100% adds the alpha
(`#0000ff80`, `rgba(…)`). `Enter` or a click outside closes the picker; `Escape` restores the
original color. With the caret outside a color, Show Color Picker inserts a new hex color.

![The color picker](docs/screenshots/color-picker.png)

![The color picker in the Anvil (light) theme with inline swatches](docs/screenshots/color-picker-light.png)

Source: docs/guide/user/json-schema.md

# JSON Schema

Forge checks JSON and YAML files against a [JSON Schema](https://json-schema.org), like
PHPStorm: properties a file must have, the types and values it allows, and the documentation
of every key. Configuration files such as `composer.json`, `package.json`, Compose files and CI
pipelines work out of the box; for your own formats you map a schema to the files.

![Problems in composer.json](docs/screenshots/json-schema-problems.png)

Everything is computed in Rust (`crates/forge-jsonschema`); the desktop app and browser mode
behave the same, and remote projects read their schema files through the remote host. No
language server is needed.

## Which files

- **JSON**, JSON with comments (`.jsonc`, `tsconfig.json`, `.eslintrc`) and JSON5 (unquoted
  keys, single quotes, trailing commas).
- **YAML**, including several documents in one file (`---`), anchors, aliases and `<<` merge keys.
  Values with a custom tag (GitLab's `!reference [...]`, Compose's `!reset`) are not judged.

## Problems

The **Compliance with JSON schema** inspection reports problems as warnings (yellow); syntax
errors stay red. They appear as you type, in the gutter, the scrollbar and the
[Problems](docs/guide/user/editor.md#problems) tool window (`Alt+6`). The messages are PHPStorm's:

| Message | When |
| --- | --- |
| Missing required property 'name' / Missing required properties 'a', 'b' | `required`; shown on the object's key (or its `{`) |
| Incompatible types. Required: string. Actual: integer. | `type` (several types: "Required one of: …") |
| Property 'x' is not allowed | `additionalProperties: false`, `unevaluatedProperties: false`, `propertyNames`, a `false` property schema |
| Value should be one of: "dev", "alpha", "beta" | `enum` and `const` |
| String violates the pattern: '…' | `pattern` (or the schema's `patternErrorMessage`) |
| String is shorter than 2 / longer than 10 | `minLength`, `maxLength` |
| Less than a minimum 1 / Greater than an exclusive maximum 10 / Is not multiple of 5 | `minimum`, `maximum`, `exclusiveMinimum`, `exclusiveMaximum`, `multipleOf` |
| Array is shorter than 1 / longer than 3, Item is not unique, Additional items are not allowed | `minItems`, `maxItems`, `uniqueItems`, `items` / `prefixItems` / `additionalItems` |
| Array does not contain an item that matches the 'contains' schema | `contains`, `minContains`, `maxContains` |
| Number of properties is less than 1 / greater than 5 | `minProperties`, `maxProperties` |
| Dependency is violated: property 'b' must be specified, since 'a' is specified | `dependencies`, `dependentRequired` |
| Validates to more than one variant / Validates against 'not' schema | `oneOf`, `not` |
| String violates the format 'email' | `format`: `date-time`, `date`, `time`, `email`, `ipv4`, `ipv6`, `uuid`, `uri` |
| Property 'x' is deprecated: … | `deprecated: true` or `deprecationMessage` — a weak warning, struck through in completion |

When none of the `anyOf`/`oneOf` alternatives matches, Forge reports the problems of the
closest one, or one merged message when they differ only in type or value.

The schema engine understands JSON Schema draft 4, 6, 7, 2019-09 and 2020-12: `$ref` (to the
same file, other files and URLs), `$defs` / `definitions`, `$id`, `$anchor`, `allOf`, `anyOf`,
`oneOf`, `not`, `if` / `then` / `else`, `dependentSchemas`, `patternProperties` and the
keywords above. `$dynamicRef` and `$recursiveRef` are followed like `$ref`.

## Completion

`Ctrl+Space` (or just typing) offers what the schema allows at the caret:

- **Property names**, required ones first and in bold, with their type and documentation.
  Choosing one writes the key, the colon and a value template: `"name": "|"` for strings,
  `{}` / `[]` for objects and arrays, the schema's `default`, and a comma when another property
  follows. In YAML it writes `key: `, or `key:` with the next line indented for objects and
  `- ` for lists. Properties already in the object are not offered again.
- **Values**: `enum` values (with `enumDescriptions` / `markdownEnumDescriptions`), `const`,
  `true` / `false`, `null`, the `default`, `examples`, and `{}` / `[]` in JSON. After choosing a
  property whose value has choices, the popup opens again for the value.

![Completion in composer.json](docs/screenshots/json-schema-completion.png)

![Completion in a GitHub Actions workflow](docs/screenshots/json-schema-yaml.png)

`anyOf` / `oneOf` alternatives and `if` / `then` / `else` are narrowed to the ones that fit
what the file already contains (for example a `type` discriminator). Docker Compose and Symfony
service files keep their own key completion and hover docs; their schema still validates them.

## Documentation and navigation

- **Hover** over a key shows its `title` and `markdownDescription` (or `description`); hovering
  an enum value shows the description of that value.
- **Go to Declaration** (`Ctrl+B`, `Ctrl+Click`) on a key opens the schema where the property
  is declared. Bundled and downloaded schemas open read-only, with a banner saying where they
  come from; a schema in the project opens as a normal file.

![The documentation of a package.json key](docs/screenshots/json-schema-hover.png)

## Which schema a file uses

Forge picks the first match:

1. **Your mappings** (see below) — they win over everything else.
2. **The file's own schema**: `"$schema": "…"` at the top level of a JSON file, a `$schema:` key
   or the `# yaml-language-server: $schema=…` modeline in YAML. A relative path is resolved
   against the file's folder; a URL needs [remote schemas](#remote-schemas).
3. **Built-in mappings**, with schemas bundled with Forge:

   | Schema | Files |
   | --- | --- |
   | composer.json | `composer.json` |
   | package.json | `package.json` |
   | tsconfig.json | `tsconfig.json`, `tsconfig.*.json`, `tsconfig-*.json` |
   | jsconfig.json | `jsconfig.json`, `jsconfig.*.json` |
   | .eslintrc | `.eslintrc`, `.eslintrc.json`, `.eslintrc.yml`, `.eslintrc.yaml` |
   | .prettierrc | `.prettierrc`, `.prettierrc.json`, `.prettierrc.json5`, `.prettierrc.yml`, `.prettierrc.yaml` |
   | Docker Compose | `docker-compose.yml`, `docker-compose.*.yml`, `compose.yml`, `compose.*.yml` (and `.yaml`) |
   | GitHub Workflow | `.github/workflows/*.yml`, `*.yaml` |
   | GitHub Action | `action.yml`, `action.yaml` |
   | GitLab CI | `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `*.gitlab-ci.yml` (and `.yaml`) |
   | Minecraft plugin descriptors | `plugin.yml`, `paper-plugin.yml`, `velocity-plugin.json`, `bungee.yml` in `src/main/resources` (schemas written for Forge, see [Minecraft plugins](docs/guide/user/minecraft.md)) |
   | Minecraft mods | `fabric.mod.json` and mixin configurations (`*.mixins.json`) (schemas written for Forge, see [Minecraft mods](docs/guide/user/minecraft.md#new-project-minecraft-mod)) |
| Unity assembly definitions | `*.asmdef` and `*.asmref` (schemas written for Forge, see [Unity and Godot](docs/guide/user/unity-godot.md#unity-file-types)) |

4. **The SchemaStore catalog** (schemastore.org), when remote schemas and the catalog are on:
   hundreds of other well-known files such as `renovate.json`, `.babelrc` or Helm charts.

### Status bar

The status bar shows the schema of the active JSON or YAML file — `JSON schema: composer.json`,
or `No JSON schema`. A warning sign means the schema could not be loaded (the tooltip says why,
for example that downloads are off). Click it to pick another schema for the file: a built-in
one, one of your mappings or **No JSON schema**. The choice is saved as a mapping of the project;
**Edit Schema Mappings…** opens the settings.

![Choosing a schema in the status bar](docs/screenshots/json-schema-status.png)

## JSON Schema Mappings

**Settings | Languages & Frameworks | Schemas and DTDs | JSON Schema Mappings** (`Ctrl+Alt+S`)
lists your mappings on the left. For each one:

- **Name** — shown in the status bar.
- **Schema file or URL** — a path relative to the project root (`schemas/app.schema.json`), an
  absolute path on this machine, or a URL. Leave it empty to turn schemas off for the files.
- **Schema version** — Automatic (from the schema's `$schema`) or JSON Schema version 4, 6, 7,
  2019-09 or 2020-12. The version decides where the drafts disagree (`items` as a list,
  boolean `exclusiveMinimum`).
- **Files** — `+` adds a file (`config/app.json`), a directory (`config/`, every file below
  it) or a file path pattern (`*.app.json`, `config/**/*.yml`, `*.{yml,yaml}`). A pattern without
  `/` matches the file name in any folder.

Mappings are project settings (`jsonSchema.mappings` in `.forge/settings.toml`). The built-in
mappings are listed below them.

![JSON Schema Mappings](docs/screenshots/json-schema-settings.png)

## Remote schemas

**Settings | Languages & Frameworks | Schemas and DTDs | Remote JSON Schemas**:

- **Allow downloading JSON schemas from remote sources** (`jsonSchema.remote.enabled`, off by
  default). Schemas named by a URL — in `$schema`, a mapping or a `$ref` to another server — are
  downloaded only when this is on. Built-in schemas never need a download.
- **Use schemastore.org JSON Schema catalog** (`jsonSchema.remote.schemaStore`, on): look up
  files without another schema in the catalog.

Downloads are cached in `<cache dir>/forge/json-schemas/` (see
[file locations](docs/guide/reference/file-locations.md)), never in the project, and refreshed once a
day; offline, the cached copy is used. A schema that cannot be downloaded is retried after five
minutes; until then its `$ref`s accept anything.

## Language servers

The JSON and YAML language servers validate with schemas too. While one of them runs for a
file, Forge leaves problems, completion and hover of that file to the server, so nothing is
reported twice; the status bar still shows the schema Forge would use.

Source: docs/guide/user/spelling-and-grammar.md

# Spelling and grammar

Forge checks spelling and a few grammar rules as you type, like PHPStorm's **Typo** and
**Grammar** inspections. Misspelled words get a green wavy underline, grammar problems a blue
one. `Alt+Enter` on a marked word offers the fixes.

![Typos and grammar problems in a PHP file](docs/screenshots/spelling-editor.png)

Everything is computed in Rust (`crates/forge-spell`): the dictionaries, splitting text into
words, suggestions and the grammar rules. The desktop app and browser mode behave the same.

## What is checked

| Where | What |
| --- | --- |
| Comments and doc comments | every word; doc tags (`@param`), `$variables`, `inline code`, URLs, e-mail addresses, paths and code references such as `Order::find()` are skipped |
| String literals | every word; escape sequences (`\n`), format placeholders (`%s`) and regular expressions are skipped |
| Code | the names of declared variables, parameters, functions, methods, classes and properties (and PHP `$variables`), split into words: `getHTTPResponse` → get, HTTP, Response; `max_retry_count` → max, retry, count. Names you only use (library functions, framework classes) are not checked. |
| Markdown and plain text files | the prose, without code blocks, inline code, URLs and link targets |
| Commit messages | the message in the Commit tool window |
| File names | optional (off by default): typos in the name of the open file are listed in the Problems tool window |

Words shorter than three letters, words with digits (`utf8`, `base64`), hex numbers and colors,
UUIDs and acronyms in text (`HTML`, `PDFs`) are never reported. A built-in list of programming
terms (`args`, `config`, `json`, `middleware`, `Laravel`, `Symfony`, `Eloquent`, …) is accepted
everywhere. Upper and lower case do not matter.

The problems appear like any other inspection: the squiggles, the inspection widget in the
top-right corner of the editor (typos and grammar problems have their own counters), the
editor tooltip, `F2` / `Shift+F2` and the **Problems** tool window (`Alt+6`).

![Problems tool window with typos and grammar problems](docs/screenshots/spelling-problems.png)

Large files are checked as they scroll into view; after an edit only the changed lines (and
the comment or string around them) are checked again, a moment after you stop typing.

## Fixing a typo (Alt+Enter)

Put the caret on a marked word and press **Show Context Actions** `Alt+Enter`
(macOS `Option+Enter`):

| Entry | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Typo: Change to...** | opens the list of suggestions; choose one to replace the word |
| **Typo: Rename to...** | for a word in a declared name: the suggested names, then the **Rename** refactoring renames every usage (as with `Shift+F6`) |
| **Save 'word' to project-level dictionary** | accepts the word in this project (shown when a project is open) |
| **Save 'word' to application-level dictionary** | accepts the word in all projects |

![Alt+Enter on a typo](docs/screenshots/spelling-intentions.png)

Suggestions are dictionary words close to what you typed, the most likely first: swapped
letters (`recieve` → `receive`), a missing or extra double letter (`adress` → `address`),
dropped vowels (`ordr` → `order`), neighbouring keys on the keyboard and similar-sounding
spellings rank before other edits. Suggestions keep the case of the word (`Recieve` →
`Receive`).

![Typo: Change to... suggestions](docs/screenshots/spelling-change-to.png)

![Typo: Rename to... suggestions for a property name](docs/screenshots/spelling-rename-to.png)

## Grammar and style

The grammar checker is a small set of Forge's own rules for English. It checks comments, doc
comments, Markdown and plain text files and commit messages (not string literals):

| Rule | Example | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Repeated words | "the the order" | Remove the repeated 'the' |
| Use of 'a' and 'an' | "a order", "an user"; acronyms are read letter by letter: "an HTML page", "a URL" | Replace with 'an' / 'a' |
| Sentences start with an uppercase letter | "/** returns the order. */" (doc comments only; tags and code such as `getName()` are skipped) | Replace with 'Returns' |
| Repeated whitespace | "the  order" (aligned columns and doc tag lines are skipped) | Replace with a single space |

`Alt+Enter` on a blue underline shows the fix.

![Alt+Enter on a grammar problem](docs/screenshots/spelling-grammar.png)

## Commit messages

The commit message in the Commit tool window (`Alt+0`) is checked too: typos and grammar
problems are underlined in the message and listed below it with the commit message
inspections. Click an entry for its fixes (the suggestions, Save to dictionary or the grammar
fix).

![Typos in a commit message](docs/screenshots/spelling-commit-message.png)

## Dictionaries

| Dictionary | Where it is stored |
| --- | --- |
| English (USA) | bundled: the SCOWL-based en_US Hunspell dictionary (about 160,000 word forms), see [licences](#licences) |
| Programming terms | bundled with Forge |
| Project-level dictionary | the setting `spelling.projectWords` in the project settings (`<project>/.forge/settings.toml`), so it can be committed and shared with the team |
| Application-level dictionary | the setting `spelling.applicationWords` in the user settings (`<config dir>/forge/settings.toml`) |
| Custom dictionaries | Hunspell `.dic` files or plain word lists you add by path |

Both word lists can be edited in **Settings | Editor | Natural Languages | Spelling**
(`+` / `−` on the list). To check another language or a technical vocabulary, add a Hunspell
dictionary under **Custom dictionaries**: the path of its `.dic` file (absolute, or relative to
the project root); the `.aff` file with the same name next to it is read too, so prefixes and
suffixes are expanded. A file without an `.aff` file is read as a word list with one word per
line. Dictionaries of LibreOffice, Firefox and most Linux distributions (`/usr/share/hunspell`)
work. Words of every dictionary are accepted; Forge does not mark a word as wrong because one
dictionary lacks it.

**Settings | Editor | Natural Languages** lists the dictionaries in use with their word counts,
and a load error for a custom dictionary that cannot be read.

![Settings | Editor | Natural Languages](docs/screenshots/spelling-natural-languages.png)

## Settings

**Settings | Editor | Natural Languages | Spelling**:

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Check spelling (Typo inspection) | on | the whole spelling inspection |
| Severity | Typo | how typos are shown: Typo (green), Grammar Error, Weak Warning, Warning or Error |
| Process comments / literals / code | on | the contexts above |
| Process Markdown and plain text files | on | |
| Process commit messages | on | |
| Process file names | off | typos in the open file's name in the Problems tool window |
| Project-level dictionary | empty | accepted words of this project |
| Application-level dictionary | empty | accepted words of all projects |
| Custom dictionaries | empty | paths of Hunspell `.dic` files or word lists |

![Settings | Editor | Natural Languages | Spelling](docs/screenshots/spelling-settings.png)

**Settings | Editor | Natural Languages | Grammar and Style**: **Check grammar and style
(Grammar inspection)**, its **Severity** (Grammar Error by default, blue) and one switch per
rule.

The inspections belong to the **Natural Languages** plugin (Settings | Plugins); disabling it
turns both off. All keys are listed in the [settings reference](docs/guide/reference/settings.md#editor--natural-languages--spelling).

## Licences

The bundled English dictionary is the en_US Hunspell dictionary of SCOWL (Spell Checker
Oriented Word Lists) by Kevin Atkinson, release 2020.12.07. Its licence is permissive
(MIT/BSD-like, with public domain parts); the full text is in
`crates/forge-spell/data/en_US.LICENSE`. The programming terms list and the grammar rules are
Forge's own. Forge does not use LanguageTool or any other grammar service, and nothing leaves
your machine.

# Language injections

Like PHPStorm's IntelliLang, Forge treats the text of some string literals as code in another
language: SQL in a `PDO::query()` call, a regular expression in `preg_match()`, JSON in
`json_decode()`, HTML in a string that starts with a tag. The injected text gets that
language's highlighting on a light green background, and the language's actions: edit it in
its own editor, run SQL in a query console.

![SQL, RegExp and JSON injected into PHP strings](docs/screenshots/injections-highlighting.png)

Injections work in PHP files (not Blade templates) and in JavaScript and TypeScript files
(`.js`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`, `.jsx`, `.ts`, `.mts`, `.cts`, `.tsx`). Where a language is injected
is decided in Rust (`crates/forge-injections`), so the desktop app and browser mode behave the
same; the highlighting itself follows every keystroke.

## Where languages are injected

In this order, the first that applies wins:

1. **A `language=` comment** before the string: `// language=SQL`, `/* language=JSON */`,
   `# language=HTML`, or `@lang` in a doc comment (`/** @lang SQL */`). The comment applies to
   the first string after it in the same statement, also when other code stands between them:

   ```php
   // language=JSON
   $defaults = '{"type": "bar", "stacked": true}';

   $html = render(/* language=HTML */ '<b>' . e($name) . '</b>');
   ```

   Language names are not case-sensitive. Besides the names in the list below, `MySQL`,
   `PostgreSQL`, `SQLite`, `JS`, `Regex` and a few more are understood. A comment always
   injects, also when the matching rule is turned off.
2. **A heredoc or nowdoc label** that names a language: `<<<SQL`, `<<<'JSON'`, `<<<HTML`,
   `<<<CSS`, `<<<JS`, `<<<XML`, `<<<REGEXP`. `<<<DQL` is left to the
   [Doctrine plugin](docs/guide/user/doctrine.md).
3. **A built-in rule** (Settings | Editor | Language Injections):

   | Host | Language | Places |
   | --- | --- | --- |
   | PHP | (from the attribute) | arguments of parameters marked `#[Language('SQL')]` (JetBrains PhpStorm attributes, found by the PHP index in the project, vendor and include paths) |
   | PHP | SQL | strings starting with a statement: `SELECT … FROM`, `INSERT INTO`, `UPDATE … SET`, `DELETE FROM`, `WITH … AS (`, `CREATE`/`ALTER`/`DROP TABLE`, `TRUNCATE`, `SHOW TABLES`, …; `SELECT` in capitals also without `FROM` |
   | PHP | SQL | `PDO::query()`/`prepare()`/`exec()` on database objects (`$pdo`, `$this->db`, `$connection`, …), `mysqli_query()`, `pg_query()`, `pg_prepare()`, Doctrine DBAL `executeQuery()`, `fetchAllAssociative()`, … and `createNativeQuery()` |
   | PHP | SQL | Laravel: `DB::select()`, `DB::statement()`, `DB::unprepared()`, `DB::raw()`, …; `selectRaw()`, `whereRaw()`, `havingRaw()`, `orderByRaw()`, `groupByRaw()` |
   | PHP | SQL | WordPress: `$wpdb->query()`, `prepare()`, `get_results()`, `get_row()`, `get_var()`, `get_col()` |
   | PHP | HTML | strings starting with a tag (`'<span class="badge">'`) |
   | PHP | JSON | `json_decode()` |
   | PHP | RegExp | `preg_match()`, `preg_match_all()`, `preg_replace()`, `preg_replace_callback()`, `preg_split()`, `preg_grep()`, `preg_filter()`: the pattern between its delimiters (`/…/i`, `#…#`, `{…}`) |
   | PHP | CSS | `wp_add_inline_style()` |
   | JavaScript | SQL | strings and templates starting with a statement; `db.query()`, `pool.query()`, `knex.raw()`, … on database objects; `` sql`…` ``, `` Prisma.sql`…` ``, `` $queryRaw`…` ``, `` $executeRaw`…` `` |
   | JavaScript | HTML | strings starting with a tag, `` html`…` ``, `innerHTML`/`outerHTML` assignments, `insertAdjacentHTML()`, `document.write()` |
   | JavaScript | CSS | `` css`…` ``, `` styled.div`…` ``, `` styled(Button)`…` ``, `` keyframes`…` ``, `` createGlobalStyle`…` ``, `style.cssText`, `insertRule()` |
   | JavaScript | JSON | `JSON.parse()` |
   | JavaScript | RegExp | `new RegExp()`, `RegExp()` (regular expression literals are highlighted by the JavaScript mode) |

Strings joined with `.` (PHP) or `+` (JavaScript) are one injection:
`'SELECT * FROM ' . $table . ' WHERE id = ?'` is highlighted as one SQL statement. Variables
inside strings (`"… $id"`, `"{$order->id}"`, `` `${id}` ``) are left out of the injected text.
`createQuery()` strings are DQL and belong to the [Doctrine plugin](docs/guide/user/doctrine.md).

The languages that can be injected: **SQL**, **HTML**, **CSS**, **JSON**, **RegExp**,
**JavaScript** and **XML**.

## Inject language or reference

Place the caret in a string and press **Show Context Actions** (`Alt+Enter`):

- **Inject language or reference** (any string without an injection) opens the list of
  languages; type to filter, `Enter` to choose. Forge writes a `// language=…` comment on the
  line before the statement, or a `/* language=… */` comment right before the string when
  other code precedes it on its line. Choosing again for a string with a comment changes the
  comment.
- **Edit &lt;language&gt; Fragment** (an injected string) opens the fragment editor, see below.
- **Un-inject Language** (an injected string) removes the `language=` comment. For a string a
  built-in rule injected, it turns the injection off for that string in this project (stored
  in the project's settings, `editor.injections.uninjected`). A string whose text changes is
  injected again; Settings | Editor | Language Injections can restore all of them.

![The intentions in an injected SQL string](docs/screenshots/injections-intentions.png)

![Inject language or reference: the language list](docs/screenshots/injections-inject-language.png)

The actions are also in Find Action (`Ctrl+Shift+A`): **Inject Language or Reference**,
**Un-inject Language** and **Edit Injected Fragment**. They have no default shortcut; assign
one in Settings | Keymap.

## Edit Fragment

**Edit &lt;language&gt; Fragment** opens the value of the string in its own editor below the
file, titled like "SQL Fragment (SalesReport.php)". It shows the string as the program sees
it, without quotes and escapes (`\'` is `'`, `\n` a line break), with the language's
highlighting, brackets and line numbers. What you type there is written back into the string
right away, escaped for its kind of literal (`'` becomes `\'` in single-quoted PHP strings,
`$` becomes `\$` in double-quoted ones and in heredocs, line breaks become `\n` in
JavaScript quotes); changes to the string in the file show up in the fragment. The undo
history of the file records every change. Close the fragment editor with its `×` button; it
closes by itself when the string or its injection disappears. For a PHP pattern the fragment
is the text between the delimiters.

![The SQL fragment editor below the PHP file](docs/screenshots/injections-edit-fragment.png)

## Run injected SQL

With the caret in an injected SQL string (or in its fragment editor), **Execute**
(`Ctrl+Enter`, macOS `Cmd+Enter`) runs the SQL: Forge opens a query console of the data
source selected in the Database tool window, puts the SQL in it and runs it, with the usual
Output and result tabs (see [Database tools](docs/guide/user/database.md)). The SQL is the string's value:
escapes are resolved and the parts of a concatenation are joined. Elsewhere `Ctrl+Enter`
keeps its PHPStorm meaning (Split Line).

When the project has data sources, a green **Run SQL in Console** icon in the gutter marks the
first line of every injected SQL string; clicking it does the same. Without a data source,
Forge asks you to add one.

![Injected SQL run in a query console](docs/screenshots/injections-run-sql.png)

Parameters (`?`, `:status`) are sent as written; the database reports them unless you replace
them in the console first.

## Settings

**Settings | Editor | Language Injections** lists the built-in rules by host language with a
check box each; the panel below the table shows where the selected rule applies. Turned-off
rules are stored in `editor.injections.disabled` (user settings). The line under the panel
counts the strings un-injected in this project; **Restore All** injects them again.

![Settings | Editor | Language Injections](docs/screenshots/injections-settings.png)

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `editor.injections.disabled` | `[]` | ids of the built-in rules that are turned off (`php-html`, `js-sql-keywords`, …) |
| `editor.injections.uninjected` | `[]` | strings turned off with Un-inject Language (`path#key`), per project |

## Not yet supported

- Custom injection rules (PHPStorm's `+` in the settings page) and the `prefix=` / `suffix=`
  parameters of `language=` comments.
- Completion, navigation and inspections inside injected text: the injected language gets
  highlighting, Edit Fragment and Run SQL. DQL has its own completion (see
  [Doctrine and DQL](docs/guide/user/doctrine.md)).
- Values for SQL parameters before running (PHPStorm's "Parameters" dialog).

Source: docs/guide/user/file-templates.md

# File and code templates

Like PHPStorm, Forge creates new files from **file templates** and shapes the code that the
Generate actions write with **code templates**. Both are edited in Settings | Editor | File and
Code Templates and use the Apache Velocity template language (`${NAME}`, `#if … #end`).

## Creating a file from a template

The templates appear in three places, always for the folder you are in:

- **Project view**: right-click a folder (or a file, for its folder) › **New**.
- **File | New** in the main menu: for the folder selected in the Project view, else the
  folder of the active editor, else the project root.
- **New…** (`Alt+Insert`, macOS `Cmd+N`) while the Project view has the focus: the same list
  as a popup next to the selected folder. In an editor `Alt+Insert` stays **Generate…**.

![New submenu of the Project view](docs/screenshots/file-templates-new-menu.png)

The list shows **File** and **Directory**, then the templates the project uses, grouped in
submenus so the common choices are two clicks away:

- **PHP ▸** **Class**, **Interface**, **Trait** and **Enum** (each opens the New PHP Class
  dialog with that kind selected), then **File** and **PHPUnit Test**, then the project's
  framework templates (Laravel or Symfony).
- **Web ▸** HTML, CSS, JavaScript and TypeScript files, Vue and React components.
- **Lua ▸** Lua file and module.
- Your own templates follow directly in the New menu, then **Edit File Templates…**.

The templates:

| Template | Offered when | Creates |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PHP File | the project uses PHP | `<?php` file |
| PHP Class | the project uses PHP | class, interface, trait or enum (New PHP Class dialog) |
| PHPUnit Test | the project uses PHP | a `TestCase` subclass |
| Laravel Controller, Laravel Model | the project uses Laravel | `make:controller` / `make:model` style classes |
| Symfony Controller | the project uses Symfony | an `AbstractController` with a `#[Route]` action |
| WordPress Plugin | the project uses WordPress | a plugin file with the plugin header, the `ABSPATH` guard and an `init` callback (see [WordPress](docs/guide/user/wordpress.md#file-templates)) |
| WordPress Theme Stylesheet | the project uses WordPress | `style.css` with the theme header |
| HTML File, CSS File, JavaScript File, TypeScript File | always | web files |
| Vue Single File Component | the project uses Vue | `<script setup lang="ts">`, `<template>`, `<style scoped>` |
| React Component, React TypeScript Component | the project uses React | `.jsx` / `.tsx` function components |
| Lua File, Lua Module | the project uses Lua | `.lua` files |
| your own templates | always | see [Editing templates](#editing-templates) |

**Edit File Templates…** at the end opens the settings page. For most templates Forge asks for
the name in a small "New HTML File" dialog. The name may include sub folders
(`components/OrderList`), which are created; the extension is added unless you typed it.
The new file opens in the editor.

![New HTML File dialog](docs/screenshots/file-templates-html-dialog-light.png)

## The New PHP Class dialog

**PHP Class** (and every PHP template that uses `${NAMESPACE}`, such as PHPUnit Test or the
Laravel and Symfony templates) opens the New PHP Class dialog:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Name | the class name; it must be a valid PHP identifier |
| Namespace | filled from the PSR-4 rules (`autoload.psr-4` and `autoload-dev.psr-4`) of composer.json for the target folder, e.g. `App\Models` for `app/Models` |
| File name | `<Name>.php` until you change it |
| Directory | the target folder; typing a namespace moves it to that namespace's PSR-4 folder (`App\Models\Billing` → `app/Models/Billing`) |
| Template | Class, Interface, Trait, Enum and the project's PHP class templates |
| Extends | parent class (for interfaces: parent interfaces, comma separated); only for templates that use `${EXTENDS}` |
| Implements | interfaces, comma separated; only for templates that use `${IMPLEMENTS}` |

Fully qualified names in Extends and Implements (`\Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model`) get a
`use` import after the namespace statement and are written by their short name; names from the
class's own namespace need no import. Templates that use variables of their own (the Enum
template's `${BACKED_TYPE}`) show a field for each one ("Backed type").

![New PHP Class dialog](docs/screenshots/file-templates-php-class-dialog.png)

`Alt+Enter` › **Create class 'Receipt'** on an undeclared class opens the same dialog as
**Create New PHP Class**, filled with the name, the namespace of the usage (and its PSR-4
directory) and the template the usage needs; see [PHP: Create from usage](docs/guide/user/php.md#create-from-usage).

The composer.json is the one set in Settings | Languages & Frameworks | PHP | Composer
(`php.composer.json`). Its PSR-4 folders are relative to the folder of that file. The mapping is
computed next to the project files, so it also works in [remote projects](docs/guide/user/remote-development.md).

![The created class](docs/screenshots/file-templates-php-class-created.png)

## Editing templates

Settings | Editor | File and Code Templates has three tabs:

- **Files**: the templates of the New menus.
- **Includes**: text pulled into other templates with `#parse`. The built-in
  **PHP File Header** is empty; put a licence or author comment there and every PHP template
  starts with it.
- **Code**: the code templates of the [Generate](docs/guide/user/php.md#generate) actions.

![File and Code Templates settings](docs/screenshots/file-templates-settings.png)

The toolbar above the list creates (`+`), removes (`−`, your own templates only), copies and
resets templates. **Reset to Default** brings a changed built-in template back. Changed
built-ins are shown in the accent color. Each template has a name, an extension (the new file's
extension) and its text; a syntax error is shown below the text with its line. The changes are
applied with OK or Apply like every other setting and stored in the `fileTemplates.custom`
setting (only your templates and the built-ins you changed).

### The template language

Templates use the part of Apache Velocity that PHPStorm's templates use:

| Syntax | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `${NAME}`, `$NAME` | a variable; an unknown variable stays as written, so `$this->x` is left alone |
| `$!{NAME}` | a variable that is empty when it is not set |
| `${NAME.toLowerCase()}` | also `toUpperCase()`, `trim()` and `replace("a", "b")` |
| `#if (${NAMESPACE}) … #elseif (…) … #else … #end` | conditions with `==`, `!=`, `&&`, `\|\|`, `!`, parentheses and strings; a variable alone is true when it is not empty |
| `#set ($ROUTE = ${NAME.toLowerCase()})` | defines a variable |
| `#parse("PHP File Header.php")` | inserts an include |
| `## comment`, `#* comment *#` | comments |
| `#[[ … ]]#`, `\$`, `\#` | text that is not parsed |

A line that holds only directives (`#if`, `#end`, `#set`, comments) leaves nothing behind in
the new file, not even an empty line. PHP attributes such as `#[Route('/x')]` are ordinary text.

### Variables

| Variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `${NAME}` | name of the new file without extension (the class name for PHP classes) |
| `${FILE_NAME}` | name of the new file with extension |
| `${NAMESPACE}` | namespace from the New PHP Class dialog |
| `${PACKAGE_NAME}` | the namespace, else the folder path with dots |
| `${DIR_PATH}` | folder of the new file, relative to the project root |
| `${PROJECT_NAME}` | name of the project |
| `${USER}` | your login name |
| `${DATE}`, `${TIME}` | current date (`2026-10-22`) and time (`14:05`) |
| `${YEAR}`, `${MONTH}`, `${MONTH_NAME_SHORT}`, `${MONTH_NAME_FULL}`, `${DAY}`, `${DAY_NAME_SHORT}`, `${DAY_NAME_FULL}`, `${HOUR}`, `${MINUTE}`, `${SECOND}` | parts of the current date and time |
| `${EXTENDS}`, `${IMPLEMENTS}` | the Extends and Implements fields of the New PHP Class dialog |

Any other variable a file template uses is asked for in its New dialog.

## Code templates

The PHP [Generate](docs/guide/user/php.md#generate) actions write their code with these templates:

| Template | Used by | Variables |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PHP Implemented Method Body | Implement Methods (`Ctrl+I`) | `${NAME}`, `${CLASS_NAME}`, `${PARAMETERS}` (`$a, ...$rest`), `${RETURN_TYPE}` |
| PHP Overridden Method Body | Override Methods (`Ctrl+O`) | as above; the default calls `parent::${NAME}(${PARAMETERS})` and returns its result unless the method returns `void` or `never` |
| PHP Function Doc Comment | Generate › PHPDoc Comment on a function or method | `${NAME}`, `${CLASS_NAME}`, `${PARAM_DOC}`, `${TYPE_HINT}`, `${THROWS_DOC}` |
| PHP Field Doc Comment | Generate › PHPDoc Comment on a property or constant | `${NAME}`, `${CLASS_NAME}`, `${TYPE_HINT}` |
| PHP Class Doc Comment | Generate › PHPDoc Comment on a class | `${NAME}`, `${NAMESPACE}` |

![Code templates](docs/screenshots/file-templates-settings-code.png)

The bodies are indented inside the method and the doc comments in front of the declaration;
empty lines (for example `${PARAM_DOC}` of a function without parameters) are dropped from doc
comments. A template with a syntax error makes the action report the error instead of writing
code.

> **Note:** templates are user settings; PHPStorm's per-project template scheme is not
> available yet.

Source: docs/guide/user/vim-emulation.md

# Vim emulation

Forge emulates Vim in the editor the way PHPStorm's IdeaVim plugin does. The emulation is part
of the bundled **Vim** plugin (`forge.vim`) and is off until you turn it on with
**Tools | Vim** (`VimPluginToggle`, `Ctrl+Alt+V`, macOS `Cmd+Alt+V`), Find Action ("Vim") or
Settings | Editor | Vim. The choice is remembered in the setting `vim.enabled`.

![Visual Line mode with search highlights](docs/screenshots/vim-emulation.png)

While it is on, every editor tab starts in Normal mode and shows a block caret. The status bar
shows the mode (`NORMAL`, `INSERT`, `VISUAL`, `VISUAL LINE`, `VISUAL BLOCK`, `REPLACE`), the
keys of an unfinished command (`2d`, `"a`), `recording @q` while a macro is recorded, and
messages such as `E486: Pattern not found`. Click it to open Settings | Editor | Vim.

Tool windows, dialogs, the terminal and other text fields keep their normal keys; only the
editor goes through Vim. The engine is written in Rust (`crates/forge-vim`) and runs in-process
as WebAssembly, so every key is answered synchronously, in the desktop app and in browser mode.

> **Note:** `Ctrl+Alt+V` is also PHPStorm's Introduce Variable shortcut. In the editor the
> refactoring's binding wins (as in PHPStorm, where the conflict is shown in Settings |
> Keymap); use Tools | Vim, Find Action or the status bar there, or give `VimPluginToggle`
> another shortcut in Settings | Keymap.

## Modes

| Mode | Enter with | Leave with |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Normal | `Escape`, `Ctrl+[`, `Ctrl+C` | |
| Insert | `i` `a` `I` `A` `o` `O` `gi` `gI`, `c`/`s`/`C`/`S` commands | `Escape`, `Ctrl+[`, `Ctrl+C` |
| Replace | `R`, `Insert` in Insert mode | `Escape` |
| Visual (character, line, block) | `v`, `V`, `Ctrl+V`; selecting with the mouse | `Escape`, the same key again |
| Command line | `:`, `/`, `?` | `Enter` runs it, `Escape` cancels |

In Insert mode the editor types as usual: completion, auto-closing brackets, live templates
and Emmet keep working, and `Escape` also closes the completion popup. Vim handles `Ctrl+W`
(delete word), `Ctrl+U` (delete to line start), `Ctrl+H`, `Ctrl+R {register}`, `Ctrl+O`
(one Normal mode command), `Ctrl+T`/`Ctrl+D` (indent), `Ctrl+E`/`Ctrl+Y` (character below or
above) and `Ctrl+J`, as far as the shortcut handlers give these keys to Vim.

## Motions

Every motion takes a count (`3w`, `5j`, `2f,`).

| Keys | Motion |
| --- | --- |
| `h` `j` `k` `l`, arrow keys, `Space`, `Backspace` | left, down, up, right |
| `w` `b` `e` `ge`, `W` `B` `E` `gE` | words (letters, digits, `_`) and WORDs (non-blank runs) |
| `0` `^` `$` `g_` `\|` | line start, first non-blank, line end, last non-blank, column |
| `gg` `G`, `{count}G`, `{count}%` | first, last or numbered line, percentage of the file |
| `f` `t` `F` `T` + character, `;` `,` | find a character on the line and repeat |
| `%` | matching `(` `)` `[` `]` `{` `}` |
| `{` `}` | paragraphs |
| `H` `M` `L` | top, middle and bottom of the visible lines (with `scrolloff`) |
| `+` `-` `Enter` `_` | next, previous, current line (first non-blank) |
| `/pattern` `?pattern` `n` `N` `*` `#` `g*` `g#` | search |
| `` `a `` `'a`, ``` `` ``` `''` | marks |

## Operators and text objects

An operator is followed by a motion or a text object (`dw`, `c$`, `yi(`, `>ip`), or doubled
for whole lines (`dd`, `cc`, `yy`, `>>`, `<<`, `==`, `g~~`, `guu`, `gUU`).

| Operator | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `d` | delete |
| `c` | change (delete and enter Insert mode) |
| `y` | yank (copy into a register) |
| `>` `<` | shift lines right and left by `shiftwidth` (default: the editor's indent) |
| `=` | re-indent lines (Forge's Auto-Indent Lines, or Reformat Code) |
| `g~` `gu` `gU` `g?` | toggle case, lower case, upper case, ROT13 |

| Text object | Selects |
| --- | --- |
| `iw` `aw`, `iW` `aW` | word, WORD (`a…` with the following blanks) |
| `i"` `a"`, `i'` `a'`, `` i` `` `` a` `` | quoted string on the line |
| `i(` `a(` (`ib`), `i[` `a[`, `i{` `a{` (`iB`), `i<` `a<` | brackets; a count selects outer pairs (`2di(`) |
| `it` `at` | the content of an HTML/XML tag, or the whole element |
| `ip` `ap` | paragraph |

Other commands: `x` `X` `s` `S` `C` `D` `Y`, `p` `P` `gp` `gP`, `J` `gJ`, `r{char}`, `~`,
`Ctrl+A`/`Ctrl+X` (increment and decrement numbers, also hexadecimal), `.` (repeat the last
change, with a new count `3.`), `u` and `Ctrl+R` (undo and redo through the editor's
history), `zz` `zt` `zb` `z.` `z-` `z<CR>`, `Ctrl+D` `Ctrl+U` `Ctrl+F` `Ctrl+B` `Ctrl+E`
`Ctrl+Y` (scrolling), `zo` `zc` `za` `zR` `zM` (folding), `gd` and `Ctrl+]` (Go to
Declaration), `gt`/`gT` (next and previous tab), `Ctrl+O`/`Ctrl+I` (Back and Forward), `K`
(Quick Documentation), `ZZ` and `ZQ`.

`Ctrl+W` followed by `w`/`h`/`j`/`k`/`l`/`p`, `v`, `s`, `c`/`q` or `o` moves between split
editors, splits vertically or horizontally, unsplits, or closes the other splits.

## Visual mode

`v` selects characters, `V` whole lines and `Ctrl+V` a block (one caret per line, `$` extends
every line to its end). Motions and text objects (`viw`, `vi{`) extend the selection; `o`
jumps to the other end and `gv` selects the previous selection again.

![A block selection with $](docs/screenshots/vim-visual-block.png)

Commands on the selection: `d` `x` `c` `s` `y`, `D` `X` `C` `S` `R` `Y` (whole lines), `>` `<`
(with a count), `=`, `~` `u` `U`, `J` `gJ`, `r{char}`, `p` `P` (replace the selection),
`Ctrl+A`/`Ctrl+X`, `:` (an ex command on the selected lines), and in block mode `I` and `A`,
which insert the typed text on every line when you press `Escape`.

## Registers, macros and marks

- `"{register}` before a command chooses the register: `"ayy`, `"ap`. `a`–`z` are named
  registers (`A`–`Z` append), `0` holds the last yank, `1`–`9` the last deleted lines, `-`
  the last small deletion, `_` discards, `.` is the last inserted text, `:` the last command
  line and `/` the last search.
- `"+` and `"*` are the system clipboard. Yanks into them are copied to the clipboard and to
  Paste from History; pasting from them uses the last text copied in Forge or pasted into an
  editor. With `set clipboard=unnamed` (or `unnamedplus`) every yank and delete goes to the
  clipboard.
- `q{register}` records a macro, `q` stops, `@{register}` plays it (`3@a`), `@@` repeats the
  last macro and `@:` the last command line.
- `m{a-z}` sets a mark; `'a` jumps to its line, `` `a `` to its position. `''` returns to
  the position before the last jump. Marks move with the text when lines are added or removed.

## Search and the command line

`/` and `?` search forward and backward with Vim's regular expressions (`\<word\>`, `\(…\)`,
`\|`, `\{n,m}`, `\v`, `\V`, `\c`), `n` and `N` repeat, `*` and `#` search the word under the
caret. `ignorecase` and `smartcase` decide case sensitivity; with `hlsearch` all matches stay
highlighted until `:noh`, with `incsearch` the caret moves to the match while you type. The
command line opens at the bottom of the editor.

![The command line](docs/screenshots/vim-command-line.png)

| Command | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `:w`, `:wa`, `:update` | save (Save All) |
| `:q`, `:q!`, `:close`; `:qa` | close the tab; close all tabs |
| `:wq`, `:x`, `ZZ` | save and close |
| `:e {file}` | open a file (relative to the project) |
| `:{line}`, `:$` | go to a line |
| `:s/pattern/replacement/flags`, `:%s/…/…/g`, `:'<,'>s/…`, `:&&`, `&` | substitute (flags `g`, `i`, `I`, `n`, `e`; `\1`, `&`, `\r`, `\u`, `\U` in the replacement) |
| `:g/pattern/command`, `:v/pattern/command` | run a command on matching (or other) lines, e.g. `:g/^$/d` |
| `:normal {keys}`, `:%normal A;` | run Normal mode keys on each line |
| `:d [x]`, `:y [x]`, `:j`, `:>`, `:<`, `:m {line}`, `:t {line}`, `:sort [i] [n] [u]` | line commands with ranges (`.`, `$`, `%`, `'a`, `+n`, `/pattern/`) |
| `:noh` | hide search highlights |
| `:set {option}` | change an option (see below) |
| `:action {ActionId}` | run any Forge action by its PHPStorm id, e.g. `:action GotoClass` |
| `:registers`, `:marks`, `:map` | list registers, marks and mappings |
| `:bn` `:bp`, `:sp` `:vs`, `:only` | next and previous tab, split, unsplit |
| `:source ~/.ideavimrc` | read the configuration file again |

### Options

`:set` (and `~/.ideavimrc`) understands `number` (`nu`), `relativenumber` (`rnu`),
`ignorecase` (`ic`), `smartcase` (`scs`), `hlsearch` (`hls`), `incsearch` (`is`),
`wrapscan` (`ws`), `scrolloff` (`so`), `shiftwidth` (`sw`), `tabstop` (`ts`), `expandtab`
(`et`), `clipboard` (`cb`), `timeout`, `timeoutlen` (`tm`), `showmode`, `showcmd`, `ideajoin`
(`J` uses the IDE's Join Lines) and `visualbell`. `no…`, `inv…`, `…!`, `…?`, `…=`, `…+=` and
`…-=` work as in Vim. Common IdeaVim extension options (`set surround`, `set commentary`, …)
are accepted and ignored.

## ~/.ideavimrc

When the emulation is turned on, Forge reads `~/.ideavimrc` (or `~/_ideavimrc`, or
`~/.config/ideavim/ideavimrc`; another file can be set in Settings | Editor | Vim |
Configuration file). `source ~/.vimrc` lines are replaced by that file's text. Use **Reload**
on the settings page, the action **Reload .ideavimrc** (`IdeaVim.ReloadVimRc`) or `:source`
after editing it.

```vim
" ~/.ideavimrc
let mapleader = " "
set number relativenumber
set ignorecase smartcase hlsearch incsearch scrolloff=5
set clipboard+=unnamedplus

inoremap jk <Esc>
nnoremap Y y$
vnoremap < <gv
vnoremap > >gv

" IDE actions
nmap <leader>r <Action>(RenameElement)
nmap <leader>f :action ReformatCode<CR>
nmap <leader>e :action SearchEverywhere<CR>
nmap gi <Action>(GotoImplementation)

sethandler <C-V> n-v:vim i:ide
if has('ide')
  nnoremap <leader>b :action ToggleLineBreakpoint<CR>
endif
```

Supported: `set`, `let mapleader`, the mapping commands `map`, `nmap`, `vmap`/`xmap`, `omap`,
`imap`, `cmap`, `noremap`, `nnoremap`, `vnoremap`/`xnoremap`, `onoremap`, `inoremap`,
`cnoremap` with their `unmap` and `mapclear` forms (`<silent>` and the other `<…>` flags are
accepted), `sethandler`, `if has('ide')` / `else` / `endif` blocks and `"` comments. Mappings
use Vim's key notation (`<leader>`, `<CR>`, `<Esc>`, `<C-w>`, `<Space>`, `<lt>`, `<Bar>`,
`<Nop>`). A right-hand side can run IDE actions with `:action ActionId<CR>` or IdeaVim's
`<Action>(ActionId)`; the ids are PHPStorm's (see the [keymap reference](docs/guide/reference/keymap.md)
or Find Action). Mappings wait `timeoutlen` milliseconds (default 1000) for the next key when
a longer mapping could still match (`jk` after `j`).

Lines Forge does not support are skipped and reported in a balloon with their line number
(for example `wincmd` or an unknown option); `syntax`, `filetype`, `colorscheme`, `autocmd`
and `Plug` lines are skipped silently.

## Shortcut conflicts

Many `Ctrl` shortcuts mean something in Vim and in the IDE: `Ctrl+R` is Redo in Vim and
Replace in PHPStorm, `Ctrl+W` window commands or Extend Selection, `Ctrl+V` Visual Block or
Paste. Settings | Editor | Vim | **Shortcut Conflicts** lists each of them with what Vim does,
and lets you choose **Vim** or **IDE** for Normal, Insert and Visual mode separately (the
setting `vim.shortcutHandlers`). By default Vim handles a shortcut in every mode where it has
a meaning, and the IDE keeps it elsewhere (for example `Ctrl+V` in Insert mode pastes).
**All Vim**, **All IDE** and **Defaults** change the whole table. `sethandler` lines in
`~/.ideavimrc` take precedence; such rows are marked `.ideavimrc` and cannot be changed in the
table.

![Settings | Editor | Vim](docs/screenshots/vim-settings.png)

Shortcuts that are not in the table (`Ctrl+S`, `Ctrl+Shift+…`, `Alt+…`, function keys) always
reach the IDE, also in Normal mode.

## Limitations

- Undo granularity follows the editor's history: a Normal mode command is one undo step,
  typing in Insert mode is grouped by the editor.
- Pasting from `"+` uses the clipboard text Forge knows about (copied in Forge or pasted into
  an editor); text copied in another application is pasted with `Ctrl+V` (IDE handler) or
  after pasting it once.
- Not supported yet: `:s` with the `c` flag, IdeaVim extensions (surround, commentary,
  easymotion, …), `:wincmd`, functions and `autocmd` in `~/.ideavimrc`, Select mode, the
  jump and change lists (`Ctrl+O`/`Ctrl+I` use the IDE's Back and Forward).

# Search Everywhere and Find Action

## Search Everywhere

Press `Shift` twice (**Double Shift**), or click the magnifier in the main toolbar.

![Search Everywhere](docs/screenshots/search-everywhere.png)

The popup has tabs; `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` switch between them:

| Tab | Opens directly with | Finds | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| All | `Double Shift` | the best few results of every tab | — |
| Classes | **Go to Class** `Ctrl+N` (macOS `Cmd+O`) | classes, interfaces, traits, enums, Lua classes | PHP index, LuaForge index, language servers (`workspace/symbol`) |
| Files | **Go to File** `Ctrl+Shift+N` (macOS `Cmd+Shift+O`) | project files; without a query, recent files | Forge's file search (respects `.gitignore`) |
| Symbols | **Go to Symbol** `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+N` (macOS `Cmd+Alt+O`) | functions, methods, constants, properties | PHP index, LuaForge index, language servers |
| Actions | **Find Action** `Ctrl+Shift+A` (macOS `Cmd+Shift+A`) | every IDE action and command | the keymap and registered commands |
| Text | — | lines of text in project files | Find in Files (`forge-find`) |

- `Up`/`Down`, `PageUp`/`PageDown` move the selection, `Enter` opens it, `Escape` closes.
- In the All tab, a "more" row under a group switches to that group's tab.
- Pressing a tab's shortcut again while the popup is open toggles the checkbox in the header:
  **Include non-project items** (most tabs) or **Include disabled actions** (Actions).

Results from language servers appear once a server for that language runs, so the Symbols
tab also finds TypeScript, Python, Go or Rust symbols in a polyglot project.

![Symbols from language servers](docs/screenshots/search-everywhere-lsp-symbols.png)

### Fuzzy matching

Matching works like PHPStorm's:

- Characters of the query must appear in order, case-insensitively.
- Matches at word starts, after separators (`/ _ - . : $` and spaces) and on **camel humps**
  score higher, so `OrCo` finds `OrderController` first and `usrctl` finds `UserController`.
- For files you can type part of the path: `models/user` finds `app/Models/User.php`.
- A file called exactly what you typed, with or without its extension, comes first (`user` puts `User.php` above `UserSeeder.php`), and files under `vendor`, `node_modules` and similar folders rank below the project's own files with the same match. When nothing matches, Go to File and the Files tab try once more with one swapped pair of neighbouring letters or one extra letter in the query (`ordre` finds `Order.php`); this is off in substring mode. In Search Everywhere's Files tab, files you opened recently and files next to the one you are editing get a small boost.
- For classes, symbols and actions a word must start where a hump or separator starts
  ("strict" matching), which keeps the lists short.

![Go to File with camel humps](docs/screenshots/goto-file-camel-humps.png)

To match only text that contains what you typed, turn off **Settings > Tools > Search > Fuzzy
matching** (`search.everywhere.fuzzy`). Files, Classes and Symbols in Search Everywhere and Go to
File then find `OrderCon` in `OrderController` but no longer `orco`. This includes the PHP and Lua class and symbol indexes; the Actions tab keeps fuzzy matching.

The button at the right end of the search field switches between fuzzy and substring matching for the current session without touching the setting.

![Substring matching switched on in Go to File](docs/screenshots/search-index-exact-toggle.png)

Ranking happens in Rust (`forge-fuzzy`), so the same rules apply in every list with a
speed search: Recent Files, the New Scratch File popup, choosers.

Classes and Symbols come from the project index. For PHP, JavaScript, TypeScript and Lua files the declarations are read with a real parser, so a `class` inside a comment or a string is not listed and the methods of JavaScript and TypeScript classes are found; other languages (and files over 256 KB) use simpler line patterns.

Results appear as each source answers: files and symbols show up at once, and a slower source (a language server, for example) adds its group when it is done instead of holding everything back.

## Find Action

**Find Action** (`Ctrl+Shift+A`, macOS `Cmd+Shift+A`) is the Actions tab on its own. Type an
action's name, for example "reformat", "commit", "new scratch" or "close project".

![Find Action](docs/screenshots/find-action.png)

- Each row shows the action, its menu group (e.g. "Code | Folding") and its shortcut.
- You can also type the action id (`ReformatCode`), which ranks below title matches.
- Actions Forge has not implemented yet are dimmed and listed last; running one shows
  "*Action* is not available yet". Turn on **Include disabled actions** to see them while
  searching.

Find Action is the fastest way to reach commands that have no shortcut and no menu yet, for
example **Close Project**, **Detect Project Type**, **Reindex PHP Files**, **Show Git Log**,
**Fetch** or **New SSH Connection…**.

## Recent Files

See [Workbench: Recent Files and Switcher](docs/guide/user/workbench.md#recent-files-and-switcher).

## Find in Files

**Find in Files** (`Ctrl+Shift+F`, macOS `Cmd+Shift+F`, also Edit | Find | Find in Files… and
the Project view's context menu) searches the text of every project file.

![Find in Files](docs/screenshots/editor-polish-find-in-files.png)

The status bar shows the size of the search index ("272,700 files", or "Indexing" while it builds or refreshes). Hover it for how many files are searched by content, how many binary or oversized files are listed by name only, and when the index was last updated.

![Search index in the status bar](docs/screenshots/search-index-status.png)

- Type the text; results update as you type, one row per matching line with the file name and
  line number. The header counts matches and files.
- Options next to the field: **Cc** match case, **W** whole words, **.\*** regular expression.
- **Scope** tabs under the field: **In Project**, **Directory** (a project-relative folder), **Open Files** (the editor tabs), **Changed Files** (files git reports as modified, added or untracked) and **Scope**, which offers PHPStorm's predefined scopes and your named scopes ([Scopes and file colors](docs/guide/user/scopes-and-file-colors.md)); **…** opens Settings | Appearance & Behavior | Scopes. The open and changed lists are taken when the search runs; the Find window keeps the list it was opened with.

![Find in Files scopes](docs/screenshots/search-index-find-scopes.png)

![Find in Files in a named scope](docs/screenshots/find-in-files-scope.png)

- The Find window (and Replace in Files) has the same scope chooser in its toolbar.

- In the Find window, the list next to the directory field adds **lines of context** (1 to 5) above and below each match. Context lines are dimmed, shown once even when two matches share them, and a click opens the file there.

![Find window with context lines](docs/screenshots/search-index-find-context.png)

- In the Find window, the first list next to the directory field orders the files: **By path** (which also groups them by folder), **By matches** (most matching lines first) or **By modified** (newest first; only for the project's own files, a remote project keeps the path order).

![Find window ordered by matches](docs/screenshots/search-index-find-sorted.png)

- When project files change after a search (a save, git, another tool), the Find window shows **Files changed since this search. Search again** next to the match count. The list is not refreshed on its own, so rows do not move while you read them.

![Find window after files changed](docs/screenshots/search-index-find-stale.png)

- **Replace in Files**: the Find window has a **Replace with** field. **Replace…** lists every line that would change (old text left, new text right) before anything is written; **Replace all** then writes the files, and **Undo replace** puts back the files the last replace changed, leaving alone any file you edited since. In regular expression mode the replacement may use `$1` and `${name}`; otherwise it is inserted as typed. It uses the same scope, file mask and options as the search, and works on remote projects too.

![Replace in Files preview](docs/screenshots/search-index-replace.png)

- **File mask**: tick it and enter patterns such as `*.php` or `*.php, !*Test.php`
  (`!` excludes).
- Scope: **In Project** or **Directory** (a folder of the project; empty means the project
  root).
- `Up`/`Down` select a row; the preview below shows the file around the match. `Enter` opens
  the file at the match, `Escape` closes.
- **Open in Find Window** (`Ctrl+Enter`, macOS `Cmd+Enter`) closes the popup and keeps the
  results as a tab of the [Find tool window](docs/guide/user/workbench.md#find-tool-window) (`Alt+3`),
  grouped by file, with **Rerun**. `Ctrl+Alt+Down` / `Ctrl+Alt+Up` (Next/Previous Occurrence)
  then walk through them.

Ignored files (`.gitignore`), binary files and very large files are skipped. In remote projects
the search runs on the host, which keeps the result and sends the rows the list shows, so large results page the same way. A remote search cannot be cancelled once started.

The **Text** tab of Search Everywhere uses the same search (from two characters on).

![Find in Files results in the Find tool window](docs/screenshots/find-window-text.png)

**Replace in Files** (`Ctrl+Shift+R`, macOS `Cmd+Shift+R`) opens the same tab with the selected
text as the query and the caret in **Replace with**.

# Inspections

Every problem Forge highlights belongs to an **inspection**: Forge's own checks (the PHP index
inspections, PHP data flow, duplicated code, requirements, Spring Boot properties, spelling)
as well as the problems of language servers and external tools (the PHP quality tools
PHPStan, Psalm, PHP_CodeSniffer, PHP CS Fixer, PHP Mess Detector and Laravel Pint, Clippy,
go vet, golangci-lint, ktlint, detekt, Composer, CMake builds). Like in PHPStorm, an **inspection
profile** decides which inspections run, how severe their problems are, and where.

## Settings | Editor | Inspections

![Inspections settings](docs/screenshots/inspections-settings.png)

- **Profile**: the profile the project uses. **Project Default** is stored in the project
  (`.forge/inspectionProfiles/Project_Default.xml`, written once it differs from the
  defaults), **Default** in your user settings. Copies are stored where you put them.
- **⚙ menu**: **Duplicate…**, **Copy to Project…** / **Copy to IDE…**, **Rename…**,
  **Delete**, **Restore Defaults**, **Export** (PHPStorm's inspection profile XML or Forge
  JSON), **Import Profile…** (both formats, so PHPStorm profiles work) and **Add Custom
  Severity…**.
- **The tree** groups the inspections by language and group (PHP | Data flow, Rust |
  External tools, …). The search field filters by name, id, group and description. The
  checkboxes switch single inspections or whole groups on and off; changed inspections are
  shown in the accent color.
- **The selected inspection**: its id (the name suppression comments use), **Enabled**,
  **Severity**, **Scopes**, **Options** and the description. **Reset to default** forgets the
  profile's changes for it.

### Severities

**Error**, **Warning**, **Weak Warning**, **Server Problem**, **Typo** and **Info**, plus
custom severities (⚙ | Add Custom Severity…) that the editor highlights like one of the
built-in ones. Problems of external tools (Clippy, golangci-lint, language servers, …) keep the
level the tool reports (**As reported by the tool**) until you choose a severity.

### Scope-specific settings

![Scopes of an inspection](docs/screenshots/inspections-settings-scopes.png)

**Scopes | +** adds a [scope](docs/guide/user/scopes-and-file-colors.md) (a named scope or a predefined one
such as Project Test Files) with its own checkbox and severity. The first scope that contains
a file wins; the last row, **Everywhere else**, is the inspection's own setting. Turning an
inspection off for tests while keeping it everywhere else is one row.

### What the profile does in the editor

The profile applies to every problem the editor and the Problems tool window show, whatever
reported it: a disabled inspection's problems disappear, severities follow the profile, and
suppression comments (below) hide problems right away.

## Inspect Code

**Code | Inspect Code…** opens **Specify Inspection Scope**:

![Specify Inspection Scope](docs/screenshots/inspections-inspect-code-dialog.png)

- **Whole project**, **Module**, **File** (the current editor), **Directory** (the current
  file's folder) or a **Custom scope**; **Include test sources**.
- **Inspection profile** and **Configure…** to edit it.

**Analyze** runs every enabled inspection over the scope in the backend (where the project
lives, also for remote projects). The status bar shows the progress with a **Cancel** button.
**Code | Analyze Code | Inspect Current File** (`Alt+Shift+I`) inspects the current file
without the dialog.

> **Note:** inspections whose problems come from a running language server or tool
> (language server problems, Clippy, ktlint, spelling, requirements, …) run in the editor
> only; Inspect Code runs Forge's own inspections and duplicated code.

## Inspection Results

![Inspection Results](docs/screenshots/inspections-results.png)

Every run opens a tab in the **Inspection Results** tool window (View | Tool Windows |
Inspection Results):

- The problems are grouped by inspection group, inspection and file. The toolbar adds
  **Group by Severity** and **Group by Directory**, **Expand All** / **Collapse All**,
  **Rerun**, **Export** (HTML or XML) and **Edit Settings**.
- Double-click (or `Enter`) opens the problem in the editor.
- The right pane shows the selected problem with its **quick fixes** (applied to the file,
  which must not have changed since the run), **Suppress…** (statement, function, class or
  file) and **Edit Inspection Profile Setting**. Fixed problems are struck through until the
  next run.
- **Duplicates** lists the duplicate groups of the run.

## Run Inspection by Name

**Code | Run Inspection by Name…** (`Ctrl+Alt+Shift+I`, macOS `Cmd+Alt+Shift+I`) picks one
inspection by name, then asks for the scope and runs only that inspection.

![Run Inspection by Name](docs/screenshots/inspections-run-by-name.png)

## Code Cleanup

**Code | Code Cleanup…** asks for a scope, applies every *safe* quick fix of the inspections
marked **Code Cleanup** in the profile (for example removing unused assignments) and shows a
preview with a diff per file. **Apply** writes the files; files that changed since the
preview are left alone.

![Code Cleanup preview](docs/screenshots/inspections-code-cleanup.png)

## Suppressing problems

`Alt+Enter` on a problem lists **Inspection '…' options** with **Edit inspection profile
setting**, **Disable inspection** and **Suppress for statement / function / class / file**:

![Suppress actions](docs/screenshots/inspections-suppress.png)

Forge writes PHPStorm's comments, so suppressions work in both IDEs:

| Language | Comment |
| --- | --- |
| PHP | `/** @noinspection PhpUnusedAssignment */` (or a line `@noinspection Id` in the doc comment of a function or class) |
| JavaScript, TypeScript | `// noinspection JSUnusedLocalSymbols` |
| Python | `# noinspection PyUnusedLocal` |
| Other languages | the language's line comment: `// noinspection Id`, `# noinspection Id`, `-- noinspection Id`, `<!-- noinspection Id -->` |

- A comment **before a statement** suppresses the listed inspections in that statement; a
  function or class declaration counts as one statement with its body.
- A comment **at the top of the file** followed by an empty line (in PHP also on the
  `<?php` line) suppresses them in the whole file.
- A comment **after code on the same line** suppresses them on that line.
- Several ids are separated by commas; `ALL` suppresses every inspection; PHPStorm's ids with
  the `Inspection` suffix work too.

## Duplicated code

The **Duplicated code fragment** inspection (General) compares the tokens of the inspected
files, so formatting and comments do not matter. Its options:

- **Minimum fragment size (tokens)**, 60 by default;
- **Anonymize identifiers**: fragments that differ only in variable, function and field
  names are duplicates too (on by default);
- **Anonymize literals**: string and number values do not matter either.

![Duplicates](docs/screenshots/inspections-duplicates.png)

**Code | Analyze Code | Locate Duplicates…** runs only this inspection over a scope. Each copy
is reported with links to the other copies, and the **Duplicates** view of Inspection Results
lists the groups.

## PHP data flow

Forge follows the values of local variables through PHP functions (branches are merged, loops
forget what they assign) and reports:

| Inspection | Example |
| --- | --- |
| **Variable is always null** | `$customer = null; … $customer->name` |
| **Undefined variable** | a variable read in a function before any path assigned it |
| **Condition is always true or false** | `if (false)`, `if (1 === 2)`, `$debug = false; if ($debug)` (not `while (true)`) |
| **Unused assignment** | `$prefix = 'ORD'; $prefix = 'INV';`, or a value never read again; the quick fix removes it (keeping a call with side effects) |

The analysis stays quiet where it cannot be sure: functions using `$$name`, `extract()`,
`compact()`, `get_defined_vars()`, `eval` or `include` are skipped, variables shared by
reference (`&$x`, `global`, `static`, `use (&$x)`) are not tracked, and a variable passed to a
call may be written by it.

## Command-line inspector

The `forge` binary inspects a project without a window, for CI:

```sh
forge inspect <project> <profile.xml|profile name> <output dir> [-format xml|json|html] [-d <directory>] [-fail-on <severity>] [-v0|-v1|-v2]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `<project>` | the project folder |
| `<profile.xml\|name>` | an inspection profile file (PHPStorm XML or Forge JSON, e.g. `.forge/inspectionProfiles/Project_Default.xml`) or the name of a profile (`Project Default`, `Default`, a copy) |
| `<output dir>` | where the results go: one XML file per inspection plus `.descriptions.xml` (PHPStorm's format, default), `inspections.json` (`-format json`) or `index.html` (`-format html`) |
| `-d <directory>` | inspect only this folder of the project |
| `-fail-on <severity>` | exit with code 1 when a problem of this severity or worse was found (`ERROR`, `WARNING`, `WEAK WARNING`, …) |
| `-v0` / `-v1` / `-v2` | quiet, normal (default), verbose |

It builds the PHP index, runs the profile's inspections that work without the IDE (the PHP
inspections, PHP data flow, duplicated code) and exits with 0, 1 (`-fail-on`) or 2 (wrong
arguments, a project or profile that cannot be found). Example for a CI job:

```sh
forge inspect . "Project Default" build/inspections -format xml -fail-on ERROR
```

> **Note:** on Windows the release build is a GUI application: it writes the results and
> sets the exit code (`start /wait forge.exe inspect …` waits for it), but prints nothing to
> the console.
