## Go to Declaration or Usages

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+B` · macOS `Cmd+B` · action id `GotoDeclaration`

Jumps to the declaration of the symbol at the caret (also `Ctrl+Click` and middle click); on a declaration it shows its usages; several targets open the Choose Declaration popup. PHP's own classes and functions open read-only in the PHP stubs.

**Menu:** Navigate | Declaration or Usages

![Ctrl+hover on \Throwable](docs/screenshots/php-nav-ctrl-hover.png)

More: [Editor](docs/guide/user/editor.md#go-to-declaration), [PHP navigation](docs/guide/user/php.md#navigation)

## Go to Implementation(s)

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Alt+B` · macOS `Cmd+Alt+B` · action id `GotoImplementation`

Lists the classes implementing or extending the class or interface at the caret, or the methods overriding the method (also `Ctrl+Alt+Click`).

**Menu:** Navigate | Implementation(s)

More: [Editor](docs/guide/user/editor.md#implementation-type-declaration-super-method)

## Go to Type Declaration

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Shift+B` · macOS `Cmd+Shift+B` · action id `GotoTypeDeclaration`

Jumps to the class of the variable, property or method return type at the caret.

**Menu:** Navigate | Type Declaration

More: [Editor](docs/guide/user/editor.md#implementation-type-declaration-super-method)

## Go to Super Method

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+U` · macOS `Cmd+U` · action id `GotoSuperMethod`

Jumps to the method the current method overrides or implements; on a class, to its parent class and interfaces.

**Menu:** Navigate | Super Method

More: [Editor](docs/guide/user/editor.md#implementation-type-declaration-super-method)

## Type Hierarchy

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+H` · macOS `Ctrl+H` · action id `TypeHierarchy`

Shows the class at the caret in the Hierarchy tool window: its parent classes and subtypes (Class Hierarchy), its supertypes or its subtypes.

**Menu:** Navigate | Type Hierarchy

More: [Type, Method and Call Hierarchy](docs/guide/user/hierarchies.md#type-hierarchy)

![Type Hierarchy](docs/screenshots/hierarchy-type.png)

## Method Hierarchy

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Shift+H` · macOS `Cmd+Shift+H` · action id `MethodHierarchy`

Shows which classes define the method at the caret, which inherit it and which should define it.

**Menu:** Navigate | Method Hierarchy

More: [Type, Method and Call Hierarchy](docs/guide/user/hierarchies.md#method-hierarchy)

## Call Hierarchy

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Alt+H` · macOS `Ctrl+Alt+H` · action id `CallHierarchy`

Shows the callers (or callees) of the method or function at the caret, one level per expanded node, with the call sites.

**Menu:** Navigate | Call Hierarchy

More: [Type, Method and Call Hierarchy](docs/guide/user/hierarchies.md#call-hierarchy)

## Back

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Alt+Left` · macOS `Cmd+[`, `Cmd+Alt+Left` · action id `Back`

Goes back to the previous caret location in your navigation history.

**Menu:** Navigate | Back

More: [Editor](docs/guide/user/editor.md#go-to-declaration)

## Forward

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Alt+Right` · macOS `Cmd+]`, `Cmd+Alt+Right` · action id `Forward`

Goes forward in the navigation history.

**Menu:** Navigate | Forward

More: [Editor](docs/guide/user/editor.md#go-to-declaration)

## Last Edit Location

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Shift+Backspace` · macOS `Cmd+Shift+Backspace` · action id `JumpToLastChange`

Goes back to the previous place where you changed text, across files. This edit history is separate from Back/Forward: edits a line or two apart count as one place, places follow later edits, renames and deletions, and the place the caret is already at is skipped. Recent Locations' **Show changed only** lists the same places.

**Menu:** Navigate | Last Edit Location

More: [Workbench](docs/guide/user/workbench.md#recent-files-and-switcher)

## Next Edit Location

**Shortcut:** none by default · action id `JumpToNextChange`

Goes forward again through the edit history after Last Edit Location. A new edit starts over at the newest place.

**Menu:** Navigate | Next Edit Location

More: [Workbench](docs/guide/user/workbench.md#recent-files-and-switcher)

## Select In

**Shortcut:** `Alt+F1` · macOS `Alt+F1` · action id `SelectIn`

Shows the current file somewhere else. Pick a target with its number, the arrow keys and `Enter`, or a click:

| Target | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Project View | Opens the Project tool window and selects the file. |
| Commit | Selects the file in the Commit tool window (only when it has local changes). |
| Structure | Opens the Structure tool window with the member at the caret selected. |
| File Structure | Opens the File Structure popup (`Ctrl+F12`). |
| Navigation Bar | Focuses the navigation bar (`Alt+Home`). |
| Git Log | Opens the Git log filtered to the file's history (Git projects). |
| Explorer / Finder / File Manager | Shows the file selected in the system file manager (local projects). |
| Terminal | Opens a terminal tab in the file's folder. |

From the Project view (with the focus in the tree) the targets apply to the selected file and Project View is left out.

**Menu:** Navigate | Select In...

![Select In](docs/screenshots/select-in.png)

More: [Project view](docs/guide/user/workbench.md#project-view)

## Next Method

**Shortcut:** `Alt+Down` · macOS `Ctrl+Down` · action id `MethodDown`

Moves the caret to the name of the next class, interface, trait, enum, function or method, or to the closing brace of a class. Works in every language with Sticky Lines: PHP, JavaScript/TypeScript (also in Vue and HTML scripts), CSS/SCSS/Less rules, Lua and other brace languages.

**Menu:** Navigate | Next Method

More: [Code structure](docs/guide/user/code-structure.md)

## Previous Method

**Shortcut:** `Alt+Up` · macOS `Ctrl+Up` · action id `MethodUp`

Moves the caret to the previous class, function, method or CSS rule.

**Menu:** Navigate | Previous Method

More: [Code structure](docs/guide/user/code-structure.md)

## Next Change

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Down` · macOS `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Down` · action id `VcsShowNextChangeMarker`

Moves the caret to the next block that differs from Git `HEAD` (the gutter change markers), wrapping around at the end of the file, and shows its popup with the old text, **Rollback** and **Show Diff**, like a click on the marker.

**Menu:** Navigate | Next Change

![Next Change](docs/screenshots/next-change.png)

More: [Git change markers](docs/guide/user/git.md#change-markers)

## Previous Change

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Up` · macOS `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Up` · action id `VcsShowPrevChangeMarker`

Moves the caret to the previous changed block and shows its popup.

**Menu:** Navigate | Previous Change

More: [Git change markers](docs/guide/user/git.md#change-markers)

# Shortcuts: Refactoring

Refactorings and code generation. Windows/Linux shortcuts first, macOS second; both are PHPStorm's defaults and can be changed in Settings | Keymap.

| Action | Windows / Linux | macOS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Refactor This…](#refactor-this) | `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+T` | `Ctrl+T` |
| [Rename…](#rename) | `Shift+F6` | `Shift+F6` |
| [Introduce Variable…](#introduce-variable) | `Ctrl+Alt+V` | `Cmd+Alt+V` |
| [Introduce Constant…](#introduce-constant) | `Ctrl+Alt+C` | `Cmd+Alt+C` |
| [Introduce Field…](#introduce-field) | `Ctrl+Alt+F` | `Cmd+Alt+F` |
| [Introduce Parameter…](#introduce-parameter) | `Ctrl+Alt+P` | `Cmd+Alt+P` |
| [Extract Method…](#extract-method) | `Ctrl+Alt+M` | `Cmd+Alt+M` |
| [Inline…](#inline) | `Ctrl+Alt+N` | `Cmd+Alt+N` |
| [Change Signature…](#change-signature) | `Ctrl+F6` | `Cmd+F6` |
| [Move…](#move) | `F6` | `F6` |
| [Copy…](#copy) | `F5` | `F5` |
| [Safe Delete…](#safe-delete) | `Alt+Delete` | `Cmd+Delete` |
| [Extract Interface…](#extract-interface) | — | — |
| [Extract Superclass…](#extract-superclass) | — | — |
| [Extract Component…](#extract-component) | — | — |
| [Pull Members Up…](#pull-members-up) | — | — |
| [Push Members Down…](#push-members-down) | — | — |
| [Make Static…](#make-static) | — | — |

| [Generate…](#generate) | `Alt+Insert` | `Cmd+N` |
| [Reformat Code](#reformat-code) | `Ctrl+Alt+L` | `Cmd+Alt+L` |

## Rename

**Shortcut:** `Shift+F6` · macOS `Shift+F6` · action id `RenameElement`

In the editor: renames the symbol at the caret in place, in every file of the project; `Enter`
applies, `Escape` cancels, `Shift+F6` again opens the Rename dialog. In the Project view:
renames the selected file or folder. One undo step (`Ctrl+Z`) undoes the whole rename.

**Menu:** Refactor | Rename…

![In-place rename](docs/screenshots/rename-in-place.png)

More: [Editor](docs/guide/user/editor.md#rename), [PHP](docs/guide/user/php.md#rename)

## Refactor This

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+T` · macOS `Ctrl+T` · action id `Refactorings.QuickListPopupAction`

A popup with only the refactorings that apply at the caret or to the selection, with their
shortcuts: on a PHP class Rename, Move, Copy, Safe Delete, Extract Interface / Superclass and Pull
Members Up / Push Members Down; on a method Rename, Change Signature, Move, Safe Delete, Inline,
Pull Up / Push Down and Make Static; on an expression or a selection Introduce Variable /
Constant / Field / Parameter and Extract Method. In JavaScript, TypeScript and Vue files it
offers Rename, Extract Component (for whole elements), Move and Copy, and the language server's
refactorings worded like PHPStorm (see [WebForge](docs/guide/user/webforge.md#language-server-refactorings)). Pick one with its number (`1`-`9`, `0`), the arrow keys and
`Enter`, or a click; typing filters the list (speed search), `Escape` clears the filter.

![Refactor This on a class](docs/screenshots/refactor-this-class.png)

![Refactor This filtered by typing](docs/screenshots/refactor-this-method.png)

**Menu:** Refactor | Refactor This…

## Introduce Variable

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Alt+V` · macOS `Cmd+Alt+V` · action id `IntroduceVariable`

Puts the selected expression (or the one picked in the **Expressions** popup when nothing is
selected) into a new local variable. With several occurrences it asks whether to replace this
one or all of them. The name is then edited in place: `Up` / `Down` choose another suggested
name, `Enter` finishes. In the editor this shortcut wins over the Vim toggle.

**Menu:** Refactor | Extract/Introduce | Variable…

![Expressions popup](docs/screenshots/introduce-variable-expressions.png)

More: [PHP](docs/guide/user/php.md#extract-introduce-and-inline)

## Introduce Constant

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Alt+C` · macOS `Cmd+Alt+C` · action id `IntroduceConstant`

Turns a constant expression into a class constant (`self::NAME`), or a global `const` outside
classes. The dialog asks for the name, the visibility and whether to replace all occurrences.

**Menu:** Refactor | Extract/Introduce | Constant…

![Introduce Constant](docs/screenshots/introduce-constant-dialog.png)

## Introduce Field

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Alt+F` · macOS `Cmd+Alt+F` · action id `IntroduceField`

Moves an expression of a method into a new property (`$this->name`), initialized in the current
method, the field declaration or the constructor.

**Menu:** Refactor | Extract/Introduce | Field…

## Introduce Parameter

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Alt+P` · macOS `Cmd+Alt+P` · action id `IntroduceParameter`

Adds a parameter for an expression to the enclosing function or method and passes the
expression at every call (or makes it the parameter's default value).

**Menu:** Refactor | Extract/Introduce | Parameter…

## Extract Method

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Alt+M` · macOS `Cmd+Alt+M` · action id `ExtractMethod`

Moves the selected statements or expression into a new method (a function outside classes).
The dialog shows the parameters (reorder and rename them), what is returned, the visibility,
**Declare static** and a signature preview, and offers to replace duplicate fragments.

**Menu:** Refactor | Extract/Introduce | Method…

![Extract Method](docs/screenshots/extract-method-dialog.png)

## Inline

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Alt+N` · macOS `Cmd+Alt+N` · action id `Inline`

Replaces a local variable by its value, a method or function call by the body, or a constant by
its value: every reference (removing or keeping the declaration) or only the one at the caret.

**Menu:** Refactor | Inline…

![Inline Method](docs/screenshots/inline-method-dialog.png)

## Change Signature

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+F6` · macOS `Cmd+F6` · action id `ChangeSignature`

Changes the name, visibility, return type and parameters of a PHP method or function (add,
remove, reorder; type, name, default value and the value new parameters get at call sites) and
updates the overriding methods and every call.

**Menu:** Refactor | Change Signature…

![Change Signature](docs/screenshots/change-signature-dialog.png)

More: [PHP](docs/guide/user/php.md#move-copy-safe-delete-change-signature-and-make-static)

## Move

**Shortcut:** `F6` · macOS `F6` · action id `Move`

In the editor: moves the PHP class at the caret to another namespace and directory (Move
Class), static members to another class (Move Members) or a function to another file. In the
Project view: moves the selected files and folders (also by drag and drop), updating namespaces
and references of PHP classes.

**Menu:** Refactor | Move…

![Move Class](docs/screenshots/move-class-dialog.png)

## Copy

**Shortcut:** `F5` · macOS `F5` · action id `CopyElement`

Copies the PHP class at the caret under a new name (Copy Class), or the selected file or folder
in the Project view.

**Menu:** Refactor | Copy File…

## Safe Delete

**Shortcut:** `Alt+Delete` · macOS `Cmd+Delete` · action id `SafeDelete`

Deletes the element at the caret (or the selected files in the Project view) after checking
that nothing uses it; **Usages Detected** offers View Usages and Delete Anyway.

**Menu:** Refactor | Safe Delete…

![Usages Detected](docs/screenshots/safe-delete-usages-detected.png)

## Extract Interface

**Shortcut:** none by default · action id `ExtractInterface`

In a PHP class or enum: creates an interface (name, namespace, directory) from the PHP Interface
file template that declares the chosen public methods with their PHPDoc and holds the chosen
constants; the class implements it. **Replace class references with interface where possible**
changes parameter types that only need the interface's methods.

**Menu:** Refactor | Extract/Introduce | Interface…

![Extract Interface](docs/screenshots/extract-interface-dialog.png)

## Extract Superclass

**Shortcut:** none by default · action id `ExtractSuperclass`

Moves the chosen members of a PHP class into a new class that the class extends (between it
and its old parent); **Make abstract** keeps a method in the class and declares it abstract in
the superclass.

**Menu:** Refactor | Extract/Introduce | Superclass…

![Extract Superclass](docs/screenshots/extract-superclass-dialog.png)

## Extract Component

**Shortcut:** none by default · action id `WebForge.ExtractComponent`

Moves the selected Vue template elements or React JSX into a new component file with props for
the names they use; the parent renders and imports it. See
[WebForge](docs/guide/user/webforge.md#extract-component).

**Menu:** Refactor | Extract/Introduce | Component…

![Extract Component](docs/screenshots/extract-component-vue-dialog.png)

## Pull Members Up

**Shortcut:** none by default · action id `MembersPullUp`

Moves members into a superclass or interface of the class (interfaces get declarations), with
**Make abstract**; members a chosen one uses are highlighted, problems are listed before the
change.

**Menu:** Refactor | Pull Members Up…

![Pull Members Up](docs/screenshots/pull-members-up-dialog.png)

## Push Members Down

**Shortcut:** none by default · action id `MemberPushDown`

Copies members into every direct subclass and removes them from the class (**Keep abstract**
leaves an abstract declaration).

**Menu:** Refactor | Push Members Down…

## Make Static

**Shortcut:** none by default · action id `MakeStatic`

Makes a PHP instance method static, passing the object or the fields it reads as parameters,
and updates its calls.

**Menu:** Refactor | Make Static…

![Make Method Static](docs/screenshots/make-static-dialog.png)

## Show Context Actions

**Shortcut:** `Alt+Enter` · macOS `Alt+Enter` · action id `ShowIntentionActions`

Opens the intention popup at the caret: quick fixes, intentions and refactorings of the
language servers and Forge's PHP intentions. `Right` opens an entry's sub-menu.

**Menu:** Code | Show Context Actions

![Context actions](docs/screenshots/context-actions.png)

More: [Editor](docs/guide/user/editor.md#show-context-actions)

## Generate

**Shortcut:** `Alt+Insert` · macOS `Cmd+N` · action id `Generate`

In PHP files: generates a constructor, getters, setters, overrides, `__toString()` or a PHPDoc block.

**Menu:** Code | Generate…

![Generate…](docs/screenshots/docs-generate.png)

More: [PHP](docs/guide/user/php.md#generate)

## Reformat Code

**Shortcut:** `Ctrl+Alt+L` · macOS `Cmd+Alt+L` · action id `ReformatCode`

Formats the file with the language server's formatter (StyLua for Lua).

**Menu:** Code | Reformat Code

More: [Editor](docs/guide/user/editor.md#reformat-code)

# Color schemes

The color scheme decides how the editor draws code: the colors of keywords, strings, comments
and the other token kinds, the editor background, the caret, the caret row, the selection,
line numbers and search results. Like in PHPStorm it is separate from the UI theme
(Settings | Appearance & Behavior | Appearance | Theme, see
[Settings and themes](docs/guide/user/settings-and-themes.md#themes)).

![Color Scheme settings](docs/screenshots/color-scheme-settings.png)

## Choosing a scheme

Settings | Editor | **Color Scheme** | **Scheme** (`editor.colorScheme.active`):

| Scheme | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Follow the theme | the default: Ember with dark themes, Anvil with light ones, High Contrast (Light) with the High Contrast themes, and the theme's own token colors (the Solarized themes bring their own) |
| Ember | Forge's dark scheme |
| Anvil | Forge's light scheme |
| High Contrast | white text on black, every token at least 7:1 (WCAG AAA), keywords bold |
| High Contrast Light | black text on white, every token at least 7:1, keywords bold |
| *your schemes* | listed under **Custom** |

A scheme you select explicitly stays the same when you switch the UI theme, so you can, for
example, use the dark Ember editor with the light Anvil UI.

## Your own schemes

The four bundled schemes cannot be changed. The **gear** next to the selector has:

- **Duplicate…**: copy the selected scheme into a new one and select it. Change it from there.
- **Rename…**, **Restore Defaults** (back to the colors of its parent bundled scheme) and
  **Delete** for your own schemes.
- **Import Scheme…** and **Export…** (see below).

## Editing attributes

The list on the left holds the attributes in two groups:

- **General**: Default text (editor foreground and background), Caret, Caret row, Selection
  background, Line number, Search result.
- **Language Defaults**: Keyword, String, Number, Comment, Variable, Function, Class name,
  Property and attribute, Operator sign, Markup tag. Every language uses them (PHP, HTML, CSS,
  JavaScript, TypeScript, Lua, SQL, Markdown, …).

For the selected attribute you can set, where it applies:

- **Bold** and **Italic**;
- **Foreground** and **Background**: tick the box and pick a color; untick it to use the
  default text color or no background;
- **Effects**: Underscored, Bold underscored, Underwaved, Strikeout, Dotted line or Bordered,
  with its own color.

Changed attributes are highlighted in the list; **Reset to Ember** (or Anvil) gives one back
its parent's value. Changes are saved as you make them and show up in every open editor right
away.

The **preview** below shows a PHP class and some HTML in the scheme. Click a word in it to
select its attribute.

![Editing a scheme](docs/screenshots/color-scheme-edit.png)

## Import and export

- **Import Scheme…** reads an IntelliJ color scheme file (`.icls`, as exported by PHPStorm,
  IntelliJ IDEA, WebStorm or downloaded from a theme site) into a new scheme and selects it.
  IntelliJ's attributes are mapped onto Forge's (for example `DEFAULT_KEYWORD` or
  `PHP_KEYWORD` → Keyword, `PHP_VAR` / `DEFAULT_LOCAL_VARIABLE` → Variable,
  `CARET_ROW_COLOR` → Caret row); references to other attributes (`baseAttributes`) are
  followed. What the file does not set comes from High Contrast when its parent is IntelliJ's
  "High contrast", from Ember when it is Darcula (or another dark scheme) and from Anvil
  otherwise.
- **Export…** writes the selected scheme as an `.icls` file with every attribute, so it looks
  the same when you import it into a JetBrains IDE.

> **Note:** attributes Forge does not have (for example language-specific ones such as PHP
> heredoc colors, or the console colors) are ignored on import.

## Where schemes are stored

Your schemes are user settings (`editor.colorScheme.schemes`, one entry per scheme with its
name, its parent and the changed attributes), so they are part of `settings.toml`, of
**Export Settings** (group Editor) and of the [settings reference](docs/guide/reference/settings.md).

# IDE language

Forge is English by default, like PHPStorm. Other languages come as translations bundled with
Forge; German (Deutsch) is the first one.

![Settings in German](docs/screenshots/i18n-settings-de.png)

## Changing the language

1. Open Settings (`Ctrl+Alt+S`, macOS `Cmd+,`) | Appearance & Behavior | System Settings |
   Language.
2. Pick **IDE language**: English or Deutsch.
3. Press OK or Apply. Forge asks to restart. **Restart** applies the language everywhere;
   **Not Now** keeps working.

Most of the UI switches at once, because it renders its text through the translation catalog.
Text that Forge computes once at startup keeps the previous language until the restart: tool
window and Settings page titles, the action list of Find Action and the keymap, and messages
that are already open. The setting is `ide.language` (`en` or `de`) and is stored in the user
settings, so it applies to every project.

## What is translated

| Area | German |
| --- | --- |
| Main menu (File … Help), its submenus and mnemonics | yes |
| Action names in Find Action, the keymap settings and the main menu | yes (PHPStorm actions) |
| Tool window titles and stripe buttons, tool window options menu | yes |
| Status bar (line separator, encoding, indent widgets) | yes |
| Settings dialog: page tree, buttons, search, Appearance, System Settings, Editor General, Editor Tabs, Font, Terminal, Git and Commit settings | yes |
| Welcome screen | yes |
| Search Everywhere and Find Action | yes |
| Find in Files, Rename, New Project, Run/Debug Configurations | yes |
| Commit tool window and Commit Options | yes |
| Project view and editor tab context menus, the editor context menu | yes |
| Notifications tool window and the balloons of the shell | yes |
| Git: Branches popup, Git log and file history, Merge, Rebase, Pull, Reset, Stash, Shelf, Patch, Worktrees, Clone and the merge window | yes |
| Debugger tool window, Breakpoints dialog, Attach to Process, Web Server Debug Validation, Servers | yes |
| Database tool window, Data Sources and Drivers, table editor and consoles, import, dump, Modify Table, schema comparison and diagrams | yes |
| Refactoring dialogs (Move, Copy, Safe Delete, Change Signature, Extract, Pull Members Up / Push Members Down, Extract Interface / Superclass), Find Usages and the Find tool window | yes |
| Run tool window, run configuration fields and types, Run on targets (Docker, Docker Compose, SSH, WSL, Dev Container) | yes |
| Forge's own actions without a PHPStorm counterpart (e.g. New Window, Code With Me, AI, Database actions) in Find Action and the keymap | yes |
| Settings pages Languages & Frameworks \| PHP (with Composer, Quality Tools, Debug, Laravel, Symfony, Doctrine, WordPress), Editor, Version Control and Tools | yes |
| Safe Mode refusals and common backend errors (no project open, file not found, I/O errors) | yes |
| Other tool windows and dialogs (.NET, C/C++, code hosts, Code With Me, game engines, Python, Java, Services, …), the settings of other language packs, file templates and New Project generator names | not yet, they stay English |

Untranslated text is always English, never a key or an empty label. The
[developer guide](docs/guide/developer/localization.md) explains how the coverage is measured and how
to add translations.

> **Note:** plugin names, settings and tool window titles of the bundled plugins are about half
> translated: the PHP, Editor, Version Control and Tools pages are German, the settings of the
> other language packs stay English for now. Third-party plugins can ship their own translations
> in their manifest.

## Find Action in two languages

With German selected, Find Action (`Ctrl+Shift+A`) and the Actions tab of Search Everywhere
show the German action names, and a query matches both names: `einstell` finds
*Einstellungen…* and `reformat` finds *Code neu formatieren* (Reformat Code), like PHPStorm with
a language pack. Matches on the German name rank first.

![Find Action matching German action names](docs/screenshots/i18n-find-action-de.png)

## Terminology

The German translation follows JetBrains' German terminology and addresses you formally
("Sie"): *Einstellungen*, *Projekt*, *Ausführen*, *Debuggen*, *Refactoring*, *Toolfenster*,
*Änderungsliste*. Git terms stay as JetBrains keeps them: *Commit*, *Push*, *Pull*, *Branch*,
*Merge*, *Rebase*, *Stash*. Keyboard shortcuts keep their English key names (`Ctrl+Alt+S`).

Numbers, dates and plurals follow the language: *1.234 Dateien*, *04.11.2026*.

![Commit window in German](docs/screenshots/i18n-commit-de.png)

![Git log in German](docs/screenshots/i18n-git-log-de.png)

![Run/Debug Configurations with Run on in German](docs/screenshots/i18n-run-on-de.png)

# Settings and themes

## The Settings dialog

**Settings** (`Ctrl+Alt+S`, macOS `Cmd+,`, or the gear in the main toolbar) opens the Settings
dialog, with the same tree as PHPStorm:

- **Appearance & Behavior**: Appearance, System Settings
- **Keymap**
- **Editor**: General, Font, Color Scheme, Code Style (schemes, General and one page per language), Inlay Hints
- **Plugins**
- **Version Control**: Git, GitLab, Forgejo / Gitea, GitHub
- **Languages & Frameworks**: Language Servers, PHP (Composer, Debug, Servers, Laravel,
  Symfony, Doctrine), Node.js, TypeScript, Lua, Template Data Languages
- **Tools**: Terminal, Database, AI Agents, AI Providers, Browser Companion, HTTP Client, SSH Configurations
- **Build, Execution, Deployment**: Docker (Docker Registry), Kubernetes

![Settings dialog](docs/screenshots/settings-light.png)

- **Search settings** at the top filters the tree and highlights matching options on every
  page, also by keywords ("theme", "autosave", "interpreter").
- **OK** applies and closes, **Apply** applies and keeps the dialog open, **Cancel** discards.
- Invalid values (out of range, wrong type) are flagged right away and not saved.
- **Reset** (top right) throws away the unapplied changes of the page; **Restore Defaults**
  sets every option of the page to its default (Apply or OK stores it).
- In the desktop app the dialog is its own window; its size and position are remembered.

![Search in settings](docs/screenshots/settings-search.png)

Every option, its key, type and default is listed in the
[settings reference](docs/guide/reference/settings.md).

## User and project settings

Settings come in four layers; a later one wins:

1. built-in defaults (declared by the plugins),
2. **user** settings: `<config dir>/forge/settings.toml`,
3. **Settings for New Projects** (project-level options only):
   `<config dir>/forge/new-project-settings.toml`,
4. **project** settings: `<project>/.forge/settings.toml`.

Pages with options that can be stored per project show **For current project** in the header;
those options are saved to the project's file, which you can commit to share them with your
team (for example the PHP language level or the Symfony environment). A value that equals
what the layers below give is not stored again, so the project keeps following them.

### Settings for New Projects

File | New Projects Setup | **Settings for New Projects…** opens the Settings dialog for the
defaults of project-level options. The pages with such options show **For new projects**;
their values apply to every project that has no value of its own: the projects you create or
open next, and open projects that never changed the option. Application options (theme, fonts,
keymap, …) are the same everywhere and are edited as usual. On the Welcome screen, without an
open project, the Settings dialog edits these defaults as well.

![Settings for New Projects](docs/screenshots/settings-for-new-projects.png)

## Export and Import Settings

File | Manage IDE Settings | **Export Settings…** writes your settings to a settings archive
(a `.zip` file). Choose the groups to export: Appearance & Behavior, Keymap, Editor, Color
Schemes, Code Style (every language's code style settings), File Types, File and Code Templates,
Live Templates, Version Control, Languages & Frameworks, Tools, Plugins (enabled and disabled
plugins), Other settings, and the files Settings for New Projects, AI Providers, Data Sources,
SSH Configurations and Installed Plugins (the list of installed third-party plugins, not the
plugins themselves). Only groups with changed settings are listed.

![Export Settings](docs/screenshots/export-settings.png)

**Import Settings…** reads such an archive, lists the groups it holds and imports the chosen
ones: each imported group replaces your settings of that group. Forge then restarts. Plugins of
an imported plugin list that are not installed are named in Settings | Plugins | Marketplace.

> **Note:** API keys, tokens and passwords live in the system keychain and are never part of a
> settings archive.

## Settings Sync

**Settings Sync** keeps your settings in step between computers without a Forge account or
cloud service: you provide the place they are shared through. Open it with File | Manage IDE
Settings | **Settings Sync…** (or Settings | Settings Sync).

![Settings Sync](docs/screenshots/settings-sync.png)

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Sync settings across machines | Sync on start and about 30 seconds after you change a setting |
| Sync through | **A folder**, for example in Dropbox, OneDrive, Google Drive, Nextcloud or a network share, or **a git repository** |
| Sync folder | Forge writes a `forge-settings-sync` folder into it |
| Git repository URL, Branch | A repository you own (SSH or HTTPS). Forge clones it into its cache folder and pushes with your git credentials |

**Sync Now** (also File | Manage IDE Settings | **Sync Settings Now**) syncs immediately and
reports what was sent and received.

The synced groups are the ones of Export Settings (by default Appearance, Keymap, Editor, Color
Schemes, Code Style, File Types, File and Code Templates, Live Templates, Plugins and the
Installed Plugins list). Each group is synced as a whole:

- changed only here → it is sent; changed only on the other computer → it is received;
- changed on both since the last sync → the **newer** change wins (last writer wins per
  group). The other version is not lost: a losing local version is saved in
  `<config dir>/forge/settings-sync-backups/<time>/`, a losing shared version in
  `forge-settings-sync/backups/<time>/` of the sync folder.

The Settings Sync options themselves (folder, repository) stay on each computer. API keys,
tokens and passwords live in the system keychain and are never synced. Received configuration
files (AI providers, data sources, SSH configurations) take effect after a restart.

## Restore Default Settings

File | Manage IDE Settings | **Restore Default Settings…** copies your configuration folder to
`<config dir>/forge-backup-<date>-<time>` and restarts Forge with the default settings (the
user settings, the Settings for New Projects and the dialog window sizes are reset).
Connections and accounts (AI providers, code hosts, data sources, SSH configurations), recent
projects and scratches are kept. To go back, copy the files from the backup folder.

### Settings files

The files are TOML with dotted keys as nested tables. You can edit them by hand; Forge picks up
changes on the next start:

```toml
# ~/.config/forge/settings.toml
[appearance]
theme = "light"
windowControls = "gnome"

[editor.font]
family = "Fira Code"
size = 14

[vcs.hosts]
refreshSeconds = 300
```

Some options have no page in the dialog and can only be set this way, such as
`vcs.hosts.statusBarPipeline` and `vcs.hosts.refreshSeconds`.

Secrets (API keys, tokens, passwords, licence keys) never go into these files; they are stored
in the operating system keychain.

## Themes

Settings | Appearance & Behavior | Appearance | **Theme** (`appearance.theme`):

| Theme | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Forge Ember (Dark) | `dark` (default) |
| Forge Anvil (Light) | `light` |
| Solarized Dark | `solarized-dark` |
| Solarized Light | `solarized-light` |
| High Contrast | `high-contrast` |
| High Contrast Light | `high-contrast-light` |

The sun/moon button in the main toolbar, **Theme: Toggle Dark/Light** and **Quick Switch
Scheme…** (`` Ctrl+` ``) toggle between dark and light.

The editor's colors follow the theme unless you choose a color scheme in Settings | Editor |
Color Scheme; see [Color schemes](docs/guide/user/color-schemes.md). The High Contrast themes meet WCAG AAA
contrast and draw borders and strong focus rings; see [Accessibility](docs/guide/user/accessibility.md).

| | |
| --- | --- |
| ![Ember](docs/screenshots/workbench-dark.png) | ![Anvil](docs/screenshots/workbench-light.png) |

## Appearance options

![Appearance](docs/screenshots/settings-appearance.png)

| Option | Setting | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| UI font (Inter, System default, Segoe UI, Roboto) | `appearance.uiFont.family` | Inter |
| UI font size (10–20) | `appearance.uiFont.size` | 13 |
| Compact mode | `appearance.compactMode` | off |
| Main menu (Hamburger menu, Merged with main toolbar, Show in separate toolbar) — see [Main menu](docs/guide/user/workbench.md#main-menu) | `appearance.mainMenu` | Hamburger menu |
| Window controls | `appearance.windowControls` | Match the system |

| Always select opened file (Project view) | `projectView.autoscrollFromSource` | off |
| Autoscroll to source / from source (Structure view) | `structureView.autoscrollToSource`, `structureView.autoscrollFromSource` | on |

Editor fonts are under Settings | Editor | Font: JetBrains Mono (default), Fira Code, Cascadia
Code, Source Code Pro, Menlo, Consolas or the system monospace font, size (13.5), line height

### Window controls

Forge draws its own title bars. **Window controls** chooses how their buttons look:

| Value | Look |
| --- | --- |
| `auto` — Match the system | detected from the OS and desktop (`XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP`, `DESKTOP_SESSION`, `KDE_FULL_SESSION`, …), including the button order of GNOME (`button-layout`) and KDE (`kwinrc`) |
| `windows` | Windows 11 buttons on the right |
| `macos` | traffic lights on the left |
| `gnome` | GNOME/Adwaita round buttons |
| `kde` | KDE Plasma (Breeze) buttons |
| `linux` | generic Linux buttons |
| `native` | the operating system draws the title bar (Forge's toolbar is then below it) |

| | | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![Windows](docs/screenshots/titlebar-windows.png) | ![macOS](docs/screenshots/titlebar-macos.png) | ![GNOME](docs/screenshots/titlebar-gnome.png) |
| ![KDE](docs/screenshots/titlebar-kde.png) | ![Linux](docs/screenshots/titlebar-linux.png) | ![GNOME light](docs/screenshots/titlebar-gnome-light.png) |

Sources and Drivers) open as their own windows with the same style:

## System Settings

![System Settings](docs/screenshots/settings-system.png)

Settings | Appearance & Behavior | System Settings:

| Option | Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Reopen projects on startup | `system.reopenLastProject` | Forge starts with the last local project |
| Confirm before exiting the IDE | `system.confirmExit` | closing the main window (or File \| Exit) asks "Are you sure you want to exit Forge?"; **Do not ask me again** turns it off. Open files are saved on exit. |
| Default project directory | `system.defaultProjectDirectory` | where New Project creates projects |
| Save files if the IDE is switched to a different application | `system.autosave.onFrameDeactivation` | saves all modified files when Forge loses the focus |
| Save files if the IDE is idle, idle time | `system.autosave.onIdle`, `system.autosave.idleSeconds` | saves after that many seconds without typing or clicking |
| Synchronize external changes when switching to the IDE window | `system.syncExternalChanges` | re-reads open files changed on disk and refreshes the Project view and Git status |

Every option in the Settings dialog applies; the [settings reference](docs/guide/reference/settings.md)
lists them all.

# Accessibility

Forge follows PHPStorm: every part of the window works with the keyboard alone, the workbench
carries the names and states screen readers need, two High Contrast themes meet WCAG AAA, and
the Presentation Assistant shows which action you just invoked. The options are in
Settings | Appearance & Behavior | Appearance, sections **Accessibility** and
**Presentation Assistant**.

## Screen readers

Forge's window is a web view, so it works with the screen reader of your system: NVDA or JAWS
on Windows, VoiceOver on macOS and Orca on Linux.

What a screen reader finds without any setting:

| Part | Role and what is read |
| --- | --- |
| Main toolbar, tool window bars, editor, status bar | landmarks with names ("Left tool window bar", "Status bar") |
| Tool window buttons | name, shortcut (`Alt+1`) and whether the window is shown (pressed) |
| Tool windows | regions named after the window ("Project", "Commit") |
| Project, Structure, Commit and Settings trees | trees with level, expanded and selected state; file names include their Git status ("User.php, modified") |
| Editor tabs | tab list; the active tab is selected, a changed file says "modified" |
| Editor | a text box named "Editor for *file*"; CodeMirror reads the line at the caret |
| Search Everywhere, Find Action, Go to File, Switcher, Choose Declaration | a search field with a list of results; the selected result is read as you move |
| Main menu and context menus | menus with items, submenus (expanded or not), check marks and disabled items |
| Dialogs | dialogs named after their title; focus stays inside until they close and then returns where it was |
| Settings | every field has its label and its description |
| Balloons and notifications | read as they appear; errors interrupt |

**Support screen readers** (`appearance.screenReader`) turns on extra announcements:

- the name of the active file when you switch tabs;
- the problems on a line when the caret moves onto it.

**Announce Caret Position** (`Alt+Shift+L`, View menu and Find Action) reads the line and
column of the caret and the problems there ("Line 12, column 5. Error: Undefined variable
$user."), with or without the setting.

## High Contrast themes

Settings | Appearance & Behavior | Appearance | **Theme**: **High Contrast** (`high-contrast`,
white on black) and **High Contrast Light** (`high-contrast-light`, black on white).

- All text reaches at least 7:1 contrast (WCAG AAA), secondary text and hints included.
- Panels, popups, dialogs, inputs and buttons have visible borders; the focus ring is 3 pixels
  wide.
- States do not rely on color alone: selected rows are outlined, the active tab is underlined
  and bold, pressed tool window buttons are framed, modified / added / unversioned files are
  underlined dotted / solid / dashed, error and warning balloons have a colored edge and an icon.
- The editor follows with the **High Contrast** and **High Contrast Light** color schemes
  (keywords bold); see [Color schemes](docs/guide/user/color-schemes.md).

The sun/moon button switches between the two High Contrast themes.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| ![High Contrast](docs/screenshots/a11y-high-contrast-dark.png) | ![High Contrast Light](docs/screenshots/a11y-high-contrast-light.png) |

**Use contrast scrollbars** (`appearance.contrastScrollbars`) draws wider scrollbars in a strong
color, in every theme.

The Forge Ember and Anvil themes meet WCAG AA (4.5:1) for text. The Solarized themes meet it
for normal text but keep the fixed Solarized palette for syntax, file status and accent colors,
some of which stay below 4.5:1; use a Forge or High Contrast theme if you need them readable.

## Keyboard-only use

Everything can be reached without a mouse. The keys are PHPStorm's and can be changed in
Settings | Keymap.

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Alt+1` … `Alt+9` (macOS `Cmd+1` …) | show a tool window and move focus into it (its tree or list); again hides it |
| `Escape` (in a tool window) | **Focus Editor**: back to the editor, the window stays open |
| `Shift+Escape` | **Hide Active Tool Window** |
| `F12` | **Jump to Last Tool Window** |
| `Ctrl+Tab` | **Switcher**: tool windows and recent files; keep `Ctrl` down, press `Tab` to move, release to open |
| `Ctrl+Shift+F6` / `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+F6` | **Focus Next Area** / **Focus Previous Area**: main toolbar, navigation bar, tool window bars, tool windows, editor, status bar; each area remembers where focus was |
| `Alt+Home` (macOS `Cmd+Up`) | **Jump to Navigation Bar** |
| `Alt+\` | main menu |
| `ContextMenu` (the menu key) | context menu of the focused item |
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | next / previous control; in a dialog, focus wraps around inside it |

In trees (Project, Structure, Commit, Settings) the arrow keys move and expand, `Home` / `End`
jump, `Enter` (or `F4`) opens; in the Commit tree `Space` includes or excludes a file. In the
editor tab bar the left and right arrows switch tabs and `Enter` returns to the editor; tabs
close with `Ctrl+F4`.

Keyboard focus is always visible: a ring in the accent color around the focused control, or
around the selected row of a focused tree or list. Clicking with the mouse does not show it.

![Focus ring on a tool window button](docs/screenshots/a11y-focus-rings.png)

## Presentation Assistant

The Presentation Assistant shows the name and shortcut of every action you invoke (from the
keyboard, a menu, Find Action or a toolbar button), for demos, screencasts and pair
programming. Turn it on in Settings | Appearance & Behavior | Appearance | Presentation
Assistant, or with View | Appearance | **Presentation Assistant**.

| Setting | Key | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Show Presentation Assistant | `appearance.presentationAssistant.enabled` | off |
| Popup size: Small, Medium, Large | `appearance.presentationAssistant.size` | Medium |
| Position: top or bottom; left, center or right | `appearance.presentationAssistant.position` | bottom center |
| Duration (ms) | `appearance.presentationAssistant.duration` | 4000 |
| Show alternate keymap | `appearance.presentationAssistant.alternateKeymap` | on |

With **Show alternate keymap**, the popup also shows the shortcut of the other PHPStorm keymap:
the macOS shortcut while you use the Windows/Linux keymap, and the other way round.

![Presentation Assistant](docs/screenshots/a11y-presentation-assistant.png)

- [Keymap](docs/guide/user/keymap.md): change any of the shortcuts above.
- [Settings and themes](docs/guide/user/settings-and-themes.md): all themes and appearance options.

# Invalidate Caches and Repair IDE

When search results, completion or the Project view no longer match the files on disk, Forge
offers the same tools as PHPStorm, from the gentlest to the most thorough.

## Reload All from Disk

File | **Reload All from Disk** (`Ctrl+Alt+Y`, macOS `Cmd+Alt+Y`) re-reads the open files that
changed on disk and refreshes the Project view and the Git status. Forge does this on its own
when you switch back to its window (Settings | Appearance & Behavior | System Settings |
Synchronize external changes).

## Repair IDE

File | **Repair IDE** runs PHPStorm's repair steps one after another. After each step a balloon
says what was done and offers the next step:

1. **Refresh project files**: as Reload All from Disk, for every folder the Project view shows.
2. **Rescan project indexes**: brings the search index in line with the disk and rescans the
   PHP index (and the Lua index in Lua projects).
3. **Reopen project**: closes the project and opens it again (editor tabs are closed).
4. **Invalidate caches and restart**: opens the [Invalidate Caches](#invalidate-caches) dialog.

![Repair IDE balloon](docs/screenshots/repair-ide-balloon.png)

In the balloon, the first link runs the next step, **Everything Works Now** ends the repair, and
**More…** lets you pick any of the remaining steps.

## Invalidate Caches

File | **Invalidate Caches…** clears Forge's indexes and caches. The files are deleted on the
next start, before Forge opens any of them, so nothing is locked; the caches are rebuilt
afterwards.

![Invalidate Caches](docs/screenshots/invalidate-caches.png)

Always cleared: the PHP index, the search index, the command line tools cache, downloaded JSON
schemas, the Packagist cache and the terminal's shell integration scripts.

Optional:

| Option | What is deleted |
| --- | --- |
| Clear file system cache and Local History | the [Local History](docs/guide/user/local-history.md) of all projects |
| Clear downloaded shared indexes | the PHP stubs downloaded for the PHP index (downloaded again when needed) |
| Delete embedded browser engine cache | the cache of the webview that draws Forge's window |
| Delete language server data | php-lsp's index cache, Intelephense data left by earlier versions and the Java language server's workspaces |

**Invalidate and Restart** schedules the cleanup and restarts Forge; **Just Restart** only
restarts; **Cancel** does nothing.

> **Note:** installed language servers, Node.js runtimes, settings, bookmarks, changelists and
> shelved changes are no caches and are never deleted. Where each cache lives is listed in
> [File locations](docs/guide/reference/file-locations.md#caches--cache-dirforge).

In browser mode (`pnpm dev`) the dialog works, but nothing is deleted and Forge does not
restart.

## On the Welcome screen

The gear at the bottom of the Welcome screen offers Settings, Settings for New Projects,
Import / Export Settings, Restore Default Settings and Invalidate Caches, so you can repair
Forge without opening a project.

![Welcome screen menu](docs/screenshots/welcome-manage-settings.png)


---

Source: docs/guide/user/plugins-and-packs.md

# Plugins and packs

Everything in Forge beyond the workbench is a **plugin**. Plugins are grouped in **packs**:

| Pack | Plugins |
| --- | --- |
| **Core** | Forge Platform (required), Git, GitLab/Forgejo/GitHub, Terminal, Run/Debug, Database Tools and SQL, Docker and Kubernetes, Language Servers, AI Assistant, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Browser Companion |
| **PHPForge** | PHP, Composer, PHPUnit, Xdebug, Laravel, Symfony, Symfony Services, Doctrine |
| **WebForge** | HTML, CSS & JavaScript, React, Vue.js, Angular |
| **LuaForge** | Lua |
| **PyForge** | Python: interpreters, packages, requirements inspections |
| **GoForge** | Go: SDK and GOPATH, modules, gofmt / goimports, go vet, golangci-lint, Go Build / Go Test, Delve, Profiler |
| **RubyForge** | Ruby: interpreters of rbenv, rvm, chruby, asdf and mise, Bundler, Rake, Ruby / Rake run configurations, RSpec and Minitest, rdbg, RuboCop, Ruby LSP, ERB, the IRB console |
| **RustForge** | Rust: rustup toolchains, the Cargo tool window, Cargo and Cargo Test configurations (nextest, doctests, coverage), Clippy, rustfmt, rust-analyzer, LLDB / GDB with Rust type renderers |
| **JavaForge** | Java (Maven, Gradle, JUnit, TestNG, the Java debugger), Groovy, Scala with sbt, Android |
| **CForge** | C and C++ (clangd, toolchains, CMake, CTest / GoogleTest / Catch2, LLDB / GDB) |
| **DotNetForge** | .NET: C#, F# and Visual Basic (SDKs, solutions and MSBuild projects, the Build and NuGet tool windows, dotnet run / watch with launch profiles, xUnit / NUnit / MSTest, netcoredbg, dotnet new, dotnet format, the Roslyn language server) |
| **KotlinForge** | Kotlin (kotlin-lsp, Kotest, coroutines debugging, ktlint, detekt) |
| **ScriptForge** / **ConfigForge** | Bash, Python / YAML, JSON, .env, Ignore Files, Docker files, Postfix, E-Mail, INI, Config Files |

The packs are built in; there is no separate download. Third-party plugins can be added from
the [Marketplace](#marketplace) or a `.forgeplugin` file (see [Third-party plugins](#third-party-plugins)).

## When plugins are active

A plugin is active when it is **enabled** and the open project **uses** it. Plugins may declare
project types (a language, framework, pack or tool id); without project types they are always
active. For example Laravel needs `laravel`, PHPUnit needs `phpunit` or `pest`, React needs
`react` or `next`. See [Project type detection](docs/guide/getting-started/project-detection.md) and
the full list in [Reference: plugins](docs/guide/reference/plugins.md).

Inactive plugins hide their tool windows, status bar widgets and editor features, and their file
types fall back to the bundled ones (in a non-Symfony project `config/services.yaml` is plain
YAML).

## Settings | Plugins

![Plugins](docs/screenshots/settings-plugins.png)

The **Installed** tab lists all plugins grouped by pack, with a search field and a details pane
(description, version, vendor, dependencies). The checkbox enables or disables a plugin;
**Forge Platform** is required and cannot be disabled. Dependent plugins follow: disabling PHP
also disables Laravel, Symfony, Doctrine, Composer, PHPUnit and Xdebug.

Disabled plugins are remembered in the user settings (`plugins.disabled`, a list of plugin ids).

## Third-party plugins

Plugins from other publishers are installed from the **Marketplace** tab or with the gear menu
⚙ | **Install Plugin from Disk…** (a `.forgeplugin` file). They are listed under
**Downloaded** on the Installed tab, where you can enable, disable and **Uninstall** them.

![Plugin permissions](docs/screenshots/plugins-permission-prompt.png)

Before a plugin is installed or updated, Forge shows what it may do, most sensitive first:

| Permission | Means |
| --- | --- |
| Start programs | run the named programs (for example `git`) in the project folder |
| Write files | write in the open project or only in the plugin's own data folder |
| Connect to the internet | send requests to the named hosts only |
| Edit the open file | change the text of the active editor |
| Read files | read the open project (or a folder of it) or its own data folder |
| Read and change IDE settings | the named settings; a plugin's own settings need no permission |
| Read the open file | text, selection and file name of the active editor |

An update that asks for more marks the new permissions. Forge enforces them: the plugin's code
runs in a sandbox and every request outside of it is checked. Plugins never load native code.

Third-party plugins live in Forge's data folder (`<data dir>/forge/plugins`, their data in
`<data dir>/forge/plugin-data`), never in a project. In [Safe Mode](docs/guide/user/project-trust.md) plugins
that may start programs or write project files are not loaded, and no plugin may start
programs or write project files.

## Marketplace

![Marketplace](docs/screenshots/plugins-marketplace.png)

The Marketplace tab reads a plugin index from the URL set with ⚙ | **Marketplace URL…**
(setting `plugins.marketplace.url`). It lists the plugins with search, details, permissions,
**Install** and **Update**; ⚙ | **Check for Updates** reports installed plugins with newer
versions. Every download is checked against the SHA-256 checksum in the index. With trusted
publisher keys (setting `plugins.marketplace.trustedKeys`, base64 Ed25519 public keys) a
valid signature from one of them is required as well.

> **Note:** no public Forge marketplace is live yet. The default URL
> `https://plugins.forge.example/index.json` is a placeholder, so the tab says that no
> marketplace is configured until you enter the URL of an index, for example one your team
> hosts. The index format is described in [Publishing plugins](docs/guide/developer/plugins/publishing.md).

To write a plugin, see the [plugin SDK](docs/guide/developer/plugins/index.md).
