# Project trust and Safe Mode

A project can contain code that runs as soon as an IDE touches it: Composer and npm scripts,
run configurations, test suites, build files, language servers or linters installed in
`node_modules` or `vendor`. Like PHPStorm, Forge asks before it opens a project you have not
trusted yet, and opens untrusted projects in **Safe Mode**, where none of their code runs.

## Trust and Open Project?

When you open a folder that is not trusted (Open…, a recent project, `forge path`, Get from
VCS, the Browser Companion), Forge asks first:

![Trust and Open Project dialog](docs/screenshots/trust-open-project.png)

- **Trust Project** opens the project normally and remembers the decision.
- **Preview in Safe Mode** opens it in Safe Mode: you can browse, search and edit the files,
  but nothing of the project runs. You can trust it later from the banner.
- **Don't Open** leaves the current project (or the Welcome screen) as it was.
- **Trust projects in `<parent folder>`** also trusts every project in the folder that
  contains this one (a *trusted location*), for example `~/Projects`. The option is missing
  when the parent is a file system root.

Projects Forge creates itself (File | **New Project…**) are trusted automatically. Reopening
the open project (Repair IDE) does not ask again.

A project passed on the command line while Forge starts (`forge path`) opens right away; when it
is not trusted it opens in Safe Mode and shows the banner.

## Safe Mode

While the project is in Safe Mode, the editor area shows a banner:

![Safe Mode banner](docs/screenshots/safe-mode-banner.png)

Click **Trust Project…** in the banner (or run *Trust Project…* through Find Action,
`Ctrl+Shift+A`) to trust it. The dialog offers the same "Trust projects in …" option:

![Trust Project dialog from the banner](docs/screenshots/safe-mode-trust-dialog.png)

After trusting, everything below is available at once; language servers that were held back
start on the next file you open.

### What does not run in Safe Mode

Forge's backend refuses these commands with an error that names the action, so they stay
blocked even if a plugin or the UI tries to start them:

| Feature | In Safe Mode |
| --- | --- |
| Run/Debug configurations, Before launch tasks, Run Anything, External Tools | not started (every run goes through one place in the backend) |
| Composer and npm scripts, Artisan, Symfony console, Command Line Tool Support | not started; the Run Command popup lists only the built-in Artisan and Symfony commands |
| Test runners (PHPUnit, Pest, Codeception, Behat, PHPSpec, Vitest, Jest, RSpec, Minitest) | not started |
| Xdebug: Start Listening, PHP Web Page | refused |
| Composer: Show Outdated, Audit | refused (Composer loads the project's plugins) |
| [Vulnerable dependency check](docs/guide/user/vulnerable-dependencies.md) (composer audit, npm / pnpm / yarn audit, pip-audit, cargo audit, govulncheck) | refused, also on project open (the tools load the project's plugins or run its Python environment) |
| Laravel routes | parsed from the route files instead of `php artisan route:list` |
| Docker Compose up and Dockerfile ▶ in the gutter, Compose **Up** in Services | refused |
| PHP interpreters: version and `phpinfo()` of an interpreter inside the project or a Docker Compose service | refused |
| Language servers installed in the project (`node_modules/.bin`, `vendor/bin`, …) | not started |
| ESLint, Tailwind CSS, rust-analyzer, Ruby LSP, Java, Kotlin, Scala (Metals) and C# language servers | not started (they load the project's config files or build scripts) |
| Gradle / Maven sync, Reload sbt Project | refused (the build definition is project code) |
| Groovy scripts, sbt tasks, Android App runs (build, `adb install`, launch) | not started (they are run configurations) |
| Actions on Save: Biome, ESLint, Stylelint, Prettier, Rector, PHP CS Fixer, phpcbf, Laravel Pint | not run |
| Web code quality tools (ESLint, Prettier, Stylelint, Biome): checks, fixes, Reformat with Prettier, Inspect Code, Validate | refused (Reformat Code uses the usual formatter) |
| PHP quality tools (PHPStan, Psalm, phpcs, PHP Mess Detector, PHP CS Fixer, Pint, Rector): checks, Reformat with …, Inspect Code, Validate | refused |
| StyLua installed in the project | not run |
| Ruby: Rake task loading, RuboCop checks and autocorrect, the IRB console | Rake tasks are read from the Rakefile instead of `rake --tasks`; RuboCop is not run (Reformat Code does nothing); IRB is refused |
| AI agents (Claude Code, Gemini CLI) | not started (they run the project's hooks and MCP servers) |
| Deployment: automatic upload on save | off (the servers and the option come from the project's own files) |
| SSH session to a deployment server (Tools \| Start SSH Session…) | asks first: the server comes from the project's files; your own SSH configurations connect without asking |

What still works: the editor, the Project view, search, the PHP and Lua indexes, Go to
Declaration, completion from the built-in analysis, language servers installed outside the
project (for example a server from npm or Forge's own install), Git, Local History,
databases, the HTTP client and [Deployment](docs/guide/user/deployment.md) actions you start yourself (upload,
download, compare and sync only copy files), and the [Remote Host](docs/guide/user/remote-host-and-ssh.md)
tool window with Edit Remote File.

The **terminal** opens in Safe Mode, because you type the commands yourself. The project's own
settings (`.forge/settings.toml`) cannot choose its shell or environment variables then; your
user settings are used.

> **Note:** Git runs in Safe Mode, like in PHPStorm. Git itself can run programs a repository
> configures in `.git/config` (for example `core.fsmonitor`); Forge does not change that.

## Trusted Locations

Settings | Build, Execution, Deployment | **Trusted Locations** lists the folders whose
projects open without asking, and the projects you trusted one by one:

![Trusted Locations settings page](docs/screenshots/trusted-locations.png)

- **+** adds a folder (`~` is your home folder). Every project inside it, at any depth, is
  trusted. A whole drive or `/` cannot be added.
- **−** removes the selected entry. When nothing trusts the open project any more, it goes
  back to Safe Mode right away.

Changes are saved immediately. Trust decisions are stored in
`<config dir>/forge/trusted-projects.toml` (see [File locations](docs/guide/reference/file-locations.md)),
never in the project and never in the settings files: a project's own `.forge/settings.toml`
cannot trust itself.

## Remote projects

Remote projects (Welcome | Remote Development) use the same rules: the project on the host is
trusted by itself or by a trusted location on the **same host, user and port**, stored as
`user@host:/path`. Because the folder on the host is only known after connecting, Forge opens
an untrusted remote project in Safe Mode first and then asks. **Don't Open** closes the project
and the connection again; nothing of it ran in the meantime. Trusted locations on this machine
never cover remote projects, and the other way round.

Dev containers are built from a folder on this machine, so the **local folder's** trust counts:
Forge asks before the image build and `postCreateCommand` (they run the project's code), refuses
both for an untrusted folder, and the project in the container is trusted with its sources. A
WSL project is trusted by its `\\wsl.localhost\<distro>\…` path. See
[Dev Containers and WSL](docs/guide/user/dev-containers-and-wsl.md).

A [Code With Me](docs/guide/user/code-with-me.md#joining-a-session) guest's window is always in Safe Mode, but
shows no banner and offers no **Trust Project…**: the host's project is not on this machine and
nothing of it runs here. Its trust is the host's decision. Leaving the session ends Safe Mode
with the project.

## Browser mode

The demo projects of browser mode live in `~/Projects`, a trusted location, so they open
normally. Opening any other folder (for example `~/Downloads/legacy-crm` from a screenshot
scenario) shows the dialog, and the run mocks refuse like the desktop app does in Safe Mode.


---

Source: docs/guide/user/run-debug.md

# Run/Debug configurations

A **run configuration** describes how to start something: a script, a test suite, a command.
Forge's configurations work like PHPStorm's.

> **Note:** nothing runs while the project is in Safe Mode (not trusted yet); trust it with
> **Trust Project…** in the banner, see [Project trust and Safe Mode](docs/guide/user/project-trust.md).

## Run widget

The run widget in the main toolbar shows the selected configuration with **Run** (▶) and
**Debug** (🐞) buttons. Its dropdown lists all configurations and has **Edit
Configurations…**; without configurations it reads **Add Configuration…**.

![Run widget](docs/screenshots/run-toolbar-dropdown.png)

| Action | Windows/Linux | macOS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Run the selected configuration | `Shift+F10` | `Ctrl+R` |
| Debug the selected configuration | `Shift+F9` | `Ctrl+D` |
| Run… (choose a configuration) | `Alt+Shift+F10` | `Ctrl+Alt+R` |
| Debug… (choose a configuration) | `Alt+Shift+F9` | `Ctrl+Alt+D` |
| Run Context Configuration (the test, script or Lua chunk at the caret) | `Ctrl+Shift+F10` | `Ctrl+Shift+R` |
| Debug Context Configuration | `Ctrl+Shift+F9` | `Ctrl+Shift+D` |
| Stop | `Ctrl+F2` | `Cmd+F2` |
| Rerun | `Ctrl+F5` | `Cmd+R` |
| Edit Configurations… | Find Action | |
| [Run Anything](#run-anything) | `Double Ctrl` | `Double Ctrl` |

In the **Run…** chooser, `Enter` runs and `Shift+Enter` (or holding `Shift`) debugs; it also
offers **Run Shell Command…** and **Edit Configuration…**.

## Run Anything

Press `Ctrl` twice (Tools | Run Anything…) to run almost anything from one popup:

![Run Anything](docs/screenshots/run-anything.png)

- **Recent**: what you ran from Run Anything in this project (kept outside the project, in
  Forge's state directory).
- **Run configurations**: run (or debug) a saved or temporary configuration by name.
- **npm scripts** of every `package.json` with the detected package manager (`pnpm run dev`),
  **Composer scripts** of `composer.json` (`composer test`).
- **PHP files**: type `php ` and part of a file name (`php User`).
- **Composer**, **Artisan** and **Symfony console commands** of
  [Command Line Tool Support](docs/guide/user/command-line-tools.md) (Symfony projects without it use the
  Symfony index);
  other plugins add their commands with `registerRunAnythingProvider`.
- **Commands**: anything else you type runs as a command in the project directory, in the Run
  tool window. When no suggestion starts with what you typed, the command itself is the first
  entry.

![Suggestions for "php art"](docs/screenshots/run-anything-query.png)

`Enter` runs the selected entry. Hold **Shift** to switch to **Debug Anything**: `Shift+Enter`
debugs it (Xdebug for PHP, `--inspect` for npm). Type `?` for help on what can be typed; picking
a help entry fills in its prefix.

![Debug Anything](docs/screenshots/run-anything-debug.png)

Typed commands become [temporary configurations](#temporary-configurations) of the matching
type, so they run like configurations:

| You type | Runs as |
| --- | --- |
| `php [options] script.php [args]` | PHP Script through the project's [CLI interpreter](docs/guide/user/php.md#cli-interpreters) (Docker, SSH, WSL included) |
| `php artisan <command>` | Artisan |
| `composer <command>` | Composer command (`composer` with `php.composer.executable`) |
| `npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn`, `bun` `run <script> [-- args]` or any other command | npm (`npm install lodash`, `yarn add x`) |
| anything else | Shell Script (`/bin/sh -c "<command>"`, `cmd.exe /C` on Windows) in the project directory |

## Run/Debug Configurations dialog

![Run/Debug Configurations](docs/screenshots/run-configurations-dialog.png)

- **+** (`Alt+Insert`) adds a configuration from a type; copy, remove and reorder with the
  toolbar. **Edit configuration templates…** sets the defaults for new configurations of a
  type.
- Common fields: **Name**, **Store as project file**, the type's own fields, **Interpreter**
  and **Interpreter options** (PHP and Lua types), **Arguments**, **Working directory**
  (default: the project root), **Environment variables** and [Before launch](#before-launch)
  tasks.
- **Run on** runs the configuration (runs, tests, coverage and debug runs) on the local
  machine, in a Docker image, a Docker Compose service, over SSH, in WSL or in a Dev
  Container, see [Run targets](docs/guide/user/run-targets.md).
- The **Command Line** preview shows exactly what will run.

### Configuration types

| Type | Fields | Runs | Debug |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PHP Script | File | `<php> <options> <file> <arguments>` | Xdebug |
| PHP Built-in Web Server | Host (`localhost`), Port (`8080`), Document root, Use router script, Open in browser after launch | `<php> <options> -S host:port -t <document root> [router]`, then opens `http://host:port/` | Xdebug for every request |
| PHP Web Page | Server (Settings \| PHP \| Servers), Start URL | opens the page in the browser | adds `XDEBUG_SESSION_START=FORGE` |
| PHP HTTP Request | Server (optional), URL, Request method, Headers, Request body | sends the request, the response appears in the Run tool window | adds the `XDEBUG_SESSION` cookie |
| PHPUnit | Test scope: Directory, File, Class, Method or "Defined in the configuration file"; Configuration file (`phpunit.xml` detected); Test runner options | `phpunit --teamcity …` (from `vendor/bin`, or as set in [Settings \| PHP \| Test Frameworks](docs/guide/user/test-frameworks.md#settings--php--test-frameworks)) | Xdebug |
| Pest, Codeception, Behat, PHPSpec | see [PHP test frameworks](docs/guide/user/test-frameworks.md#run-configurations) | `pest --teamcity …`, `codecept run …`, `behat …`, `phpspec run …` | Xdebug |
| Artisan | Command (`migrate --seed`) | `<php> artisan <command>` | Xdebug |
| Composer Script | Script | `composer run <script>` with `php.composer.executable` | Xdebug |
| npm | package.json, Command (`run`, `install`, …), Scripts, Package manager | `npm`/`pnpm`/`yarn`/`bun` | sets `NODE_OPTIONS=--inspect` |
| Shell Script | Execute: Script file or Script text; Script path / text | the shell | — |
| Lua Script | File | `<lua> <options> <file> <arguments>`, LÖVE games as `love <dir>` | — |
| Native Application | Executable, Debugger (LLDB, GDB or a pack's adapter), Stop at the beginning of the program, Launch options (JSON) | `<executable> <program arguments>` | the chosen [debug adapter](docs/guide/user/debugging.md#debug-adapter-sessions) |
| Compound | Configurations, Allow multiple instances | starts every configuration, each in its own Run tab | debugs every member |

The PHP interpreter defaults to the project's CLI interpreter (`php.interpreter`, Settings |
Languages & Frameworks | PHP), the Lua interpreter to `lua.interpreter`. The **Interpreter**
field of PHP Script, PHPUnit and Artisan configurations lists the project default, every
[CLI interpreter](docs/guide/user/php.md#cli-interpreters) and **Custom…** (a path to a local `php`):

![Interpreter of a run configuration](docs/screenshots/php-interpreters-run-config.png)

A Docker, Docker Compose, SSH or WSL interpreter wraps the command line: `docker run --rm …`,
`docker compose run/exec …`, `ssh user@host …` or `wsl.exe -d … --exec php …`, with paths in
the arguments and the working directory mapped into the container or host, the environment
variables passed along (`-e NAME=value`, `env NAME=value`) and the interpreter's
configuration options as `-d name=value`. Paths in the output (stack traces, PHPUnit
failures) are mapped back to project files, so they stay clickable in the Run console.
Composer Script and Composer command configurations run `composer` through an interpreter
when their Interpreter field names one; otherwise they use `php.composer.executable` locally.

![Artisan through a Docker Compose interpreter](docs/screenshots/php-interpreters-run.png)

Debugging (`Shift+F9`) through an interpreter works the same way: Xdebug connects to
`host.docker.internal` from containers (`docker run` adds
`--add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway`; Compose services on Linux need an
`extra_hosts: ["host.docker.internal:host-gateway"]` entry), SSH runs forward the debug port
back with `ssh -R 9003:127.0.0.1:9003`, and the run sets `PHP_IDE_CONFIG=serverName=<interpreter>`
so breakpoints use the interpreter's path mappings.

![PHP Built-in Web Server](docs/screenshots/run-builtin-server.png)

The built-in web server runs through the configuration's interpreter too: Docker and Compose
interpreters publish the port (`-p 8080:8080`, the server binds `0.0.0.0` inside the
container), SSH interpreters forward it (`ssh -L 8080:127.0.0.1:8080`), so the page opens on
`localhost` either way.

![PHP Web Page](docs/screenshots/run-web-page.png)

> **Note:** the type "PHP Remote Debug" is declared by the Xdebug plugin but not available yet.
> To debug requests started elsewhere, use
> [Start Listening for PHP Debug Connections](docs/guide/user/debugging.md#listening-for-connections).

### Compound configurations

A **Compound** configuration starts several configurations together, for example the Laravel
server and the Vite dev server. Add the configurations with **+** and order them with the
arrows; a compound may contain other compounds.

![Compound configuration](docs/screenshots/run-configurations-compound.png)

- **Run** starts every member (after its own Before launch tasks), each in its own tab of the
  Run tool window. **Debug** debugs each member that can be debugged.
- **Stop** (`Ctrl+F2` or the toolbar's ■ while the compound is selected) stops all members.
- Without **Allow multiple instances**, running the compound again restarts members that still
  run; with it, new instances start next to them.
- Missing members and cycles are reported before anything starts.

### Before launch

Every configuration (except compounds) can run tasks before it starts. They run one after
another in the listed order; when a task fails (exit code other than 0, a missing
configuration or tool), the launch stops and a balloon says which task failed.

![Before launch tasks](docs/screenshots/run-configurations-before-launch.png)

| Task (**+** menu) | Value | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Run External tool | a tool of [External Tools](#external-tools) | runs the tool and waits for it |
| Run Another Configuration | a configuration | runs it (with its own Before launch tasks) and waits for it; a compound runs each member |
| Launch Web Browser | a URL | opens the URL |
| Run npm script | a script name | `<package manager> run <script>` in the configuration's working directory |
| Run Composer script | a script or command | `composer <script>` |
| Run Artisan command | a command (Laravel projects) | `php artisan <command>` through the configuration's interpreter |
| Run Shell Command… | a command line | runs it with the shell |

Each task runs in its own tab of the Run tool window. Reorder tasks with **↑** / **↓**.

### Where configurations are stored

| | File |
| --- | --- |
| Shared ("Store as project file") | `<project>/.forge/runConfigurations.toml` — commit it to share with your team |
| Local configurations, the selected one, templates | `<project>/.forge/runConfigurations.local.toml` |

## Temporary configurations

Gutter ▶ icons create temporary configurations: tests of PHPUnit, Pest, Codeception, Behat and
PHPSpec ([PHP test frameworks](docs/guide/user/test-frameworks.md#gutter-icons)), `package.json` scripts, Lua
main chunks, scratch files and HTTP requests. A double-click in the npm tool window and
commands run from [Run Anything](#run-anything) do the same.

## External Tools

**Settings | Tools | External Tools** lists programs you start from Forge with arguments
that come from the current file, caret or selection, such as linters, formatters or deploy
scripts. Tools are kept in your user settings (`tools.externalTools`), so they exist in every
project.

![External Tools](docs/screenshots/external-tools-settings.png)

The toolbar adds (**+**), removes, edits (or double-click), copies and moves tools; the check
boxes of tools and groups hide them from menus and the keymap without deleting them.

**Create Tool / Edit Tool**:

![Edit Tool](docs/screenshots/external-tools-edit.png)

- **Name**, **Group** (the submenu it appears in; default "External Tools") and
  **Description**.
- **Program**, **Arguments** and **Working directory** (default `$ProjectFileDir$`). Each can
  contain macros; **Insert Macro…** lists them with a preview of their value for the current
  editor:

  ![Insert Macro](docs/screenshots/external-tools-macros.png)

  | Macro | Value |
  | --- | --- |
  | `$FilePath$`, `$FileDir$`, `$FileName$`, `$FileNameWithoutExtension$`, `$FileNameWithoutAllExtensions$`, `$FileExt$`, `$FileDirName$`, `$FileParentDir$` | the file in the editor, or the file the Project view menu was opened on |
  | `$FilePathRelativeToProjectRoot$`, `$FileDirRelativeToProjectRoot$`, `$FileRelativePath$`, `$FileRelativeDir$` | the same, relative to the project |
  | `$ProjectFileDir$`, `$ContentRoot$`, `$ProjectName$` | the project |
  | `$LineNumber$`, `$ColumnNumber$`, `$SelectedText$`, `$SelectionStartLine$`, `$SelectionEndLine$`, `$SelectionStartColumn$`, `$SelectionEndColumn$` | caret and selection (1-based) |
  | `$ClipboardContent$` | the clipboard text |
  | `$Prompt$` | asks for a value when the tool runs (once per occurrence) |
  | `$PhpExecutable$` | the project's PHP interpreter |
  | `$FileEncoding$`, `$OSName$`, `$UserHome$` | file encoding, operating system, home directory |

  Arguments are split like a shell command line before the macros are expanded, so a path with
  spaces stays one argument. A macro without a value here (`$FilePath$` with no file open) is
  replaced by nothing and reported in a balloon.
- **Advanced Options**: **Synchronize files after execution** (refreshes the Project view),
  **Open console for tool output** (without it the tool runs in the background), **Make console
  active on message in stdout / stderr** (the console appears with the first such message) and
  **Output filters**.
- **Output filters** turn tool output into links: one regular expression per line with
  `$FILE_PATH$`, `$LINE$` and `$COLUMN$`, e.g. `$FILE_PATH$:$LINE$` or
  `^$FILE_PATH$:$LINE$:` for PHPStan's raw format. Everything else is a regular expression
  (escape `(` as `\(`). Invalid filters are reported when you click OK.

  ![Invalid output filter](docs/screenshots/external-tools-light.png)

Run a tool from:

- **Tools | External Tools**, ![Tools | External Tools](docs/screenshots/external-tools-menu.png)
- the editor's context menu (a submenu per group) and the Project view's context menu (the
  macros then use the clicked file), ![Editor context menu](docs/screenshots/external-tools-editor-menu.png)
- a shortcut: each tool is the action `Tool_<group>_<name>` in Settings | Keymap and Find
  Action,
- a [Before launch](#before-launch) task.

The output appears in the Run tool window, with the output filters' matches as links; tools run
on the machine that hosts the project (remote projects included).

![PHPStan run with an output filter](docs/screenshots/external-tools-run.png)

## Run tool window

The **Run** tool window (`Alt+4`) has one tab per run. Tabs can be pinned and closed (`Ctrl+Shift+F4`).

- Output is shown with ANSI colors; `\r` progress lines update in place.
- File references (`app/User.php:42`, stack traces) and URLs are clickable.
- Toolbar: **Rerun**, **Stop**, **Soft-Wrap**, **Scroll to the End**, **Clear All**.
- Typing sends input to the process (stdin).
- Stop sends SIGTERM to the process group, then SIGKILL after 2 seconds (`taskkill /T` on
  Windows).

Settings | Editor | General | Console: **Use soft wraps in console** (`run.console.softWrap`)
and **Override console cycle buffer size (KB)** (`run.console.cycleBufferKb`, 1024): a console
keeps the newest output up to that size and drops the oldest lines.

## Analyze Stack Trace

**Code | Analyze Stack Trace or Thread Dump…** (`AnalyzeStacktraceOnError`, no default
shortcut) opens a dialog to paste a stack trace from a log file, a bug report, an error page or
a server. When the clipboard holds a trace, the dialog starts with it.

![Analyze Stack Trace dialog](docs/screenshots/analyze-stack-trace.png)

**Analyze** opens it in a **Stack Trace** tab of the Run tool window. Every frame that names a
project file is a link to its line; the exception message is red, frames in libraries
(`vendor/`, `node_modules/`) and files outside the project are dimmed. **Rerun** opens the
dialog again with the same text.

![Stack trace in the Run tool window](docs/screenshots/stack-trace-tab.png)

Recognized formats:

| Language | Frames |
| --- | --- |
| PHP | `#0 /var/www/app/User.php(12): …`, `… in /path/File.php:42`, `… on line 7`, Laravel and Symfony exception traces and logs, Xdebug's `0.0012 402456 1. {main}() /path/index.php:0` |
| JavaScript / Node | `at fn (/app/src/cart.ts:10:5)`, `at /app/src/x.js:3:1`, `file:///…`, `webpack:///./src/…` |
| Lua | `main.lua:12: attempt to …`, `lib/util.lua:4: in function 'load'` |
| Others | any `path:line[:column]` or `path(line)` |

A trace copied from a JSON log as one line with escaped line breaks (`\n#1 …`) is split into
lines first.

Paths of a server or container are mapped into the project:

1. the path mappings of the PHP servers (Settings | PHP | Servers,
   [Debugging](docs/guide/user/debugging.md)),
2. the bind mounts of the project's Docker Compose file (`./:/var/www/html`),
3. the project root,
4. otherwise the longest trailing part of the path that exists in the project
   (`/srv/app/releases/42/app/Models/Order.php` → `app/Models/Order.php`).

Files are looked up through the project's backend, so this works in
[remote projects](docs/guide/user/remote-development.md) too. Detecting traces copied to the clipboard outside
Forge automatically is not supported.

## Test results

Test runners of every pack show a **Test Results** tree next to the console: TeamCity service
messages (PHPUnit with `--teamcity`, Pest), JUnit reports (Codeception, Behat, PHPSpec), TAP
(busted) and the other formats of the shared [test runner](docs/guide/user/testing.md). **Run with Coverage**
shows which lines the tests ran, see [Code coverage](docs/guide/user/coverage.md).

![PHPUnit test tree](docs/screenshots/run-phpunit-tree.png)

- Pass/fail/ignored per test with durations; **Show Passed**, **Show Ignored**, **Sort
  Alphabetically**, **Sort by Duration**, **Expand/Collapse All**.
- **Previous/Next Failed Test** and **Rerun Failed Tests**.
- **Toggle Auto-Test** reruns the tests after files are saved, and **Test History** reopens the
  last test runs of the project, see [PHP test frameworks](docs/guide/user/test-frameworks.md#test-history).
- A failed assertion shows a **Comparison Failure** with Expected and Actual.
- Double-click a test to open it.

## Debugging

**Debug** on a PHP configuration (PHP Script, PHPUnit, Artisan, Composer, PHP Built-in Web
Server) starts Forge's Xdebug listener and runs the process with the Xdebug environment
(`XDEBUG_MODE=debug`, `XDEBUG_SESSION`, `XDEBUG_CONFIG`). **Debug** on PHP Web Page, PHP HTTP
Request and requests of `.http` files starts listening and adds the Xdebug trigger to the
request. See [Debugging](docs/guide/user/debugging.md#debugging-web-pages-and-http-requests).

**Debug** on a Native Application configuration, or on a configuration type whose language
pack registers a debug adapter, starts a [debug adapter session](docs/guide/user/debugging.md#debug-adapter-sessions).

> **Note:** Run/Debug configurations work in [remote projects](docs/guide/user/remote-development.md): the
> process runs on the remote host.


---

Source: docs/guide/user/testing.md

# Testing

Every pack runs its tests through the same test runner, so tests look and behave the same in
PHP, Lua and every language pack that follows:

- green ▶ **gutter icons** on test files, classes, `describe` blocks and single tests;
- a **run configuration type** per test framework (Run | Edit Configurations…);
- the **test tree** in the Run tool window with statuses, durations, output per test and
  **Click to see difference** for failed comparisons;
- **Rerun Failed Tests**, the **Test History**, **auto-test**;
- **Run with Coverage** ([Coverage](docs/guide/user/coverage.md)) and **Run on** a Docker image, a Docker
  Compose service, an SSH host, WSL or a Dev Container ([Run targets](docs/guide/user/run-targets.md)).

![A busted test run in the Lua demo](docs/screenshots/test-runner-busted.png)

## Test frameworks

| Framework | Pack | Results | Coverage |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PHPUnit, Pest, Codeception, Behat, PHPSpec | PHPForge ([PHP test frameworks](docs/guide/user/test-frameworks.md)) | TeamCity, JUnit XML | PHPUnit and Pest (Clover, Xdebug or PCOV) |
| busted | LuaForge ([LuaForge](docs/guide/user/luaforge.md#tests-with-busted)) | TAP | LCOV (luacov) |
| JUnit 5/4/3, TestNG | JavaForge ([JavaForge](docs/guide/user/java.md#tests)), through Gradle or Maven | JUnit XML of the build (`build/test-results/test`, `target/surefire-reports`) | JaCoCo XML |
| Spock | JavaForge ([Groovy and Scala](docs/guide/user/groovy-scala.md#spock)), through Gradle or Maven | JUnit XML of the build | JaCoCo XML |
| ScalaTest, MUnit | JavaForge ([Groovy and Scala](docs/guide/user/groovy-scala.md#scalatest-and-munit)), through sbt `testOnly` | JUnit XML of `target/test-reports` | — |
| Kotest, JUnit 5 in Kotlin | KotlinForge ([KotlinForge](docs/guide/user/kotlin.md#tests)), through Gradle or Maven | JUnit XML of the build | JaCoCo XML |
| Jest, Vitest, Mocha, Playwright, Cypress, `node --test` | WebForge ([JavaScript test runners](docs/guide/user/javascript-debugging.md#test-runners)) | Jest / Vitest JSON, TAP, Playwright JSON, JUnit XML | LCOV (Jest, Vitest, c8 for Mocha, Node's reporter) |
| GoogleTest, Catch2, CTest | CForge ([CForge](docs/guide/user/cpp.md#tests)), the CMake target's executable or `ctest` | JUnit XML (`--gtest_output=xml`, Catch2's JUnit reporter, `ctest --output-junit`) | LCOV from gcov or llvm-cov |
| pytest, unittest, tox | PyForge ([PyForge](docs/guide/user/python.md#testing-with-pytest-unittest-and-tox)) | JUnit XML or report log (pytest), TeamCity (Forge's unittest runner), environments as tests (tox) | pytest-cov (Cobertura) |

Language packs declare their frameworks in their plugin manifest
(`[[contributions.testFrameworks]]`, see [Contribution points](docs/guide/developer/contribution-points.md#test-frameworks));
the framework then appears everywhere on this page without further code.

A framework is used in a project when its files are there (`.busted`, `spec/*_spec.lua`) or a
project file names it (a rockspec that depends on busted). When several frameworks claim the
same files (Jest and Vitest both run `*.test.ts`), the gutter uses the one the project uses.

## Running tests

- **Gutter icons** — click the ▶ next to a test, a `describe` block, a class or the file:
  **Run '…'** (`Ctrl+Shift+F10`), **Run '…' with Coverage**, **Debug '…'** (`Shift+F9`) and
  **Modify Run Configuration…**. After a run the icon shows the test's last result (✓ or ✗).
- **Run Context Configuration** (`Ctrl+Shift+F10`) runs the test at the caret, else the whole
  test file.
- **Run configurations** — each framework is a configuration type. Manifest frameworks have a
  **Test scope**: *All tests*, *Directory*, *File*, *Test* (a test or a `describe` block by its
  full name) or *Pattern*, plus **Executable** (default: the framework's setting, e.g.
  `lua.busted.path`) and **Test runner options**.

![The gutter menu of a busted test](docs/screenshots/test-runner-gutter-menu.png)

## The test tree

The Run tool window (`Alt+4`) shows a test run as a tree next to the console, like PHPStorm:

- suites (files, classes, packages, `describe` blocks) with their tests; statuses (passed,
  failed, ignored, running) and durations; the status line "Tests failed: 1, passed: 3 of 4
  tests – 51 ms" with a progress bar;
- selecting a test shows its own output and failure; **Click to see difference** opens the
  expected and actual values in the diff viewer;
- double-click or `F4` jumps to the test (by line, else by its function, method, `it` / `test`
  call or scenario);
- **Show Passed** / **Show Ignored**, **Sort Alphabetically** / **by Duration**, **Expand /
  Collapse All**, **Previous / Next Failed Test**;
- **Rerun Failed Tests** runs only the failed tests (PHPUnit / Pest `--filter`, busted
  `--filter` per test, …), **Toggle Auto-Test** reruns the tab a few seconds after files are
  saved (`run.autoTest.delay`), the **Test History** reopens one of the last 10 runs.

## Result formats

Forge reads what the tools print; the parsers live in Rust (`forge-output`) and turn every
format into the same test events:

| Format | Tools | Arrives |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TeamCity service messages | PHPUnit `--teamcity`, Pest, Jest and Mocha TeamCity reporters | streamed on stdout |
| JUnit XML | Codeception, Behat, PHPSpec, PHPUnit `--log-junit`, pytest `--junitxml`, Gradle, Maven | a report file or a document on stdout |
| TAP 12–14 | busted `--output=TAP`, `node --test --test-reporter=tap`, prove, Bats, node-tap | streamed on stdout |
| Go `test2json` | `go test -json` | streamed on stdout |
| libtest JSON | `cargo test -- -Z unstable-options --format json` (nightly), nextest | streamed on stdout; cargo's `Running` lines on stderr name the suites |
| libtest plain text | `cargo test` on stable toolchains | streamed on stdout; failures are read from their `---- <test> stdout ----` sections |
| pytest report log | `pytest --report-log=…` | streamed on stdout or a report file |
| Jest / Vitest JSON | `jest --json`, `vitest run --reporter=json` | a document on stdout or a report file |
| Playwright JSON | `playwright test --reporter=json` (`PLAYWRIGHT_JSON_OUTPUT_NAME`) | a report file |
| RSpec JSON | `rspec --format progress --format json --out <file>` | a report file |
| Minitest verbose output | `ruby -Itest test/x_test.rb -v`, `rake test TESTOPTS=-v` | streamed on stdout; failures, errors and skips are read from the summary |

Failures keep their message, the failure location (a stack frame) and, where the tool reports
them, the expected and actual values: `Expected` / `Received` (Jest, Vitest), `got … want …`
(Go), `left` / `right` (Rust), `assert a == b` (pytest), `Passed in` / `Expected` (busted),
`expected: … got: …` (RSpec), `Expected:` / `Actual:` (Minitest).

## Safe Mode

Running tests runs the project's code: in [Safe Mode](docs/guide/user/project-trust.md) every test run,
coverage run and debug run is refused until the project is trusted.


---

Source: docs/guide/user/coverage.md

# Code coverage

**Run with Coverage** runs tests (or a Node.js program) and shows which lines they executed,
like PHPStorm:

![Coverage of the PHP demo](docs/screenshots/coverage-tool-window.png)

## Run with Coverage

- the gutter menu of a test: **Run '…' with Coverage**;
- **Run | Run with Coverage** for the selected configuration (action `Coverage`) and
  **Run Context Configuration with Coverage** (`RunCoverage`) for the test at the caret.

When the run ends, Forge reads the report, maps its paths into the project (container and
remote paths through the run's path mappings) and shows the suite. Coverage runs work on
every [run target](docs/guide/user/run-targets.md) and through every PHP CLI interpreter (Docker, Compose,
SSH, WSL): the report names the container's paths, Forge maps them back. In
[Safe Mode](docs/guide/user/project-trust.md) they are refused like every run.

## What works per language

| Language | Configurations | How Forge measures | Report | Branches | Methods | Tests per line |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PHP | PHPUnit, Pest | `--coverage-clover` with Xdebug or PCOV ([driver](#php-coverage-driver)); `--path-coverage` on request | Clover XML | Clover `cond` lines (not written by PHPUnit) | yes | yes, with **Track per-test coverage** (`--coverage-xml`) |
| PHP | Codeception | `run --coverage-xml=<file>` (Codeception's Clover); `coverage: enabled: true` in `codeception.yml` | Clover XML | — | yes | yes, with **Track per-test coverage** (`--coverage-phpunit=<dir>`) |
| PHP | Behat | [behat-code-coverage](https://github.com/dvdoug/behat-code-coverage) with a `clover` report in `behat.yml` | Clover XML | — | yes | — |
| PHP | PHPSpec | [phpspec-code-coverage](https://github.com/friends-of-phpspec/phpspec-code-coverage) with a `clover` output in `phpspec.yml` | Clover XML | — | yes | — |
| JavaScript / TypeScript | Vitest | `--coverage.enabled --coverage.reporter=json`; provider v8 or istanbul (configuration or **Coverage provider**) | Istanbul JSON | yes | yes | — |
| JavaScript / TypeScript | Jest | `--coverage --coverageReporters=json`; provider babel or v8 | Istanbul JSON | yes | yes | — |
| JavaScript / TypeScript | Mocha | runs under **c8** (default) or **nyc** (**Coverage tool**) | LCOV | yes | yes | — |
| JavaScript / TypeScript | Node.js Test Runner | `--experimental-test-coverage` with Node's LCOV reporter | LCOV | yes | yes | — |
| JavaScript / TypeScript | Node.js (a program) | runs under c8 or nyc (Code Coverage group) | LCOV | yes | yes | — |
| Python | pytest | pytest-cov (`--cov --cov-report=xml`) | Cobertura | with `--cov-branch` | — | — |
| Python | Unittests | coverage.py inside Forge's runner, branches on | Cobertura | yes | — | — |
| Java, Groovy | JUnit, TestNG, Spock | Gradle `jacocoTestReport` (XML report enabled) or Maven `jacoco:report`, when the build configures JaCoCo | JaCoCo XML | yes | yes | — |
| Kotlin | Kotest (JUnit as Java) | as Java (JaCoCo; Kover's XML report reads the same) | JaCoCo XML | yes | yes | — |
| Go | Go Test | `go test -coverprofile` | Go coverprofile | partly covered lines | — | — |
| Rust | Cargo Test | cargo-llvm-cov (`--lcov`) | LCOV | when branch coverage is on (nightly) | yes | — |
| C, C++ | GoogleTest, Catch2, CTest | gcov (GCC `--coverage`) or llvm-cov (Clang profiles) | LCOV | yes | yes | — |
| Lua | busted | `busted --coverage` with luacov and luacov-reporter-lcov (`.luacov`: `runreport = true`, `reporter = "lcov"`) | LCOV | — | — | — |

Not supported: Playwright and Cypress (browser tests), tox and Django test configurations,
.NET (there is no .NET pack yet). Per-test coverage needs a report that names the tests of
each line: PHPUnit's and Codeception's XML report, and LCOV tracefiles with test names
(`TN:`). JaCoCo sessions, coverage.py contexts and Istanbul reports do not carry it.

### PHP coverage driver

The **Code Coverage** group of a PHP test configuration (Run/Debug Configurations) chooses how
coverage is measured:

![The coverage driver of a PHPUnit configuration](docs/screenshots/coverage-driver.png)

| Option | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| **Coverage driver: Auto** | `XDEBUG_MODE=coverage`; php-code-coverage uses PCOV when it is enabled, else Xdebug |
| **Xdebug** | `-dxdebug.mode=coverage -dpcov.enabled=0` |
| **PCOV** | `-dpcov.enabled=1` and `XDEBUG_MODE=off` (PCOV is much faster, lines only) |
| **Branch and path coverage** (PHPUnit, Pest) | `--path-coverage` (PHPUnit 10+, Xdebug only). PHPUnit writes branches and paths to its HTML and XML reports; its Clover report, which Forge reads, keeps lines, so the gutter shows line coverage |
| **Track per-test coverage** (PHPUnit, Pest, Codeception) | also writes PHPUnit's XML report: Forge records the tests of every covered line |

Behat and PHPSpec have no coverage of their own: install their extension, add a Clover
report to its configuration, and Forge reads that file after the run:

```yaml
# behat.yml
default:
  extensions:
    DVDoug\Behat\CodeCoverage\Extension:
      filter:
        include:
          directories:
            'src': ~
      reports:
        clover:
          target: build/coverage-behat/clover.xml
```

```yaml
# phpspec.yml
extensions:
  FriendsOfPhpSpec\PhpSpec\CodeCoverage\CodeCoverageExtension:
    format: [clover]
    output:
      clover: build/coverage.xml
```

### JavaScript and TypeScript

Jest and Vitest write Istanbul's JSON report (`coverage-final.json`), which keeps every
statement, branch and function: a line is partly covered when a branch on it was not taken or
some statements on it did not run.

![Istanbul branch coverage of a Vitest run](docs/screenshots/coverage-istanbul.png)

The **Coverage provider** field of a Vitest (v8 / istanbul) or Jest (babel / v8)
configuration overrides the provider of the configuration file; the provider's package
(`@vitest/coverage-v8`, `@vitest/coverage-istanbul`) must be installed. Mocha and Node.js
configurations run under c8 (or nyc) from the project's `node_modules` (the `c8Package` /
`nycPackage` options name another one).

## Coverage tool window

**View | Tool Windows | Coverage** (on the right, shown once there is coverage data) lists the
directories and files of the suite:

| Column | Shows |
| --- | --- |
| Element | the project, folders (single-child folders compacted: `src/main/java`) and files |
| Method, % | called and total functions and methods (reports that name them) |
| Line, % | covered and total lines: `85% (17/20)` with a bar |
| Branch, % | taken and total branches (Clover conditions, Cobertura, LCOV, Istanbul, JaCoCo) |

Double-click a file to open it, a folder to collapse it. The toolbar **hides / shows** the
coverage in the editor and the Project view, **Show Coverage Data…** chooses suites,
**Import External Coverage Report…** reads a report, **Generate Coverage Report…** writes
HTML and **Close** drops the suite.

## Coverage in the editor and the Project view

While coverage is shown, the editor gutter marks every line of the report:

- green: the line ran (and all its branches were taken);
- yellow: the line ran, but some branches (or, in Go, some blocks on the line; with Istanbul,
  some statements) did not;
- red: the line never ran.

Hovering a mark shows the hits: "Hits: 3, branches: 1 of 2 covered", and with per-test
coverage the number of tests. **Clicking** such a mark lists the tests covering the line;
clicking a test searches for it (Search Everywhere).

![Tests covering a line](docs/screenshots/coverage-per-test.png)

The Project view shows "62% lines covered" next to covered files and
"50% files, 62% lines covered" next to folders, at every folder level.

![Coverage in the light theme](docs/screenshots/coverage-light.png)

## Show Coverage Data

**Run | Show Coverage Data…** (`Ctrl+Alt+F6`, action `SwitchCoverage`) opens **Choose Coverage
Suite to Display** with the session's last suites. Check one suite to show it, or several to
merge them into a new suite ("Unit + Feature"); **No Coverage** hides the marks.
**Run | Hide Coverage** (`HideCoverageInfo`) hides them as well.

![Choose Coverage Suite to Display](docs/screenshots/coverage-suites.png)

![A merged suite](docs/screenshots/coverage-merged.png)

**Import External Coverage Report…** (desktop app: a file dialog; the Project view: right-click
a report, **Show Coverage Data from This Report**) reads:

| Format | Written by |
| --- | --- |
| LCOV (`lcov.info`) | c8, Istanbul / nyc, Jest and Vitest `lcov`, luacov-reporter-lcov, grcov, cargo-llvm-cov |
| Cobertura XML | coverage.py `coverage xml`, Istanbul `cobertura`, cargo-llvm-cov, gcovr |
| Clover XML | PHPUnit `--coverage-clover`, Codeception, Istanbul `clover` |
| JaCoCo XML | JaCoCo, Kover |
| Go coverprofile | `go test -coverprofile` |
| Istanbul JSON (`coverage-final.json`) | Istanbul / nyc `json`, Jest, Vitest, c8 `json` |

The format is recognized from the content.

## Generate Coverage Report

**Run | Generate Coverage Report…** (`GenerateCoverageReport`, also in the Coverage tool
window's toolbar) writes the shown suite as one HTML file: the totals, the folders and files
with method, line and branch coverage, and each file's source with its covered, partly covered
and uncovered lines, hits and tests. The desktop app asks where to save it; in the browser it
is downloaded.

![The HTML coverage report](docs/screenshots/coverage-html-report.png)

# Run targets (Run on)

Like IntelliJ's run targets, every run configuration can **run on** another machine: the
configuration's runs, test runs, coverage runs and debug runs then execute there, while Forge
keeps the project, the test tree, the console links and the debugger local.

![Run on: Docker image](docs/screenshots/run-on-selector.png)

## Choosing a target

**Run | Edit Configurations…** → the configuration → **Run on**:

| Target | Fields | Runs as |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Local machine | — | the program itself |
| Docker image | Image, Docker run options, Project path on target (default `/opt/project`) | `docker run --rm -i -v <project>:<path> -w <dir> -e K=V <options> <image> <program> …` |
| Docker Compose service | Compose files, Service, Lifecycle (*Always start a new container* / *Connect to existing container*) | `docker compose -f … run --rm -T …` or `exec -T …` |
| SSH | Host, Port, User name, Private key file, Project path on target | `ssh -o BatchMode=yes … user@host "cd <dir> && env K=V <program> …"` |
| WSL | Distribution, User name | `wsl.exe -d <distribution> --cd <dir> --exec env K=V <program> …` |
| Dev Container | Container, User name, Project path in the container | `docker exec -i -u <user> -w <dir> -e K=V <container> <program> …` |

The configuration's **Working directory** and **Environment variables** apply on the target;
the target's own environment is added to every run. The Docker CLI is `docker.cliPath`
(Settings | Build, Execution, Deployment | Docker). The run configuration stores the target in
`runOn`, so a shared configuration (`.forge/runConfigurations.toml`) carries it for the team.

PHP configurations whose **CLI interpreter** is itself a Docker, Compose, SSH or WSL
interpreter run through that interpreter ([PHP](docs/guide/user/php.md#cli-interpreters)); the run target
applies to PHP configurations with a local interpreter and to every other configuration type.

## Path mappings

Forge maps paths both ways:

- the project folder and the working directory, and absolute project paths in the arguments,
  become paths on the target;
- paths in the output, test locations and coverage reports become project files again, so
  console links, the test tree's navigation and the [coverage](docs/guide/user/coverage.md) marks work;
- debuggers get the same pairs for breakpoints.

Automatic mappings: a Docker image mounts the project at its project path, a Compose service
uses the bind mounts of its `volumes`, WSL sees `C:\work\shop` as `/mnt/c/work/shop`, SSH hosts
and Dev Containers use their project path. **Path mappings** (`<project folder>=<path on
target>; …`) add your own; yours win for the same folder.

## Debugging on a target

Debug runs make the debugger's port reachable:

- debuggers that connect back to the IDE (Xdebug) reach it as `host.docker.internal` in
  containers (`--add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway`) and through a reverse tunnel
  (`ssh -R`) over SSH; PHP runs also get `PHP_IDE_CONFIG=serverName=<target>` and a debugger
  server with the target's path mappings;
- debuggers the IDE connects to (debug adapters listening in the program) get their port
  published (`-p`) or forwarded (`ssh -L`).

## Safe Mode

Runs on a target run the project's code like local runs: in [Safe Mode](docs/guide/user/project-trust.md)
they are refused until the project is trusted.


---

Source: docs/guide/user/test-frameworks.md

# PHP test frameworks

Forge runs the tests of PHPUnit, Pest, Codeception, Behat and PHPSpec projects the way
PHPStorm does: gutter ▶ icons on every test, a run configuration type per framework, the test
tree in the Run tool window with the results of each test, **Rerun Failed Tests**, the **Test
History** and **auto-test**. Every run goes through the project's
[CLI interpreter](docs/guide/user/php.md#cli-interpreters), so tests run locally, in Docker, Docker Compose,
over SSH or in WSL alike. The frameworks are part of the shared [test runner](docs/guide/user/testing.md) of
every pack; all of them run with [coverage](docs/guide/user/coverage.md) (Xdebug or PCOV, per-test coverage
for PHPUnit, Pest and Codeception; Behat and PHPSpec through their coverage extensions).

![Pest tests from the gutter](docs/screenshots/test-frameworks-pest.png)

## Settings | PHP | Test Frameworks

**Settings | Languages & Frameworks | PHP | Test Frameworks** (`php.testFrameworks`, stored per
project) lists one configuration per framework and interpreter, like PHPStorm:

![Test Frameworks settings](docs/screenshots/test-frameworks-settings.png)

- **+** adds PHPUnit, Pest, Codeception, Behat or PHPSpec, **Local** or **by Remote
  Interpreter** (one of the [CLI interpreters](docs/guide/user/php.md#cli-interpreters)); **−** removes it.
- **<Framework> library**: **Use Composer autoloader** with the path to `vendor/autoload.php`
  (the framework's script in `vendor/bin` is run), or **Path to <executable>** (a script or a
  phar such as `phpunit.phar`).
- **Test Runner**: the **Default configuration file** (`phpunit.xml`, `codeception.yml`,
  `behat.yml`, `phpspec.yml`) and, for PHPUnit and PHPSpec, the **Default bootstrap file**.
  A run configuration's own configuration file wins.
- Frameworks the project uses but that are not configured are listed as **detected**: from
  `require-dev` of composer.json, the scripts in `vendor/bin` and the frameworks'
  configuration files (`tests/Pest.php` for Pest). Changing a detected entry adds it.
- A run uses the entry of its interpreter, else the Local one.

**Auto-test delay (seconds)** (`run.autoTest.delay`, default 3) is on the same page, see
[Auto-test](#auto-test).

## Run configurations

**Run | Edit Configurations…** has a type per framework (PHPUnit is described in
[Run/Debug configurations](docs/guide/user/run-debug.md#configuration-types)). The gutter icons and
**Run Context Configuration** (`Ctrl+Shift+F10`) create temporary configurations of these types.

![A Pest configuration](docs/screenshots/test-frameworks-pest-configuration.png)

| Type | Test scope | Runs | Results |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pest | Directory, File, Test (a `test()`, `it()` or `describe()` description), Defined in the configuration file | `pest --teamcity [--configuration f] [path] [--filter …]` | streamed TeamCity messages |
| Codeception | Type (suite), Directory, File, Method, Defined in the configuration file; Groups, Environments | `codecept run [suite \| file[:method]] [-g group] [--env env] [-c f] --xml <report>` | the JUnit report read when the run ends |
| Behat | Directory, File, Scenario (feature file and line), Defined in the configuration file; Profile | `behat [--config f] [--profile p] --format=progress --out=std --format=junit --out=<reports>` | progress in the console, the JUnit reports in the tree |
| PHPSpec | Directory, Spec, Example (spec file and line), Defined in the configuration file | `phpspec run --format=junit --no-interaction [--config f] [--bootstrap f] [file[:line]]` | the JUnit document on stdout |

Every type has **Configuration file** and **Test runner options**, plus the common fields
(interpreter, interpreter options, working directory, environment variables, Before launch).
**Debug** (`Shift+F9`) runs the tests with Xdebug.

Codeception and Behat write their JUnit reports into a folder that Forge reads and deletes
when the run ends: the system temp folder when the project and the interpreter are local,
otherwise `.forge/test-reports/` inside the project, which a container or remote host reaches
through the interpreter's path mappings.

## Gutter icons

A green ▶ in the gutter runs or debugs a test, or opens **Modify Run Configuration…**. After a
run the icon shows the test's last result (✓ passed, ✗ failed).

| File | Icons |
| --- | --- |
| PHPUnit test class (`*Test`, extends `…TestCase`) | the class, `test*` methods, `@test` and `#[Test]` methods |
| Pest file | every `test()`, `it()` and `describe()` call, every row of an inline `->with([...])` dataset |
| Codeception `*Cest.php`, `*Cept.php`, `extends \Codeception\Test\Unit` | the class or file, public Cest methods, `test*` methods |
| Behat `.feature` | the feature, every scenario and scenario outline, every example row |
| PHPSpec `*Spec.php` (`extends ObjectBehavior`) | the spec, every `it_*` and `its_*` example |

The tests of a file are found in Rust while you type.

## Test results

The test tree of the Run tool window works for every framework:

![Behat results](docs/screenshots/test-frameworks-behat.png)

- Pass, fail and ignored state with durations, **Show Passed** / **Show Ignored**, sorting,
  **Previous/Next Failed Test** and double-click to open a test. Pest tests open at their
  `test()` / `it()` call, Behat scenarios at their `Scenario:` line, Codeception tests at the
  line of the report.
- A failed comparison shows **<Click to see difference>**.
- **Rerun Failed Tests** runs only the failed tests: PHPUnit and Pest with `--filter`,
  Codeception with `-g failed` (Codeception's list of the failed tests), Behat with `--rerun`,
  PHPSpec the failed spec file.

![Codeception results with auto-test on](docs/screenshots/test-frameworks-codeception.png)

![PHPSpec results](docs/screenshots/test-frameworks-phpspec.png)

### Test History

The **Test History** button (clock with an arrow) in the test tree's toolbar lists the last
ten test runs of the project with their result and time. Picking one opens it in a Run tab
with its tree and failure details; **Rerun** runs its configuration again. Runs are kept in
Forge's data folder (`<data dir>/forge/test-history/<project>/`), never in the project. Find
Action: **Test History…**.

![Test History](docs/screenshots/test-frameworks-history.png)

### Auto-test

**Toggle Auto-Test** in the Run tool window's toolbar (or Find Action) reruns that tab's
configuration automatically after files are saved, once the auto-test delay passed since the
last save (`run.autoTest.delay`, default 3 seconds). A run that is still going finishes first.

## Behat

`.feature` files are highlighted as Gherkin: `Feature`, `Background`, `Scenario`,
`Scenario Outline` and `Examples` headings, the step keywords `Given`, `When`, `Then`, `And`,
`But` and `*`, tags, comments, tables (with the header row of examples), doc strings, quoted
arguments, numbers and `<placeholders>`.

**Go to Declaration** (`Ctrl+B`, `Ctrl+Click`) on a step opens its step definition: the
context method whose pattern matches the step, from a doc comment (`@Given /^I have (\d+)
apples?$/`, `@When I add :product to the basket`) or an attribute (`#[Given('…')]`,
`#[\Behat\Step\Then("…")]`). Turnip patterns support `:placeholders` (a quoted string or a
word), optional parts such as `product(s)` and alternatives such as `buy/purchase`; steps of a
scenario outline match with the values of the first example row. Several matching
definitions open a chooser.

![Go to the step definition](docs/screenshots/test-frameworks-behat-step.png)

> **Note:** Gherkin keywords in other languages (`# language: de`) are not supported yet.


---

Source: docs/guide/user/command-line-tools.md

# Command Line Tool Support

The Command Line Tools Console runs the command line tools of a PHP project, like PHPStorm's
Command Line Tool Support: Composer, Laravel Artisan, Symfony Console, WP-CLI, Drush, any tool
built on Symfony Console, and plain PHP scripts. You type a command as
`alias command [arguments]`, for example `c require laravel/sanctum`,
`a make:model Order -m` or `s cache:clear`, and Forge completes commands, options and
arguments as you type.

The feature is the plugin **Command Line Tool Support** (`forge.command-line-tools`) of the
PHPForge pack. It is active in PHP and Composer projects.

## Run Command

**Tools | Run Command…** (`Ctrl+Shift+X`, macOS `Cmd+Shift+X`, action id
`CommandLineToolsAction`) opens the Run Command popup. Its header lists the aliases of the
project's tools.

![Run Command popup with command completion](docs/screenshots/cli-tools-commands.png)

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| typing | completion of the alias, the command, options, option values and arguments |
| `Tab` | insert the selected (or first) completion item |
| `↓` / `↑` | move through the completion list; with no list, browse the history |
| `Enter` | run the command (or insert the item you moved to with the arrow keys) |
| `Ctrl+C` | stop the running command (when nothing is selected in the input) |
| `Esc` | close the completion list, then the popup |

Completion knows:

- **aliases** of the configured tools (also found by the tool's name),
- **commands**, by prefix, by any part (`model` finds `make:model`) and by Symfony-style
  abbreviations (`m:mi` for `make:migration`, `d:s:u` for `doctrine:schema:update`);
  WP-CLI subcommands word by word (`wp plugin list`),
- **options** (`--migration`, `-m`) of the command, the command's own first and the
  application's global ones (`--help`, `--ansi`, `--env`) after them; options you already used
  are not offered again unless they may repeat,
- **option values** that the tool lists (WP-CLI `--format=table|csv|json|…`),
- **arguments**: the expected argument is shown below the input (`<name>: The name of the
  model`); `help <command_name>` completes command names and `list <namespace>` namespaces.

While you type the arguments of a command, the help of the command is shown under the list:
its description, usage, arguments and options, with the argument or option at the cursor
highlighted. Hovering a completion item shows its description.

![Options with the command's help](docs/screenshots/cli-tools-options.png)

## The console and the output

A command's output goes to the **Command Line Tools Console** tool window (one tab per
command), or stays in the popup when the tool's **Show console in** is **Pop-up window**.
The console shows the command line, colored output, clickable file paths (`app/Models/Order.php`
opens in the editor) and URLs, and the exit code (`Process finished with exit code 0`). Input
typed into a running console goes to the command (questions of `make:` commands, `tinker`).

![Command Line Tools Console tool window](docs/screenshots/cli-tools-console.png)

The tool window has an input with completion at the bottom (the completion opens above it),
and a toolbar with **Rerun**, **Stop**, **Scroll to the End**, **Soft-Wrap** and **Clear
All**. Its header has **Reload Command Lists** and a link to the settings. Middle-click or `×`
closes a tab.

Commands run where the project's PHP runs: through the tool's PHP interpreter, or the project
default of Settings | PHP | CLI Interpreter, including Docker, Docker Compose, SSH and WSL
interpreters (see [PHP](docs/guide/user/php.md)). Container paths in the output are mapped back to project
files, so links work there too. Remote projects run the tools on the remote host.

## Command lists and the cache

Forge reads the commands of a tool by running it once:

| Tool | List command |
| --- | --- |
| Composer, Laravel Artisan, Symfony Console, Drush, Tool based on Symfony Console | `<tool> list --format=json` |
| WP-CLI | `wp cli cmd-dump` |
| Tool based on PHP script | none (no completion of commands) |

The result is cached per project and tool in Forge's cache directory
(`<cache dir>/forge/command-line-tools`) and reused until the tool's path, its interpreter or
`composer.lock` changes, so installing or updating packages brings new commands in. **Reload
Command Lists** (in the popup header and the tool window header) lists all tools again. When
Artisan or the Symfony console cannot run (no `vendor/`, a broken application), the standard
commands of Laravel or Symfony are offered instead.

## Settings | Tools | Command Line Tool Support

![Command Line Tool Support settings](docs/screenshots/cli-tools-settings.png)

The table lists the project's tools. Tools the project uses are **auto-detected** (shown in
italics) as long as no tool of that kind or alias is configured:

| Tool | Detected from | Alias | Path |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Composer | `composer.json` | `c` | the Composer executable of Settings \| PHP \| Composer (`composer`) |
| Laravel Artisan | `artisan` | `a` | `artisan` |
| Symfony Console | `bin/console` | `s` | `bin/console` |
| WP-CLI | `wp-cli.phar`, `vendor/bin/wp`, or a WordPress site (`wp-config.php`, `wp-content/`) | `wp` | `wp-cli.phar`, `vendor/bin/wp` or `wp` |
| Drush | `vendor/bin/drush` | `drush` | `vendor/bin/drush` |

**Tools | WP-CLI…** ([WordPress](docs/guide/user/wordpress.md#wp-cli)), **Tools | Drush…** and **Tools |
Shopware Console…** ([Drupal, Joomla and Shopware](docs/guide/user/cms.md#drush-and-the-shopware-console))
open the console with the tool's alias typed in.

**+** opens **Choose Tool to Add** with these tools plus **Tool based on Symfony Console** and
**Tool based on PHP script** (any PHP script, run as `php <script> <arguments>`). **−**
removes a tool, the pencil (or a double-click) edits it; editing an auto-detected tool adds it
to the list. The checkbox turns a tool off. Each tool has:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Name | shown in the table, the popup header and the tool window |
| Alias | the first word of a command line; unique, without spaces |
| Path | a project script (`artisan`, `bin/console`), a `.phar` (run with PHP) or a program name (`composer`, `wp`) |
| PHP interpreter | the CLI interpreter that runs it; **Project default** uses Settings \| PHP |
| Show console in | **Tool window** or **Pop-up window** |

Scripts and `.phar` files always run with the PHP interpreter. Programs such as `composer` or
`wp` run as they are, and inside the interpreter's environment (for example in the Docker
container) when the tool names an interpreter.

The tools are stored in the project settings (`commandLineTools.tools`), so a team can share
them through `.forge/settings.toml`. **Add the tools the project uses automatically**
(`commandLineTools.autoDetect`) turns auto-detection off.

## Laravel and Symfony

**Tools | Laravel | Run Artisan Command…** opens the Run Command popup with the Artisan alias
typed in. The Symfony plugin keeps its own **Run Console Command…** list with the
application's commands and gutter icons (see [Symfony](docs/guide/user/symfony.md)). For commands you run often
with a debugger, create an **Artisan** or **Composer** run configuration
(see [Run/Debug configurations](docs/guide/user/run-debug.md)).

# JavaScript debugging and testing

Two WebForge plugins bring WebStorm's JavaScript run, debug and test support to Forge. Both
are active in projects with a `package.json` (Settings | Plugins):

| Plugin | Id | What it adds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| JavaScript Debugger | `forge.js-debugger` | the **Node.js**, **JavaScript Debug** and **Attach to Node.js/Chrome** run configurations, and Debug of Node.js programs, npm scripts, tests and browser pages with js-debug |
| JavaScript Test Runners | `forge.js-testing` | **Jest**, **Vitest**, **Mocha**, **Playwright**, **Cypress** and **Node.js Test Runner** (`node --test`) on the shared [test runner](docs/guide/user/testing.md) |

![A Node.js debug session stopped at a breakpoint in TypeScript](docs/screenshots/js-debug-node-typescript.png)

## The debugger: js-debug

Forge debugs JavaScript with Microsoft's **js-debug**, the debugger of VS Code (MIT licence),
over the Debug Adapter Protocol. It is not bundled with Forge. The first time you debug a
JavaScript configuration, Forge asks to download it:

![Forge asks before downloading js-debug](docs/screenshots/js-debug-download.png)

- Forge downloads one pinned release (`js-debug-dap-v1.140.0.tar.gz`) from the GitHub
  releases of `microsoft/vscode-js-debug`, checks its SHA-256 checksum and unpacks it into
  `<data dir>/forge/debug-adapters/js-debug/<version>`. A download with another checksum is
  discarded.
- js-debug runs on Node.js 18 or newer: the **Node interpreter** of Settings | Languages &
  Frameworks | Node.js, else `node` on the `PATH`, else the Node.js Forge downloads from
  nodejs.org for its language servers (also SHA-256 checked).
- **Run | Download JavaScript Debugger (js-debug)** (Find Action) downloads it ahead of time.
- To use a js-debug you unpacked yourself, set **js-debug folder** (the folder with
  `src/dapDebugServer.js`) in Settings | Languages & Frameworks | Node.js.

Each debug session starts js-debug's DAP server. js-debug runs the program in a **child
session** (it asks for it with the `startDebugging` request); the Debug tool window shows the
launcher and the program as two tabs, `server` and `server [48211]`, and the program's tab
stops at breakpoints. Child processes of the program (workers, test runners that fork) get
their own tabs too.

### Breakpoints in TypeScript

Breakpoints, stepping and the stack work in the files you write: TypeScript, JSX, Vue single
file components and bundled code are mapped through **source maps** by js-debug. Compile with
source maps (`"sourceMap": true` in `tsconfig.json`, Vite and webpack create them in
development) or run TypeScript directly with a loader such as `tsx` (`--import tsx` in the
configuration's Node options). Conditions, hit counts and logpoints work as for every
debugger (see [Debugging](docs/guide/user/debugging.md)).

**Do not step into** (Settings | Node.js) lists scripts the debugger steps over, separated by
`;`; the default skips Node.js' own modules (`<node_internals>/**`).

## Run configurations

![The JavaScript Debug run configuration](docs/screenshots/js-debug-chrome-configuration.png)

| Type | Run | Debug |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Node.js** | `node [Node options] <file> [Application parameters]` in the Run tool window | the same under js-debug |
| **JavaScript Debug** | opens the URL in the browser | launches Chrome, Edge or Chromium with a separate profile under js-debug; breakpoints in the page's sources |
| **Attach to Node.js/Chrome** | (Debug only) | attaches to `host:port`: Node.js started with `--inspect` (port 9229) or a browser started with `--remote-debugging-port` (9222) |
| **npm** | the script | the script under js-debug (`npm run <script>` with the debugger attached to every Node.js process it starts) |

- **Node.js**: *JavaScript file*, *Interpreter* (default: the project's Node interpreter),
  *Interpreter options* (Node options such as `--import tsx`), *Application parameters*,
  working directory and environment variables.
- **JavaScript Debug**: *URL*, *Browser* (the default of Settings | Node.js | Browser for
  JavaScript Debug: Auto, Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge or Chromium; or a path to a browser)
  and *Browser arguments*. Forge looks for the browsers at their usual install paths and on
  the `PATH`.
- **Attach to Node.js/Chrome**: *Attach to* (Node.js, Chrome, Edge), *Host*, *Port* and
  *Remote root* (the project's folder inside a container, for path mapping).
- **Run | Attach to Process…** lists local processes; picking a Node.js process attaches
  js-debug to it (Node.js opens its inspector on request).
- The ▶ icons next to scripts in `package.json` and the npm tool window offer **Debug** as
  well. Without js-debug (you declined the download, or the plugin is disabled), Debug of an
  npm script falls back to Node's inspector through `NODE_OPTIONS` (*Node options when
  debugging scripts*, default `--inspect`).

**Run | Profile with V8** and **Profile Allocations with V8** run a Node.js or npm
configuration with `--cpu-prof` / `--heap-prof` and open the profile in the Profiler tool
window, see [Profiling PHP and Node.js](docs/guide/user/profiling.md).

Launching a program runs project code and is refused in [Safe Mode](docs/guide/user/project-trust.md);
attaching is not.

## Test runners

![Vitest tests in the test tree, with the failed comparison](docs/screenshots/js-tests-vitest.png)

| Runner | Detected by | Results from | Coverage |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Jest** | `jest` in `package.json`, `jest.config.*` | Jest's JSON report (`--json --outputFile`) | `--coverage`, Istanbul JSON; **Coverage provider** babel or v8 |
| **Vitest** | `vitest` in `package.json`, `vitest.config.*`, `vitest.workspace.*` | the JSON reporter (`--reporter=json --outputFile.json`) | `--coverage.enabled`, Istanbul JSON; **Coverage provider** v8 or istanbul (needs `@vitest/coverage-v8` or `-istanbul`) |
| **Mocha** | `mocha` in `package.json`, `.mocharc.*` | the TAP reporter | through **c8** or **nyc** (**Coverage tool**, from `node_modules`), LCOV |
| **Playwright** | `@playwright/test` in `package.json`, `playwright.config.*` | the JSON reporter (`PLAYWRIGHT_JSON_OUTPUT_NAME`) | — |
| **Cypress** | `cypress` in `package.json`, `cypress.config.*` | `cypress run --reporter junit` | — |
| **Node.js Test Runner** | `node --test` in a `package.json` script | TAP (`--test-reporter=tap`) | Node's LCOV reporter (`--experimental-test-coverage`) |

- **Gutter icons** on `describe` / `context` / `suite`, `it` / `test` / `specify` (with
  `.only`, `.skip`, `.each`, `test.describe` and the other modifiers) whose name is a string.
  The nesting follows the calls, so a test's full name is the names of its `describe` blocks
  and its own. Each icon offers **Run**, **Run with Coverage** (Jest, Vitest, Mocha,
  `node --test`; a **Node.js** configuration runs with coverage under c8 or nyc), **Debug** and **Modify Run Configuration…**; after a run it shows the test's
  result.
- **Which runner a file belongs to**: the runner the project uses (detected from
  `package.json` and config files). Files that import `vitest`, `@jest/globals`, `mocha` or
  `node:test` belong to that runner, files that import `@playwright/test` (or lie in `e2e/`)
  to Playwright, and `*.cy.*` files and the `cypress/` folder to Cypress.
- **Scopes**: all tests, a directory, a file, a test or `describe` block (`-t` / `--grep` /
  `--test-name-pattern` with the full name), or a name pattern.
- **Run configurations** of each runner add *Node interpreter*, *Node options*, the runner's
  *package* (default `node_modules/<runner>`, for monorepos) and its *Configuration file*.
  The runner's CLI script runs with Node.js (`node node_modules/jest/bin/jest.js …`), so no
  `npx` or shell shim is involved.
- **Rerun Failed Tests** runs the failed tests again by name, limited to their files (Cypress,
  which cannot filter names without `@cypress/grep`, reruns the failed spec files).
- **Debug** runs the same command under js-debug with the runner in one process and without
  timeouts (Jest `--runInBand`, Vitest `--no-file-parallelism`, Playwright `--workers=1`,
  Mocha `--no-timeouts`). Cypress tests run in the browser Cypress drives; debug them with
  **Open Cypress** and the browser's DevTools.
- **Tools | Show Playwright Report** opens the HTML report (`playwright show-report`), **Tools
  | Open Cypress** starts the Cypress app (`cypress open`).

![Playwright tests with the failed request](docs/screenshots/js-tests-playwright.png)

See [Testing](docs/guide/user/testing.md) for the test tree, Click to see difference, Test History and
auto-test, and [Code coverage](docs/guide/user/coverage.md) for the Coverage tool window.

## Settings

Settings | Languages & Frameworks | Node.js:

| Setting | Key | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Node interpreter | `web.node.interpreter` | empty: `node` on the `PATH`, else Forge's Node.js |
| js-debug folder | `web.jsDebug.path` | empty: the version Forge downloads |
| Browser for JavaScript Debug | `web.jsDebug.browser` | `auto` |

The debugger lives in [`webforge-js-debug`](docs/guide/developer/crates/webforge-js-debug.md) (the
pinned release, the `pwa-node` / `pwa-chrome` / `pwa-msedge` adapters registered with
[`forge-dap`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-dap.md), browser detection and the launch requests of

`[[contributions.testFrameworks]]` entries of WebForge's manifest.
