Source: docs/guide/user/remote-host-and-ssh.md

# Remote Host and SSH sessions

Like PHPStorm, Forge lets you look at and change the files of a
[deployment server](docs/guide/user/deployment.md) without leaving the IDE, and open a shell on any host you
have an SSH configuration for, also in projects that live on this machine.

## Remote Host tool window

**Tools | Deployment | Browse Remote Host** opens the **Remote Host** tool window (right
stripe) on the project's default server; without a default server Forge asks which one. The
selector at the top switches to another server of the project; **Refresh** reads the selected
folder again (with the folders open below it), **Collapse All** closes the tree and the gear
opens the server settings. Find Action has **Remote Host** (`ActivateRemoteHostToolWindow`)
to show the window; it has no default shortcut, bind one in Settings | Keymap.

![Remote Host tool window](docs/screenshots/remote-host-tree.png)

The tree starts at the server's root path (`/var/www/shop`; the login folder when the root path
is empty) and loads each folder when you expand it. It works for every server type: SFTP,
FTP/FTPS and local or mounted folders.

- Folders that are the deployment path of a [mapping](docs/guide/user/deployment.md#mappings-tab) are
  **green**, with the project folder they belong to next to them ("project root", "public").
- Paths excluded on the deployment side (Excluded Paths tab) are dimmed.
- Hover a file or folder to see the project path it is mapped to.

Double-click a folder to expand it, a file to edit it.

### Context menu

![Remote Host context menu](docs/screenshots/remote-host-context-menu.png)

| Entry | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Edit Remote File | Downloads the file into a temporary copy and opens it in the editor. Saving (`Ctrl+S`, automatic saves) uploads it back, see below. |
| Download from Here | Downloads the file or folder into the project path it is mapped to, like Download from… (the transfer appears in the File Transfer tool window). |
| Upload to Here | Uploads the project file or folder mapped to this path, like Upload to…. |
| Compare with Local Version | Opens the diff of the server file and the project file it is mapped to. |
| New › File / Directory | Creates an empty file (opened with Edit Remote File) or a folder in the selected folder. |
| Rename… | Renames the file or folder on the server. |
| Delete… | Deletes the file, or the folder with everything in it, after a confirmation. The root folder is never deleted. |
| Copy Path | Copies the absolute path on the server. |
| Refresh | Reads the folder again. |

Download from Here, Upload to Here and Compare with Local Version need a mapping that covers
the path; the entries are disabled otherwise. They follow the
[Deployment options](docs/guide/user/deployment.md#options) (excluded names, overwrite rules, timestamps) and
ask before overwriting newer files, like every transfer.

### Edit Remote File

![Edit Remote File](docs/screenshots/remote-host-edit.png)

The editor tab shows the server and the path in the breadcrumbs. The temporary copy lives in
Forge's cache folder (`<cache dir>/forge/remote-edit/<server>/…`), never in the project, and
is removed when you close the tab. Each save uploads the text, but first checks the server copy:
when someone else changed (or deleted) the file since you opened it, Forge asks before it
overwrites their version (**Overwrite** / **Upload**, or **Cancel** to keep your changes
unsaved).

## SSH configurations

Settings | Tools | **SSH Configurations** keeps the SSH connections of
[remote development](docs/guide/user/remote-development.md#saved-configurations), SFTP deployment servers and
SSH sessions in one list: **+** adds, **−** removes and the copy button duplicates a
configuration.

![SSH Configurations](docs/screenshots/ssh-configurations.png)

| Field | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| Host, Port | A host name, an address or a `Host` alias of `~/.ssh/config`; port 22 by default |
| Username | The account on the host |
| Authentication type | **Password**, **Key pair (OpenSSH or PuTTY)** with the private key file and its passphrase, or **OpenSSH config and authentication agent** (keys of the running ssh-agent, the `IdentityFile`s of `~/.ssh/config` and the default keys in `~/.ssh`) |
| Save password / Save passphrase | Stores the secret in the OS keychain (service `forge-ssh`); off: Forge asks every time |
| Parse config file `~/.ssh/config` | On (the default): the host may be a `Host` alias, and the host name, port, user, identity files, `ProxyJump` and `ProxyCommand` come from `~/.ssh/config`. Off: the host is taken literally. |

**Test Connection** connects with the values in the form, including a password you have not
saved yet. An unknown host key is shown with its fingerprint; trusting it adds it to
`~/.ssh/known_hosts`.

## SSH sessions

**Tools | Start SSH Session…** (`RunSshConsole`, no default shortcut) and **SSH Session…** in
the Terminal's new-tab dropdown (the arrow next to **+**) open a chooser:

![Start SSH Session](docs/screenshots/ssh-session-chooser.png)

- **SSH Configurations**: your saved configurations.
- **Deployment Servers**: the project's SFTP servers, connected with their SSH configuration.
- **Edit credentials…**: host, port, user name and authentication typed in; Forge saves them as
  an SSH configuration (an existing one for the same account is updated) and connects.

The session opens as a new tab of the [Terminal](docs/guide/user/terminal.md) tool window, named after the
host (`shop.example.com`, `shop.example.com (2)`). It is a real pseudo terminal on the SSH
channel (`xterm-256color`), so `htop`, `vim` or `php artisan tinker` work and the window size
follows the tool window. Typing `exit` closes the tab; other exit codes stay visible.
Configurations that do not save their password or passphrase ask for it first, and an unknown
host key is asked about like in Test Connection.

![SSH session in the Terminal](docs/screenshots/ssh-session-terminal.png)

![The Terminal's new-tab dropdown](docs/screenshots/terminal-ssh-dropdown.png)

## Safe Mode

Browsing a server, Edit Remote File and the transfers only copy files and never run project
code, so they work in an untrusted project opened in [Safe Mode](docs/guide/user/project-trust.md).

An SSH session logs you in on a host with your credentials. Your own SSH configurations
connect right away. A deployment server, however, comes from the project's
`.forge/deployment.toml`: in Safe Mode Forge asks before it starts a session to it ("The
deployment server … is defined in the files of this untrusted project. Connect … over SSH with
your credentials?"), so an untrusted project cannot choose a host for you. The backend refuses
the session without that confirmation. Trusted projects never ask.

> **Note:** Download from Here, Upload to Here and Compare with Local Version need a project on
> this machine, like every [Deployment](docs/guide/user/deployment.md) transfer. In a
> [remote project](docs/guide/user/remote-development.md) the project files and the terminal already are on
> the host.


---

Source: docs/guide/user/ai.md

# AI

AI is part of Forge's core and works with **your own** providers and tools; Forge ships no
credentials and no subscription. There are four parts:

- **AI providers**: language model APIs Forge calls itself, used for AI in the editor, AI
  commit messages and available to plugins.
- **AI in the editor**: inline code completion, "Explain with AI" and "Fix with AI" in
  `Alt+Enter`, and AI-generated documentation and tests, all with a diff preview.
- **AI Chat**: Claude Code or Gemini CLI, installed on your machine with your own login, run
  headless and rendered as a native chat.
- **Agent Tasks**: an agent works on a task in a sandbox copy of the project, runs the tests,
  fixes failures and leaves a diff for you to review and apply.

## Providers

Settings | Tools | **AI Providers**:

![AI Providers](docs/screenshots/ai-providers-settings.png)

**Add Provider** offers presets:

| Kind | Default base URL | API key | Default model |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Anthropic (Claude, Messages API) | `https://api.anthropic.com/v1` | required (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` as fallback) | Forge's current Claude default |
| OpenAI | `https://api.openai.com/v1` | required (`OPENAI_API_KEY`) | `gpt-4.1` |
| OpenRouter | `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` | required (`OPENROUTER_API_KEY`) | `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5` |
| Ollama | `http://localhost:11434/v1` | not required | pick one |
| LM Studio | `http://localhost:1234/v1` | not required | pick one |
| llama.cpp (`llama-server`) | `http://localhost:8080/v1` | not required | pick one |
| OpenAI-compatible (custom) | `http://localhost:8000/v1` | optional | pick one |

![Add a preset](docs/screenshots/ai-providers-add-preset.png)

For each provider set **Name**, **Base URL**, **API key** and **Default model**. **Fetch
Models** lists the models the server offers (for local servers: "Fetch models from the running
server"). **Test Connection** reports latency and the number of models, or a hint such as "is
Ollama running? Start it with `ollama serve`".

![Test connection](docs/screenshots/ai-providers-test-connection.png)

- API keys are stored in the OS keychain (service `forge-ai`), never in files ("Will be stored
  in the system keychain on Apply"). Without a stored key, the environment variables above are
  used.
- The provider list lives in `ai.toml` in Forge's config folder.
- **Set as Default Provider** chooses the provider used by features without their own choice.
- **Models per feature**: pick the provider/model for **Chat**, **Code completion** ("prefer a
  fast local model") and **Commit messages** separately.

> **Note:** the **Chat** model is used by the editor actions (Explain, Fix, Generate) and the
> **Code completion** model by inline completion; the AI Chat tool window itself uses the
> agent CLIs below. The "Google Gemini" provider kind declared in the AI plugin manifest has
> no implementation yet; use Gemini through Gemini CLI or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

A provider can be switched off with its **Enabled** checkbox; Forge then sends nothing to it,
also not through a feature that selected it.

## AI in the editor

Settings | Tools | **AI Assistant** (`ai.assistantSettings`) turns the editor features on and
picks their models. Nothing is sent before you add a provider; inline completion is off until
you enable it.

![AI Assistant settings](docs/screenshots/ai-assistant-settings.png)

| Setting | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Actions model | Provider and model of Explain, Fix and Generate with AI and of the AI code review (the **Chat** model of Settings \| Tools \| AI Providers). |
| Enable AI features in this project (`ai.enabled`) | A **project** setting: off keeps all of the project's code away from AI. |
| Completion model | Provider and model of inline completion (the **Code completion** model). A fast local code model such as `qwen2.5-coder` on Ollama works best. |
| Enable inline code completion (`ai.completion.enabled`) | Gray suggestions while you type. Also in the status bar widget and as Enable/Disable AI Inline Completion (`ai.toggleInlineCompletion`). |
| Suggestion length (`ai.completion.multiline`) | **Automatic**: several lines on an empty line and after a block opener such as `{`, else one line; or always **Single line** / **Multi-line**. |
| Request type (`ai.completion.mode`) | **Fill-in-the-middle** sends the code before and after the caret to the server's `/completions` endpoint (code models on Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, other OpenAI-compatible servers); **Chat** asks a chat model with a `<CURSOR>` marker (Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter). **Automatic** picks fill-in-the-middle for local servers and chat for hosted APIs. |
| Delay before asking (`ai.completion.debounceMs`) | How long typing must pause before a suggestion is requested (350 ms). |
| Disable for languages (`ai.completion.disabledLanguages`) | Language ids without inline completion, e.g. `markdown`, `json`. |

### Excluding files: .aiignore

An `.aiignore` file in the project root (gitignore syntax; `.aiexclude` is read too) keeps
files away from every AI feature: inline completion is not asked there and the actions report
"… is excluded from AI by .aiignore".

```text
# secrets and generated code never go to a model
.env
*.pem
config/secrets/
src/**/generated/*.ts
!docs/examples/*.pem
```

A pattern without `/` matches the name anywhere; with a `/` it is relative to the project root;
a trailing `/` matches folders and everything in them; `!` includes a file again (not inside an
excluded folder).

### Inline completion

While you type, Forge asks the completion model after a short pause and shows the answer as
gray text at the caret, like PHPStorm's AI Assistant. Typing on cancels the request; typing
the characters the suggestion starts with keeps the rest.

![Inline completion](docs/screenshots/ai-inline-completion.png)

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Tab` | Insert Inline Proposal (`InsertInlineCompletionAction`) |
| `Ctrl+Right` (macOS `Alt+Right`) | Insert Inline Proposal Word (`InsertInlineCompletionWordAction`) |
| no default | Insert Inline Proposal Line (`InsertInlineCompletionLineAction`) |
| `Alt+]` / `Alt+[` | Show Next / Previous Inline Proposal: asks the model for alternatives and cycles through them |
| `Alt+Shift+\` | Call Inline Completion (`CallInlineCompletionAction`): ask now |
| `Escape` | Dismiss the suggestion |

The keys are keymap actions (rebind them in Settings | Keymap, group Editor Actions | Inline
Completion). They act only while a suggestion is shown, so `Tab` still indents and
`Ctrl+Right` still moves by word otherwise; while the code completion popup is open, `Tab`
chooses its item.

![Accepted suggestion](docs/screenshots/ai-inline-completion-accepted.png)

What the model gets: the code before and after the caret (about 8 KB / 2.5 KB), the file's
imports when they are outside that window, the path, and the beginning of up to three other
open files (same language first). Answers are cleaned before they are shown: Markdown fences,
end tokens and code the model repeated from before the caret are removed, the text that is
already after the caret (`)`, `;`, a closing `}` line) is not suggested twice, single-line mode
keeps one line, and multi-line suggestions end with the block they are in.

The **status bar widget** (✨) shows whether inline completion is on for the current file, a
spinner while a suggestion is asked and red after an error. Click it to enable or disable
inline completion, turn it off for the file's language, or open the settings.

![Status bar widget](docs/screenshots/ai-inline-status-menu.png)

### Explain with AI and Fix with AI

`Alt+Enter` offers **Explain with AI** everywhere and **Fix with AI** on a line with a problem
(errors and warnings of the language servers and inspections). They are also in the editor's
context menu under **AI Actions** and in Find Action.

![Alt+Enter](docs/screenshots/ai-intentions.png)

- **Explain with AI** explains the selection, or the function or class around the caret. The
  explanation streams into the **AI Chat** tool window as a new turn; its footer names the
  provider and model.

  ![Explanation in the AI Chat](docs/screenshots/ai-explain-chat.png)

- **Fix with AI** sends the problems at the caret with the code around them and shows the
  proposed change as a diff. **Apply** (`Ctrl+Enter`) changes the editor in one undoable step;
  **Discard** (`Escape`) changes nothing. If the file changed while the AI was answering, Forge
  asks you to run the action again.

  ![Fix with AI](docs/screenshots/ai-fix-preview.png)

### Generate documentation and tests

**Generate** (`Alt+Insert`) lists **Documentation with AI…** and **Tests with AI…** below the
language's own entries (in files without a Generate menu only these two); they are also under
**AI Actions** in the editor's context menu.

![Generate menu](docs/screenshots/ai-generate-menu.png)

- **Generate Documentation with AI** (`ai.generateDocs`) writes the documentation comment of
  the function or class at the caret in the language's format: PHPDoc, JSDoc, Javadoc, KDoc,
  Doxygen, rustdoc `///`, LuaDoc `---`, Go `//` comments or a Python docstring. It goes above
  attributes and annotations and replaces an existing doc comment.

  ![Generate Documentation](docs/screenshots/ai-generate-docs-preview.png)

- **Generate Tests with AI** (`ai.generateTests`) writes tests for the selection or the
  declaration at the caret with the language's usual framework (PHPUnit, Vitest, pytest,
  busted, Go `testing`, JUnit, …) into the conventional test file: `tests/Unit/…Test.php`,
  `name.test.ts`, `tests/test_name.py`, `name_test.go`, `src/test/java/…Test.java`,
  `spec/name_spec.lua`; Rust tests are appended to the file as `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`. An
  existing test file is sent along and extended. **Create File** / **Apply** writes the file
  and opens it.

  ![Generate Tests](docs/screenshots/ai-generate-tests-preview.png)

![Fix with AI, light theme](docs/screenshots/ai-fix-preview-light.png)

## AI code review

Pull and merge requests have an **AI Review** tab: **Summarize PR** (overview, risk areas, a
summary per file and a test plan), **AI Review** (inline findings you can add to your review as
pending comments or dismiss) and **Explain** on a hunk of the diff. They use the **Actions
model** and the same rules as the editor actions: `ai.enabled`, `.aiignore` (excluded files
are neither sent nor named) and no request without a configured provider. The provider and
model are shown above the results. Nothing is posted to the code host until you submit the
review. See [Code hosts](docs/guide/user/code-hosts.md#ai-summary-and-ai-review).

## AI commit messages

In the Commit tool window, **Generate Commit Message with AI** writes a message for the ticked
changes. See [Git](docs/guide/user/git.md#ai-commit-messages).

## AI Chat

The **AI Chat** tool window (right stripe, or the ✨ button in the main toolbar) runs an
agentic coding CLI in your project and renders its output as a chat: text, thinking, tool calls
as cards, file edits as diffs, permission questions as buttons. No terminal is involved.

![AI Chat](docs/screenshots/ai-chat-streaming.png)

### Agents

| Agent | Needs | Install |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Claude Code** | the `claude` CLI, logged in (subscription or API key) | `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code` |
| **Gemini CLI** | the `gemini` CLI, logged in | `npm install -g @google/gemini-cli` |

Pick the agent in the chat header. If the CLI is not found, the chat says "Not installed" with
the install command; set its path in Settings | Tools | **AI Agents** (`agents.<id>.path`;
empty = find it on `PATH`).

![Agent picker](docs/screenshots/ai-chat-agent-picker.png)

![Agents settings](docs/screenshots/settings-ai-agents.png)

### Writing messages

- `Enter` sends, `Shift+Enter` inserts a line break, `Esc` stops the running turn.
- **Attach context** (`@`) attaches the current file, the current selection
  (`file:12-20`), or another open file.
- Slash commands: `/clear` starts a new chat; for Claude Code also `/compact`, `/review`,
  `/init` and `/cost`. `Tab` completes them.
- Suggested prompts appear in an empty chat.

![Attach context](docs/screenshots/ai-chat-attach.png)

### Models and modes

The header has a **Model** and a **Permission mode** selector; defaults come from Settings |
Tools | AI Agents (`agents.<id>.model`, `agents.<id>.permissionMode`).

| Claude Code mode | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Ask before edits (default) | confirm every edit and command |
| Auto-accept edits | apply file edits without asking; commands still ask |
| Plan mode | explore and plan, no changes |
| Bypass permissions | never ask — trusted projects only |

Gemini CLI cannot ask inside the IDE, so its mode decides which tools it gets:

| Gemini CLI mode | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Read-only (default) | read and search, no edits or commands |
| Auto-accept edits | edit files without asking, no commands |
| YOLO | edits and commands, never asks |

![Gemini modes](docs/screenshots/gemini-modes.png)

### Permission requests

With Claude Code in "Ask before edits", each edit or command shows a card: **Allow once**,
**Allow for this session** ("Don't ask again for this exact command until the chat ends") or
**Deny**. Edit cards show the diff; **Open diff** opens it in a dialog.

![Permission for a command](docs/screenshots/chat-permission-command.png)

![Edit diff](docs/screenshots/ai-chat-diff-dialog.png)

Files changed by the agent are reloaded in open editor tabs automatically.

### History

![Chat history](docs/screenshots/ai-chat-history.png)

**Chat history** lists the chats of the open project, newest first; selecting one shows it
again and resumes the CLI's conversation with the next message. **New chat** starts over.
Chats are saved after every turn in Forge's data directory (`<data dir>/forge/chat-history`,
the newest 100 per project), never in the project. The end of a turn shows duration, tokens and cost when
the CLI reports them.

![Finished turn](docs/screenshots/ai-chat-finished.png)

In [remote projects](docs/guide/user/remote-development.md) the agent CLI runs **on the host**: install and log
in to `claude` or `gemini` there. Forge finds the executable on the host and the agent works
next to the files.

## Agent Tasks

The **Agent Tasks** tool window (right stripe, below AI Chat; **New Agent Task…** in Find
Action) hands a task to an agent that works on its own: it explores the code, edits files,
runs the tests and fixes failures until they pass, then stops for your review. It never
touches your working tree: every task runs in a **sandbox**, and nothing changes in your
project until you apply its diff.

![Agent Tasks](docs/screenshots/agent-tasks-review.png)

### Creating a task

Click **+** in the tool window header:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Task** | What to do, e.g. "Fix the failing CheckoutTest". `Ctrl+Enter` starts it. |
| **Files it may change** | Comma-separated files and folders (`app/Services, tests/Unit`). The agent can read everything (except `.aiignore`d files) but writes only there. Empty: the whole project. |
| **Agent** | **Forge agent** (Forge's own agent over a model of Settings \| Tools \| AI Providers: the default provider or a chosen one, the Chat model), **Claude Code** or **Gemini CLI** (your installed CLI, see [AI Chat](#agents)). |
| **Verify with** | **No tests**, one of the project's **run configurations** (its test runner and result format), or a **command** such as `vendor/bin/phpunit`. |

![New Agent Task](docs/screenshots/agent-tasks-new.png)

Tasks run one at a time per project; later ones wait as **Queued**. The list shows each task's
status: **Queued**, **Running**, **Needs review**, **Applied**, **Discarded**, **Failed** or
**Cancelled**. **Stop** cancels a running task (what it changed so far stays reviewable).

### The sandbox

A task's sandbox is a detached **git worktree** in Forge's cache folder
(`<cache dir>/forge/agent-tasks/<project>/<task>`, e.g. `~/.cache/forge/...` on Linux), never
inside the project. It starts from a snapshot of your working tree, taken without touching it
(`git stash create`): committed files, uncommitted changes and untracked files that are not
ignored. The review shows only what the agent changed against that snapshot. Agent tasks need
a Git repository with at least one commit; remote projects are not supported yet.

### Run, test and fix

The **Forge agent** works in steps, one tool per model turn, all confined to the sandbox:

| Tool | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `list_files`, `read_file`, `search` | explore the project (no `.git`, no `.aiignore`d files, no paths outside the sandbox or through symlinks) |
| `write_file`, `edit_file`, `delete_file` | change files inside the task's scope |
| `run_tests` | run the tests of the task and get the failures (parsed by Forge's test runners) |
| `run_command` | run one program in the sandbox without a shell (no pipes), after your approval unless allowlisted |
| `finish` | report what it did |

When the agent says it is done, Forge runs the tests again if files changed since the last
run. If they fail, the failures go back to the agent and it keeps fixing. The task stops when
the tests pass, when the **step budget** is used up or when the **test runs** are used up; the
last step says which. There are no network tools; `curl`, `wget`, `ssh`, `scp`, `rsync`, `nc`
and similar programs are always refused.

**Claude Code** runs headless in the sandbox. Each tool it wants to use is checked by Forge:
reads and edits inside the sandbox (edits inside the scope) are allowed, shell commands need
your approval unless allowlisted, web tools are refused. **Gemini CLI** cannot ask in headless
mode, so it may edit files (in the sandbox) but gets no shell. For both, Forge runs the tests
after each turn and sends failures back until they pass.

### Approving commands

A command that is not allowlisted shows **Run this command?** in the task's log with **Allow**
and **Deny**; the agent waits for the answer.

![Command approval](docs/screenshots/agent-tasks-approval.png)

### Reviewing and applying

When a task needs review, **Changes** lists the changed files with added and removed lines.
Double-click a file (or its diff button) to open it in the diff viewer: the snapshot on the
left, the agent's version on the right.

![Diff of a task](docs/screenshots/agent-tasks-diff.png)

| Button | Does |
| --- | --- |
| **Apply** | patches your working tree. All or nothing: if a file changed meanwhile so the patch does not apply cleanly, nothing is changed and the conflicting files are listed. The ✓ next to a file applies just that file. |
| **Commit…** | applies, then commits only the agent's files with your message (other staged changes stay staged). |
| **Branch…** | commits the changes on a new branch (default `agent/<title>`); your working tree stays as it is. Use it when Apply reports conflicts. |
| **Discard** | removes the sandbox without applying anything. |
| **Remove** | deletes the task from the list (and its sandbox). |

After a complete Apply, Commit or Branch the sandbox is removed and the task is **Applied**.

### Settings and safety

Settings | Tools | **AI Assistant** › Agent Tasks:

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Step budget per task (`ai.agentTasks.maxSteps`) | 40 | model turns (Forge agent) or CLI turns per task |
| Test runs per task (`ai.agentTasks.maxTestRuns`) | 6 | test runs while fixing failures |
| Commands that run without asking (`ai.agentTasks.allowedCommands`) | none | command prefixes, e.g. `composer test`, `php -l`, `npm run lint` |

Agent tasks run project code (tests, commands, the agent CLI's tools), so they are refused in
[Safe Mode](docs/guide/user/project-trust.md). They are refused as well when AI is turned off for the project
(`ai.enabled`), and the Forge agent never reads files matched by `.aiignore`. Tasks and their
logs are stored next to the sandboxes in the cache folder; a task that was running when Forge
quit shows as Cancelled.

## Privacy

Forge sends data only to the providers you configure and the CLIs you run: commit diffs to the
commit message provider, code around the caret to the completion provider (only with inline
completion enabled), the code an editor action is about to the actions provider, a pull
request's title, description and diff to the actions provider when you ask for an AI summary,
AI review or explanation, and your chat
messages and attached context to the agent CLI (which talks to its own service). Nothing is
sent anywhere by default. Disabled providers, projects with AI turned off and files in
`.aiignore` are never sent. A local provider (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp) keeps everything
on your machine. Apart from Agent Tasks, none of the AI features runs project code, so they
work the same in [Safe Mode](docs/guide/user/project-trust.md). Agent Tasks send the task, the files the agent
reads and the test output to the chosen provider or CLI.

## External agents (MCP)

Agents that run outside Forge (Claude Code in a terminal, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Gemini CLI,
Codex) can use Forge's tools through its built-in MCP server: search and navigation with
Forge's indexes, the problems it shows, undoable edits in the editor, run configurations and
tests, Git and read-only database queries, with approval cards and the same `ai.enabled`,
`.aiignore` and Safe Mode rules. It is off by default; see [MCP Server](docs/guide/user/mcp-server.md).


---

Source: docs/guide/user/mcp-server.md

# MCP Server

Like JetBrains IDEs, Forge has a built-in [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io)
server (`forge.mcp-server`). External agents such as Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor,
Gemini CLI or Codex connect to the running Forge and use its tools on the project open in it:
they see what you are looking at, search and navigate with Forge's indexes, read the problems
Forge shows, edit in the editor (so every change is undoable), run your run configurations and
tests, look at Git, and query your data sources read-only.

![MCP Server settings](docs/screenshots/mcp-server-settings.png)

The server is **off by default**. Turn it on in Settings | Tools | MCP Server (`mcp.enabled`).

## Connecting a client

Settings | Tools | MCP Server shows the server's address and, under **Client Configuration**,
a ready-made configuration for each client. Pick the client and click **Copy**:

| Client | Transport | Where it goes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Code | Streamable HTTP | run the copied `claude mcp add --transport http forge http://127.0.0.1:64342/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer …"` |
| Claude Desktop | stdio proxy | `claude_desktop_config.json` (Settings › Developer › Edit Config) |
| Cursor | Streamable HTTP | `~/.cursor/mcp.json` or `.cursor/mcp.json` |
| Gemini CLI | Streamable HTTP | `~/.gemini/settings.json` (`httpUrl` with the `Authorization` header) |
| Codex CLI | stdio proxy | `~/.codex/config.toml` |
| VS Code (Copilot) | Streamable HTTP | `.vscode/mcp.json` |

The server listens on `127.0.0.1` only, on port `64342` (`mcp.port`; when it is taken the next
9 ports are tried and the configurations show the port in use). Every request needs the
**bearer token** from the configuration. The token is kept in the system keychain, so copied
configurations keep working after a restart; **Regenerate Token** replaces it (connected
clients and old configurations stop working).

Clients that only start stdio servers run `forge --mcp-stdio`. This hidden mode of the `forge`
executable finds the running Forge through `<config dir>/forge/mcp-server.json` (port and
process id, no secrets) and forwards every message to it, with the token from the keychain or
the `FORGE_MCP_TOKEN` environment variable. When Forge is not running the proxy answers every
request with an error saying so, and connects as soon as Forge is back.

Older clients that still use the HTTP+SSE transport of protocol version 2024-11-05 can connect
to `http://127.0.0.1:64342/sse` with the same token.

## Tools

Paths are relative to the project root, lines and columns are 1-based.

| Group (setting) | Tools |
| --- | --- |
| Read the project (`mcp.tools.read`) | `get_open_editors`, `get_current_file` (caret, selection, optionally the unsaved text), `open_file_in_editor`, `read_file` (optionally a line range), `list_directory`, `find_files` (like Go to File), `search_in_files` (Find in Files with regex, case, whole words, file masks, directory), `find_symbol` (Go to Symbol / Class), `go_to_definition`, `find_usages`, `get_problems` (what the editor and the Problems tool window show), `run_inspections` (the project's inspection profile on a file or folder), `list_run_configurations` |
| Version control (`mcp.tools.vcs`) | `git_status`, `git_diff` (working tree or staged, optionally for some paths) |
| Edit files (`mcp.tools.edit`) | `replace_text_in_file`, `write_file`, `reformat_file` (Reformat Code with the project's code style) |
| Run configurations and tests (`mcp.tools.run`) | `run_configuration`: runs it in the Run tool window and waits: exit code, test results with the failed tests, the end of the console |
| Terminal commands (`mcp.tools.terminal`, off by default) | `execute_terminal_command` in the project root, with exit code and output |
| Databases (`mcp.tools.database`) | `list_data_sources`, `run_sql_query` (read-only) |

Edits are made **in Forge's editor**: the file opens, the change is one undo step and the file
is saved. `Ctrl+Z` (macOS `Cmd+Z`) in Forge reverts it, and Local History has it too.

The server also offers **resources** (the open editors as `forge://project/<path>`, any project
file through the `forge://project/{path}` template) and three **prompts**: `review_changes`,
`fix_problems` and `explain_selection`.

## Approval and safety

- **Approval cards.** With **Ask before tools that edit files, run configurations or query
  databases** (`mcp.requireApproval`, on by default), every such call shows a card above the
  status bar: which client, what it wants to do ("edit app/Models/Order.php", the command, the
  query, the replaced text) and **Allow**, **Allow for This Session** (that tool, until the
  client disconnects) or **Deny**. A card nobody answers within two minutes is denied.
  Terminal commands always ask, on every call, whatever the setting says.
- **Tool groups.** Each group can be turned off; its tools then disappear from the client's
  tool list and calls are refused.
- **Safe Mode.** In a project you have not trusted, run configurations and terminal commands
  are refused before anything is asked. Reading and editing still work.
- **AI switch and `.aiignore`.** When AI features are turned off for the project
  (`ai.enabled`, Settings | Tools | AI Assistant) every call is refused. Files matched by
  `.aiignore` or `.aiexclude` cannot be read, searched or edited, and they are left out of
  listings and search results (the result says how many were left out). Paths outside the
  project are refused.
- **Databases.** `run_sql_query` only runs read-only statements (`SELECT`, `SHOW`, `EXPLAIN`,
  …); writes and schema changes are refused before they reach the database, and the data
  source's own read-only and production guards still apply.
- **Loopback only.** The server binds `127.0.0.1`, refuses requests whose `Host` is not a
  loopback name (against DNS rebinding) and requests with a foreign `Origin` (web pages), and
  compares the token in constant time.

## Status bar and call log

While the server is on, the status bar shows **MCP** and the connected client
("MCP: Claude Code", "MCP: 2 clients"). Clicking it shows the connected clients (with
**Disconnect**), the latest tool calls with their result (done, failed, refused by the
settings, denied by you) and duration, and a link to the settings. The full call log is at the
bottom of Settings | Tools | MCP Server. Find Action: **Show MCP Server Calls**,
**MCP Server Settings**.

![MCP status popup](docs/screenshots/mcp-server-popup.png)

![Approval card](docs/screenshots/mcp-server-approval.png)

## Settings

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mcp.enabled` | `false` | run the server |
| `mcp.port` | `64342` | first port tried |
| `mcp.requireApproval` | `true` | approval cards for edit, run and database tools |
| `mcp.tools.read`, `mcp.tools.vcs`, `mcp.tools.edit`, `mcp.tools.run`, `mcp.tools.database` | `true` | tool groups |
| `mcp.tools.terminal` | `false` | terminal commands |

Only the first project window runs the server; the tools work on the project open in it. See
the [settings reference](docs/guide/reference/settings.md#tools--mcp-server) and, for developers, the
[forge-mcp crate](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-mcp.md).

Source: docs/guide/user/browser-companion.md

# Browser Companion

The Browser Companion (`forge.browser-companion`) connects Forge with the outside world:

- the **Forge Companion** browser extension: click a React, Vue, Angular or Svelte component in
  your running app and its source opens in Forge at the right line;
- **`forge://` links** from error pages (Laravel Ignition, Symfony, Whoops, Xdebug);
- the **`forge` launcher** used by Vite, Vue DevTools and other "open in editor" features.

## The browser extension

![Extension in inspect mode](docs/screenshots/browser-companion-extension.png)

- **Inspect mode**: press `Alt+Shift+F` in the page (or use the toolbar popup), hover to see the
  component and its file, click to open it. `Esc` stops.
- **Alt+Click** opens the component under the cursor directly.
- **Context menu**: "Open Component in Forge", and "Open “…” in Forge" on selected text with a
  `file:line` reference (stack traces, compiler output).
- **Popup**: connection status, pairing, inspect toggle, recently opened files, the Forge port
  and **path mappings** for apps running in Docker or on another machine
  (`/var/www/html => /home/me/shop`).

Supported: Chrome, Chromium, Edge, Brave 111+ and Firefox 128+ (Manifest V3).

| Framework | Source of the location | Precision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| React ≤ 18 (dev) | `_debugSource` from the development JSX transform | element, line and column |
| React 19 (dev) | component name; Forge finds the declaration | component |
| Vue 3 / Vue 2 (dev) | the component's `__file` | component file |
| Angular (`ng serve`) | `ng.getComponent` → class name; Forge finds the class | component class |
| Svelte 4/5 (dev) | `__svelte_meta.loc` | element, line and column |
| Any | `data-source-file`/`data-source-line`, react-dev-inspector, vite-plugin-vue-inspector, code-inspector-plugin attributes | element |

### Installing the extension

The extension is not in the browser stores yet. Build and load it unpacked:

```sh
cd browser-extension
pnpm install
pnpm build            # dist/chrome and dist/firefox
```

- **Chrome, Edge, Brave**: `chrome://extensions` → **Developer mode** → **Load unpacked** →
  `browser-extension/dist/chrome`.
- **Firefox**: `about:debugging#/runtime/this-firefox` → **Load Temporary Add-on…** →
  `browser-extension/dist/firefox/manifest.json`, then allow access to `127.0.0.1` in the
  extension's permissions.

### Pairing

1. In Forge open Settings | Tools | **Browser Companion** and click **Pair New Browser…**.
2. Click the Forge icon in the browser toolbar and type the 6-digit code.

![Pairing code](docs/screenshots/browser-companion-pairing.png)

The code works once and expires after five minutes. The browser then keeps a random token;
Forge stores only its SHA-256 hash (in `browser-companion.json` in Forge's config folder) and
lists the browser under **Paired Browsers** with its last use. **Unpair Browser** revokes it
immediately.

![Browser Companion settings](docs/screenshots/browser-companion-settings.png)

### What happens when a file is requested

The request is matched against the open project and your recent projects:

- a file of the **open project** opens right away (and Forge comes to the front, setting
  `browserCompanion.focusWindow`);
- a file of a **recent project** or **outside any project** asks first ("Open the project in
  this window?", **Open Project**, **Open Folder**, **Open File Outside Projects**), because
  links can come from any web page.

![Confirmation](docs/screenshots/browser-companion-confirm.png)

### Security

The built-in server listens on `127.0.0.1` only, port **63342** (`browserCompanion.port`; if it
is taken, for example by PhpStorm, the next nine ports are tried). It accepts requests only with
a loopback `Host`, no web-page `Origin` (extension origins only) and, except for ping and
pairing, a valid token. Turn it off with **Accept open requests from paired browsers**
(`browserCompanion.enabled`).

## Framework integrations

The settings page lists ready-made snippets, the ones for frameworks detected in the open
project first (**Show detected only**). Some have an **Apply** button that writes one variable
into `.env` / `.env.local` ("An existing value of the variable is replaced; nothing else in the
file changes").

![Integrations](docs/screenshots/browser-companion-integrations.png)

| Integration | Setup |
| --- | --- |
| Laravel error page (Ignition) | `.env`: `IGNITION_EDITOR=forge`, plus a `forge` entry in `config/ignition.php` `editor_options` with URL `forge://open?file=%path&line=%line` |
| Symfony error page and profiler | `.env.local`: `SYMFONY_IDE="forge://open?file=%f&line=%l"` (or `framework.ide` in `framework.yaml`) |
| Xdebug | `php.ini`: `xdebug.file_link_format = "forge://open?file=%f&line=%l"` |
| Whoops | `$handler->addEditor('forge', 'forge://open?file=%file&line=%line'); $handler->setEditor('forge');` |
| Vite, Vue DevTools, dev overlays (launch-editor) | `export LAUNCH_EDITOR=forge` (Next.js: `REACT_EDITOR=forge`); the `forge` command must be on your `PATH` |
| React 19, Preact, Solid | a dev-only Babel plugin that adds `data-source-file`/`data-source-line` (shown on the page) |
| Angular | nothing to configure with `ng serve` |

## forge:// links and the launcher

```text
forge://open?file=/home/me/shop/app/Models/User.php&line=42&column=5
forge://open-symbol?name=UserCardComponent&kind=component
```

```sh
forge app/Models/User.php:42
forge --line 42 --column 5 app/Models/User.php
forge app/Models/User.php 42 5
```

The scheme is registered by the installers (and at runtime for AppImages and development
builds). A second launch is forwarded to the running Forge window. Files given on the command
line are trusted and open without asking. Full syntax:
[CLI arguments and forge:// links](docs/guide/reference/cli-and-links.md).

In a [remote project](docs/guide/user/remote-development.md) the settings page reads the project's frameworks
and applies `.env` changes on the host, and files the browser asks for open in the remote
project: the host's absolute paths below the project, paths relative to it, and paths of other
machines or containers (`/app/src/App.tsx`, `C:\Users\…\src\App.tsx`), which are matched by
their longest tail that exists in the project. Symbol lookups search the host's files.

## Live Edit

With the extension paired, saved style sheets are swapped in the open pages without a reload
(also while typing), and pages reload when HTML, scripts or templates they loaded are saved.
The extension asks Forge for changes with `GET /api/forge/live-edit` (paired browsers only).
See [Web tooling](docs/guide/user/web-tooling.md#live-edit) for the settings.

# Keymap reference

Forge's default keymaps are PHPStorm's (`crates/forge-keymap/data/phpstorm.json`), keyed by
PHPStorm's action ids. This page is the complete list. The other bundled keymaps (VS Code,
Eclipse, Sublime Text, Emacs) change only some of these shortcuts; see
[Keymap](docs/guide/user/keymap.md#other-keymaps). To learn the shortcuts the way the
JetBrains help teaches them, start with:

- [Keymap reference card](docs/guide/user/shortcuts/reference-card.md): the 62 most important shortcuts
  on one printable page;
- [Shortcuts by topic](docs/guide/user/shortcuts/index.md): one page per area (editing, navigation,
  search, refactoring, run and debug, Git, tool windows, general) that explains every
  implemented action, where it is in the menus, and shows its result;
- [Main menu reference](docs/guide/reference/main-menu/index.md): every menu entry with its shortcut and status;
- [Keymap](docs/guide/user/keymap.md): changing shortcuts, chords and focus contexts.

## How to read the tables

Actions are grouped as in Settings | Keymap. The **In Forge** column says whether the action does
something on this version (checked against the commands the UI registers):

- **yes**: implemented;
- **native**: handled by the editor or the operating system (undo, clipboard, caret movement);
- **—**: not implemented yet; the shortcut stays reserved and shows "*Action* is not available
  yet", and its main menu entry is disabled.

Shortcuts marked `Fn+…` in PHPStorm are left out. Several Forge commands implement PHPStorm
actions under another id (aliases): `search.everywhere` → `SearchEverywhere`, `settings.open` →
`ShowSettings`, `run.run` → `Run`, `run.debug` → `Debug`, `run.editConfigurations` →
`editRunConfigurations`, `git.branches` → `Git.Branches`, `git.commit` → `CheckinProject`,
`git.push` → `Vcs.Push`, `git.update` → `Vcs.UpdateProject`, `git.fetch` → `Git.Fetch`,
`git.newBranch` → `Git.CreateNewBranch`, `git.log` → `Vcs.Show.Log`, `git.annotate` →
`Annotate`, `php.generate` → `Generate`, `workspace.open` → `OpenFile`, `workspace.close` →
`CloseProject`, `ExtractVariable` → `IntroduceVariable`. `Exit` exists only in the desktop app.

## Commands without shortcuts

Forge also registers commands that are not PHPStorm actions. They have no default shortcut but
appear in Find Action and can be bound in Settings | Keymap, for example: Show Git Log
(`git.log`), Fetch (`git.fetch`), New Branch… (`git.newBranch`), Show Diff (`git.showDiff`),
Create Merge Request… (`forges.createMergeRequest`), View Pull/Merge Requests
(`forges.showMergeRequests`), Refresh Pull/Merge Requests (`forges.refresh`), Detect Project
Type (`project.redetect`), Reindex PHP Files (`php.reindex`), Generate PHPDoc Comment
(`php.generatePhpDoc`), Reindex Lua Files (`lua.reindex`), Refresh Symfony Index
(`symfony.refresh`), Refresh Doctrine Entities (`doctrine.refresh`), Refresh Services
(`Services.Refresh`), Pull Image… (`Docker.PullImage`), New SSH Connection…
(`Remote.NewSshConnection`), Reconnect to Remote Host (`Remote.Reconnect`), SSH
Configurations… (`remote.settings`), Language Servers… (`langservers.settings`), AI Providers…
(`ai.settings`), AI Assistant Settings… (`ai.assistantSettings`), Enable/Disable AI Inline
Completion (`ai.toggleInlineCompletion`), Open AI Chat (`AIChat.Focus`), New AI Chat (`AIChat.NewChat`), Browser
Companion Settings (`BrowserCompanion.Settings`), Keymap Settings (`settings.keymap`).

Source: docs/guide/reference/main-menu/index.md

# Main menu reference

Forge's main menu has PHPStorm's structure. Open it with the ☰ button or `Alt+\`, or show it as a
menu bar (Settings | Appearance & Behavior | Appearance | **Main menu**); see
[Workbench: Main menu](docs/guide/user/workbench.md#main-menu).

Entries Forge has not implemented yet are visible but **disabled**, so the menu doubles as a map
of what is there and what is still to come. Plugins add their own entries (Tools | Docker,
Tools | Laravel, Tools | Symfony, Run | Start Listening for PHP Debug Connections) while they are
active.

| Menu | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| [File](docs/guide/reference/main-menu/file.md) | projects, new files and scratches, settings, Save All |
| [Edit](docs/guide/reference/main-menu/edit.md) | undo, clipboard, find and replace, Find in Files, selection, line editing |
| [View](docs/guide/reference/main-menu/view.md) | tool windows, appearance, Parameter Info, Recent Files |
| [Navigate](docs/guide/reference/main-menu/navigate.md) | back/forward, Search Everywhere, Go to Class/File/Symbol/Line, declarations, problems |
| [Code](docs/guide/reference/main-menu/code.md) | completion, Generate, folding, comments, Reformat Code, moving lines |
| [Refactor](docs/guide/reference/main-menu/refactor.md) | refactorings (not implemented yet) |
| [Run](docs/guide/reference/main-menu/run.md) | run configurations, debugging actions, breakpoints, Xdebug listener |
| [Tools](docs/guide/reference/main-menu/tools.md) | terminal, Docker, Laravel, Symfony |
| [Git](docs/guide/reference/main-menu/git.md) | commit, push, update, branches, log, blame |
| [Window](docs/guide/reference/main-menu/window.md) | active tool window, editor tabs |
| [Help](docs/guide/reference/main-menu/help.md) | Find Action, Keymap Reference, About |

The menu structure, labels, mnemonics and enabled states are computed in Rust
(`crates/forge-keymap/src/menu.rs`); an entry is enabled when a command implements its action.
These pages were generated from the menu of the browser-mode Laravel demo project.


---

Source: docs/guide/reference/main-menu/file.md

# File menu

Projects, new files and scratches, settings and saving. Open it with ☰ (`Alt+\`) or from the menu bar, see [Main menu](docs/guide/user/workbench.md#main-menu).

# Refactor menu

Refactorings. Every entry works: Refactor This, Rename, Rename File, Change Signature, Extract/Introduce Variable, Constant, Field, Parameter, Method, Interface, Superclass and Component (Vue, React), Inline, Move, Copy, Safe Delete, Pull Members Up, Push Members Down and Make Static. | Debugging Actions › Evaluate Expression… | `Alt+F8` | `Alt+F8` | yes | Evaluates a PHP expression in the current frame. [More](docs/guide/user/debugging.md#the-debug-tool-window) |

| Debugging Actions › Show Execution Point | `Alt+F10` | `Alt+F10` | yes | Shows the line where the debugger is paused. [More](docs/guide/user/debugging.md#the-debug-tool-window) |
| **Toggle Breakpoint** | | | | submenu |
| Toggle Breakpoint › Line Breakpoint | `Ctrl+F8` | `Cmd+F8` | yes | Adds or removes a line breakpoint at the caret. [More](docs/guide/user/debugging.md#breakpoints) |
| Toggle Breakpoint › Temporary Line Breakpoint | `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+F8` | `Cmd+Alt+Shift+F8` | yes | Adds a breakpoint that is removed once it is hit. [More](docs/guide/user/debugging.md#breakpoint-properties-logpoints-and-temporary-breakpoints) |

| Start Listening for PHP Debug Connections | — | — | yes | Starts or stops listening for incoming Xdebug connections on port 9003. [More](docs/guide/user/debugging.md#listening-for-connections) |
| Web Server Debug Validation… | — | — | yes | Checks the Xdebug configuration of a web server or CLI interpreter. [More](docs/guide/user/debugging.md#web-server-debug-validation) |

**Start Listening for PHP Debug Connections** and **Web Server Debug Validation…** are added by the Xdebug plugin (`forge.xdebug`) in PHP projects; Start Listening is a toggle with a check mark while Forge listens.

In C/C++ projects the C/C++ plugin (`forge.cpp`) adds **Run with Valgrind Memcheck** and
**Profile with perf** after Debug; they run the selected CMake Application, Google Test or
Catch2 configuration under Valgrind or perf ([more](docs/guide/user/cpp-tools.md)).

# Settings reference

All settings are declared by plugin manifests (`[[contributions.settings]]` in
`app/src-tauri/plugins/*.toml`) and shown on the Settings page whose id is their `group`. Values
are layered: default < user (`<config dir>/forge/settings.toml`) < Settings for New Projects
(`<config dir>/forge/new-project-settings.toml`, project-level settings only) < project
(`<project>/.forge/settings.toml`). See [Settings and themes](docs/guide/user/settings-and-themes.md).

- **Type**: `bool`, `int`, `number`, `string`, `enum` (allowed values listed), `path`,
  `list` (a list of strings) or `objects` (a list of tables with string values, edited in a
  table). Ranges are given as (min–max).
- **Scope**: `user` settings are global; `user, project` settings can also be stored per
  project ("For current project" in the dialog).
-: the option is declared and shown, but no code reads it on this version.

Settings written by Forge itself and not declared in a manifest:

| Key | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `plugins.disabled` | list of disabled plugin ids (Settings \| Plugins) |
| `project.announcedFrameworks` | `<root>#<framework>` pairs whose "project detected" balloon was shown |
| `langservers.servers.<id>.enabled` | per-server toggle on the Language Servers page |
| `langservers.servers.<id>.path` | custom executable of a language server |
| `langservers.servers.<id>.settings` | extra JSON settings of a language server |
| `langservers.hints.dismissed` | servers whose install banner was turned off (also declared below) |
| `<language>.codeStyle.<option>`, `editor.codeStyle.<option>` | the code style options of the Default scheme (user settings) and the Project scheme (project settings), e.g. `php.codeStyle.indent`, `php.codeStyle.spaces.afterComma`, `editor.codeStyle.hardWrapAt`; the options are listed in [Editor](docs/guide/user/editor.md#code-style) and defined in `crates/forge-codestyle` |
| `editor.codeStyle.scheme` | the scheme the project uses: `default`, `project` or an IDE scheme id |
| `editor.codeStyle.schemes.<id>.name`, `editor.codeStyle.schemes.<id>.values.<language>.<option>` | further IDE code style schemes (Duplicate, Copy to IDE, Import Scheme) |
| `inspections.profiles` | IDE inspection profiles (Default when changed, and copies): a list of `{ name, level, tools }` (Settings \| Editor \| Inspections, page id `editor.inspections`) |
| `inspections.severities` | custom severities `{ id, name, editor }` |
| `inspections.profile` | the profile the project uses (project settings; user settings without a project) |
| `inspections.projectProfiles` | project inspection profiles besides Project Default; each is stored in `.forge/inspectionProfiles/<Name>.xml` |

# File types reference

Detection order: file names and path patterns, then the longest matching extension, then the
interpreter of a `#!` line. File names may contain `*` anywhere and `/` to match a path suffix
(`config/services*.yaml`). Bundled types indent with 4 spaces unless a plugin type says
otherwise. See [File types and syntax highlighting](docs/guide/user/file-types.md).

## File types of plugins

Active only while their plugin is active; a plugin type with the id of a bundled type replaces it.

| Id | Name | Plugin | Extensions | File names | Shebang interpreters | Indent |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `python` | Python | `forge.python` | `.py`, `.pyw`, `.pyi`, `.pyx`, `.pxd`, `.gyp` | `SConstruct`, `SConscript`, `wscript`, `.pythonstartup`, `.pythonrc` | `python`, `python3`, `pypy`, `pypy3` | 4 |

## Template data languages

Template types (marked *Template* above) highlight the content between their tags in a data
language: `html` (default), `xml`, `latex`, `css`, `scss`, `less`, `javascript`, `typescript`,
`json`, `sql`, `yaml`, `ini`, `shell`, `go`, `text`.

Chosen from the setting `templates.dataLanguages` (`pattern=language` entries), then from a
compound file name, then HTML. Compound inner extensions:

| Inner extension | Data language |
| --- | --- |
| `html`, `htm`, `xhtml` | HTML |
| `xml`, `svg`, `rss`, `atom` | XML |
| `tex`, `latex`, `sty`, `cls` | LaTeX |
| `css` / `scss` / `less` | CSS / SCSS / Less |
| `js`, `mjs` | JavaScript |
| `ts` | TypeScript |
| `json` | JSON |
| `sql` | SQL |
| `yml`, `yaml` | YAML |
| `ini`, `env`, `conf` | INI / Properties |
| `sh` | Shell Script |
| `go` | Go |
| `txt`, `text`, `md`, `csv`, `eml` | Plain text |

Example: `invoice.tex.twig` → LaTeX, `report.sql.twig` → SQL, `style.css.tpl` → CSS,
`welcome.text.erb` → plain text.

## Soft wraps

Files matching `editor.softWrapFiles` (default `*.md; *.txt; *.rst; *.adoc`) are soft-wrapped
when `editor.softWraps` is on.

Source: docs/guide/reference/language-servers.md

# Language servers reference

Generated from `crates/forge-langservers/catalog.toml` and `pack_servers.toml`. Servers are
grouped as on Settings | Languages & Frameworks | Language Servers. See
[Language servers](docs/guide/user/language-servers.md) for how detection, installation and per-server
settings work.

- **Install**: npm commands (`npm install -g …`) become managed installs into Forge's server
  folder, never global ones; Forge downloads Node.js itself when none (>= 18) is installed.
  "Download … from PyPI" fetches the official wheel of the platform (ruff, ty), checks its
  SHA-256 against PyPI and copies the executable to `<data dir>/forge/langservers/bin`.
  Commands with `sudo` are only shown for you to run. Links are download pages.
- **Alternative group**: only the first enabled and installed server of a group starts.
- **Needs plugin**: the server starts only while that plugin is enabled and active.
- The PHP servers are started by the PHP pack (Settings | Languages & Frameworks | PHP), not by
  the catalog.

## Languages

Languages the catalog detects in a project (the project scan reads up to
`langservers.scanLimit` files, skipping ignored files, `node_modules` and `vendor`).

| Language id | Name | Extensions | File names |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `javascript` | JavaScript | `.js`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`, `.jsx` |  |
| `typescript` | TypeScript | `.ts`, `.mts`, `.cts`, `.tsx` |  |
| `vue` | Vue | `.vue` |  |
| `svelte` | Svelte | `.svelte` |  |
| `astro` | Astro | `.astro` |  |
| `html` | HTML | `.html`, `.htm`, `.xhtml` |  |
| `css` | CSS | `.css` |  |
| `scss` | SCSS | `.scss` |  |
| `less` | Less | `.less` |  |
| `json` | JSON | `.json`, `.jsonc`, `.json5` | `.babelrc`, `.eslintrc`, `.prettierrc` |

# CLI arguments and forge:// links

## The `forge` launcher

```text
forge [PROJECT_DIR | FILE[:LINE[:COLUMN]] | forge://…] …
```

| Form | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `forge` | start with the Welcome screen |
| `forge ~/Projects/shop` | open a directory as the project |
| `forge src/App.tsx` | open a file (in the project it belongs to) |
| `forge src/App.tsx:12` / `forge src/App.tsx:12:3` | at line 12 (column 3) |
| `forge --line 12 --column 3 src/App.tsx` | JetBrains style; short `-l`, `-c` |
| `forge src/App.tsx 12 3` | `launch-editor` style: numbers after a file are its line and column |
| `forge 'forge://open?file=…&line=…'` | a link (treated like a link from a web page) |

- Relative paths are resolved against the current directory. Arguments that name nothing on
  disk are skipped with a warning (in the log).
- Other options starting with `-` are ignored.
- If Forge is already running, the arguments are handed to the running window
  (single instance) and the new process exits.
- Files given on the command line are **trusted**: they open without a confirmation, also
  outside known projects.
- Log output: set `RUST_LOG` (e.g. `RUST_LOG=debug forge`).

### `forge --mcp-stdio`

A stdio MCP server for clients that only start stdio servers (Claude Desktop, Codex): it
forwards newline-delimited JSON-RPC from stdin to the running Forge's MCP server and writes the
answers to stdout. It finds the server through `<config dir>/forge/mcp-server.json` and takes
the token from the keychain or `FORGE_MCP_TOKEN`. See [MCP Server](docs/guide/user/mcp-server.md).

### `forge inspect`

```text
forge inspect <project> <profile.xml|profile name> <output dir> [-format xml|json|html] [-d <directory>] [-fail-on <severity>] [-v0|-v1|-v2]
```

The command-line inspector: runs the profile's inspections over the project without a window
and writes the results (one XML file per inspection plus `.descriptions.xml`, `inspections.json`
or `index.html`). Exit code 0, 1 with `-fail-on` when a problem of that severity or worse was
found, 2 for wrong arguments. See [Inspections](docs/guide/user/inspections.md#command-line-inspector).

The deb and rpm packages put `forge` on the `PATH`. For the AppImage, create a link yourself,
e.g. `ln -s ~/Applications/Forge_0.1.0_amd64.AppImage ~/.local/bin/forge`.

## forge:// links

Registered as a URL scheme by the installers; AppImages and development builds register it when
they start (Linux, Windows).

### `forge://open`

```text
forge://open?file=/home/me/shop/app/Models/User.php&line=42&column=5
```

| Parameter | Aliases | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `file` | `path`, `url` | absolute path, `file://` URL, or a path relative to `project` (required) |
| `line` | `l` | 1-based line |
| `column` | `col`, `c` | 1-based column |
| `project` | | project root for relative paths |
| `symbol` | | symbol to locate when no line is given |

`forge:open?…` (without `//`) works too. Values are percent-decoded. Absurd line/column numbers
and over-long paths are rejected.

### `forge://open-symbol`

```text
forge://open-symbol?name=UserCardComponent&kind=component
```

Finds the declaration of a component (`kind=component`) or class (`kind=class`) by name in the
open and recent projects and opens it.

### Confirmation

Links can come from any web page, so files outside the open project ask first: a file of a
recent project offers to open that project; a file outside any project asks before it opens.

## Browser Companion HTTP API

A small HTTP server on `127.0.0.1:63342` (or the next nine ports; setting
`browserCompanion.port`) serves the browser extension:

| Request | Body | Auth |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/forge/ping` | — | none |
| `POST /api/forge/pair` | `{ "code": "123456", "name": "Chrome" }` → token | none (one-time code) |
| `POST /api/forge/open` | `{ "file", "line"?, "column"?, "project"?, "symbol"? }` | `Authorization: Bearer <token>` |
| `POST /api/forge/open-symbol` | `{ "name", "kind"? }` | `Authorization: Bearer <token>` |

Requests need a loopback `Host` header and no web-page `Origin` (browser extension origins
only). Pairing codes are 6 digits, valid for five minutes and for one use. See
[Browser Companion](docs/guide/user/browser-companion.md).

# Config, cache and data locations

Forge uses the platform's standard folders (Rust's `dirs` crate):

| Placeholder | Linux | macOS | Windows |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<config dir>` | `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` or `~/.config` | `~/Library/Application Support` | `%APPDATA%` (`C:\Users\<you>\AppData\Roaming`) |
| `<cache dir>` | `$XDG_CACHE_HOME` or `~/.cache` | `~/Library/Caches` | `%LOCALAPPDATA%` |
| `<data dir>` | `$XDG_DATA_HOME` or `~/.local/share` | `~/Library/Application Support` | `%APPDATA%` |
| `<state dir>` | `$XDG_STATE_HOME` or `~/.local/state` | `~/Library/Application Support` | `%LOCALAPPDATA%` |

## User configuration — `<config dir>/forge/`

| File | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `settings.toml` | user settings (including keymap changes and disabled plugins) |
| `new-project-settings.toml` | [Settings for New Projects](docs/guide/user/settings-and-themes.md#settings-for-new-projects): defaults of project-level settings |
| `recent-projects.json` | the Welcome screen's recent projects |
| `trusted-projects.toml` | [trusted projects and trusted locations](docs/guide/user/project-trust.md) (`projects`, `locations`: local paths or `ssh://user@host:port/path`) |
| `ai.toml` | AI providers and model choices (no keys) |
| `forges.toml` | GitHub/GitLab/Forgejo accounts (no tokens) |
| `ssh.toml` | saved SSH configurations (no passwords) |
| `dataSources.toml` | global database data sources (no passwords) |
| `browser-companion.json` | paired browsers (SHA-256 hashes of their tokens only) |
| `mcp-server.json` | port and process id of the running MCP server, for `forge --mcp-stdio` (no token) |
| `dialog-windows.json` | size and position of dialog windows |
| `updates.json` | update checks: time of the last check, the skipped version and a postponed ("Later") version |
| `scratches/` | scratch files and buffers |
| `scratches.json` | per-scratch options (the data source of SQL scratches) |
| `settings-sync-state.json` | [Settings Sync](docs/guide/user/settings-and-themes.md#settings-sync): the groups' hashes at the last sync and its report |
| `settings-sync-backups/<ms>/<group>.data` | local settings groups that lost a Settings Sync conflict |

## Caches — `<cache dir>/forge/`

| Path | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `php-index/<project>-<hash>.json` | PHP index cache per project |
| `db-models/<data source>-<hash>.json` | the Database tool window's model of each data source (schemas, tables, routines, roles), so the tree shows without connecting; refreshed with Refresh |
| `project-windows.json` | the running project windows (one Forge instance each) and their local control ports, for Window \| Next Project Window |
| `json-schemas/<sha256 of the URL>.json` | downloaded JSON schemas and the SchemaStore catalog (only with remote JSON schemas allowed), refreshed daily |
| `php-stubs/<version>/` | JetBrains phpstorm-stubs for Go to Declaration on PHP's own symbols (downloaded on first use, checked against a pinned digest of its files, with its `LICENSE`) |
| `packagist/p2/<vendor>/<package>.json`, `packagist/search/` | Packagist package metadata (6 hours) and searches (1 hour) for Composer completion, versions and outdated packages (only while `php.composer.packagist` is on) |
| `vulnerabilities/<project hash>/<tool>-<folder hash>.json` | the last result of each audit tool of the vulnerable dependency check, with the hash of the manifest and lock file it was made from; reused on project open while the files are unchanged and younger than `vulnerabilities.cacheHours` |
| `profiles/<project>/<time>-<name>.pstats` (+ `.json`) | cProfile snapshots of Run \| Profile (Python) for the Profiler tool window; the newest `python.profiler.snapshots` are kept |
| `pypi/json/<name>.json`, `pypi/search/` | PyPI package metadata (12 hours) and searches (1 hour) for Python Packages, requirements completion and latest versions (only while `python.packages.pypi` is on) |
| `code-review/<host>-<server>-<repository>/<number>.json` | review mode of a pull/merge request: viewed files (with a digest of their diff), pending review comments and the AI summary and findings of the last head commit |
| `php-lsp/` | php-lsp's index cache and unpacked PHP stubs (`storagePath`) |
| `jdtls/config-<version>/`, `jdtls/workspaces/<project>-<hash>/` | Eclipse JDT LS: its OSGi configuration and the workspace data of each project (never inside the project) |
| `jupyter/kernel-<key>.json` | connection files of running Jupyter kernels (ports and signing key, readable only by you); deleted when the kernel stops |
| `shell-integration/` | the bash and zsh scripts of the terminal's shell integration (also on remote hosts, in their cache dir) |
| `settings-sync-git/` | the clone of your Settings Sync git repository |
| `remote-edit/<server>/…` | temporary copies of the files opened with Edit Remote File (Remote Host tool window); removed when the tab closes |

The search index lives in `<cache dir>/Forge/search/<hash of the project root>.bin`. The
embedded browser engine (the webview) keeps its cache in `<cache dir>/dev.forge.ide` (WebView2 on
Windows: the `Cache` folders of `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dev.forge.ide\EBWebView\Default`).

Caches can be deleted at any time; Forge rebuilds them. File | [Invalidate Caches…](docs/guide/user/repair-ide.md#invalidate-caches)
deletes them for you on the next start. Without a platform cache folder the PHP
index falls back to `<project>/.forge/cache/php-index.json`.

## Data — `<data dir>/forge/`

| Path | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `langservers/` | language servers installed by Forge (`node_modules/.bin`, `package.json`, `.forge-update-check.json`; `bin/` and `pypi-tools.json` for ruff and ty from PyPI) |
| `plugins/installed.json`, `plugins/<id>/` | [third-party plugins](docs/guide/user/plugins-and-packs.md#third-party-plugins): versions, enablement, granted permissions, and each unpacked package |
| `plugin-data/<id>/` | a plugin's own data (`${pluginData}`), removed with the plugin |
| `composer/composer.phar` | composer.phar downloaded from getcomposer.org with Settings \| PHP \| Composer, checked against its published SHA-256 sum |
| `runtimes/node-<version>/` | the Node.js build Forge downloaded for language servers (only when no Node.js 18+ was installed) |
| `projects/<name>-<hash>/bookmarks.json` | the bookmarks and bookmark lists of a project (`<hash>` of the project root, for remote projects of `user@host:/path`); kept out of the project |
| `projects/<name>-<hash>/local-history/` | the project's [Local History](docs/guide/user/local-history.md): `changes.jsonl` (one change set per line: saves, refactorings, VCS operations, external changes, labels) and `content/` (file contents, zlib-compressed and stored once per content hash); cleaned up after the configured working days and size; kept out of the project |
| `projects/<name>-<hash>/changelists.json` | the changelists of the Commit tool window (names, comments, the active list, which files and changes belong where); kept out of the project |
| `projects/<name>-<hash>/shelf/<id>/` | shelved changelists (Git ▸ Shelve Changes): `changes.json` (name, date, branch, files) and `shelved.patch`; kept out of the project |
| `pending-maintenance.json` | work for the next start written by Invalidate Caches and Restore Default Settings; removed once it ran |
| `chat-history/<project>-<hash>/<chat>.json` | the AI chats of each project (the newest 100), see [AI](docs/guide/user/ai.md) |

Restore Default Settings copies `<config dir>/forge` to `<config dir>/forge-backup-<date>-<time>`
first (the time is UTC).

## State — `<state dir>/forge/`

| Path | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `layouts/<project>-<hash>.json` | the tool window layout (placements, open tool windows, sizes) and open editor tabs of each project |
| `layouts/_default.json` | the layout stored with Window \| Layouts \| Store Current Layout as Default |

## In the project — `<project>/.forge/`

| File | Content | Commit? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `settings.toml` | project settings ("For current project") | yes |
| `runConfigurations.toml` | shared run configurations ("Store as project file") | yes |
| `runConfigurations.local.toml` | local run configurations, the selection, templates | no |
| `breakpoints.json` | Xdebug breakpoints | optional |
| `php-servers.json` | PHP servers and path mappings | yes |
| `dataSources.toml` | project data sources (no passwords) | yes |
| `database/virtual.toml` | virtual foreign keys and columns of the Database tool window | yes |
| `deployment.toml` | deployment servers, mappings, excluded paths and the default server (no passwords) | yes |
| `inspectionProfiles/*.xml` | project inspection profiles in PHPStorm's format (`Project_Default.xml` once it differs from the defaults) | yes |

Add `.forge/runConfigurations.local.toml` (and `.forge/cache/` if it appears) to your
`.gitignore`. In the project root, `http-client.env.json` and `http-client.private.env.json` are
read by the [HTTP client](docs/guide/user/scratches-and-http.md#environments).

## Secrets — the OS keychain

Secrets are stored with the system keychain (Secret Service/GNOME Keyring/KWallet on Linux,
Keychain on macOS, Credential Manager on Windows), never in files:

| Service | Account | Secret |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `forge-ai` | provider id | AI provider API key |
| `forge-forges` | account id | GitHub/GitLab/Forgejo token |
| `forge-ssh` | SSH configuration id | SSH password or key passphrase |
| `forge-db` | data source id | database password |
| `forge-deploy` | `ftp://user@host:port` | FTP/FTPS deployment password |
| `forge-containers` | `registry:<server>` | Docker registry password |
| `forge-jupyter` | `server:<base URL>` | Jupyter server token |
| `forge-mcp` | `server-token` | bearer token of the MCP server |

## Remote hosts

| Path on the host | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `~/.cache/forge-agent/<version>/` | the uploaded Forge agent |
| `~/.ssh/known_hosts` (local) | host keys you accepted |

## WebView data

The desktop app's WebView keeps its own storage in the app's data folder (identifier
`dev.forge.ide`, e.g. `~/.local/share/dev.forge.ide` on Linux). Forge keeps only conveniences
there (the last theme while settings load); everything that matters is in the files above.

## Clean slate

To reset Forge completely, quit it and delete `<config dir>/forge`, `<cache dir>/forge`,
`<data dir>/forge` and `<state dir>/forge`, and remove the `forge-*` entries from your keychain.

# Environment variables

## Read by Forge

### Forge's own

| Variable | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `FORGE_NEW_WINDOW` | set by Forge when it starts another project window (Open Project › New Window): the instance skips the single-instance hand-over, the splash and the update check; it is removed from the environment at once, so terminals do not inherit it |
| `FORGE_GIT` | git executable to use instead of `git` on the `PATH` (e.g. a bundled git on Windows) |
| `FORGE_REMOTE_AGENT_DIR` | folder with the remote agent binaries (`forge-remote-agent-<arch>-linux[.gz]`), searched before the bundle's `agents/` folder |
| `FORGE_AGENT_LOG` | log filter of the remote agent on the host (e.g. `debug`); the agent logs to stderr |
| `FORGE_MCP_TOKEN` | bearer token for `forge --mcp-stdio` when the system keychain has none (see [MCP Server](docs/guide/user/mcp-server.md)) |
| `RUST_LOG` | log filter of the desktop app (e.g. `RUST_LOG=forge_lsp=debug`; `forge_app_lib::startup=debug` logs the splash steps) |
| `FORGE_SIMULATE_UPDATE` | e.g. `0.2.0`: the splash and Help \| Check for Updates… offer this version as a simulated update with a fake download; nothing is installed (for development, works in any build) |
| `APPIMAGE` | set by the AppImage runtime; Forge then registers the `forge://` scheme at startup |
| `APPIMAGE_EXTRACT_AND_RUN` | read by the AppImage runtime: `1` runs without FUSE (see [Installation](docs/guide/getting-started/installation.md#running-the-appimage-without-fuse)) |

### Credentials (fallbacks when nothing is stored in the keychain)

| Variable | Used for |
| --- | --- |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | Anthropic provider |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | OpenAI provider |
| `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` | OpenRouter provider |
| `GITLAB_TOKEN` | gitlab.com |
| `FORGEJO_TOKEN`, `GITEA_TOKEN` | Forgejo / Gitea (public servers) |
| `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GH_TOKEN` | github.com |
| `AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT` | Azure DevOps Services (`dev.azure.com` organizations) |

### Tools and environment

| Variable | Used for |
| --- | --- |
| `PATH`, `PATHEXT` | finding git, php, composer, node, language servers, agent CLIs |
| `SHELL` | the terminal's default shell (Linux/macOS) |
| `ComSpec` | the last-resort terminal shell on Windows |
| `HOME`, `USERPROFILE`, `APPDATA` | home and config folders |
| `NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX` | npm's global folder when looking for language servers |
| `VIMRUNTIME` | Neovim runtime for lua-language-server's Neovim environment |
| `DOCKER_HOST`, `DOCKER_CONTEXT` | the Docker daemon (also `ssh://` hosts) or Docker context when `docker.connection` is `auto` |
| `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` | rootless Docker socket |
| `KUBECONFIG` | kubeconfig when `kubernetes.kubeconfig` is empty |
| `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` | kept if set; otherwise Forge runs git with `ssh -o BatchMode=yes` |
| `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP`, `XDG_SESSION_DESKTOP`, `DESKTOP_SESSION`, `KDE_FULL_SESSION`, `GNOME_DESKTOP_SESSION_ID` | detecting the desktop for "Window controls: Match the system" |
| `USER`, `USERNAME`, `HOSTNAME` | default values (SSH user, display names) |

## Set by Forge for processes it starts

| Variable | When |
| --- | --- |
| `XDEBUG_MODE=debug`, `XDEBUG_SESSION=FORGE`, `XDEBUG_CONFIG=client_host=127.0.0.1 client_port=<port> idekey=FORGE`, `PHP_IDE_CONFIG=serverName=<server>` | Debug of a PHP run configuration |
| `NODE_OPTIONS=<web.npm.debugArguments>` | Debug of an npm script |
| the entries of `terminal.environment` | new terminal tabs |
| the configuration's **Environment variables** | run configurations |
| `GIT_SSH_COMMAND=ssh -o BatchMode=yes` | git commands, unless already set |

## Build and development

| Variable | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `FORGE_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1` | `cargo test -p forge-app` rewrites the browser-mode snapshots of the plugin manifests and project generators |
| `FORGE_URL` | base URL of the dev server for `scripts/screenshots.mjs` (default `http://localhost:1420`) |
| `CHROMIUM_PATH` | Chromium for the screenshot script |
| `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` | separate target folder per git worktree |
| `CC_<triple>`, `CFLAGS_<triple>`, `CARGO_TARGET_AARCH64_UNKNOWN_LINUX_MUSL_LINKER` | cross-compiling the remote agents (`pnpm agents`) |
| `FORGE_UPDATER_PUBKEY` | at build time: the updater public key compiled into the app; without it the build never checks for updates (see [Release builds](docs/guide/developer/release-builds.md#updates-and-signing)) |
| `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY`, `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD` | at build time: sign the updater artifacts; `pnpm tauri build` / `pnpm release` turn on `createUpdaterArtifacts` only when the key is set |

# Plugins reference

Generated from the manifests in `app/src-tauri/plugins/*.toml`. A plugin is active when it is
enabled (Settings | Plugins) and, if it lists project types, when the open project uses one of
them (a language, framework, pack or tool id from
[project detection](docs/guide/getting-started/project-detection.md)). Disabling a plugin also disables
the plugins that depend on it.

Pack ids: `core`, `phpforge`, `webforge`, `luaforge`, `pyforge`, `javaforge`, `goforge`, `rustforge`, `rubyforge`, `kotlinforge`, `cforge`, `dotnetforge`, and `scriptforge` / `configforge` for the
script and config language plugins.
