Source: docs/guide/developer/plugins/api-reference.md

# Plugin API reference

The types are in [`sdk/plugin-api/index.d.ts`](sdk/plugin-api/index.d.ts)
(`@forge/plugin-api`); Rust validates manifests in `forge_plugins::manifest`.

## The manifest: `forge-plugin.json`

```json
{
  "manifestVersion": 1,
  "id": "acme.todo-sync",
  "name": "TODO Sync",
  "version": "2.3.0",
  "publisher": "Acme",
  "description": "Turns TODO comments into issues.",
  "license": "MIT",
  "homepage": "https://acme.dev/todo-sync",
  "engines": { "forge": ">=0.1.0" },
  "main": "dist/plugin.js",
  "activationEvents": ["workspaceContains:.todo-sync.json", "onCommand:acme.todo-sync.push"],
  "permissions": { "network": ["api.acme.dev"], "fs": { "read": ["${project}"] } },
  "contributes": { "commands": [{ "id": "acme.todo-sync.push", "title": "Push TODOs" }] }
}
```

| Field | Rules |
| --- | --- |
| `manifestVersion` | `1` |
| `id` | lowercase reverse-DNS (`publisher.name`, letters, digits, `-`), at most 64 characters; `forge.*` is reserved |
| `name` | 1 to 64 characters |
| `version` | SemVer (`1.2.3`, `1.0.0-beta.1`) |
| `engines.forge` | SemVer range of Forge versions (`>=0.1.0`, `^1.2`); installing on another version is refused |
| `main` | the UI bundle, a relative `.js` path inside the package |
| `backend` | reserved: `{ "kind": "wasm", "module" }` or `{ "kind": "process", "command", "args" }`; not run yet (see [Plugin SDK](docs/guide/developer/plugins/index.md#what-is-deferred)) |
| `activationEvents` | when `main` is loaded, see below |
| `permissions` | see [Permissions](docs/guide/developer/plugins/permissions.md) |
| `contributes` | see below |
| `l10n` | optional translations by locale: `{ "de": { "plugin.<id>.name": "…", "action.<command id>": "…", "toolwindow.<id>.title": "…", "setting.<key>.title": "…" } }`; keys and message syntax as in [Localization](docs/guide/developer/localization.md#plugin-manifests) |

Every contributed id (commands, status items, tool windows, settings pages) and setting key
must start with the plugin id and a dot: `acme.todo-sync.push`.

### Activation events

| Event | Loads the plugin |
| --- | --- |
| `onStartup` | when Forge starts (and after install) |
| `onCommand:<command id>` | the first time the command runs |
| `onView:<tool window id>` | when the tool window is opened |
| `onLanguage:<file type id>` | when a file of that type becomes the active editor (`markdown`, `php`, …) |
| `workspaceContains:<path>` | when the open project has that file (relative path) |

Commands and tool windows also load their plugin on first use without an event.

### Contributions

| Key | Entries |
| --- | --- |
| `commands` | `{ id, title, category? }`: actions in Find Action and the Keymap settings (group Plugins/<name>) |
| `keybindings` | `{ command, key, keymap? }`: default shortcuts, e.g. `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+W`; `keymap: "macos"` or `"default"` limits one to a platform keymap |
| `statusItems` | `{ id, alignment: "left" \| "right", order, command? }`: text set with `forge.statusBar.update`, clicking runs `command` |
| `toolWindows` | `{ id, title, anchor: "left" \| "right" \| "bottom", icon?, order }`: content set with `forge.toolWindows.setHtml` |
| `settingsPages` | `{ id, title }`: a page under Tools in the Settings dialog showing the plugin's settings |
| `settings` | typed settings like the built-in ones (`key`, `title`, `description`, `type` = `bool`, `int`, `number`, `string`, `enum`, `path`, `list`, `default`, `group` = one of the plugin's pages, `order`) |
| `languages` | file types: `{ id, name, extensions, fileNames, indentSize? }` |

## The `forge` API

Inside the bundle, `forge` is a global; every call returns a promise.

### Lifecycle

```ts
export function activate(context: PluginContext): void | Promise<void>;
```

`context.plugin` is `{ id, name, version }`; push disposables to `context.subscriptions`.

### `forge.commands`

| Call | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `register(id, handler)` | implement a contributed command |
| `execute(id)` | run any action: a PHPStorm action id (`ReformatCode`) or a plugin command |

### `forge.statusBar`

`update(id, { text, tooltip? })` sets a status item; empty text hides it.

### `forge.toolWindows`

| Call | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `setHtml(id, html)` | the tool window's content, rendered in its own sandboxed frame with `--bg`, `--fg`, `--fg-muted`, `--accent` and `--border` from the current theme |
| `postMessage(id, data)` | send data to the frame's scripts (`forgeView.onMessage(cb)`) |
| `onMessage(id, callback)` | receive what the frame sends with `forgeView.postMessage(data)` |

### `forge.editor`

| Call | Permission | Does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `getActive()` | `editor: read` | `{ path, language, text, selection: { from, to } }` or `null` |
| `onDidChange(callback)` | `editor: read` | the active editor or its text changed (debounced) |
| `replaceSelection(text)` | `editor: write` | replace the selection of the active editor (one undo step) |

### `forge.window`

`showMessage(text, type?)` shows a balloon (`info`, `warning`, `error`) in the Plugins
notification group.

### `forge.settings`

`get(key)`, `set(key, value)` (user settings, checked against the setting's type) and
`onDidChange(callback)` for the plugin's own settings, or keys granted by `permissions.settings`.

### `forge.workspace`

`root()`: the open project's folder, or `null`.

### `forge.fs`, `forge.http`, `forge.process`

| Call | Permission |
| --- | --- |
| `fs.readFile(path)` | `fs.read` (or `fs.write`) scope covering the absolute path |
| `fs.writeFile(path, contents)` | `fs.write` scope; in the project only outside Safe Mode |
| `http.fetch(url, { method, headers, body })` | `network` host; redirects only to granted hosts; returns `{ status, headers, body }` |
| `process.run(program, args)` | `process` program; runs in the project folder, never in Safe Mode; returns `{ exitCode, stdout, stderr }` |

Refused calls reject with a message like
``plugin `acme.todo-sync` has no permission to connect to evil.example``.


---

Source: docs/guide/developer/plugins/permissions.md

# Plugin permissions

A plugin declares everything it needs outside its sandbox in `permissions`; the user sees the
list before installing (most sensitive first) and grants it as a whole. An update that asks for
more marks the new entries and must be accepted again.

```json
"permissions": {
  "fs": { "read": ["${project}"], "write": ["${pluginData}"] },
  "network": ["api.acme.dev", "*.cdn.acme.dev"],
  "process": ["git"],
  "settings": ["editor.font.*", "appearance.theme"],
  "editor": ["read", "write"]
}
```

| Permission | Values | Prompt line | Checked by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `process` | program names, no paths | Start programs (high) | `plugin_host_run` |
| `fs.write` | `${project}`, `${pluginData}`, optionally `/<sub folder>` | Write files (high in the project, low in its data folder) | `plugin_host_write_file` |
| `network` | host names; `*.example.com` covers subdomains only | Connect to the internet (medium) | `plugin_host_fetch` (also every redirect) |
| `editor: write` | | Edit the open file (medium) | the host |
| `fs.read` | as `fs.write`; writable scopes are readable | Read files (medium) | `plugin_host_read_file` |
| `settings` | keys or `prefix.*` | Read and change IDE settings (medium) | `plugin_host_setting_*` |
| `editor: read` | | Read the open file (low) | the host |

What needs no permission: the plugin's own settings (`<plugin id>.…`), its contributions,
balloons, tool window HTML, running IDE actions with `forge.commands.execute`.

## Enforcement

- The plugin's code runs in a sandboxed iframe with an opaque origin and
  `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'`: it cannot reach Forge's DOM, Tauri's IPC,
  storage or the network. Every request goes through the host by `postMessage`.
- File paths must be absolute. Forge resolves `..` and symbolic links before comparing them
  with the granted folders, so a link inside an allowed folder cannot point outside of it.
- `${project}` is the open local project; without one (or for remote projects) no project
  scope applies. `${pluginData}` is `<data dir>/forge/plugin-data/<id>`, removed on uninstall.
- Network requests must be `http` or `https` to a granted host; IP addresses and other schemes
  are refused.
- Programs are found on `PATH` and run without a shell.
- Settings writes are checked against the setting's declared type, like the Settings dialog.
- Downloaded packages must match the permissions their marketplace listing showed, or the
  install is refused.

## Safe Mode

In an untrusted project ([Project trust](docs/guide/user/project-trust.md)) Forge refuses:

- loading plugins that declare `process` or a `${project}` write scope;
- `process.run` for every plugin;
- writing files inside the project.

Reading files and the other permissions still work, as reading does not run project code.

## Limits

API 1 grants permissions per plugin, not per call, and cannot narrow a scope after install
other than by uninstalling. Rust enforces file, network, program and settings access; editor
access is enforced by the host in the webview, which is the only place that has the editor.


---

Source: docs/guide/developer/plugins/publishing.md

# Publishing plugins

## The package

A `.forgeplugin` file is a zip archive with `forge-plugin.json` at its root and the files it
names. `pnpm plugin pack <folder>` (or `npm run pack` in a scaffolded project) writes
`<id>-<version>.forgeplugin` with the manifest, `dist/`, and `README.md`, `LICENSE`,
`CHANGELOG.md` when present, and prints its SHA-256.

Forge refuses packages that are larger than 64 MB (packed or unpacked), have more than 4096
files, contain absolute paths, `..`, drive letters or symbolic links, lack the manifest or the
`main` file, or whose manifest does not validate for the running Forge version.

## The marketplace index (format 1)

A marketplace is a static JSON file anyone can host (a web server, object storage, GitHub
Pages). Forge reads it from the URL in `plugins.marketplace.url`.

```json
{
  "formatVersion": 1,
  "name": "Acme plugins",
  "plugins": [
    {
      "id": "acme.todo-sync",
      "name": "TODO Sync",
      "publisher": "Acme",
      "description": "Turns TODO comments into issues.",
      "homepage": "https://acme.dev/todo-sync",
      "license": "MIT",
      "tags": ["todo", "issues"],
      "downloads": 12400,
      "versions": [
        {
          "version": "2.3.0",
          "engines": { "forge": ">=0.1.0" },
          "url": "files/acme.todo-sync-2.3.0.forgeplugin",
          "size": 4211,
          "sha256": "9f2c…(64 hex digits)",
          "signature": "base64 Ed25519 signature of the package bytes (optional)",
          "permissions": { "network": ["api.acme.dev"], "fs": { "read": ["${project}"] } },
          "released": "2026-10-28",
          "changes": "Links issues back into the comments."
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `formatVersion` | `1`. An index with a higher number is refused with "update Forge"; new optional fields may be added within format 1 |
| `plugins[].id`, `name` | as in the manifest |
| `versions[].url` | the package, absolute or relative to the index URL (`http`/`https` only) |
| `versions[].sha256` | required; the download must match it |
| `versions[].size` | optional; when set, the download must have exactly this size |
| `versions[].signature` | optional; required when the user configured trusted keys |
| `versions[].permissions` | must equal the package manifest's permissions; shown in the install prompt |
| `versions[].engines` | the newest version whose range contains the running Forge is offered |

Entries with an invalid id, version, range or checksum are skipped (and reported), so one
broken entry does not hide the whole marketplace.

## Updates

The Marketplace tab marks installed plugins with a newer compatible version (**Update**), and
⚙ | Check for Updates lists them. Updating installs the new package next to the old one and
swaps it in, keeping the plugin's enablement and data.

## Signatures

Checksums protect against broken or swapped downloads when the index itself is trusted
(served over HTTPS). To also protect against a compromised download host, sign each package
with Ed25519 and publish your public key: users add it (base64, 32 bytes) to
`plugins.marketplace.trustedKeys`. With at least one trusted key, Forge installs only packages
whose `signature` verifies with one of them.

## Testing an index locally

Serve a folder with the index and the packages, for example
`python3 -m http.server 8000`, and set the Marketplace URL to
`http://localhost:8000/index.json`. Forge's own tests use a local mock server the same way;
no public marketplace is involved.


---

Source: docs/guide/developer/adding-a-language.md

# Adding a language

Recipe: [`add-language-support`](.claude/skills/add-language-support/SKILL.md).

A language has up to four parts:

| Part | Where |
| --- | --- |
| **File type** (names, extensions, shebangs, label, indentation) | Rust: `crates/forge-filetypes/src/builtin.rs` (bundled) or a manifest's `[[contributions.fileTypes]]` |
| **Syntax mode** (highlighting) | UI: `app/ui/src/editor/languages.ts` or `registerLanguage` |
| **Editor features** without a server (completion, hover, folding, checks) | UI: `app/ui/src/features/languages/<name>.ts` |
| **Language server** | catalog: `crates/forge-langservers/catalog.toml` |

## 1. File type

```toml
[[plugin.contributions.fileTypes]]
id = "neon"
name = "NEON"                      # status bar label
extensions = ["neon"]              # longest match wins: "html.twig" beats "html"
fileNames = ["phpstan.neon*"]      # exact names, `*` anywhere, `/` for path suffixes
interpreters = ["neon"]            # optional: `#!` lines of extensionless scripts
indentSize = 2                     # optional, default 4
```

A plugin type with the id of a bundled type replaces it while the plugin is active. After
changing a manifest run `FORGE_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1 cargo test -p forge-app`. Add detection tests
to `crates/forge-filetypes/src/tests.rs` (bundled) or `file_types_detect_like_phpstorm` in
`app/src-tauri/src/plugins.rs` (manifests).

The UI asks Rust for a file's type (`filetypes_detect`) and caches it per path; use
`languageIdFor`, `languageLabel` and `indentFor` from `editor/languages.ts`, and
`await ensureFileType(path)` before building something synchronous.

## 2. Syntax mode

Pick, in this order: an official Lezer package (`@codemirror/lang-<x>`), a legacy mode
(`@codemirror/legacy-modes`) wrapped with `StreamLanguage.define`, or your own `StreamParser`
(use `streamLanguage` from `src/editor/tokens.ts` to map token names to Lezer tags). Then:

```ts
registerLanguage({ id: "neon", load: () => yaml() });
```

Token colors come from `forgeHighlight` in `src/editor/forgeTheme.ts` (Lezer tags → `--syn-*`
CSS variables). Add a style there instead of hard-coding colors. Add a file icon in
`src/shell/FileIcon.tsx`.

## 3. Editor features without a server

Language packs for config and script formats live in `app/ui/src/features/languages/` (see
`bash.ts`, `compose.ts`, `postfix.ts`). Each file calls `registerLanguage` and
`registerEditorExtension`; `shared.ts` provides hover docs, folding and `syntaxDiagnostics`,
which feeds the Problems view unless a listed language server runs for the file. Parsers are
unit-tested without an editor (`testkit.ts`).

## 4. Language server

Add a `[[language]]` and a `[[server]]` entry to `crates/forge-langservers/catalog.toml`:
command and args, `languages`, `group`, `install` options (npm commands are rewritten to
Forge's own prefix), `license`, `homepage`, optional `alternative`, `plugin` and `when`. Server
settings and initialization options go into the entry; project-specific values are added in
`crates/forge-langservers/src/config.rs`. If a file uses a feature only the server provides, add
an install hint to `SERVER_HINTS` (`features/langservers/serverHint.ts`).

## Template languages and data languages

HTML-based template engines (Twig, Smarty, Latte, Jinja, Handlebars, Go templates) are a
`TemplateSyntax` for the shared template parser in `src/editor/templates.ts`, drawn as a
decoration layer (`templateOverlay.ts`) over the data language's real editor support. The data
language is chosen in Rust (`crates/forge-filetypes/src/data.rs`): the
`templates.dataLanguages` setting, then compound names (`invoice.tex.twig`), then HTML.

- Another data language: add it to `DATA_LANGUAGES` and `COMPOUND` in `data.rs`, and to
  `DATA_LANGUAGES` in `src/editor/templateData.ts` with a `parser` (and a `support` factory if
  one exists).
- Another template engine: describe it as a `TemplateSyntax` (delimiters, keywords, builtins)
  and register it with the `template(...)` helper in `languages.ts`; mark its type as a template
  in `builtin.rs` (`TEMPLATES`).
- Configurable delimiters: list the engine with its delimiter fields and defaults in
  `CONFIGURABLE_TEMPLATES` (`crates/forge-filetypes/src/delimiters.rs`) and give it a syntax
  builder in `SYNTAX` (`src/editor/templateDelimiters.ts`). Rust resolves the delimiters of each
  file from the `templates.delimiters` setting (one entry per template and data language pair;
  the LaTeX entries are default data in `core.toml`) into `FileTypeInfo.delimiters`.

## Check

Add a sample to `app/ui/src/mock/demoConfigFiles.ts`, a scenario to
`app/ui/scripts/scenarios/syntax.mjs`, capture it and look at it in both themes.


---

Source: docs/guide/developer/settings.md

# Settings

Recipe: [`add-setting`](.claude/skills/add-setting/SKILL.md). User documentation:
[Settings and themes](docs/guide/user/settings-and-themes.md); every key:
[settings reference](docs/guide/reference/settings.md).

## Model

`forge_core::Settings` merges four layers: schema defaults < user
(`<config dir>/forge/settings.toml`) < Settings for New Projects
(`<config dir>/forge/new-project-settings.toml`, scope `newProjects`, only settings declared
with `project = true`) < project (`<project>/.forge/settings.toml`). Keys are
dotted (`editor.font.size`) and stored as nested TOML tables. Values are JSON so they cross IPC
unchanged. Writing a value persists its layer and notifies subscribers with the new effective
value (`SettingsChange { key, value, scope }`), which the shell forwards as `settings://changed`.

IPC: `settings_get_all` (effective values and the `user`, `newProjects` and `project` layers),
`settings_set(key, value, scope)`, `settings_schema`, `settings_search`, `settings_validate`,
`plugins_list`, `plugin_set_enabled`.

In the UI, `scopeFor(key, forNewProjects?)` picks the layer: project-level settings go to the
open project, or to `newProjects` when no project is open or the dialog edits the Settings for
New Projects (`openSettingsForNewProjects()`, `forNewProjects()` in `dialogState.ts`).
`saveSettings` removes an override instead of storing a value equal to what the layers below
give (`inheritedValue`). Every schema page gets **Restore Defaults** (`restorePageDefaults`)
next to **Reset** (discard the page's draft).

## Declaring a setting

```toml
[[contributions.settings]]
key = "projectView.openFilesWithSingleClick"
title = "Open files with single click"
description = "Shown under the option."
type = "bool"            # bool | int | number | string | enum | path | list
default = true
group = "appearance"     # settings page id
section = "Project View" # optional heading on the page
order = 40
project = true           # optional: may be stored per project
# int/number: min = 10, max = 20 (number: step)
# enum: options = [{ value = "auto", label = "Platform default" }, …]
```

Regenerate the snapshot: `FORGE_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1 cargo test -p forge-app`.

## Pages

`group` is a page id. Pages generated from the schema are listed in `schemaPages` in
`app/ui/src/features/settings/index.tsx`; features register their own pages with
`registerSettingsPage` and usually render `<SchemaPage pageId="…" />` (optionally with extra
content, see the Docker page's Test Connection). Custom pages (tables, test buttons) are plain
components that use `draftValue`/`setDraft` from `features/settings/dialogState.ts` so OK,
Cancel and Apply work. Pages whose edits are not plain settings keep them in their own store
and register it with `registerDraftSource({ modified, hasChanges, apply, discard, resetPage })`
(the Code Style schemes do), so the tree marks, Reset, Apply, OK and Cancel include them. Open
a page programmatically with `openSettings("<page id>")`.

The dialog's search, highlighting and validation are computed in Rust
(`forge_plugin_api::settings_model`, `settings_validate`).

## Reading settings

- UI: `getSetting<boolean>("projectView.openFilesWithSingleClick", false)` from
  `src/state/settings.ts`; reactive in effects and JSX. `saveSetting(key, value, scope)` writes.
- Rust: `state.read_settings().get_as::<bool>("…")`; subscribe with `Settings::subscribe`
  (listeners run under the settings lock — do work on another thread, as `lib.rs` does).

## Rules

- Secrets (API keys, tokens, passwords, licence keys) never go into settings: store them with the
  `keyring` crate (see `forge-ai`, `forge-db`, `forge-forges`, `forge-langservers::licence`).
- Do not keep persistent state in `localStorage`; use settings.
- A declared setting should be applied; if it is not yet, the user docs must say so.


---

Source: docs/guide/developer/localization.md

# Localization

Forge's UI text goes through message catalogs. English is the source language; German is the
first translation. The logic (parsing, lookup, fallback, plurals, number and date formats)
lives in the Rust crate [forge-i18n](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-i18n.md); the UI calls it synchronously
through WebAssembly, in the desktop app and in browser mode alike.

## Catalogs

Catalogs are flat JSON files `crates/forge-i18n/locales/<locale>/<area>.json`, one object of
`key → message` per file, compiled into the binary and the WebAssembly bundle:

```json
{
  "vcs.commit": "Commit",
  "vcs.files": "{count, plural, one {# file} other {# files}}",
  "find.summary": "{count}{plus} {count, plural, one {match} other {matches}} in {files}{plus} {files, plural, one {file} other {files}} in {duration}"
}
```

| Area | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `common` | buttons and words many places share (`common.ok`, `common.cancel`, `common.apply`) |
| `shell` | main toolbar, status bar, tool window chrome, editor tabs and menus, notifications, Problems |
| `settings` | the Settings dialog, page titles (`settings.page.<id>`), groups, Plugins page |
| `search`, `vcs`, `run`, `dialogs` (Project view, Rename, New Project, …), `welcome`, `errors` | their features |
| `git`, `debug`, `database`, `codeintel` | the Git dialogs and tool window, the Debugger, the Database tools, refactorings / Find Usages / hierarchy dialogs; keys `<area>.<component>.<name>` (`git.branchesPopup.newBranch`, `database.objects.tableDialog.createTable`) |
| `commands` | titles of Forge's own actions without a PHPStorm id (`action.NewWindow`, `action.Database.NewTable`), registered with `registerCommand` / `registerKeymapActions` in the UI |
| `menu`, `actions`, `plugins` | **generated in English** (see below), translated by hand |

A new area file must also be listed in `BUILTIN` in `crates/forge-i18n/src/catalog.rs`; a test
fails when a file on disk is missing there.

### Messages

Messages use [ICU MessageFormat](https://unicode-org.github.io/icu/userguide/format_parse/messages/):

| Syntax | Example |
| --- | --- |
| argument | `Open {name}?` |
| plural (`zero one two few many other`, `=n`, `#`, `offset:`) | `{count, plural, =0 {No files} one {# file} other {# files}}` |
| ordinal | `{n, selectordinal, one {#st} two {#nd} few {#rd} other {#th}}` |
| select | `{kind, select, file {File} other {Folder}}` |
| number (`integer`, `percent`) | `{size, number}` → *1,234.5* / *1.234,5* |
| date / time (`short`, `medium`, `long`), milliseconds since the epoch | `{when, date, medium}` → *Nov 4, 2026* / *04.11.2026* |

An apostrophe before a brace quotes it: write `Run ''{name}''` for *Run 'app'*. A lone
apostrophe elsewhere (`don't`) needs no escaping. The key-parity test reports a translation
whose arguments differ from the English message, which also catches a forgotten `''`.

### Key naming

Keys are dotted, lower camel case segments, starting with the area or feature:
`toolwindow.project.title`, `vcs.commitOptions`, `settings.page.editor.general`,
`statusbar.indent.tooltip`. Keys derived from ids keep the id as it is:

| Text | Key | English source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| main menu submenu | `menu.group.<slug>` (`_Recent Projects` → `recent-projects`) | `crates/forge-keymap/src/menu.rs` |
| own label of a menu action | `menu.<action id>` | `menu.rs` |
| action title (Find Action, keymap, menu) | `action.<action id>` | `crates/forge-keymap/data/phpstorm.json`, manifest commands |
| plugin name / description | `plugin.<id>.name`, `plugin.<id>.description` | manifests |
| tool window title | `toolwindow.<id>.title` | manifests or `registerToolWindow` |
| setting title / description / option / section | `setting.<key>.title`, `.description`, `.option.<value>`, `setting.section.<page>.<slug>` | manifests |
| run configuration type | `runconfig.<id>.name`, `.description`, `.field.<key>` | manifests |
| Settings page / group | `settings.page.<page id>`, `settings.group.<slug>` | `registerSettingsPage` |

`locales/en/menu.json`, `actions.json` and `plugins.json` are generated from the code that owns
the English text by snapshot tests; never edit them. After changing `menu.rs`, the PHPStorm
action catalog or a manifest, run:

```sh
FORGE_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1 cargo test -p forge-keymap -p forge-app
```

## Using translations in the UI

```ts
import { T, t, tOr } from "@/i18n";

t("vcs.commit");                                  // "Commit" / "Committen"
t("vcs.files", { count: n });                     // "3 files" / "3 Dateien"
t("toolbar.settings", { shortcut: "Ctrl+Alt+S" }); // shortcuts stay arguments
tOr(`search.tab.${id}`, fallback);                // a key built from data that may not exist
<T k="common.apply" />                            // reactive JSX text
```

- Add the English message to the right `locales/en/<area>.json` and the German one to
  `locales/de/<area>.json` in the same change. Hand-written areas must be complete in German
  (a test enforces it).
- `t()` reads the current language from a signal, so text rendered in JSX or a memo follows a
  language change at once. Text computed once (titles passed to `registerToolWindow`,
  `registerSettingsPage` or `registerContextMenu` at startup) is translated with the language
  of the session; changing the language offers a restart for that reason.
- Never build sentences from pieces (`` `${n} file${n === 1 ? "" : "s"}` ``): use one message with
  arguments and a plural. Keep keyboard shortcuts, file names and code as arguments.
- Do not translate command titles passed to `registerCommand` or `registerKeymapActions`: they
  stay English, and the keymap (Rust) shows the `action.<id>` translation with the English
  title as `titleEn`, which Find Action also matches. For a new action id that is not a
  PHPStorm action, add `action.<id>` with the English title to `locales/en/commands.json` and
  the German one to `locales/de/commands.json`.
- A local variable called `t` (common for "tab" or "type") shadows the import; rename the
  variable, or import `t as tr` as `features/run/ConfigurationsDialog.tsx` does.
- In vitest, `t()` loads the WebAssembly module synchronously on first use, so components
  render English text in tests without setup.

## Rust-side text

Text that Rust produces for the user goes through the process-wide localizer, whose language
the desktop app sets from `ide.language` at startup and whenever the setting changes (the
UI does the same for its WebAssembly instance):

```rust
forge_i18n::t("errors.safeMode.refused");
forge_i18n::t_args("errors.safeMode.refused", &forge_i18n::args! { "what" => what });
forge_i18n::t_or("menu.SaveAll", "Save _All"); // translation, or the English text from code
```

`ForgeError` (forge-core) serializes to the UI in the selected language: `not found`, `path is
outside of the workspace`, I/O errors and `ForgeError::no_project()` use `errors.*` keys, while
`Display` stays English for logs. Messages of `ForgeError::Other` are shown as they are, so build
them with `forge_i18n::t` when users commonly see them (`errors.collab.noSession`,
`errors.noDeclaration`).

The main menu and action titles (`forge-keymap`), plugin manifests
(`forge_plugin_api::l10n::localize_plugin` / `localize_settings`, used by `plugins_list` and
`settings_schema`), Settings group titles (`settings_model`) and Safe Mode refusals
(`forge-trust`) are localized this way. Tests that need a language use their own
`Localizer` (`Localizer::new("de")`, or `Localizer::empty` plus `add_messages`) instead of the
process-wide one, so parallel tests do not interfere.

## Plugin manifests

Built-in manifests need no keys: their English text is the source and the keys above are
derived from ids. Third-party plugins can ship translations in their manifest:

```toml
[l10n.de]
"plugin.acme.tools.name" = "Acme-Werkzeuge"
"setting.acme.mode.title" = "Modus"
"setting.acme.mode.option.fast" = "Schnell"
```

The bundled catalogs win over a manifest's own table; locales follow the same fallback chain
(`de-AT` → `de` → English).

## Checking coverage

```sh
cd app/ui && pnpm i18n:check            # summary
pnpm i18n:check --list src/features/git  # every hard-coded string below a path
pnpm i18n:check --missing-de             # English keys without a German translation
```

The check fails (exit code 1) only when the code uses a key that the English catalog does not
have. It also reports German coverage per area and finds hard-coded user-visible strings in
`.tsx` files heuristically (JSX text, `title`, `placeholder`, `aria-label`, `label`, balloon
calls); `scripts/i18n-allowlist.json` lists strings that need no translation (product names,
units). Legacy strings do not fail the quality gates yet.

The Rust tests in `forge-i18n` are the hard gate for the catalogs: every file parses, no key is
defined twice, every German key exists in English with the same arguments (key parity), and
the hand-written areas are fully translated.

strings):

| Measure | Value |

## Adding a language

1. Add the locale to `locales()` in `crates/forge-i18n/src/catalog.rs` with its own name
   (`Français`), create `locales/<id>/` with the area files and list them in `BUILTIN`.
2. Check the plural rules in `plural.rs` and the separators and date patterns in `format.rs`
   for the language; add them when missing.
3. Add the option to `ide.language` in `app/src-tauri/plugins/core.toml` and regenerate the
   snapshots (`FORGE_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1 cargo test -p forge-app`), then `pnpm wasm`.
4. Translate, run `cargo test -p forge-i18n` and `pnpm i18n:check`, and take screenshots of
   the main window, Settings, Find Action and the Commit window in the new language to check
   for truncated text (`app/ui/scripts/scenarios/localization.mjs` shows how).

# Writing accessible UI

Every panel, dialog and popup must work with a screen reader and with the keyboard alone, and
must stay readable in all themes. The shared pieces live in
`app/ui/src/features/accessibility/`; this page lists the rules and the checks. The user side
is described in [Accessibility](docs/guide/user/accessibility.md).

## Rules

1. **Use the element that means what it does.** A `<button>` for actions, `<input>` / `<select>`
   for values, `<a>` for links. A clickable `<div>` or `<span>` is not reachable with Tab.
2. **Every control has a name.** Icon buttons get `title` and `aria-label` (translated, see
   [Localization](docs/guide/developer/localization.md)); inputs get a `<label for>` (or are inside their label) and
   `aria-describedby` for their description, as `SchemaPage` does. Decorative icons and
   initials badges get `aria-hidden="true"`.
3. **Trees and lists use their roles.** A focusable container with `role="tree"` /
   `role="listbox"` and rows with `role="treeitem"` / `role="option"`, `aria-selected`,
   `aria-level` and `aria-expanded` (trees). Either the container keeps focus and points at the
   active row with `aria-activedescendant` (Project, Structure, Commit, Search Everywhere), or
   the rows use a roving `tabIndex` (0 on the selected row, -1 on the others: Settings tree,
   editor tabs). Arrow keys, `Home`, `End` and `Enter` come from
   `features/project/treeNavigation.ts` (`navigate`), so every tree behaves the same.
4. **Dialogs are `role="dialog"` with a name.** Inside a backdrop (`*-backdrop`) they are
   modal. `features/accessibility/dialogs.ts` finds every dialog in the window: it names it
   after its title, sets `aria-modal`, connects `<label>` elements to the control after them,
   keeps Tab inside the topmost modal dialog and returns focus to the opener when it closes.
   Focus the first field when the dialog opens, and close it with `Escape`.
5. **Shortcuts only through the keymap** ([Keymap actions](docs/guide/developer/keymap-actions.md)). Keys inside a
   widget (arrows in a tree, `Enter` in a list, `Escape` in a dialog) belong to the widget's
   own `onKeyDown`; anything that is a command gets an action id. Never trap Tab: a widget may
   take Tab only when `Escape` leaves it (Search Everywhere switches tabs with Tab).
6. **Focus is visible.** Do not remove outlines from focusable controls; the global
   `:focus-visible` ring in `accessibility.css` draws one (`--focus-ring`,
   `--focus-ring-width`). A container that keeps focus with `aria-activedescendant` shows the
   ring on its selected row instead.
7. **Colors come from the theme tokens.** Text uses `--fg`, `--fg-strong`, `--fg-muted` or
   `--fg-faint` on the `--bg-*` tokens; status colors use `--danger`, `--warning`, `--success`,
   `--info` and `--vcs-*`. Never write a color literal: the High Contrast themes replace the
   tokens. Do not show a state by color alone: add an icon, a text, a border or an underline
   (the High Contrast themes add outlines and underlines in `accessibility.css`).
8. **Announce what is not visible to a screen reader.** `announce(text)` from
   `@/features/accessibility` speaks through a live region that exists from startup;
   `announceForScreenReader(text)` only with **Support screen readers** on. Balloons are
   announced already (`.balloons` is a live region; errors are `role="alert"`).
9. **Name the areas.** Landmarks (`header`, `nav`, `main`, `footer`, `section`) need a unique
   `aria-label`. A new tool window gets its name from `registerToolWindow`'s title.

## The building blocks

| Module | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `features/accessibility/announce.ts` | live regions, `announce`, `announceForScreenReader`, `screenReaderMode` |
| `features/accessibility/dialogs.ts` | dialog names, `aria-modal`, label association, focus trap and return, `tabbables()` |
| `features/accessibility/areas.ts` | **Focus Next / Previous Area**, **Focus Editor**, `focusToolWindowContent` (used by `Alt+<n>`) |
| `features/accessibility/presentation.ts` | the Presentation Assistant, fed by `onCommandInvoked` in `state/commands.ts` |
| `features/accessibility/ide.ts` | the editor's accessible name, **Announce Caret Position**, problem announcements |
| `features/accessibility/accessibility.css` | `.sr-only`, focus rings, High Contrast extras, contrast scrollbars |
| `theme/contrast.ts` | WCAG contrast of the theme tokens |

`runCommand(id, actionId)` notifies `onCommandInvoked` listeners before running a command;
`runAction` passes the PHPStorm action id, so the Presentation Assistant shows the action's
title and shortcuts (and the other PHPStorm keymap's shortcut from the keymap snapshot's
`alternate` field, computed in `forge-keymap`).

## Themes and contrast

Theme tokens live in `app/ui/src/theme/theme.css`. `src/theme/contrast.test.ts` (part of
`pnpm test`) computes WCAG contrast ratios for the token pairs in `theme/contrast.ts`
(`themePairs`): text tokens on every background, syntax colors on the editor, secondary text,
status and VCS colors, also on the selected row, and the accent button. The normal themes must
reach AA (4.5:1 for text), the `high-contrast*` themes AAA (7:1) plus visible borders. Only the
Solarized palette has documented exceptions. A new token that text is drawn with belongs in
`themePairs`.

A new theme needs: a block in `theme.css`, its id in `THEMES` (`state/theme.ts`), the option in
`appearance.theme` (`app/src-tauri/plugins/core.toml`), and, for an editor scheme of its own, a
bundled scheme in `forge-colorscheme` (`Bundled`).

## Checks

| Check | Command | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Theme contrast | `pnpm test src/theme` | nothing (part of `pnpm test`) |
| Dialog focus, live regions, focus areas, Presentation Assistant, Settings dialog with the keyboard | `pnpm test src/features/accessibility` | nothing (part of `pnpm test`) |
| axe-core audit of the main screens and dialogs in all themes you pass | `pnpm a11y:audit --themes=dark,light,high-contrast,high-contrast-light` | `pnpm dev` running |
| Keyboard-only flow: open a file, rename, focus areas, Switcher, commit, Settings | `pnpm a11y:keyboard` | `pnpm dev` running |

`pnpm a11y:audit` runs [axe-core](https://github.com/dequelabs/axe-core) (MPL-2.0, a
development dependency only, never bundled) in Chromium and exits with 1 on a serious or
critical violation (`--report` only prints, `--json=file` writes the results). Add a screen to
`SCREENS` in `scripts/a11y-audit.mjs` when you add a major dialog or tool window. The keyboard
flow fails on any mouse event; extend it when a feature adds a keyboard path users depend on.

When the audit was introduced, axe reported 98 critical and 232 serious violations (counted
per element, summed over the audited screens) in the dark theme and 98 critical and 260 serious
in the light theme: unnamed editor, selects and checkboxes, nested interactive editor tabs, a
tree without tree items, text below 4.5:1 and scroll areas without keyboard access. All of them were fixed: the Forge Ember, Anvil and both
High Contrast themes pass without serious or critical findings. The Solarized themes keep
color-contrast findings that come from the Solarized palette itself (VCS colors, the blue
accent with light text, search highlights).

# Keymap actions

Recipe: [`add-keymap-action`](.claude/skills/add-keymap-action/SKILL.md). Every
shortcut goes through the keymap engine. **Never** add a `keydown` listener for a shortcut: it
breaks user overrides, focus contexts and conflict detection, and causes double toggles.

## The engine

`crates/forge-keymap` (pure Rust):

- `shortcut`: parsing (`Ctrl+K Ctrl+C`, `Shift Shift`, `Cmd+,`), canonical ids, display strings
  (`Ctrl+Shift+A` / `⇧⌘A`) and physical key names of DOM events;
- `catalog`: PHPStorm's default keymaps from `data/phpstorm.json` (id, title, group,
  Windows/Linux and macOS shortcuts, `native` flag) and `ACTION_ALIASES`;
- `engine`: bindings, conflicts and the `Resolver` state machine (chords, double taps, focus
  contexts `editor`, `input`, `toolwindow`, `diff`, `global`, `terminal`);
- `keymap`: `KeymapService` combining the catalog, plugin actions, registered commands and user
  overrides from the `keymap.*` settings.

The UI (`app/ui/src/keymap/`) captures key events, classifies the focus context and asks the
resolver — synchronously, through the WebAssembly build, in desktop and browser mode alike —
then runs the returned action with `runAction`. Unimplemented actions show "not available yet".
IPC: `keymap_actions`, `keymap_register_actions`, `keymap_set_override`, `keymap_conflicts`,
`keymap_find_by_shortcut`, `keymap_resolve`, `keymap_import_legacy`.

## Implementing a PHPStorm action

Most actions already exist with the right default keys. Register a command with that id:

```ts
registerCommand({ id: "ActivateStructureToolWindow", title: "Structure",
  run: () => toggleToolWindow("structure") });
```

If your feature already uses another id, alias it in `ACTION_ALIASES`
(`crates/forge-keymap/src/catalog.rs`):

```rust
("Generate", &["php.generate"]),
```

Rebuild the browser bundle after changing Rust keymap code: `pnpm --dir app/ui wasm`.

## Plugin actions

```ts
registerKeymapActions([
  { id: "CommandLineToolsAction", title: "Run Command…", group: "Tools",
    shortcuts: { $default: ["Ctrl+Shift+X"], macOS: ["Cmd+Shift+X"] } },
  { id: "Console.Jdbc.Execute", title: "Execute", group: "Database", context: "editor",
    shortcuts: { $default: ["Ctrl+Enter"], macOS: ["Cmd+Enter"] } },
]);
registerCommand({ id: "CommandLineToolsAction", title: "Run Command…", run: () => openRunCommand() });
```

- `group` places the action in the Keymap tree (`Plugins/<Name>` by convention, or a
  `Main Menu/...` group).
- `context: "editor" | "toolwindow" | "diff"` limits where the shortcut applies, so the same
  keys can mean different things (`Alt+Insert` adds a row in a data grid, opens Generate in the
  editor; `F7` is Next Difference inside the merge window, an element with
  `data-focus-context="diff"`, and Step Into elsewhere).
- Shortcut syntax: `Ctrl+Shift+A`, `Alt+Insert`, chords `Ctrl+K Ctrl+C`, double taps
  `Shift Shift`, macOS `Cmd`/`Opt`. Physical key codes are used, so layouts work.

Manifests can also declare `[[contributions.keybindings]]` (`command`, `key`, optional `keymap`
and `when`).

> **Note:** some editor-local keys are bound with CodeMirror keymaps inside a feature's editor
> extension (for example `Ctrl+O`/`Ctrl+I` in PHP files, `Mod-b`, `Mod-p`, `Mod-Alt-l`). Prefer
> the keymap engine for new actions.

## Checks

- `cargo test -p forge-keymap`: the tests detect unexpected conflicts in the default keymaps.
- Find Action lists the action with its shortcut; Settings | Keymap shows it and lets users
  rebind it.
- Update [the keymap reference](docs/guide/reference/keymap.md).

# Screenshots and scenarios

Every UI change needs screenshots, and you must look at them. Recipe:
[`verify-ui-with-screenshots`](.claude/skills/verify-ui-with-screenshots/SKILL.md).

## How it works

Forge runs entirely in a browser with mocked IPC, so every feature can be captured headless.
`app/ui/scripts/screenshots.mjs` opens the dev server in Chromium (Playwright), runs a scenario
and writes `docs/screenshots/<scenario>.png` at 1440×900.

## Steps

1. Start the dev server on a free port:

   ```sh
   cd app/ui && pnpm dev --port 1430
   ```

2. Add or update a scenario in `app/ui/scripts/scenarios/<feature>.mjs`:

   ```js
   /** @type {Record<string, (page: import("playwright-core").Page) => Promise<void>>} */
   export default {
     "routes-tool-window": async (page) => {
       await page.click('[data-tool-window="routes"]');
       await page.waitForSelector(".routes-table tr");
     },
   };
   ```

   - The page starts with the demo project open and `User.php` in the editor (`.cm-content` is
     visible).
   - Start elsewhere with properties on the function: `fn.query = "?welcome"`,
     `fn.waitFor = ".welcome-project"`.
   - In the Project tree a double click opens folders and files:
     `page.dblclick('.tree-row[data-path="app/Models"]')`.
   - Run commands: `page.evaluate(() => window.__forgeRunCommand("settings.open"))`.
   - Press keys: `page.keyboard.press("Control+Alt+KeyS")`.
   - Light theme: `document.documentElement.dataset.theme = "light"`.

3. Capture:

   ```sh
   FORGE_URL=http://localhost:1430 node scripts/screenshots.mjs <scenario> [more…]
   ```

   Without arguments all scenarios run. Chromium is found under `/opt/pw-browsers/…` or set
   `CHROMIUM_PATH`.

4. **Open every image** and compare it with PHPStorm's New UI: layout, spacing, wording and
   states; colors must come from the Forge theme. Check the light theme too.
5. Commit the PNGs with the change.

## Existing scenario files

`ai-chat`, `ai-providers`, `browser-companion`, `context-menu`, `database`, `debugger`,
`dialog-windows`, `docker`, `editor-lsp`, `file-menu`, `forges`, `gemini`, `integration-polish`,
`javaforge`, `language-servers`, `laravel`, `luaforge`, `navigation`, `php`, `project-tree`, `project-wizard`,
`remote`, `scratches`, `settings`, `symfony`, `syntax`, `terminal-run`, `vcs`, `webforge`,
`welcome`, `workbench`.

The guide links these screenshots relatively (`../../screenshots/<name>.png`); when you rename a
scenario, update the pages that use it.

## Troubleshooting

- `Timeout … .cm-content`: the dev server restarted (e.g. Vite re-optimized dependencies after
  `pnpm add`). Run the scenario again.
- `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED`: the dev server is not running on that port.

# Quality gates

Run all of these and fix every failure before committing. CI runs only on manual dispatch, so
local checks are the gate. Recipe:
[`quality-gates`](.claude/skills/quality-gates/SKILL.md).

## Rust (repository root)

```sh
cargo fmt --all --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace
```

- With several worktrees, give each its own `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`.
- After changing plugin manifests or project generators:
  `FORGE_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1 cargo test -p forge-app`.

## UI (`app/ui`)

```sh
pnpm typecheck
pnpm test        # vitest
pnpm build
pnpm version:check   # Cargo.toml, tauri.conf.json and package.json agree
pnpm workflows:check # release.yml runs only on pushed `v*` tags, ci.yml only manually
```

## Accessibility (`app/ui`, with `pnpm dev` running, for UI changes)

```sh
pnpm a11y:audit --themes=dark,light,high-contrast,high-contrast-light  # axe-core: no serious or critical violations
pnpm a11y:keyboard   # keyboard-only flow: open file, rename, focus areas, commit, Settings
```

The theme contrast check (WCAG AA, AAA for the High Contrast themes) and the keyboard tests of
dialogs and the Settings tree run in `pnpm test`. See [Writing accessible UI](docs/guide/developer/accessibility.md).

## Browser extension (`browser-extension`, only when it changed)

```sh
pnpm typecheck
pnpm test
pnpm build       # dist/chrome and dist/firefox
```

## Test rules

- Tests must not need network access, installed language servers or real code-host accounts.
  Use fakes and local mock servers: a fake language server (`crates/forge-lsp/tests/fake_server.rs`),
  recorded agent CLI streams and fake CLI scripts (`crates/forge-agent-cli/tests/`), in-memory
  pipes for the remote protocol, local HTTP mock servers for code hosts and AI providers,
  SQLite for database tests.
- Parsers and models are tested in Rust; UI logic with vitest (pure modules, e.g. tree
  navigation, settings application, keymap dispatch).

## Before you commit

- UI changes have screenshots that you looked at ([Screenshots](docs/guide/developer/screenshots.md)).
- No stray files: mocks never write into real projects; caches go to the user cache dir.
- User-visible changes update the matching page in `docs/guide/`.
- Small commits with imperative English subjects, no trailers ([Git workflow](docs/guide/developer/git-workflow.md)).

# Release builds

Recipe: [`build-release`](.claude/skills/build-release/SKILL.md).

## Bundles

From `app/ui`:

```sh
pnpm release --bundles appimage       # Linux AppImage with the remote agents
pnpm tauri build --bundles appimage   # Linux AppImage without them
pnpm tauri build --bundles deb,rpm    # Linux packages
pnpm tauri build                      # all bundles for this OS (dmg on macOS, msi/nsis on Windows)
```

`pnpm tauri` runs the Tauri CLI from `app/`; it builds the UI first (`pnpm build`). Output:
`target/release/bundle/<type>/` (e.g. `Forge_0.1.0_amd64.AppImage`) and the plain binary
`target/release/forge`. A build from scratch takes about six minutes.

Cross-compiling is not supported: build Windows and macOS bundles on those systems.

## Official releases

Versions follow Pride Versioning and are bumped with `pnpm version:bump`; see
[Versioning](docs/guide/developer/versioning.md).

Pushing a version tag (`git tag v0.2.0 && git push origin v0.2.0`) runs
`.github/workflows/release.yml`, and nothing else does (`pnpm workflows:check` in the
[quality gates](docs/guide/developer/quality-gates.md) fails if a workflow gets another trigger). It:

1. `meta`: decides the channel from the tag (`vX.Y.Z` stable, `vX.Y.Z-beta.N` beta), stops
   when the tag does not match the app version in `tauri.conf.json`, and creates a draft
   release `Forge <version>` with generated notes (a pre-release for the beta channel); a
   re-run of the same tag reuses that draft,
2. builds the static remote agents on Linux,
3. builds the bundles on Ubuntu (AppImage, deb, rpm), Windows (NSIS, MSI) and macOS (Apple
   Silicon and Intel) with `pnpm tauri build --config src-tauri/tauri.agents.conf.json`,
   [signing](#code-signing) them when the certificates are configured,
4. signs the updater artifacts and uploads everything plus `latest.json` to the draft,
5. `checksums`: uploads `SHA256SUMS` (and `SHA256SUMS.asc` with a GPG key) and, for a
   pre-release, the beta feed `latest-beta.json` (see [Channels](#channels)),
6. `publish`: publishes the release once every asset is uploaded. If a job fails, the release
   stays a draft; fix the cause and re-run the workflow.

Forge's updater reads `https://github.com/Reeperk/Forge/releases/latest/download/latest.json`,
so a published (not draft, not pre-release) release is what stable users get offered.

Linux build jobs (remote agents, Linux bundles) run on the project's self-hosted runner
(labels `self-hosted`, `Linux`, `X64`); Windows and macOS bundles and the small `meta`,
`checksums` and `publish` jobs run on GitHub's runners (`checksums` needs `gh` and `gpg`). The self-hosted
runner needs the Debian packages listed in `.github/scripts/linux-deps.sh`. The script installs
missing ones when the runner is root or has passwordless sudo; otherwise the job stops and
prints the `apt-get install` command to run once as root on the runner.

### Secrets and variables

Set them once in the repository settings (Settings | Secrets and variables | Actions). Only the
updater key and `PHP_LSP_TOKEN` are needed for a working release; every other row is optional,
and a missing one skips that step with a notice in the log. Never commit certificates or keys.

| Name | Kind | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` | secret | updater private key from `pnpm tauri signer generate` |
| `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD` | secret | its password |
| `FORGE_UPDATER_PUBKEY` | secret or variable | the matching public key, built into the app |
| `PHP_LSP_TOKEN` | secret | fine-grained token with read access (Contents) to the private `stdimnet/php-lsp`; GitHub's runners cannot build without it |
| `WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE` | secret | Authenticode certificate: the `.pfx` file, base64-encoded |
| `WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` | secret | the `.pfx` password |
| `AZURE_CLIENT_ID`, `AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET`, `AZURE_TENANT_ID` | secrets | Azure Trusted Signing: the app registration allowed to sign |
| `AZURE_SIGNING_ENDPOINT`, `AZURE_SIGNING_ACCOUNT`, `AZURE_CERTIFICATE_PROFILE` | variables | Azure Trusted Signing: endpoint (e.g. `https://weu.codesigning.azure.net`), account and certificate profile |
| `APPLE_CERTIFICATE` | secret | "Developer ID Application" certificate: the `.p12` file, base64-encoded |
| `APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` | secret | the `.p12` password |
| `APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY` | secret | e.g. `Developer ID Application: Jane Doe (TEAMID1234)` |
| `APPLE_ID`, `APPLE_PASSWORD`, `APPLE_TEAM_ID` | secrets | notarisation with an Apple ID and an app-specific password |
| `APPLE_API_KEY`, `APPLE_API_ISSUER`, `APPLE_API_KEY_P8` | secrets | notarisation with an App Store Connect API key instead: key ID, issuer ID and the contents of `AuthKey_<id>.p8` |
| `RELEASE_GPG_PRIVATE_KEY`, `RELEASE_GPG_PASSPHRASE` | secrets | armored private key and passphrase for `SHA256SUMS.asc` |

Keep the private key offline as well: losing it means installed copies can no longer verify
updates.

## Updates and signing

Forge updates itself with `tauri-plugin-updater`: it reads `latest.json`, downloads the bundle
for its platform, verifies the bundle's minisign signature against the public key built into
the app, installs it and restarts. When and what to offer (once a day, skipped versions,
channel, version compare) is decided in [`forge-update`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-update.md); the shell side
is `app/src-tauri/src/commands/updates.rs` and the splash steps are in
`app/src-tauri/src/startup.rs`.

### Create the key pair (once)

```sh
cd app/ui
pnpm tauri signer generate -w ~/.tauri/forge.key   # asks for a password
```

This writes the private key `~/.tauri/forge.key` and the public key `~/.tauri/forge.key.pub`.

- Store the private key and its password as the secrets `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` and
  `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD` (repository settings), and in a password manager.
- Store the public key (the contents of `forge.key.pub`) as the secret (or variable) `FORGE_UPDATER_PUBKEY`.
- Never commit either file. The public key is not secret, but it lives in the build
  environment, not in the repository, so forks and local builds do not pretend to be official.

### How the keys reach a build

`pnpm tauri` runs `app/ui/scripts/tauri.mjs`, which passes everything to the Tauri CLI and adds
one `--config` to `tauri build` (applied last):

| Build environment | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` set | `bundle.createUpdaterArtifacts` on: every bundle gets a signed `.sig` next to it |
| `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` not set | `createUpdaterArtifacts` off, so the build succeeds without the key (even though `tauri.agents.conf.json` turns it on for releases) |
| `FORGE_UPDATER_PUBKEY` set | written to `plugins.updater.pubkey`; the Rust code also compiles it in (`option_env!`) |
| `FORGE_UPDATER_PUBKEY` not set | the app never checks for updates: it logs "update checks are disabled: this build has no updater public key" and the Updates settings page says "Updates are not configured in this build" |

The release workflow's call `pnpm tauri build --config src-tauri/tauri.agents.conf.json` goes
through the same script, as does `pnpm release`. A local signed build:

```sh
export TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY="$(cat ~/.tauri/forge.key)"
export TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD='…'
export FORGE_UPDATER_PUBKEY="$(cat ~/.tauri/forge.key.pub)"
pnpm release --bundles appimage   # Forge_0.1.0_amd64.AppImage + Forge_0.1.0_amd64.AppImage.sig
```

### latest.json

The workflow's `tauri-action` (`includeUpdaterJson: true`) writes `latest.json` from the `.sig`
files and attaches it to the release. Its format, for a feed you publish yourself:

```json
{
  "version": "0.2.0",
  "notes": "What changed.",
  "pub_date": "2026-11-02T10:00:00Z",
  "platforms": {
    "linux-x86_64": { "signature": "<contents of the .AppImage.sig>", "url": "https://…/Forge_0.2.0_amd64.AppImage" },
    "windows-x86_64": { "signature": "…", "url": "https://…/Forge_0.2.0_x64-setup.exe" },
    "darwin-aarch64": { "signature": "…", "url": "https://…/Forge.app.tar.gz" }
  }
}
```

Keys are `{os}-{arch}` or `{os}-{arch}-{installer}` (`linux-x86_64-deb`); the more specific one
wins. Forge also sends a `HEAD` request to the download to show its size. An optional
`"channel": "beta"` marks a beta feed, which installations on the stable channel ignore.

The channels and their feeds are described in [Channels](#channels).

### Trying the update flow without a release

Development builds never check for real updates. Simulate one instead; it shows the update
panel with a fake 94 MB download and installs nothing:

```sh
FORGE_SIMULATE_UPDATE=0.2.0 pnpm tauri dev
```

In browser mode: `http://localhost:1420/?splash&simulateUpdate=0.2.0` (the splash, then the
workbench) or `?simulateUpdate=0.2.0` with Help | Check for Updates…. To test a real update,
build a signed release of the old version, publish a feed with a newer signed build on a local
`https` server and point `updates.endpoint` at it.

## Code signing

Signing happens in the `bundles` job, before `tauri-action` builds; the Tauri bundler then
signs the binaries and installers itself. Nothing is signed in local builds unless you set the
same environment variables.

### Windows (Authenticode)

Two ways; the workflow uses the first one that is configured.

**A `.pfx` certificate (OV or EV exported with its key)** is the default. Encode it and store
it with its password:

```sh
base64 -w0 forge-codesign.pfx > forge-codesign.pfx.b64   # paste into WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE
```

The workflow imports it into the runner's `CurrentUser\My` store and sets
`FORGE_WINDOWS_CERT_THUMBPRINT`. `app/ui/scripts/tauriArgs.mjs` turns that into
`bundle.windows.certificateThumbprint` (with `digestAlgorithm: sha256` and the timestamp server
`http://timestamp.digicert.com`, or `FORGE_WINDOWS_TIMESTAMP_URL`), and Tauri runs `signtool`
on `forge.exe`, the NSIS installer and the MSI. Locally on Windows, import the certificate and
set `FORGE_WINDOWS_CERT_THUMBPRINT` before `pnpm tauri build`.

**Azure Trusted Signing** suits certificates that cannot be exported (most EV certificates
since 2023). Set the three `AZURE_*` secrets and three variables above. The workflow installs
`trusted-signing-cli` (`cargo install`) and sets `FORGE_AZURE_SIGNING_ENDPOINT`, `_ACCOUNT` and
`_PROFILE`; `tauriArgs.mjs` sets `bundle.windows.signCommand` to
`trusted-signing-cli -e <endpoint> -a <account> -c <profile> -d Forge %1`, which Tauri calls
for every file it signs.

Check a signed build with `Get-AuthenticodeSignature .\Forge_0.2.0_x64-setup.exe`.

### macOS (Developer ID and notarisation)

The app is signed with the hardened runtime and `app/src-tauri/Entitlements.plist`
(`bundle.macOS.entitlements`), which allows JIT and unsigned executable memory for the webview's
JavaScript engine. Forge is not sandboxed. Tauri reads the `APPLE_*` variables: it imports
`APPLE_CERTIFICATE` into a temporary keychain, signs with `APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY`, submits the
app with `notarytool`, waits for the result and staples the ticket. The workflow exports only
the secrets that exist:

| Configured | Result |
| --- | --- |
| no certificate or identity | unsigned (Gatekeeper asks users to allow the app in System Settings) |
| certificate + identity | signed, not notarised (a warning in the log) |
| + `APPLE_API_KEY`, `APPLE_API_ISSUER`, `APPLE_API_KEY_P8` | signed and notarised with an API key (preferred) |
| + `APPLE_ID`, `APPLE_PASSWORD`, `APPLE_TEAM_ID` | signed and notarised with an Apple ID |

Export the certificate from Keychain Access as `.p12` and encode it with
`base64 -i cert.p12 | pbcopy`. Check a build with `codesign -dv --verbose=4 Forge.app`,
`spctl -a -vv Forge.app` and `xcrun stapler validate Forge.app`.

## Checksums

The `checksums` job downloads every asset of the release, writes `SHA256SUMS` (the output of
`sha256sum`) and uploads it. With `RELEASE_GPG_PRIVATE_KEY` it also uploads the detached
signature `SHA256SUMS.asc`. Users verify a download with:

```sh
sha256sum --ignore-missing -c SHA256SUMS
gpg --verify SHA256SUMS.asc SHA256SUMS   # with the project's public key
```

The AUR and Flatpak packages take their checksums from this file.

## Channels

Forge has two update channels, chosen with "Update channel" (`updates.channel`) under
Settings | Appearance & Behavior | System Settings | Updates. The logic is in
[`forge-update`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-update.md) (`Channel::endpoints`, `pick_feed`).

| Release | Tag | Published as | Feed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| stable | `v0.2.0` | release | `latest.json` of the release; GitHub's `releases/latest` points at it |
| beta | `v0.3.0-beta.1` | pre-release | `latest.json` and `latest-beta.json` (`"channel": "beta"`) of the pre-release, and `latest-beta.json` of the release tagged `beta` |

| Setting | Feeds read | Offered |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `updates.channel = stable` (default) | `https://github.com/Reeperk/Forge/releases/latest/download/latest.json` | stable releases only |
| `updates.channel = beta` | `https://github.com/Reeperk/Forge/releases/download/beta/latest-beta.json`, then the stable feed | the newer of both, so a stable `0.3.0` replaces `0.3.0-beta.2` |
| `updates.endpoint` set | that URL only (release builds require `https`) | as the channel allows |

The beta feed needs a fixed URL, so it lives on a long-lived release tagged `beta`. Create it
once on GitHub: tag `beta`, title "Beta update feed", marked as **pre-release**, no assets.
The tag does not match `v*`, so it starts no workflow. From then on every pre-release replaces
its `latest-beta.json`. Until it exists, beta
installations simply get stable releases (the workflow prints a warning).

Pre-release versions come from `pnpm version:bump default --pre beta.1` and the next ones from
`pnpm version:bump pre` (see [Versioning](docs/guide/developer/versioning.md)). The `meta` job creates a tag with a
`-label` as a pre-release, so a beta never becomes GitHub's "latest".

The MSI cannot carry a SemVer pre-release, so on Windows `pnpm tauri build` sets
`bundle.windows.wix.version` to a numeric version (`0.1.1-beta.1` → `0.1.1.1`) and keeps
`bundle.windows.allowDowngrades` on, so betas and the final release of a version install over
each other ([MSI version](docs/guide/developer/versioning.md#msi-version)). The NSIS installer and the bundle file
names keep the SemVer version (`Forge_0.1.1-beta.1_x64-setup.exe`). Without this, WiX stops with
"optional pre-release identifier in app version must be numeric-only".

## Linux packages

### Flatpak

`packaging/flatpak/` holds the manifest `dev.forge.ide.yml`, the desktop file and the AppStream
metainfo. The manifest repackages the release's `.deb` (the same binary as the AppImage) on the
GNOME runtime, which ships webkit2gtk-4.1; it needs no Rust or Node toolchain and no generated
cargo/pnpm source lists, so a release only changes one URL and checksum. A source build with
`flatpak-cargo-generator` and `flatpak-node-generator` is what Flathub would prefer; it is
possible later, but means regenerating thousands of source entries for every release.

Permissions (`finish-args`) and why Forge needs them:

| Permission | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `--socket=wayland`, `--socket=fallback-x11`, `--share=ipc`, `--device=dri` | the window and GPU-accelerated webview |
| `--share=network` | AI providers, Git remotes, Composer/npm, update checks, remote development |
| `--filesystem=home`, `/media`, `/run/media`, `/mnt` | projects can live anywhere in the home directory or on other drives |
| `--socket=ssh-auth` | Git over SSH and SSH remote development use the user's agent |
| `--talk-name=org.freedesktop.secrets` | AI keys and passwords are stored in the Secret Service (keyring) |
| `--talk-name=org.freedesktop.Notifications` | notifications |
| `--talk-name=org.freedesktop.Flatpak` | `flatpak-spawn --host` to run PHP, Composer, Node, language servers, Docker and the terminal shell, which are installed on the host |

> **Note:** Forge does not yet route its tool runs through `flatpak-spawn --host`; inside the
> Flatpak it finds only the tools of the GNOME runtime. Until it does, the Flatpak suits
> editing and Git; prefer the AppImage, the `.deb` or the AUR package for full tool support.
> Updates of a Flatpak come from Flatpak itself, not from Forge's updater.

Build it locally (needs `flatpak-builder` and `flatpak install --user flathub
org.gnome.Platform//48 org.gnome.Sdk//48`; without `flatpak-builder` the script says so and
exits):

```sh
pnpm --dir app/ui flatpak                                   # the release .deb from the manifest
pnpm --dir app/ui flatpak target/release/bundle/deb/Forge_0.1.0_amd64.deb   # a local build
flatpak install --user target/flatpak/Forge.flatpak
appstreamcli validate packaging/flatpak/dev.forge.ide.metainfo.xml
desktop-file-validate packaging/flatpak/dev.forge.ide.desktop
```

The manifest carries `x-checker-data`, so on Flathub the external data checker proposes the
update for each stable release.

### AUR

`packaging/aur/forge-bin/PKGBUILD` repackages the release's `.deb`; `packaging/aur/forge-git`
builds the `main` branch from source (`pnpm tauri build --no-bundle`). Both follow stable
releases only; the AUR has no beta package.

After a stable release, point the packages at it:

```sh
pnpm --dir app/ui packaging:update v0.2.0            # fetches the release's SHA256SUMS
pnpm --dir app/ui packaging:update v0.2.0 --sums ~/Downloads/SHA256SUMS   # offline
```

This sets `pkgver` (and `pkgrel=1`) and the `.deb` checksum in `forge-bin/PKGBUILD`, points the
Flatpak manifest at the same `.deb`, adds the release to the metainfo and regenerates both
`.SRCINFO` files (`pnpm --dir app/ui packaging:srcinfo` does only the last step). Commit the
changes.

Publishing to the AUR is manual and never done by agents or workflows. With an AUR account and
SSH key (on an Arch system, so `makepkg` can check the result):

```sh
git clone ssh://aur@aur.archlinux.org/forge-bin.git aur-forge-bin
cp packaging/aur/forge-bin/{PKGBUILD,.SRCINFO} aur-forge-bin/
cd aur-forge-bin
makepkg -si                                   # builds and installs it as a test
makepkg --printsrcinfo | diff - .SRCINFO      # must be empty
git commit -am "Update to 0.2.0" && git push
```

The first upload creates the package; check beforehand that the name `forge-bin` is still free
on the AUR. `forge-git` is published the same way; its `pkgver` is computed by `makepkg`, so
regenerate its `.SRCINFO` there.

## Remote agents

Remote projects need the headless agent (`forge-remote-agent`) for the host's architecture. Build
the static Linux agents first:

```sh
rustup target add x86_64-unknown-linux-musl          # aarch64-unknown-linux-musl as well
pnpm --dir app/ui agents                              # or: pnpm agents x86_64
```

This writes `target/agents/forge-remote-agent-{x86_64,aarch64}-linux.gz` (gzip-compressed,
because AppImage tools would patch an uncompressed ELF file in the bundle). Architectures whose
musl target is not installed are skipped. aarch64 needs a cross compiler and linker
(`CC_aarch64_unknown_linux_musl`, `CARGO_TARGET_AARCH64_UNKNOWN_LINUX_MUSL_LINKER`); the
tree-sitter C code of the native architecture is built with the host's `gcc` (fortify off).

`pnpm release` builds the agents and then the bundles with
`src-tauri/tauri.agents.conf.json`, which ships `target/agents/` as the bundle's `agents/`
resource folder. Arguments go to `tauri build`.

At runtime Forge looks for agents in `FORGE_REMOTE_AGENT_DIR`, the bundle's `agents/`
resources, `agents/` next to its executable and `target/agents`; a development build of
`forge-remote-agent` next to the executable serves hosts of the same architecture. Plain or
`.gz` binaries are accepted. The agent is uploaded to `~/.cache/forge-agent/<version>/` on the
host.

## Smoke test on a headless Linux box

```sh
APPIMAGE_EXTRACT_AND_RUN=1 xvfb-run -a -s "-screen 0 1440x900x24" \
  sh -c './Forge_0.1.0_amd64.AppImage /path/to/project & sleep 15; import -window root shot.png'
```

Check the screenshot: the splash appears first; then, without a project argument, the last
project or the Welcome screen; with one, the workbench, file tree and Git branch. Use a throwaway
`HOME` (or `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`) so the run does not reopen your own last project. Make sure the run created no files in the project
(`git status` stays clean).

## Versioning

The version (0.1.0) is set in `[workspace.package]` of the root `Cargo.toml`,
`app/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` and `app/ui/package.json`. The bundle identifier is
`dev.forge.ide`; the `forge://` scheme is declared under `plugins.deep-link` in
`tauri.conf.json`.

# Search benchmark

`crates/forge-search/examples/bench.rs` runs the same scenarios against any project folder and
prints a Markdown table. Run it before and after a change to the index, the matchers or Find in
Files, and keep a change only when the numbers support it.

```sh
cargo run --release -p forge-search --example bench -- <project folder>
```

Each scenario reports the best of three runs. The first build of the index depends on the disk
cache: run it twice and compare the second result.

## Baseline

Measured on a source tree (272,700 files, Windows 11, release build, files in the OS cache).

| Scenario | Best of 3 | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cold index | 5458 ms (8130 ms with tree-sitter symbols) | 272700 files, 272700 added |
| Load saved index | 1287 ms | 272700 files, cache 283 MB |
| Refresh, nothing changed | 336 ms | 0 changed |
| Go to File `usr` | 7.5 ms | 100 hits |
| Go to File `ordctl` | 4.5 ms | 100 hits |
| Go to File `index.php` | 4.1 ms | 100 hits |
| Go to File `zzqxvk` (typo pass) | 37 ms | 1 hit |
| Go to File `index`, substring | 11.1 ms | 100 hits |
| Classes `order` | 1.5 ms | 50 hits |
| Classes `user` | 1.3 ms | 50 hits |
| Find `return` | 248 ms | 508159 matches in 36900 files |
| Find `->get(` | 16.5 ms | 3325 matches in 1029 files |
| Find `function \w+\(` regex | 137 ms | 138491 matches in 15722 files |
| Find `.*` regex | 1078 ms | 13462140 matches in 168727 files |
| Find rare word `zzqxv` | 6.5 ms | 23 matches in 6 files |
| Find `.*` regex, cancelled after 100 ms | 116 ms | Search cancelled |

The first cold index after a rebuild or a reboot took 77 s on the same folder, because the
files were not in the OS cache. That time is disk speed, not the index.

## Tried and rejected

Measured with the benchmark above on the same tree.

| Change | Result | Why not |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rarest trigram first with early stop | `->get(` 16.5 to 19.8 ms, `return` 248 to 249 ms | Choosing candidates is not where the time goes; reading and scanning files is |
| Skip lockfiles, `.min.js`, `.min.css`, `.map` | About 20 MB of 272,700 files | Too little to gain, and Find in Files would stop matching them |
| Identifier-run trigrams instead of byte trigrams | Cache 283 to 169 MB, load 1287 to 861 ms, but `->get(` 16 to 274 ms | Queries with punctuation lose most of their narrowing; a hybrid needs both indexes |

## Against ripgrep

ripgrep 15.1.0 on the same folder, same excludes (`--hidden --no-require-git`, case-insensitive, `-c`, best of 3, nothing else running). It reads every file on each run; the index reads only the candidates.

| Query | ripgrep | Forge index |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `return` | 46,228 ms | 248 ms |
| `->get(` | 57,746 ms | 16.5 ms |
| `function \w+\(` regex | 11,914 ms | 137 ms |
| `.*` regex | 56,040 ms | 1,078 ms |
| `zzqxv` | 24,074 ms | 6.5 ms |

The ripgrep times are dominated by reading 272,700 files on this machine (virus scanning included) and vary a lot between runs, so read them as a gap in magnitude, not as exact ratios. No query was faster with ripgrep. The index costs a one-off build (5.5 s warm, 283 MB on disk) and a refresh (340 ms) that ripgrep does not need.

# Versioning

Forge versions follow [Pride Versioning](https://pridever.org) 0.3.0: **PROUD.DEFAULT.SHAME**.

| Part | Bump it for | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PROUD | a release we are really proud of; DEFAULT and SHAME go back to 0 | `1.2.3` → `2.0.0` |
| DEFAULT | a normal release; SHAME goes back to 0 | `1.2.3` → `1.3.0` |
| SHAME | a fix too embarrassing to admit | `1.2.3` → `1.2.4` |

The written form stays `X.Y.Z`, so Cargo, npm and Tauri's updater parse and order versions like
SemVer. Pre-releases use a SemVer label (`0.2.0-beta.1`); they go to the beta update channel
(`updates.channel`).

### MSI version

The Windows MSI installer (WiX) accepts only numeric versions `major.minor.build[.revision]`
(at most 255.255.65535.65535), not `0.2.0-beta.1`. `pnpm tauri build` therefore passes a
derived `bundle.windows.wix.version` on Windows (`app/ui/scripts/tauriArgs.mjs`); the app, the
NSIS installer and the updater keep the SemVer version.

| App version | MSI version |
| --- | --- |
| `0.1.1` | `0.1.1` |
| `0.1.1-beta.1`, `0.1.1-alpha.1`, `0.1.1-rc.1` | `0.1.1.1` |
| `0.1.1-rc.2` | `0.1.1.2` |
| `0.1.1-7` | `0.1.1.7` |
| `0.1.1-beta` | `0.1.1.0` |

The label is dropped and its number becomes the fourth field. Windows Installer compares only
the first three fields for an upgrade, so every pre-release of `0.1.1` and the final `0.1.1`
count as the same version. They still install over each other because the MSI allows
downgrades (`bundle.windows.allowDowngrades`, Tauri's default, which makes WiX's `MajorUpgrade`
remove any installed Forge, the same version included): `beta.1` → `beta.2` → `rc.1` → `0.1.1`
each replace the previous install. A later version (`0.1.2-beta.1` → `0.1.2.1`) is an ordinary
upgrade.

So a version must stay MSI-compatible: PROUD and DEFAULT at most 255, SHAME at most 65535, and
a pre-release label of the form `<label>.<N>` (`beta.1`, `rc.2`), a bare number or a bare label,
with `N` at most 65535. `pnpm version:bump` refuses anything else (`beta.1.2`, `beta.70000`), and
`pnpm version:check` fails on it and when `tauri.conf.json` pins `bundle.windows.wix.version` or
turns `allowDowngrades` off. `pnpm workflows:check` makes sure the workflows build through
`pnpm tauri` (tauri-action's `tauriScript: pnpm --dir ui tauri`), which adds the MSI version.

## Where the version lives

The same version is written in three files:

- `Cargo.toml` (`[workspace.package] version`; every crate inherits it),
- `app/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` (the bundles' version and what the updater compares),
- `app/ui/package.json`.

Never edit them by hand. From `app/ui`:

```sh
pnpm version:check                        # fails when the files disagree or there is no MSI version
pnpm version:bump default                 # 0.1.0 → 0.2.0 in all three files + Cargo.lock
pnpm version:bump shame                   # 0.2.0 → 0.2.1
pnpm version:bump proud                   # 0.2.1 → 1.0.0
pnpm version:bump default --pre beta.1    # 1.0.0 → 1.1.0-beta.1
pnpm version:bump pre                     # 1.1.0-beta.1 → 1.1.0-beta.2
pnpm version:bump pre --pre rc.1          # 1.1.0-beta.2 → 1.1.0-rc.1
pnpm version:bump release                 # 1.1.0-rc.1 → 1.1.0 (the final release)
```

`proud`, `default` and `shame` always raise a number, also on a pre-release
(`1.1.0-rc.1` → `shame` → `1.1.1`). `pre` keeps PROUD.DEFAULT.SHAME and only moves the
pre-release label on: without `--pre` it adds one to the label's last number (`beta` becomes
`beta.1`); with `--pre` it takes the new label, which must come after the current one in SemVer
order (`beta.2` → `rc.1`, not back to `beta.1`). `pre` and `release` work only on a pre-release
version.

The script (`app/ui/scripts/version.mjs`, logic and tests in `versionBump.mjs`) updates
`Cargo.lock` for the workspace crates, prints the release tag and does nothing else: it never
commits, tags or publishes.

## Releasing a version

1. `pnpm version:bump <part>` and run the [quality gates](docs/guide/developer/quality-gates.md).
2. Commit (`Release 0.2.0`) and merge to the release branch.
3. Tag that commit and push the tag: `git tag v0.2.0 && git push origin v0.2.0`.
4. The [release workflow](docs/guide/developer/release-builds.md#official-releases) creates the release (a
   pre-release for `-beta` versions), builds the bundles, signs them, uploads them with
   `latest.json` and `SHA256SUMS` and publishes it; a pre-release also updates the beta feed
   ([Channels](docs/guide/developer/release-builds.md#channels)). Installed copies offer the update on their next
   start.
5. For a stable release, run `pnpm packaging:update v0.2.0` and commit the AUR and Flatpak
   changes ([Linux packages](docs/guide/developer/release-builds.md#linux-packages)).

> **Note:** Only the project owner bumps versions and pushes version tags. Agents never bump a
> version unless they are asked to, and never push version tags or publish releases.


---

Source: docs/guide/developer/git-workflow.md

# Git workflow

- Repository: <https://github.com/Reeperk/Forge>, default branch `main`.
- **Branch names** describe the work: `feat/…`, `fix/…`, `docs/…`, `chore/…`
  (`feat/laravel-plugin`, `fix/tree-double-click`, `docs/user-and-developer-guide`).
- **Small commits** with imperative English subjects: "Add routes tool window",
  "Fix double toggle of the Terminal".
- **No co-author or other trailers** in commit messages, and no mention of AI tools.
- **Commit early and often** during long tasks so work is not lost.
- Do not push or open pull requests unless you were asked to.

## CI

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs **only on manual dispatch** (`workflow_dispatch`): UI
typecheck/test/build on Ubuntu, and fmt, clippy and tests on Ubuntu, Windows and macOS. Never
trigger workflows yourself, and every branch must keep the `workflow_dispatch`-only trigger.
Run the [quality gates](docs/guide/developer/quality-gates.md) locally instead. When the owner dispatches it, the UI
and Linux jobs run on the project's self-hosted runner (`.github/scripts/linux-deps.sh` checks
its system packages), Windows and macOS on GitHub's runners.

`.github/workflows/release.yml` runs **only when a version tag `v*` is pushed**. It creates a
draft GitHub release for the tag, builds the Linux, Windows and macOS bundles (with the remote
agents), signs the updater artifacts, uploads them plus `latest.json` and publishes the release.
Only the project owner pushes version tags; never add branch push, pull request or schedule
triggers to any workflow. See [Release builds](docs/guide/developer/release-builds.md).

## Worktrees

Several git worktrees can build in parallel; give each its own `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` (a shared target
dir can return stale builds of workspace crates) and keep the dev profile as it is, so each
target dir holds one copy of every artifact.

## Pull requests

- Run the quality gates.
- Attach screenshots for UI changes.
- Update the docs: the matching page in `docs/guide/` for every user-visible change (see
  [`docs/guide/README.md`](docs/guide/README.md)), `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` for new IPC contracts, the
  README and `docs/ROADMAP.md` for new plugins.


---

Source: docs/guide/developer/crates/index.md

# Crates

Every Rust crate of the workspace. The pages are generated from each crate's `lib.rs` documentation, module headers and `Cargo.toml`, plus the IPC commands in `app/src-tauri/src/commands/` that use it. The desktop shell itself is the crate `forge-app` in `app/src-tauri` (see [Architecture overview](docs/guide/developer/architecture.md)).
