# forge-agent-cli

`crates/forge-agent-cli` — Runs AI coding agent CLIs (Claude Code, Gemini CLI) headless and normalizes their output.

## Purpose

Drive AI coding agent CLIs (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, ...) headless and expose their
output as a normalized `AgentEvent` stream for Forge's chat UI.

Forge never ships credentials: each adapter runs the user's own installed CLI with its
own login or API key.

Every CLI is an `AgentCli` adapter: its command line, how messages reach it
(`Transport`), an `EventParser` from its stream format to `AgentEvent`s, permission
prompts and session resume. `profile` describes each one (models, permission modes,
install hint).

`conversation` folds the events into the chat as the UI renders it (with `diff`s of
edits and Markdown ASTs). It, the event/prompt/profile modules and the Gemini parser are
pure; the adapters and sessions need the `runtime` feature (default).

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `claude.rs` | Claude Code adapter: `claude -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json`. |
| `cli.rs` | The adapter trait every agent CLI implements, plus start options and detection. |
| `conversation.rs` | The chat conversation as the UI renders it: the `AgentEvent` stream folded into turns and blocks (text with its Markdown AST, thinking, tool cards with diffs, permission requests, errors), plus the derived texts the cards show. |
| `diff.rs` | Line diffs of edit tool calls (`Edit`, `MultiEdit`, `Write`) for the chat's edit cards and permission previews. |
| `event.rs` | The normalized event stream every agent adapter produces. The UI only knows these events, so adding a new CLI never touches the chat UI. |
| `gemini.rs` | Gemini CLI adapter: `gemini --output-format stream-json`, one process per turn. |
| `host.rs` | Where an agent CLI runs: this machine (`LocalHost`) or, for a project on a remote host, that host (the app implements `AgentHost` over the project backend's process API, so the CLI sees the project's files and its own login there). |
| `profile.rs` | Static descriptions of the built-in agent CLIs: models, permission modes as each CLI understands them, and how to install it. Pure, so the browser-mode mock shows the same picker entries as the desktop app. |
| `prompt.rs` | Turns a chat message plus editor context (attached files, selection) into the prompt text sent to the agent. |
| `session.rs` | Runs agent CLI processes for a conversation and streams their normalized events: one long-running process (`Transport::Persistent`) or one process per message (`Transport::PerTurn`). |

## Main public items

```rust
pub use claude::ClaudeCode;
pub use cli::{…};
pub use conversation::{Chat, ChatUpdate, PermissionStatus};
pub use event::{AgentEvent, EventParser, Usage};
pub use gemini::GeminiCli;
pub use host::{AgentHost, LocalHost, SpawnedAgent};
pub use profile::{AgentProfile, PermissionMode, PermissionModeInfo};
pub use prompt::{compose_prompt, MessageContext, Selection};
pub use session::{AgentSession, EventSink};
pub fn builtin_agents() -> Vec<Arc<dyn AgentCli>> { … }
pub fn agent_by_id(id: &str) -> Option<Arc<dyn AgentCli>> { … }
pub fn pure_parser(agent_id: &str) -> Option<Box<dyn EventParser>> { … }
```

## Used by

- IPC: `agent_list`, `agent_start`, `agent_send`, `agent_respond_permission`, `agent_interrupt`, `agent_stop` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/agent.rs`)
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/ai-chat`
- Browser mode: built into `forge-wasm`

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: [`forge-core`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-core.md), [`forge-markdown`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-markdown.md)
- External: `serde`, `serde_json`, `similar`, `tokio`, `tracing`
- Features: `default` = `runtime`; `runtime` = `dep:forge-core`, `dep:tokio`, `dep:tracing`

## Tests

11 source files, about 3477 lines; 27 unit tests and 15 integration tests in `tests/` (`gemini_session.rs`, `parse_fixtures.rs`, `session.rs`).

```sh
cargo test -p forge-agent-cli
```

# forge-ai

`crates/forge-ai` — Forge IDE AI provider layer: Anthropic and OpenAI-compatible chat models.

## Purpose

Forge AI provider layer.

A `Provider` turns a provider-neutral `CompletionRequest` into a one-shot
`Completion` or a stream of `Delta`s; providers whose servers support it also answer
fill-in-the-middle `FimRequest`s (`Provider::fim`, OpenAI-compatible `POST {base}/completions`
with `prompt` + `suffix`; `ProviderKind::supports_fim`: Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, custom)
for inline code completion. Two wire protocols are implemented:
the Anthropic Messages API and OpenAI-compatible chat completions (OpenAI, OpenRouter,
LM Studio, Ollama, llama.cpp, custom servers). `AiService` stores provider configs in
`ai.toml` and API keys in the OS keychain.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `anthropic.rs` | Anthropic Messages API (`POST /v1/messages`). |
| `config.rs` | Provider configuration, persisted as TOML in `<config dir>/forge/ai.toml`. API keys are never written here; see `crate::secrets`. |
| `error.rs` |  |
| `openai.rs` | OpenAI-compatible chat completions (`POST {base}/chat/completions`): OpenAI, OpenRouter, LM Studio, Ollama, llama.cpp server and any other compatible endpoint. |
| `provider.rs` | The `Provider` trait plus HTTP helpers shared by the implementations. |
| `secrets.rs` | API key storage: the OS keychain (service `forge-ai`, account = provider id) with an environment-variable fallback per provider kind. |
| `service.rs` | `AiService`: owns the provider config + key store and builds providers on demand. This is what the app's IPC layer talks to. `selection` / `resolve` refuse disabled providers (`AiError::ProviderDisabled`). |
| `sse.rs` | Minimal Server-Sent Events parser (WHATWG event-stream format). |
| `types.rs` | Provider-neutral request/response types. |

## Main public items

```rust
pub use config::{…};
pub use error::{AiError, AiResult};
pub use provider::{cancellable, collect_text, DeltaStream, Endpoint, Provider};
pub use secrets::{KeySource, KeyringStore, MemoryStore, SecretStore};
pub use service::{AiService, ProviderInfo, ProvidersState, TestResult};
pub use tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken;
pub use types::{…};
```

## Used by

- IPC: `ai_complete`, `ai_stream`, `ai_cancel`, `ai_providers_list`, `ai_provider_save`, `ai_provider_delete`, `ai_provider_test`, `ai_models`, `ai_set_default` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/ai.rs`); `ai_inline_complete`, `ai_inline_cancel`, `ai_editor_status`, `ai_action`, `ai_explain` with [`forge-ai-editor`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-ai-editor.md) (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/ai_editor.rs`)
- Code review: [`forge-code-review`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-code-review.md) (Summarize PR, AI Review, Explain this change)
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/ai`, `app/ui/src/features/ai-editor`, `app/ui/src/features/git (AI commit messages)`
- Browser mode: not built to WebAssembly (runtime code); browser mode uses mocks

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: [`forge-core`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-core.md)
- External: `async-stream`, `async-trait`, `bytes`, `dirs`, `futures-util`, `keyring`, `reqwest`, `serde`, `serde_json`, `thiserror`, `tokio`, `tokio-util`, `toml`, `tracing`

## Tests

10 source files, about 2000 lines; 10 unit tests and 18 integration tests in `tests/` (`providers.rs`, against a local mock HTTP server: chat, streaming, fill-in-the-middle, errors).

```sh
cargo test -p forge-ai
```

# forge-ai-editor

`crates/forge-ai-editor` — AI in the editor: inline completion context and post-processing,
AI actions (explain, fix, tests, docs) and the `.aiignore` policy. Pure logic (no network, no
file system), also built to WebAssembly for browser mode.

## Purpose

- **Inline (ghost text) completion** (`inline.rs`): `build_context` cuts the code around the
  caret (UTF-16 offsets from CodeMirror) to a prefix and suffix window, collects the file's
  imports outside the window and the heads of other open files (same language first), and
  decides single or multi-line (`MultilinePolicy`). `build_prompt` makes both request forms: a
  fill-in-the-middle prompt with a commented context header and stop sequences, and a chat
  prompt with a `<CURSOR>` marker. `postprocess` cleans the answer: end tokens and markers,
  Markdown fences, code echoed from before the caret, re-indented first lines, the
  single-line cut, the end of the block for multi-line suggestions (indentation and bracket
  depth), and overlap with the text after the caret (closing brackets, a duplicated `}` line).
- **AI actions** (`actions.rs`): `prompt` builds the request of "Explain with AI", "Fix with
  AI" (the problems at the caret, the region with context before and after), "Generate
  Documentation with AI" (the declaration at the caret, the language's doc format) and
  "Generate Tests with AI" (the code under test, the framework and the conventional test
  file, `test_path`). `proposal` turns the reply into a `Proposal`: the new text with a diff
  (`forge_agent_cli::diff::text_diff`) and, for the requesting file, the minimal `TextEdit`.
  Doc comments go above attributes and replace an existing one; Python docstrings go into the
  body; Rust tests are appended as `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`.
- **Policy** (`policy.rs`): `Policy::check` decides whether code of a file may be sent:
  `ai.enabled` for the project, `.aiignore` / `.aiexclude` (gitignore syntax: anchored and
  unanchored patterns, `**`, character classes, `!`, folder rules) and, for inline completion,
  the languages turned off.
- `lang.rs`: language ids, comment and doc styles, declaration and import lines, test
  frameworks.

The network calls are made by the app with [`forge-ai`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-ai.md) providers.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `actions.rs` | AI actions in the editor: prompts and proposals with diff previews. |
| `inline.rs` | Inline completion: context, fill-in-the-middle / chat prompts, post-processing. |
| `lang.rs` | What the AI features need to know about a language. |
| `policy.rs` | Whether code may be sent: project switch, `.aiignore`, per-language switch. |
| `text.rs` | UTF-16 / byte offsets, lines and indentation, code from fenced replies. |

## Main public items

```rust
pub use actions::{explain_prompt, prompt, proposal, test_path, ActionKind, ActionPrompt, ActionRequest, Problem, Proposal, TextEdit};
pub use inline::{build_context, build_prompt, finish, postprocess, CompletionMode, InlineContext, InlinePrompt, InlineRequest, MultilinePolicy, RelatedFile};
pub use lang::{language_of, Language};
pub use policy::{AiIgnore, Feature, Policy, Verdict};
```

## Used by

- IPC: `ai_inline_complete`, `ai_inline_cancel`, `ai_editor_status`, `ai_action`, `ai_explain` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/ai_editor.rs`)
- [`forge-code-review`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-code-review.md): the `.aiignore` policy for pull request diffs
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/ai-editor`
- Browser mode: [`forge-wasm`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-wasm.md) `ai_editor.rs` (`ai_inline_finish`, `ai_action_prompt`, `ai_action_proposal`, `ai_policy_check`) for `app/ui/src/mock/aiEditorMock.ts`

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: [`forge-agent-cli`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-agent-cli.md) (without the `runtime` feature, for the diff)
- External: `serde`, `serde_json`

## Tests

6 source files; 21 unit tests (context and trimming, multi-line policy, post-processing,
region detection, fix / docs / tests proposals in PHP, Rust, Python and Lua, test paths,
`.aiignore` matching and the policy).

```sh
cargo test -p forge-ai-editor
```

# forge-agent-tasks

`crates/forge-agent-tasks` — agent tasks: an AI agent works on a task in a sandbox (a git
worktree in Forge's cache folder), runs the tests, fixes failures and leaves a diff for the
user to review. The user's working tree is not touched until they apply it.

## Purpose

- **Task model** (`task.rs`): `AgentTask` with its `TaskRequest` (prompt, scope, backend,
  tests, step budget), `TaskStatus` (queued, running, needs review, applied, discarded,
  failed, cancelled), the log of `Step`s (info, thought, tool call, command approval, test
  run, error, finished) and the `Outcome` (completed, step budget exhausted, tests still
  failing). `TaskStore` keeps a project's tasks as `tasks.json` next to the sandboxes; tasks
  that were running when Forge quit load as cancelled.
- **Sandbox** (`sandbox.rs`): `create` adds a detached worktree of the project's repository
  in the given folder (refused inside the project), starting from `git stash create` (the
  working tree and index without touching them) or HEAD, copies untracked non-ignored files
  and commits that snapshot as the base, so the review shows only the agent's changes.
  `changes` lists the changed files (`--name-status` + `--numstat` against the base),
  `file_versions` gives both sides for the diff viewer, `patch` the binary patch.
  `apply` is all or nothing (`git apply --check` first; conflicting files are parsed from its
  errors), `apply_as_commit` applies and commits only the agent's files (`git commit --only`),
  `apply_as_branch` commits in the sandbox and creates a branch (shared refs, so it shows up
  in the repository at once), `remove` removes the worktree and its folder.
- **Workspace** (`workspace.rs`): the agent's view of the sandbox. `normalize` refuses absolute
  paths, `..` escapes and `.git`; `resolve` also refuses symlinks that lead out of the sandbox
  and files matched by `.aiignore`; writes are limited to the task's scope. File tools:
  `list` (breadth first, dependency folders not descended into), `read` (line ranges),
  `search` (case-insensitive), `write`, `edit` (unique match), `delete`.
- **Tools** (`tools.rs`): the built-in agent's tools and the text protocol — one JSON call
  `{"tool": ..., "args": ...}` per turn inside a `<tool>` tag (fenced or bare JSON accepted),
  so it works with every chat model of [`forge-ai`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-ai.md); bad calls are explained to
  the model. `system_prompt` describes the tools, the scope and the test loop.
- **Commands** (`commands.rs`): `split_command` (quotes and escapes, shell operators refused —
  no shell runs), `allowlisted` (word prefixes from `ai.agentTasks.allowedCommands`),
  `refused` (network clients: curl, wget, ssh, scp, rsync, nc, ...), `run_process` (timeout,
  cancellation, `CI=1`) and `evaluate_tests`, which parses test output with the line parsers
  of [`forge-output`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-output.md) (TeamCity, TAP, libtest, go test2json, ...) or goes by
  the exit code.
- **Loops** (`agent.rs`): `run_builtin` asks a `forge_ai::Provider` for one tool call per turn,
  runs it in the sandbox and returns the result until the agent calls `finish`; with tests,
  `finish` is verified by a test run (when files changed since the last run) and failures are
  sent back until the tests pass or the step / test-run budget is used up. Commands that are
  not allowlisted wait for `Host::approve`. `run_cli` drives an agent CLI turn by turn
  (`CliTurns`) and runs the tests between turns, sending failures back.
- **CLI permissions** (`cli.rs`): `permission` maps a permission request of Claude Code or
  Gemini CLI to allow (reads inside the sandbox, edits inside the scope, bookkeeping tools),
  deny (outside the sandbox, `.aiignore`, network tools, unknown tools) or ask the user (shell
  commands that are not allowlisted).

The app (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/agent_tasks.rs`) owns the queue, the `Host` (processes,
approvals, the log as `agent-tasks://changed` events), maps run configurations into the
sandbox and starts agent CLIs through [`forge-agent-cli`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-agent-cli.md).

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `agent.rs` | The built-in tool-calling loop and the run-test-fix loop around agent CLIs. |
| `cli.rs` | Permission requests of agent CLIs mapped to the sandbox. |
| `commands.rs` | Command lines without a shell, allowlist, refused programs, processes, test results. |
| `sandbox.rs` | The git worktree sandbox: create, changes, diff sides, apply, commit, branch, remove. |
| `task.rs` | Task model, steps, outcomes and the task store. |
| `tools.rs` | Tool calls of the built-in agent, the text protocol and the system prompt. |
| `workspace.rs` | Path confinement, `.aiignore` and scope checks, file tools. |

## Main public items

```rust
pub use agent::{run_builtin, run_cli, Budget, CliTurns, Host, TaskContext};
pub use cli::{permission, CliVerdict};
pub use commands::{RunOutput, ShellCommand, TestSpec};
pub use sandbox::{ApplyResult, ChangeKind, FileChange, Sandbox};
pub use task::{AgentBackend, AgentTask, ApprovalState, Outcome, OutcomeKind, Step, StepKind, TaskRequest, TaskStatus, TaskStore, TestChoice, TestResult};
pub use workspace::Workspace;
```

## Used by

- IPC: `agent_tasks_list`, `agent_task_create`, `agent_task_cancel`, `agent_task_approve`,
  `agent_task_changes`, `agent_task_file_diff`, `agent_task_apply`, `agent_task_discard`,
  `agent_task_remove` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/agent_tasks.rs`), event
  `agent-tasks://changed`
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/agent-tasks` (Agent Tasks tool window)
- Browser mode: `app/ui/src/mock/agentTasksMock.ts` replays a scripted task (nothing runs)

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: [`forge-ai`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-ai.md) (the `Provider` trait), [`forge-ai-editor`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-ai-editor.md)
  (`.aiignore`), [`forge-output`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-output.md) (test output parsers), [`forge-vcs`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-vcs.md)
  (git binary, patch splitting)
- External: `serde`, `serde_json`, `tokio`, `async-trait`

## Tests

```sh
cargo test -p forge-agent-tasks
```

# forge-backend

`crates/forge-backend` — Forge IDE project backends: the Backend trait, the local backend and the remote agent protocol.

## Purpose

Project backends: where an open project's files, git, processes, language servers and
PHP index live.

- `Backend` is what the app's workspace, file system, git, terminal, run, LSP and PHP
  commands talk to. The UI never knows which implementation answers.
- `LocalBackend` serves a folder on this machine.
- `RemoteBackend` serves a folder on another machine through the Forge agent
  (`crates/forge-remote-agent`), which is itself a `LocalBackend` behind the
  `protocol`. `rpc::RpcClient` multiplexes calls, events and byte channels over any
  stream (SSH in `crates/forge-remote`, an in-memory pipe in tests).

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `frameworks.rs` | Laravel, Symfony and Doctrine analysis of a project, Related Symbol (`FrameworkCall::Related`, `forge_codeintel::related` over the project's files) and Go to Test / Create New Test (`FrameworkCall::TestTargets`, `NewTestPlan`), run where its files are. |
| `langservers.rs` | Which catalog language servers (`forge-langservers`) start for a project, planned on the machine that has the project's files and the installed servers: the desktop app for a local project, the Forge agent for a remote one (its servers then start on the host through the LSP byte channel). |
| `local.rs` | A project folder on this machine. |
| `paths.rs` | Path helpers that do not touch the file system (the project may live on another machine). |
| `php.rs` | The PHP index of a project and the PHP language server lookup, wherever the project lives. Offsets are UTF-16 (JS strings), see `phpforge_lang_php::service`. |
| `process_io.rs` | Processes started through a `Backend` (on this machine or on a remote host) used like local child processes: line by line with cancelation (`run_lines`, artisan and Symfony console runs) or as async stdio streams (`spawn_stdio`, agent CLIs). |
| `protocol.rs` | The Forge agent protocol: MessagePack frames over a byte stream (the agent's stdio). |
| `remote.rs` | A project on another machine, served by the Forge agent over an `RpcClient`. |
| `ssr.rs` | Structural Search and Replace over a project (`forge-ssr`): `search_workspace` behind `Backend::structural_search` (agent call `StructuralSearch` for remote projects) and `replace_all`, which writes the matched files through the backend and keeps them for Undo like Replace in Files. |
| `rpc.rs` | The client end of the agent `protocol`(crate::protocol): calls with out-of-order answers, pushed events and byte channels over one stream pair. |
| `tunnels.rs` | Port forwarding between this machine and a remote project's host (SSH tunnels). Local projects have none; `forge-remote` implements them over the project's SSH connection. |

## Main public items

```rust
pub use frameworks::{framework_call, FrameworkCall};
pub use langservers::{LangServersAnswer, LangServersRequest};
pub use local::LocalBackend;
pub use php::PhpBackend;
pub use remote::RemoteBackend;
pub use tunnels::{PortForward, Tunnels};
pub struct RemoteHost { … }
pub struct BackendInfo { … }
pub struct TerminalSpec { … }
pub trait Terminal: Send + Sync { … }
pub trait Process: Send + Sync { … }
pub trait Backend: Send + Sync { … }
pub struct BackendFiles(pub Arc<dyn Backend>);
pub fn folder_name(root: &Path) -> String { … }
```

## Used by

- IPC: every project command (workspace, fs, git, terminal, run, php, lua) goes through `AppState::backend()`
- UI: `app/ui/src/state/workspace.ts`
- Browser mode: not built to WebAssembly (runtime code); browser mode uses mocks

## Dependencies

# forge-bookmarks

`crates/forge-bookmarks` — Bookmarks: lists, mnemonics and line tracking through edits (pure, WebAssembly-friendly).

## Purpose

The model behind PHPStorm's bookmarks (`F11`, `Ctrl+F11`, the Bookmarks tool window `Alt+2`).

- `Bookmarks` holds named bookmark lists; one of them is the default list that `F11` adds
  to. A bookmark marks a line of a project-relative file and may carry a mnemonic (`0`–`9`,
  `A`–`Z`, unique across all lists) and a description.
- Every change is an `Op` applied with `Bookmarks::apply` (toggle, set mnemonic, describe,
  move between lists, add/rename/remove lists, …), so the desktop app and browser mode share
  the logic.
- Line positions follow edits: the editor reports each document change as `LineEdit`s in
  old-document coordinates and `Op::ApplyEdits` moves the bookmarks below them; a bookmark on
  a removed line stays where the change happened. Renamed and deleted files are
  followed with `Op::RenamePath` / `Op::RemovePath`.

The crate has no I/O; the state is serialized as JSON by the caller.

## Main public items

```rust
pub const DEFAULT_LIST: &str = "Bookmarks";
pub struct Bookmark { … }
pub struct BookmarkList { … }
pub struct Bookmarks { … }
pub struct LineEdit { … }
pub enum Op { … }
pub fn normalize_mnemonic(c: char) -> Option<char> { … }
pub fn map_line(line: usize, edit: &LineEdit) -> usize { … }
```

## Used by

- IPC: `bookmarks_get`, `bookmarks_apply` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/workbench.rs`; stored in
  `<data dir>/forge/projects/<name>-<hash>/bookmarks.json`, never in the project)
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/bookmarks` (tool window, gutter icons, mnemonic popup)
- Browser mode: built into `forge-wasm` (`bookmarks_apply`)

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: none
- External: `serde`

## Tests

1 source file, about 570 lines; 7 unit tests (toggling, mnemonics, lists, line tracking
through inserted and removed lines, renames).


# forge-code-review

`crates/forge-code-review` — review mode of pull/merge requests: viewed files, pending review
comments submitted as one review, and the AI features "Summarize PR", "AI Review" and
"Explain this change". Logic only; the host API is [`forge-forges`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-forges.md), the
models are [`forge-ai`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-ai.md) providers and the `.aiignore` policy comes from
[`forge-ai-editor`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-ai-editor.md).

## Purpose

- **Diff context** (`context.rs`): `plan` orders the changed files by `Priority` (source,
  tests, configuration, documentation; lock files, minified, vendored and generated files are
  only named), larger changes first, renders each hunk with new-file line numbers in front of
  added and context lines, cuts files to `Budget::max_file_chars` at hunk or line boundaries
  and fills chunks of `Budget::max_chars` (at most `max_chunks`; the rest is "omitted").
  Files the policy refuses (new or old path in `.aiignore`, AI off for the project) are
  `Excluded`: they appear in no text, not even by name.
- **Prompts** (`prompt.rs`): summary (JSON: overview, risks, files, testPlan), review (JSON
  findings with path, line, endLine, severity, title, explanation, suggestion; one request
  per chunk) and explain (one hunk with the start of its file's diff).
- **Parsing** (`parse.rs`): the first JSON value in the answer (fences and prose around it are
  ignored), field synonyms, severities mapped from the words models use (`critical`, `nit`, …),
  at most 40 findings; prose without JSON becomes the summary's overview.
- **Anchoring** (`anchor.rs`): findings matched to changed files (exact, old path or an
  unambiguous path suffix) and to lines shown in the diff; a line up to three lines away snaps
  to the nearest shown line, a range becomes a multi-line comment when both ends are in one
  hunk, anything else stays unplaced (it goes into the review body). Ids are stable hashes,
  so a dismissal survives a re-run.
- **Batching** (`batch.rs`): `Draft`s become one `forge_forges::NewReview`; drafts whose line
  left the diff and general drafts are added to the review body; `finding_body` writes a
  finding as a comment with a `suggestion` block on GitHub and GitLab.
- **Store** (`store.rs`): `ReviewRecord` per request in
  `<cache dir>/forge/code-review/<kind>-<server>-<repo>/<number>.json`: viewed files with a
  digest of their diff (a new push makes them unviewed), drafts, and the summary and findings
  of one head SHA.
- **Runs** (`run.rs`): `summarize`, `review` and `explain` check the policy, call the provider
  and return what was excluded and omitted. Nothing is posted to the host here.

## Main public items

```rust
pub use anchor::{anchor, Finding};
pub use batch::{build_review, draft_from_finding, finding_body, Draft};
pub use context::{plan, Budget, ContextFile, ContextPlan, DiffChunk, Inclusion, Priority};
pub use parse::{parse_findings, parse_summary, FileSummary, RawFinding, Risk, Severity, Summary};
pub use prompt::{Prompt, RequestMeta};
pub use run::{explain, review, summarize, AiRun, Explanation, ReviewError, ReviewOutcome};
pub use store::{digest, CachedFindings, CachedSummary, ReviewRecord, ReviewStore};
```

## Used by

- IPC: `review_session`, `review_set_viewed`, `review_save_draft`, `review_delete_draft`,
  `review_submit`, `review_summarize`, `review_ai`, `review_finding`, `review_explain`
  (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/code_review.rs`)
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/forges` (`MergeRequestTab.tsx`, `ReviewDiff.tsx`, `ReviewPanel.tsx`,
  `ReviewCards.tsx`), client `app/ui/src/ipc/codeReview.ts`
- Browser mode: not built to WebAssembly (it depends on the HTTP crates); `app/ui/src/mock/codeReviewMock.ts`
  serves the demo pull request #41 with canned AI answers and applies the same `ai.enabled`
  and `.aiignore` rules through the AI mocks.

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: [`forge-ai`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-ai.md), [`forge-ai-editor`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-ai-editor.md), [`forge-forges`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-forges.md), [`forge-vcs`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-vcs.md)
- External: `dirs`, `serde`, `serde_json`, `thiserror`

## Tests

Unit tests with a fake provider (no network): prioritisation and chunking, `.aiignore`
exclusion from prompts, prompt contents, lenient parsing, anchoring and snapping, review
batching and the cache store. The hosts' `submit_review` is tested against a local mock
server in `crates/forge-forges/tests/`.

```sh
cargo test -p forge-code-review
```

# forge-codeintel

`crates/forge-codeintel` — Code intelligence models: workspace edits with LSP positions, Find Usages grouping, documentation helpers, file structure, navigation bar and related files, Go to Test and Create New Test (pure, WebAssembly-friendly).

## Purpose

Code intelligence models shared by the language server client, the language packs, the app
and the browser-mode UI. Pure Rust, so it also runs as WebAssembly.

- `edit`: text edits and workspace edits with LSP positions (0-based line, UTF-16
  character): applying them to file contents atomically (rename, quick fixes), undoing them,
  and previewing the affected lines (Refactoring Preview).
- `actions`: Show Context Actions: language server code actions and a pack's own intentions
  in PHPStorm's order, "fix all" actions nested under their quick fix, and the light bulb.
  An action may carry a `caret` (where the caret goes after its edit) and `data` (arguments
  of its UI action, which makes it a fix rather than a link); `lsp_creates` tells whether a
  language server already offers to create a symbol (Create from usage).
- `rename`: Rename (Shift+F6): the edit from references (PHP index fallback), identifier
  validation, the class file rename, conflicts, and the plan that splits an edit between open
  editors and the project backend.
- `usages`: Find Usages: the usage type of each reference (method call, import, new
  instance, ...) from its line, and the result tree grouped by usage type and file.
- `usage_options`: the Find Usages settings: options per kind of element
  (`UsageOptions::effective`, the dialog's checkboxes in `UsageOptions::fields`,
  `UsageTarget`), search scopes (`UsageScope`: Project Files, Open Files, Current File,
  Recently Changed Files, Directory, custom globs) and the text occurrences added on request
  (comments and strings, non-code files).
- `highlight`: Highlight Usages in File and the highlighting of the element at the caret:
  read / write access of usages, the exit points of a function on `return` / `throw` and a
  lexical fallback (the identifier in its scope, comments and strings left out).
- `docs`: the documentation actions of the View menu: External Documentation URLs, Quick
  Definition snippets, Context Info headers and Type Info from hovers and signatures.
- `structure`: the scopes of a document (classes, functions, control blocks, CSS rules,
  HTML elements, Lua blocks) for Sticky Lines, breadcrumbs and the Structure view of web
  files, the custom folding regions, the Structure view grouped by regions, and the stops of
  Next/Previous Method (`Alt+Down` / `Alt+Up`).
- `file_structure`: the File Structure popup's rows (Ctrl+F12): toggles, fuzzy speed search
  that keeps parents, the node at the caret.
- `navbar`: the Navigation Bar's segments (project, folders, file, members at the caret).
- `related`: Related Symbol (Ctrl+Alt+Home): tests, Laravel views / routes / migrations /
  factories / policies, Twig templates, component tests, stories and styles.
- `test_nav`: Go to Test (Ctrl+Shift+T) and the Create New Test dialog: test ↔ subject,
  the dialog's initial values from composer.json / package.json and the generated test.
- `hierarchy`: Type, Method and Call Hierarchy: the data model sources fill (`TypeGraph`,
  `CallNode`), the views of the Hierarchy tool window, scopes, sorting and merging.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `actions.rs` | Context actions (`ContextAction`, `ActionKind`) and `order_actions`: quick fixes first, preferred ones on top, duplicates removed, "fix all" actions (`source.fixAll*`, "Fix all …") moved into the `children` of their server's quick fix (`nest_fix_all`); `bulb_for` picks the red / yellow light bulb. |
| `docs.rs` | `symbol_at` (the identifier at the caret with its qualifier, call, tag and CSS context, imported frameworks) and `external_doc_url` (php.net, Laravel API, MDN, Vue, React, Lua manual); `definition_snippet` (docblock and attributes above, body to the matching brace or Lua `end`, at most 80 lines); `context_headers` (enclosing class, function and CSS rule headers); `type_from_hover` / `type_from_signature`; `language_of`. |
| `file_structure.rs` | `file_structure_view(FileStructureRequest)` → `FileStructureView { rows, selected, hasFields, hasLambdas, hasInherited }` over Structure view nodes (JSON): "Show Fields" / "Show Inherited" / "Show Lambdas" / "Sort Alphabetically", fuzzy matching with `forge-fuzzy` keeping the parents of matches, the best match or the node at the caret (`caretLine`, `enclosing` scope headers) selected. |
| `hierarchy.rs` | The model of Type / Method / Call Hierarchy: `HierarchyItem` (id, name, kind, container, LSP position, `handle` with a server's own item), `TypeGraph { root, types: TypeEntry { item, extends, implements, method? }[], method? }` and `CallNode { item, calls: CallSite { path, range, preview }[] }`. `type_view` (Class Hierarchy: superclass chain then subtypes; Supertypes; Subtypes), `method_view` (subtypes of the topmost declaring type with `MethodMark` defined / abstract / shouldDefine / inherited, "Hide Classes Where Method Is Not Implemented"), `call_view` (one level of callers / callees), `HierarchyScope` All / Production / Test / This Class (parents of matches stay), alphabetical sorting, `merge_type_graphs` / `merge_call_nodes` (entries at the same place are one), `is_test_path`. Cycles and huge graphs are cut. |
| `imports.rs` | Optimize Imports and Auto Import for every language: `summary` / `folder_summary` (PHPStorm's notifications), `minimal_edit` (one replacement for an optimized text, so the caret stays), `optimize_targets` (the files of a folder: supported types, "Only VCS changed files"), `on_the_fly_allowed` (a language server's on-the-fly import edit only away from the caret's line and the last edit). |
| `navbar.rs` | `nav_bar_segments(NavBarRequest { project, path, scopes, showMembers })` → `NavSegment { kind: project / directory / file / member, label, path, scopeKind?, line?, column? }[]`; members are the class-like and function scopes around the caret. |
| `related.rs` | `related(RelatedRequest { path, text }, files, read)` → `RelatedItem { kind, group, name, path, line, column }[]` grouped in a fixed order. Text scans, no parser: PHP class ↔ `*Test.php`, Laravel `view()` / `View::make` / `Route::view` / Inertia, `routes/*.php` lines naming a controller, model ↔ migrations (`_create_<table>_table`, `$table`), factory, policy, seeder; Symfony `render()` / `#[Template]` ↔ `templates/`; JS/TS/Vue/Svelte files ↔ `*.test.*`, `*.spec.*`, `__tests__/`, `tests/`, `*.stories.*`, style sheets. The caller lists the files and reads them lazily. |
| `test_nav.rs` | `test_targets(TestNavRequest { path, text, composerPath }, files, read)` → `TestTargets { isTest, name, targets, canCreate }` (Related Symbol's test items, best folder match first); `new_test_plan` → `NewTestPlan { frameworks, framework, subject, subjectFqn, className, namespace, directory, superclass, superclasses, fileName, members }`: PHPUnit / Pest from composer.json, namespace and folder from `autoload-dev` PSR-4 rules (`forge-file-templates`), Laravel `tests/Unit` / `tests/Feature` mirroring `app/`, Symfony `App\Tests` and `WebTestCase`, public methods from `editor_structure`; Vitest / Jest from package.json and the project's test layout (colocated, `__tests__`, `tests/`, `.test` / `.spec`), exports from a line scan. `test_source(TestSourceRequest)` → `TestSource { path, text, line }`: PHPUnit class with `setUp()` / `tearDown()` and `test<Method>()` stubs, Pest `beforeEach` / `test()` blocks, Vitest / Jest `describe` / `it` with the subject imported. |
| `edit.rs` | `TextEdit`, `WorkspaceEdit` (`edit` / `create` / `rename` / `delete` changes), `apply_workspace_edit` over a `FileStore` (all or nothing), `revert_applied`, `preview_workspace_edit`, `word_range`, UTF-16 offset helpers. |
| `structure.rs` | `editor_structure(text, language)` → `EditorStructure { scopes, regions }`: braces (PHP without inline HTML and heredocs, JS/TS with template literals, CSS, C-like), tags (HTML/XML/Vue/templates, `<script>` / `<style>` bodies as code) and Lua's block keywords outside strings and comments; each `Scope` has its kind, crumb name (`User`, `orders()`, `forEach callback`, `div#app.card`), header line and column, end and parent, and whether it sticks or is a crumb. `Region`s come from `// region` / `#region` / `<!-- region -->` / `/* region */` / `-- region` / `<editor-fold desc defaultstate>` comments. `group_by_regions` nests Structure view nodes (JSON with `line`) under their regions; `method_stops` / `method_target` give Next/Previous Method's stops (class-like, function, method and CSS rule names, closing braces of classes); `STRUCTURE_LANGUAGES` lists the languages with scopes. |
| `rename.rs` | `edit_from_locations` (references → `WorkspaceEdit`, keeping `$` where the old text had it, dynamic usages skipped), `validate_identifier`, `is_class_file` / `suggest_file_rename` / `renamed_path` (PHPStorm renames `User.php` with `class User`), `edit_conflicts` (overlapping edits, renames onto existing files) and `plan_edit` (`EditPlan`: text edits of open editors, the backend's part, files to save first, tabs to reopen or close). |
| `usages.rs` | `UsageKind` (PHPStorm's usage types and their group labels), `classify_usage` from the line around a reference, `group_usages` into a `UsageTree` by usage type and file (the declaration and duplicates removed). |

# forge-codestyle

`crates/forge-codestyle` — Code style schemes (Settings | Editor | Code Style): options per language, presets, scheme storage and resolution, import/export and the formatting passes and previews (pure, WebAssembly-friendly).

## Purpose

Everything behind Settings | Editor | Code Style, as in PHPStorm. The UI
(`app/ui/src/features/codeStyle`) renders the pages from the model and keeps the edited
schemes as a draft of the Settings dialog; everything else happens here.

- `model`: the options of the General page and of the 13 language pages (PHP, HTML,
  CSS/SCSS/Less, JavaScript, TypeScript, JSON, YAML, Lua, Blade, Twig, SQL, XML, Markdown).
  Each option has a key (`spaces.afterComma`), title, tab ("Tabs and Indents", "Spaces",
  "Wrapping and Braces", "Blank Lines" and language tabs such as "Code Conversion",
  "Punctuation", "Case", "Other"), section, kind (bool, int range, choice, text), default and
  its name in PHPStorm's XML. Languages list the file types they format (`scss` → CSS,
  `tsx` → TypeScript) and their "Set from…" presets: PSR-12, PER Coding Style 2.0, Symfony,
  Laravel, WordPress and Drupal for PHP; JavaScript Standard Style, Airbnb-like and Prettier
  defaults for JavaScript and TypeScript; stylelint-config-standard; StyLua defaults; …
- `scheme`: where schemes live. Values are keyed `<language>.<option>`. The **Default**
  scheme is the user settings layer under the keys every page always used
  (`php.codeStyle.indent`, `editor.codeStyle.hardWrapAt`), the **Project** scheme the same
  keys in the project layer (options it does not set come from Default), further IDE schemes
  are stored under `editor.codeStyle.schemes.<id>.name` / `.values.<language>.<option>`.
  `editor.codeStyle.scheme` selects the project's scheme; without it a project with code
  style settings uses its Project scheme. `load` builds the schemes from the layers,
  `selected_values` gives the values formatting uses, `effective_settings` replaces the code
  style keys of the effective settings with them (for `forge_text::resolve_format` and the
  PHP code style), `plan_save` turns edited schemes into settings writes (only values that
  differ from the scheme's base, removed schemes deleted) and `apply_preset` is "Set from…".
  The single PHP brace option of older versions (`php.codeStyle.braces`: `psr12`, `allman`,
  `kr`) is read as the three brace options and removed on the next save.
- `io`: export and import. Forge's JSON (`{ "forgeCodeStyle": 1, "name", "values" }`) has every
  option; the PHPStorm XML subset (`<code_scheme>` with root options, `<…CodeStyleSettings>`,
  `<codeStyleSettings language="…">` and `<indentOptions>`, also inside
  `.idea/codeStyles/Project.xml`) maps Forge's options to PHPStorm's names, and options
  PHPStorm has no name for go into a `<ForgeCodeStyleSettings>` element so a scheme survives
  the round trip. The XML reader is a small built-in parser.
- `format`: a lossless lexer (`format::lexer`) for PHP, JavaScript/TypeScript, CSS, JSON,
  Lua and SQL, and the formatters:
  - `preview(language, values)` lays the page's sample out completely with the options
    (indentation from the nesting, brace placement, spaces, blank lines, conversions; markup
    by element/directive nesting, YAML by nesting, SQL clauses, Markdown blocks). The
    General page's sample shows the formatter markers.
  - `post_format(request, values)` runs after a language server or tool formatted a file:
    for PHP the spaces, brace and `else`/`catch`/`finally` placement and the code conversions
    (array syntax, trailing commas, `true`/`false`/`null` case) on the existing lines (it
    never re-indents), quotes in plain JavaScript/TypeScript files (not JSX), hex color case in
    CSS, SQL keyword case, the Markdown spaces and blank lines, Blade/Twig delimiters, blank
    lines, indents on empty lines and the `@formatter:off` / `@formatter:on` regions, which get
    their text from before formatting.
- `lsp`: the options handed to external formatters: `settings_patch(language, values)` for
  the language servers (`intelephense.format.braces`, `typescript.format` /
  `javascript.format` and the quote preference, `css`/`scss`/`less.format`, `html.format`,
  `json.format.keepLines`, `yaml.format`, `xml.format`, `Lua.format.defaultConfig`) and
  `stylua_args(values)` for StyLua when the project has no `stylua.toml`.

## Main public items

```rust
pub fn model() -> &'static CodeStyleModel { … }
pub fn load(layers: Layers<'_>) -> SchemesState { … }
pub fn selected_values(layers: Layers<'_>) -> Values { … }
pub fn effective_settings(effective: &Map<String, Value>, layers: Layers<'_>) -> Map<String, Value> { … }
pub fn plan_save(layers: Layers<'_>, state: &SchemesState) -> Result<Vec<SettingWrite>, String> { … }
pub fn apply_preset(values: &Values, language: &str, preset: &str) -> Option<Values> { … }
pub fn export(name: &str, values: &Values, format: ExportFormat) -> String { … }
pub fn import(text: &str) -> Result<ImportedScheme, String> { … }
pub fn preview(language: &str, values: &Values) -> Option<String> { … }
pub fn post_format(req: &PostFormatRequest, values: &Values) -> String { … }
pub fn lsp::settings_patch(language: &str, values: &Values) -> Value { … }
pub fn lsp::stylua_args(values: &Values) -> Vec<String> { … }
```

## Used by

- IPC (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/code_style.rs`, client `app/ui/src/ipc/codeStyle.ts`):

# forge-colors

`crates/forge-colors` — Color values in code: finding CSS colors (hex, rgb, hsl, hwb, named, Tailwind) in CSS, markup and script files, parsing and formatting them in their notation (pure, WebAssembly-friendly).

## Purpose

The logic behind the editor's color previews and the color picker. The UI
(`app/ui/src/features/colors`) draws the swatches and the picker; offsets are UTF-16.

- `color`: `Rgba` (channels 0–255 with fractions, alpha 0–1), `parse` for every CSS notation
  (hex with 3/4/6/8 digits, `rgb()`/`rgba()`, `hsl()`/`hsla()`, `hwb()`, legacy commas and
  modern spaces with `/ alpha`, percentages, `deg`/`rad`/`grad`/`turn`, `none`, names) with
  its `Notation`, and `format`, which writes a color in the notation of the original text
  (short hex while possible, the same function name and separators, `rgb` → `rgba` in legacy
  syntax when an alpha appears, percentages kept, names kept or replaced by hex).
- `named`: the 148 CSS color names plus `transparent`, and Tailwind CSS's default palette
  (22 colors × 11 shades, `black`, `white`).
- `find`: colors of a document by language: declarations in CSS/SCSS/Less (selectors and
  comments skipped, `var()` and `url()` left alone) and Sass/Stylus lines, `<style>` blocks and
  `style` attributes of markup, strings of scripts (whole-string color names, hex and color
  functions), and Tailwind color classes (`bg-blue-500`, `text-white/50`) in class attributes
  and strings (not editable).

## Main public items

```rust
pub fn find(req: &FindRequest) -> Vec<ColorMatch> { … }
pub fn find_colors(text: &str, language: &str) -> Vec<ColorMatch> { … }
pub fn parse(text: &str) -> Option<(Rgba, Notation)> { … }
pub fn format(color: Rgba, original: &str) -> String { … }
pub fn format_color(req: &FormatRequest) -> String { … }
pub fn parse_color(text: &str) -> Option<Parsed> { … }
```

## Used by

- IPC: `colors_find`, `colors_format`, `colors_parse` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/emmet.rs`).
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/colors` (gutter swatches as line markers, inline swatches, the color
  picker, Show Color Picker). Swatches and the picker call Rust in-process through
  `forge-wasm` in both modes.
- Browser mode: built into `forge-wasm` (`emmet.rs`).

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: none
- External: `serde`

## Tests

Unit tests for parsing every notation, HSL/HWB conversions, formatting in each notation, the
named colors and the Tailwind palette, finding colors in CSS, SCSS, Sass, HTML, Vue and TSX,
and UTF-16 offsets.

# forge-containers

`crates/forge-containers` — Forge IDE containers: Docker Engine API, Docker Compose and Kubernetes for the Services tool window.

## Purpose

Containers for the Services tool window: Docker, Docker Compose and Kubernetes.

Pure parts (no I/O, built for WebAssembly too):
- `docker`: Docker Engine API JSON (containers, images, volumes, networks) into models.
- `compose`: `compose.yaml` / `docker-compose.yml` parsing, project names, command lines
  and the mapping of containers to services by their labels.
- `kube`: kubeconfig parsing and Kubernetes API objects (pods, deployments, services).
- `kubectl`: kubectl command lines and output for Kubernetes on a remote project's host.
- `logs`: the multiplexed Docker log stream and Kubernetes log lines.
- `pull`: image pull progress from the Engine's JSON messages.
- `endpoint`: where the Docker daemon is (`DOCKER_HOST`, settings, platform defaults).
- `tree`: the Services tree, details (Dashboard / Inspection) and toolbar state.
- `gutter`: ▶ markers for compose services and Dockerfiles.
- `portforward`: the Kubernetes port-forward channel protocol and active forwards.
- `ws`: WebSocket handshake and framing (Kubernetes streaming subresources).

With the `runtime` feature: an HTTP/1.1 client over Unix sockets, Windows named pipes,
TCP (+TLS) and SSH-forwarded sockets (`http`, `ssh`), the Docker Engine client
(`engine`), the Kubernetes API client (`kubeclient`), port-forward connections
(`forward`), compose / CLI processes (`cli`) and registry credentials in the OS
keychain (`secrets`), and the `hub` that holds the Services state for the app.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `cli.rs` | `docker compose …`, `docker build` / `docker run` (Dockerfile ▶) and other CLI runs with their output streamed line by line. Compose has no Engine API, so these are processes; everything else talks to the Engine directly (`crate::engine`). |
| `compose.rs` | Docker Compose files (`compose.yaml`, `docker-compose.yml`, overrides): services with their images, builds, ports, profiles and env files, the project name, `${VAR}` interpolation from the project's `.env`, and the `docker compose` command lines. |
| `docker.rs` | Docker Engine API objects (`GET /containers/json`, `/images/json`, `/volumes`, `/networks`, `/version`) as models for the tree. The raw JSON is parsed leniently: missing fields get defaults so older and newer Engine versions both work. |
| `endpoint.rs` | Where the Docker daemon listens: Settings \| Build, Execution, Deployment \| Docker (`docker.connection`, `docker.socketPath`, `docker.tcp.*`, `docker.ssh.*`, `docker.context`), else `DOCKER_HOST`, else the current Docker context (`~/.docker/contexts`), else the platform default (named pipe on Windows; `/var/run/docker.sock`, Docker Desktop's `~/.docker/run/docker.sock`, rootless `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/docker.sock` or Podman elsewhere). |
| `engine.rs` | Docker Engine API client (no CLI): snapshot of containers, images, volumes and networks, container lifecycle, inspect, log streaming, image pulls with progress and the event stream that tells the tree to refresh. |
| `exec.rs` | Interactive command lines that run in a terminal PTY: a shell inside a container (`docker exec -it`), attaching to a container's console (`docker attach`) and a shell in a pod (`kubectl exec -it`) and attaching to a pod's container (`kubectl attach -it`). |
| `forward.rs` | Port-forward connections: the WebSocket upgrade to a pod's `portforward` subresource and the pump between a local TCP connection and the pod port (`crate::portforward` has the channel protocol, `crate::ws` the framing). |
| `gutter.rs` | ▶ gutter markers: on `services:` (up all) and every service of a compose file (up one), and on the first `FROM` of a Dockerfile (build the image and run a container), plus the command lines those markers run. |
| `http.rs` | A small HTTP/1.1 client for the Docker Engine API and the Kubernetes API server: one connection per request over a Unix socket, a Windows named pipe or TCP (optionally TLS), `Content-Length`, chunked and read-to-close bodies, and streaming bodies for logs, events and pulls. |
| `hub.rs` | The Services backend: one `Hub` per app holds the Docker connection (with a watcher that follows the Engine's events and reconnects), the project's compose files, the kubeconfig with lazily loaded namespaces and workloads, running log streams and the consoles (Log tabs). |
| `kube.rs` | Kubernetes: kubeconfig files (clusters, users, contexts) and the API objects the tree shows (namespaces, pods, deployments, services). |
| `kubectl.rs` | Kubernetes through `kubectl` on a remote project's host: command lines (`config view`, `get -o json`, `logs -f`, `port-forward`, `apply -f` / `delete -f`), the kubectl per host (`kubernetes.hostKubectlPaths`), parsing its output (the port of `Forwarding from …`), Kubernetes manifests in YAML files, and (runtime) the `KubectlClient` that runs them through the project's backend. |
| `kubeclient.rs` | Kubernetes API client for one kubeconfig context: TLS with the cluster's CA (rustls), bearer tokens, client certificates, basic auth and exec credential plugins (`gke-gcloud-auth-plugin`, `aws eks get-token`, …). |
| `logs.rs` | Container log streams. |
| `portforward.rs` | Kubernetes port forwarding (`kubectl port-forward`, PHPStorm's Forward Ports): the `portforward` subresource over a WebSocket with the `v4.channel.k8s.io` channel protocol, and the list of active forwards the Services tool window shows. |
| `pull.rs` | Image pulls: `POST /images/create?fromImage=…` answers with one JSON message per line (`{"status":"Downloading","id":"a1b2","progressDetail":{"current":1,"total":9}}`). |
| `secrets.rs` | Docker registry credentials in the OS keychain (service `forge-containers`, account `registry:<server>`). The list of servers and user names is not secret and is passed in by the caller (settings); only passwords and tokens go to the keychain. |
| `ssh.rs` | The Docker API of an `ssh://user@host` daemon: one SSH session (`forge-remote`: ssh-agent, `~/.ssh` keys and `~/.ssh/config`, `known_hosts`) and a forwarded Unix socket (`direct-streamlocal`) to the daemon's socket per HTTP request. |
| `time.rs` | Timestamps: RFC 3339 parsing (Kubernetes, volumes) and the "5 minutes ago" texts. |
| `tree.rs` | The Services tool window model: the tree (Docker → Containers / Images / Networks / Volumes, Docker Compose → projects → services → containers, Kubernetes → contexts → namespaces → Pods / Deployments / Services), the details pane (Dashboard rows, available tabs) and which toolbar actions apply to a node. |
| `ws.rs` | WebSocket (RFC 6455) pieces for the Kubernetes streaming subresources: the upgrade handshake headers and `Sec-WebSocket-Accept` check, frame encoding (client frames are masked) and an incremental frame decoder that also joins fragmented messages. |

## Main public items

```rust
pub struct Error(pub String);
```

## Used by

- IPC: `services_tree`, `services_refresh`, `services_compose_changed`, `services_expand`, `services_details`, `services_action`, `services_inspect`, `services_console`, `services_logs_start`, `services_logs_stop`, `services_terminal`, `services_port_forward_start`, `services_port_forward_stop`, `services_port_forwards`, `services_pull`, `services_compose_up`, `services_dockerfile_run`, `services_gutter`, `services_kube_selection`, `services_kube_select`, `services_kube_apply`, `services_status`, `docker_test_connection`, `docker_contexts`, `docker_registry_login`, `docker_registry_logout`, `docker_registry_status` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/services.rs`)
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/services`
- Browser mode: built into `forge-wasm`

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: [`forge-output`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-output.md), [`forge-remote`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-remote.md)
- External: `base64`, `dirs`, `keyring`, `rustls`, `serde`, `serde_json`, `sha1`, `tokio`, `tokio-rustls`, `tracing`, `webpki-roots`, `yaml-rust2`

# forge-core

`crates/forge-core` — Forge IDE core: workspace, file system, settings and event bus.

## Purpose

Forge core: the language-agnostic foundation every pack builds on.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `error.rs` | `ForgeError`: English `Display` for logs, serialized to the UI in the IDE language (`errors.*` keys of forge-i18n); `ForgeError::no_project()`. |
| `excludes.rs` | The project's excluded paths (`Excludes`, a handle shared by every clone of a `Workspace`, computed by `forge_scopes::structure::ExcludeSet`): walks, `list_dir` (`FileEntry::excluded`) and the watcher follow it. |
| `gitignore.rs` | Which project files git ignores, so the project tree can gray them out like PHPStorm. |
| `paths.rs` | Path spelling that works the same on every platform. `paths::canonicalize` is `std::fs::canonicalize` without Windows' verbatim `\\?\` prefix (when the path means the same without it; `simplify_verbatim` holds the rules and is tested on every platform), so project roots, the paths handed to language servers, Git and other tools, and the paths they report back use the ordinary spelling. `relative_to(root, abs)` makes a path project-relative across Windows spellings (`\\?\C:\…`, `c:\…`, `/` or `\`). `Workspace::open` uses `canonicalize`. |
| `project_files.rs` | Project-relative files that Forge itself keeps in a project (`.forge/settings.toml`, `.forge/dataSources.toml`, `.forge/breakpoints.json`, ...) and project files it reads (`.env`), wherever the project lives: `LocalFiles` for a folder on this machine, the project backend (`forge_backend::BackendFiles`) for a project on a remote host. |
| `search.rs` | Fuzzy file search for "Go to File" / Search Everywhere, and Find in Files. |
| `settings.rs` | Layered settings: built-in defaults < user < Settings for New Projects (`SettingsScope::NewProjects`, `new-project-settings.toml`) < project. `Settings::set_many` stores several values and saves each layer once (the Code Style schemes); `parse_settings_toml` / `settings_to_toml` convert between flat keys and the nested files (settings archives). |
| `watch.rs` | Watches the open project for changes made outside the editor (git checkouts, composer, code generators, other editors) and reports them in debounced batches. |
| `workspace.rs` |  |

## Main public items

```rust
pub use error::{ForgeError, Result};
pub use project_files::{LocalFiles, MemoryFiles, ProjectFiles, SharedFiles};
pub use search::{fuzzy_match, fuzzy_match_with, FileMatch, FuzzyMatch, MatchOptions};
pub use settings::{Settings, SettingsChange, SettingsScope};
pub use watch::{FsChanges, ProjectWatcher};
pub use workspace::{FileEntry, FileKind, Workspace};
```

## Used by

# forge-devenv

`crates/forge-devenv` — Forge IDE Dev Containers and WSL: devcontainer.json, docker command lines, WSL distributions and path mapping, and the Forge agent over a process's stdio.

## Purpose

Dev Containers and WSL projects, like PHPStorm / JetBrains Gateway: the project's
services run in a container or a WSL distribution through the Forge agent
(`crates/forge-remote-agent`), which Forge starts over the stdio of `docker exec` or
`wsl.exe` instead of SSH; the project then opens as a `forge_backend::RemoteBackend`
(`RemoteHost.kind` = `RemoteKind::DevContainer` / `RemoteKind::Wsl`).

Pure modules (also built for WebAssembly without the `runtime` feature):
- `jsonc`: JSON with comments and trailing commas.
- `devcontainer`: `devcontainer.json` locations, parsing and resolving.
- `docker`: Docker CLI command lines and the `docker ps` list of dev containers.
- `wsl`: `wsl.exe -l -v` (UTF-16) parsing, command lines and Windows ↔ Linux paths.

With `runtime` (the default):
- `runner`: processes on this machine behind a trait (fakes in tests).
- `agent`: copying the agent in and starting it over a process's stdio.
- `connection`: a live agent connection that restarts the agent when it ends.
- `up`: building / starting a dev container with a build log.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `agent.rs` | The agent over `docker exec -i` / `wsl.exe -d <distro> --exec`: the probe, upload (`cat`) and start commands of `forge_remote::deploy` wrapped by an `AgentTarget` (`DockerTarget`, `WslTarget`), the ready marker skipped, then the usual `RpcClient`. |
| `connection.rs` | `StdioConnection`: the `forge_backend::remote::Connection` of such a project; restarts the agent with backoff (1–30 s) when its process ends and calls the reconnect hooks (`RemoteBackend::reattach`). |
| `devcontainer.rs` | `devcontainer.json` model (`image`, `build`, `dockerComposeFile` + `service`, `workspaceFolder`, `workspaceMount`, `forwardPorts`, lifecycle commands, `remoteUser`, `containerEnv`, `mounts`, `features`, …), `resolve` against the local folder (absolute paths, `${localWorkspaceFolder}` and the other variables, defaults), configuration locations and the gutter line. |
| `docker.rs` | `docker build` / `pull` / `run`, the compose override file and `docker compose up` / `down`, `docker exec` for lifecycle commands, the agent and terminals, the labels (`forge.devcontainer.*`, `devcontainer.local_folder`, `devcontainer.config_file`) and the `docker ps` list. |
| `jsonc.rs` | Comment and trailing-comma removal that keeps positions. |
| `runner.rs` | `Runner` (`output`, `stream`, `spawn_stdio`) and `SystemRunner` (tokio processes, no console window on Windows). |
| `up.rs` | Create or start a dev container: find it by label, pull / build / compose up, `docker run`, `onCreateCommand` / `postCreateCommand` / `postStartCommand`, every step and output line as `LogLine`. |
| `wsl.rs` | UTF-16LE decoding of `wsl.exe` output, `wsl.exe -l -v` parsing (localized headers and states), `--exec` / `--cd` command lines, `C:\…` ↔ `/mnt/c/…` and `\\wsl$\<distro>\…` / `\\wsl.localhost\…` ↔ Linux paths. |

## Used by

- IPC: `devcontainer_configs`, `devcontainer_gutter`, `devcontainer_list`, `devcontainer_up`, `devcontainer_cancel`, `devcontainer_action`, `devcontainer_open`, `wsl_distributions`, `wsl_map_path`, `wsl_windows_path`, `wsl_connect`, `wsl_browse`, `wsl_open_project`, `wsl_disconnect` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/devenv.rs`)

# forge-diff

`crates/forge-diff` — Forge IDE comparisons: folder diff (Compare Directories), pure and
WebAssembly-friendly.

## Purpose

The folder diff of PHPStorm's Compare Directories (see the
[user guide](docs/guide/user/git.md#compare-files-and-folders)). Text diffs of two files are
computed by the diff viewer itself.

- `compare_listings`: two listings (paths relative to the compared folders, a size and an
  FNV-1a content digest per file) → rows in tree order (folders first, children after their
  folder) with `equal`, `different`, `leftOnly` or `rightOnly`; a folder is equal when
  everything below it is.
- `list_tree` / `compare_trees`: read two folders on this machine (`.git`, `.hg`, `.svn`
  skipped, symbolic links compared by their target, at most `MAX_ENTRIES` per side).

## Main public items

```rust
pub fn compare_listings(left: &Listing, right: &Listing) -> DirCompare
pub fn compare_trees(left: &Path, right: &Path) -> io::Result<DirCompare>
pub fn list_tree(root: &Path, limit: usize) -> io::Result<Listing>
pub struct DirDiffEntry { path, dir, depth, status: DiffStatus, left_size, right_size, left_modified, right_modified }
```

## Used by

- `forge-backend`: `Backend::compare_dirs` (local: `compare_trees`; remote: the agent call
  `CompareDirs`, protocol 9) and `compare::copy_entry` (Copy to Left / Right)
- IPC: `compare_dirs`, `compare_copy` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/compare.rs`)
- Browser mode: `compare_dir_listings` in `forge-wasm` on the demo files

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: none
- External: `serde`

## Tests

Unit tests with fixture folders (every state, nesting, file against folder, limits).

# forge-deploy

`crates/forge-deploy` — Deployment (Tools | Deployment): servers, path mappings, transfers and
comparing with the deployed files.

## Purpose

The logic behind [Deployment](docs/guide/user/deployment.md).

Pure modules (also built for WebAssembly with `default-features = false`):

- `config`: `DeployServer` (`kind`: `sftp | ftp | ftps | local`, the SSH configuration id,
  FTP host / port / user / anonymous / passive, `root_path`, `web_url`, `mappings`,
  `excluded`) and `DeploymentConfig { default_server, servers }`, stored as
  `.forge/deployment.toml` (`PROJECT_FILE`, `parse`, `to_toml`, `upsert` with ids from the
  name, `remove` moving the default). `validate()` lists the form's problems.
- `mapping`: `DeployServer::resolve(local)` → `Resolution::Mapped(deployment path) |
  NotMapped | Excluded` (the longest local path wins; no mappings = root to root; `..` is
  never mapped), `local_path(deployment)` back, `web_url_of`, `display_path` (root path
  included), `is_excluded(side, path)`, and `ExcludeNames` ("Exclude items by name" with `*`
  and `?`).
- `options`: `DeployOptions` (`AutoUpload::{Always, Explicit, Never}`, overwrite up-to-date
  files, preserve timestamps, delete target items, create empty directories,
  `WarnNewer`, `CompareBy`).
- `compare`: `Entry` (path, dir, size, modified, digest), `compare(local, remote, by)` on top
  of `forge_diff::compare_listings` (the digest carries content, nothing or the timestamp),
  `is_up_to_date` and `is_newer_on_target`.
- `browse`: the Remote Host tree. `nodes(server, entries)` → `RemoteNode { path, name, dir,
  size, modified, local, mapping_root, excluded }` (folders first, by name ignoring case;
  `local` is the mapped project path, `mapping_root` a mapping's deployment path),
  `check_name`, `child_path`, `renamed_path` (New File / New Directory / Rename) and
  `absolute_path` (Copy Path).

With `client` (the default):

- `fs::ServerFs`: `stat`, `list`, `read`, `write`, `mkdir`, `remove_file`, `remove_dir`,
  `rename`, `set_modified`, `describe`, `invalidate` (forget cached listings), plus
  `mkdir_all` / `remove_all`; paths are relative to the server's root path.
- `local::LocalFolder` (local servers and the project side of every transfer),
  `ftp::FtpFs` (suppaftp, MIT OR Apache-2.0; FTPS is explicit TLS with rustls and
  `webpki-roots`; `MLSD` with a `LIST` fallback, `MFMT` for timestamps, a listing cache per
  session) and `sftp::SftpFs` (russh-sftp, Apache-2.0, on a `forge_remote::session::SshSession`
  with its own one-thread runtime; `SshSession::open_subsystem("sftp")`).
- `transfer::Deployer` (`new(project, server_fs, server, options)`, `skip_local`,
  `cancel`, `on_progress`): `transfer(Upload | Download, paths, overwrite_newer)`,
  `delete_remote`, `read_remote`, `sync_compare(folder)`; results are `Summary` with a
  `FileResult` per file (`Transferred`, `UpToDate`, `NewerOnTarget`, `Excluded`,
  `NotMapped`, `Deleted`, `Failed`).
- `connect::open(server, secret, project)` opens any server type (`ssh_params` builds the
  SSH parameters of a saved configuration with its keychain secret); `connect::test` is Test
  Connection.
- `secrets`: FTP passwords in the keychain (service `forge-deploy`, account
  `ftp://user@host:port`).
- `remote_host`: `Connections` (open connections by server id, reused while the server is
  unchanged and `stat("")` works, closed after a failed operation), `list`, `create`,
  `rename`, `delete`, `read_text`, and Edit Remote File: `start_edit(fs, server, path, cache)`
  downloads into `<cache>/remote-edit/<server>/<path>` (`temp_path`), `save_edit(fs, edited,
  data, force)` uploads unless the server copy's digest changed (`SaveOutcome::Uploaded |
  Conflict { deleted }`).

## IPC

`app/src-tauri/src/commands/deployment.rs`: `deploy_config`, `deploy_server_save({ server,
secret? })`, `deploy_server_delete({ id })`, `deploy_set_default({ id })`,
`deploy_validate({ server })`, `deploy_test({ server, secret? })`, `deploy_transfer({ id,
serverId?, direction, paths, overwriteNewer? })`, `deploy_delete({ id, serverId?, paths })`,
`deploy_cancel({ id })`, `deploy_auto_upload({ id, paths, explicit })`,
`deploy_sync_compare({ serverId?, path })`, `deploy_read_remote({ serverId?, path })`; events
`deploy://transfer` (`started`, `file`, `finished`). Browser mode: `app/ui/src/mock/deploymentMock.ts`
with `crates/forge-wasm/src/deploy.rs` (`deploy_validate`, `deploy_resolve`,
`deploy_compare`, `deploy_remote_nodes`, `deploy_entry_path`).

Remote Host (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/remote_host.rs`): `remote_host_list({ serverId, path
}) -> { root, rootNode, nodes }`, `remote_host_create({ serverId, dir, name, folder })`,
`remote_host_rename({ serverId, path, newName })`, `remote_host_delete({ serverId, paths })`,
`remote_host_edit({ serverId, path }) -> { text, temp, remote }`, `remote_host_save_edit({
serverId, path, text, force? }) -> { status: "uploaded" } | { status: "conflict", deleted }`,
`remote_host_close_edit`, `remote_host_disconnect({ serverId? })`. Browser mode:
`app/ui/src/mock/remoteHostMock.ts`.

Transfers never run project code, so they work in Safe Mode; `deploy_auto_upload` does
nothing in Safe Mode.

## Dependencies

`forge-diff`, `serde`, `toml`; with `client`: `forge-remote`, `russh-sftp`, `suppaftp`
(`rustls-ring`), `webpki-roots`, `tokio`, `keyring`, `filetime`, `dirs`.

## Tests

Unit tests for the configuration, mappings, exclusions, options, comparison, MFMT timestamps,
local folders and keychain accounts. `tests/servers.rs` runs the whole feature set (upload with
mappings and exclusions, up-to-date skips, newer files, Sync with Deployed, download,
Compare with Deployed Version, delete target items, delete on server, cancel) against a local
folder, an in-process FTP server (`tests/common/ftp.rs`, also without `MLSD`/`MFMT`, wrong
passwords, refused TLS) and an in-process SSH server with the SFTP subsystem
(`tests/common/sftp.rs`, host key confirmation). The same run covers the Remote Host tree
and its operations (listing with mappings, New Directory / New File, Rename, Refresh after
outside changes, Edit Remote File with the conflict check, Delete) on every server type. No
network beyond 127.0.0.1.

# forge-dap

`crates/forge-dap` — Forge IDE shared debugging layer: Debug Adapter Protocol client, adapter
registry and native debugger views.

## Purpose

The debugger of every language pack except PHP (which uses Xdebug through
[forge-debug](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-debug.md)). It is a client of the
[Debug Adapter Protocol](https://microsoft.github.io/debug-adapter-protocol/) and maps DAP
sessions onto Forge's debugger model, so the Debug tool window drives Xdebug and DAP sessions
with the same `debug_*` commands and `debug://*` events.

- `client::DapClient` speaks the protocol: Content-Length framing (`codec`), requests with
  sequence numbers and timeouts, responses, events and reverse requests.
- `transport::Transport`: an adapter process on stdio, a TCP connection to an adapter that
  listens (started by Forge with `${port}`, or already running: "Attach to DAP server"), or a
  TCP server Forge opens for an adapter that connects back. `${port}` is a free port below the
  system's ephemeral range (20000-32767) from [`forge-ports`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-ports.md), so no other
  program is handed the same port before the adapter binds it.
- `adapter`: `DebugAdapterDescriptor` (how to start an adapter and build its `launch` /
  `attach` arguments), `ManifestAdapter` (adapters declared with
  `[[contributions.debugAdapters]]`, request templates with `${program}`, `${args}`,
  `${cwd}`, `${env}`, `${pid}`, `${core}`, `${stopOnEntry}`), `AdapterRegistry` and
  `LaunchRequest` (launch, attach to a process, attach to a DAP server, attach to a
  debuggee's port (`AttachPort`: `node --inspect`, a browser's remote debugging port), core
  dump). `adapterArgs` and `adapterCommand` change a manifest adapter's command line for one
  session (CForge's GDB `-iex` commands for STL pretty printers, a cross toolchain's
  `gdb-multiarch`); such requests count as running code (`runs_code`), so Safe Mode refuses
  them.
- `manager::DapManager` starts and tracks sessions (`register_adapter` / `unregister_adapter`
  for adapters implemented in Rust, such as [webforge-js-debug](docs/guide/developer/crates/webforge-js-debug.md)'s js-debug), shares the project's breakpoints with
  Xdebug through a `BreakpointHost` (the app's `DebugServer`) and resends them when they
  change. Relative program and working directory paths are resolved against the project.
- `session::DapSession`: initialize → launch/attach → breakpoints → configurationDone (for
  adapters that announce `initialized` early, like GDB, breakpoints go first), stopped /
  continued / output / thread / breakpoint / terminated / exited / module / process / memory /
  capabilities / invalidated events, the reverse requests `runInTerminal` (Forge starts the
  program with its output in the console) and `startDebugging` (child sessions; when Forge
  started the parent's adapter as a TCP server, the child connects to that same server, as
  js-debug needs). Requests:
  threads, stackTrace, scopes, variables, setVariable / setExpression, evaluate (watch, repl,
  hover), completions, continue / next / stepIn / stepOut (also by instruction), pause, goto,
  restart, terminate, disconnect, setBreakpoints (conditions, hit counts, logpoints),
  setFunctionBreakpoints, setExceptionBreakpoints (filters stored as breakpoints),
  dataBreakpointInfo + setDataBreakpoints (watchpoints), readMemory / writeMemory,
  disassemble, modules, loadedSources.
- `views`: rows of the Memory view (hex/ASCII), Disassembly instructions, address parsing.
- `processes`: local processes for Attach to Process (`/proc` on Linux, `ps` on macOS,
  `tasklist` on Windows; no third-party crate).
- `fake`: a simulated adapter running a small C program, used by the tests and available as
  the `forge-dap-fake` binary (stdio, `--connect <port>`, `--listen <port>`, and
  `--serve <port>` for many clients).

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `adapter.rs` | Debug adapter descriptors: how to start an adapter and which `launch` / `attach` arguments it gets. |
| `client.rs` | One connection to a debug adapter: requests, responses, events and reverse requests. |
| `codec.rs` | DAP base protocol: `Content-Length` framed JSON messages. |
| `error.rs` | `DapError`, convertible to `ForgeError`. |
| `fake.rs` | The simulated adapter (`DEMO_SOURCE`, `FakeAdapter`, `serve`). |
| `manager.rs` | `DapManager`: adapter registry and running sessions; `BreakpointHost`, `DapConfig`. |
| `processes.rs` | Local processes for "Attach to Process…". |
| `protocol.rs` | DAP messages and the typed bodies Forge uses. |
| `session.rs` | A DAP session bridged to Forge's debugger model (`SessionInfo`, `Frame`, `Property`, `DebugEvent`). |
| `transport.rs` | Stdio, TCP connect and TCP listen transports. |
| `views.rs` | Memory rows, instructions and addresses of the native views. |

## Main public items

```rust
pub use adapter::{AdapterInfo, AdapterRegistry, DebugAdapterDescriptor, LaunchMode, LaunchRequest, ManifestAdapter, ResolvedLaunch};
pub use error::{DapError, DapResult};
pub use manager::{BreakpointHost, DapConfig, DapManager};
pub use processes::{list_processes, ProcessInfo};
pub use session::{DapSession, LoadedSource};
pub use transport::{AdapterCommand, Transport};
pub use views::{Instruction, MemoryBlock, MemoryRow};

pub trait DebugAdapterDescriptor: Send + Sync {
    fn info(&self) -> AdapterInfo;
    fn resolve(&self, request: &LaunchRequest) -> DapResult<ResolvedLaunch>;
    /// Breakpoints follow `launch` / `attach` even when `initialized` comes right after
    /// `initialize` (rdbg maps breakpoint paths only after `attach`). Default: false.
    fn breakpoints_after_request(&self) -> bool { false }
}
```

## Used by

- IPC: `dap_adapters`, `dap_start`, `dap_restart`, `dap_threads`, `dap_goto`, `dap_registers`,
  `dap_read_memory`, `dap_write_memory`, `dap_disassemble`, `dap_modules`,
  `dap_loaded_sources`, `dap_data_breakpoint`, `dap_processes`
  (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/dap.rs`); the shared `debug_*` commands route `dap-<n>`
  session ids here (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/debug.rs`). `DapSession::read_bytes` (raw
  `readMemory`) serves CForge's Peripherals view (`cpp_svd_read`,
  `app/src-tauri/src/commands/embedded.rs`).
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/debug` (`dapApi.ts`, `adapters.ts`, `nativeViews.tsx`,
  `AttachDialogs.tsx`)
- Browser mode: not built to WebAssembly (runtime code); browser mode uses
  `app/ui/src/mock/dapMock.ts`, the same simulated C program.

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: [`forge-core`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-core.md), [`forge-debug`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-debug.md),
  [`forge-plugin-api`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-plugin-api.md), [`forge-ports`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-ports.md) (free adapter
  ports), [`forge-runtools`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-runtools.md)
- External: `base64`, `serde`, `serde_json`, `thiserror`, `tokio`, `tracing`

## Tests

12 source files, about 6300 lines; 25 unit tests and 10 integration tests in `tests/`
(`fake_adapter.rs`): launch, breakpoints, stack, threads, variables, stepping, logpoints,
conditions and hit counts, function and exception breakpoints, watchpoints, memory read and
write, disassembly, instruction stepping, goto, set value, attach to a process and to a DAP
server, adapters that listen or connect back, `runInTerminal`, child sessions, core dumps and
restart, all against the fake adapter. No real debugger is needed; an ignored smoke test runs
GDB's DAP server (`gdb -i dap`, GDB 14+) with a C compiler when both are installed.
