# forge-testing

`crates/forge-testing` — the shared test runner and coverage model of every pack (pure, also
built to WebAssembly).

## Purpose

What [Testing](docs/guide/user/testing.md) and [Code coverage](docs/guide/user/coverage.md) compute
besides the test results themselves (those are [`forge-output`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-output.md)'s test event
protocol and parsers). Packs register test frameworks as manifest data or as code; the backend
asks one registry for gutter discovery, command lines and Rerun Failed Tests, and reads
coverage reports into one model.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `targets.rs` | `TestFile` (the tests of a file with their temporary configurations and result keys), `TestTarget`, `TargetKind` (`class`, `method`, `file`, `describe`, `test`, `dataset`, `feature`, `scenario`, `example`, `suite`), `FailedTest`. |

| `spec.rs` | `TestFrameworkSpec`, the manifest contribution `[[contributions.testFrameworks]]`: detection (globs, dependency files), test file globs, line-pattern discovery nested by indentation with full names, per-scope arguments with placeholders (`${file}`, `${test}`, `${testPattern}`, `${pattern}`, `${reportDir}`, `${coverageFile}`), escaping (regex, Lua patterns), rerun by pattern, location rules and coverage; `SpecProvider`; `glob_regex`, `expand`. |
| `provider.rs` | The contribution point: `TestFrameworkProvider` (`id`, `types`, `accepts`, `discover`, `rerun_failed`, `command`, `supports_coverage`), `CommandContext` (report folder, coverage file, settings), `TestCommand` (program, arguments, environment, `TestReport`, `JUnitFlavor`, location rules, default file, coverage request) and the `TestFrameworks` registry (`register`, `register_specs`, `for_type`, `discover`, `discover_in_project` (the frameworks the project uses first), `rerun_failed`, `command`, `info`). |

# forge-trust

`crates/forge-trust` — Project trust and Safe Mode: trusted projects and locations, and what
may run.

## Purpose

The logic behind [Project trust and Safe Mode](docs/guide/user/project-trust.md):

- `TrustStore { projects, locations }` is `<config dir>/forge/trusted-projects.toml`
  (`TrustStore::default_path`, `load`, `save`). `reason(project)` says why a project is
  trusted (`TrustReason::Project` or `Location { location }`), `check(project)` builds the
  `TrustCheck` the dialog and banner show (key, display text, parent folder for "Trust
  projects in …"). `trust`, `distrust`, `add_location` (expands `~`, refuses relative paths
  and file system roots) and `remove_location` edit it.
- Keys: `local_key(path)` is the canonical local path (symlinks resolved, no Windows `\\?\`
  prefix); `remote_key(user, host, port, path)` is `ssh://user@host:port/path`.
  `normalize` cleans separators, `.` and `..`; `contains(location, project)` matches whole path
  components on the same machine (case-insensitive for local paths on Windows); `display`
  shows remote keys as `user@host:/path`.
- `SafeMode` is the shared flag of the open project; `check(what)` returns the error
  `refusal(what)` while it is on.
- `runs_project_program(root, program, args)` tells whether a command starts a program from
  the project (the program or a path argument lies inside `root`), lexically so it works for
  remote roots; `server_runs_project_code(id)` lists catalog language servers that execute
  project files (`SERVERS_RUNNING_PROJECT_CODE`; DotNetForge adds `roslyn` and `fsautocomplete`, which load MSBuild projects).
- `ssh_session_needs_confirmation(safe_mode, SshTarget)`: an SSH terminal session to a
  deployment server (`SshTarget::ProjectServer`, defined in the project's files) needs the
  user's confirmation in Safe Mode; the user's own SSH configurations
  (`SshTarget::UserConfiguration`) never do. `ssh_confirmation_required(server)` is the error
  `terminal_open` returns without it.

## IPC

`app/src-tauri/src/commands/trust.rs`: `trust_check({ path })`, `trust_status()`,
`trust_project({ path?, location? })`, `trust_locations()`, `trust_location_add({ path })`,
`trust_location_remove({ key })`; `trust://changed` carries the open project's status.
`AppState::safe_mode` is set when a project opens (`refresh_safe_mode`) and every command that
starts project programs calls `AppState::require_trusted`; the LSP manager's launcher is
wrapped by `SafeModeLauncher`.

## Dependencies

`forge-core` (errors), `serde`, `toml`, `dirs`.

## Tests

Unit tests in `src/lib.rs`: normalization, remote keys, locations and their hosts, parent
locations, the store round trip, roots and relative paths, Safe Mode errors and project
program detection. `commands::trust` tests the app state following the store.

# forge-update

`crates/forge-update` — Forge update checks: when to check, which release is an update, the update feed, simulated updates and download speed.

## Purpose

The Tauri shell downloads, verifies (minisign signature) and installs updates with
`tauri-plugin-updater`. Everything that decides *whether* and *what* to offer lives here,
without a window or an app handle, so it is unit tested.

- `policy`: the update channel, the remembered state (last check, skipped and postponed
  versions), when a check is due (`plan`) and which release counts as an update (`evaluate`).
- `feed`: the `latest.json` feed that `pnpm tauri build` produces (`createUpdaterArtifacts`),
  fetching it, the download size and the `UpdateOffer` the splash screen shows.

## Channels

| Channel | Feeds read (`Channel::endpoints`) | Offered |
| --- | --- | --- |
| stable | `DEFAULT_ENDPOINT` | releases without a pre-release label |
| beta | `BETA_ENDPOINT`, then `DEFAULT_ENDPOINT` | the newest release of both feeds, pre-releases included |

`pick_feed` takes the newest release among the answers: a missing beta feed (404) is ignored as
long as the stable feed answers, and a feed marked `"channel": "beta"` never counts on the
stable channel. The offer remembers its feed (`UpdateOffer::feed`), so the download reads the
same one. An `updates.endpoint` override is the only feed read.
- `simulate`: a fake offer and download for `FORGE_SIMULATE_UPDATE` (desktop dev builds) and
  `?simulateUpdate` (browser mode). Nothing is installed.
- `meter`: the download speed shown while an update downloads.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `policy.rs` | `Channel` (its feeds `endpoints`, `of_release` for tags), `UpdateState`, `plan` (once a day, dev builds, missing key, simulation) and `evaluate` (newer, channel, skipped, postponed). |
| `feed.rs` | `Feed` (`latest.json`, optional `channel` field), `pick_feed` (newest release among the channel's feeds), `check`, `fetch_feed`, `download_size`, `client`, `UpdateOffer` and its one-line summary. |
| `simulate.rs` | Simulated offer and chunk sizes of the fake download. |
| `meter.rs` | `SpeedMeter`: bytes per second over a two-second window. |

## Main public items

```rust
pub use feed::{check, client, fetch_feed, pick_feed, CheckOutcome, CheckRequest, Feed, FeedPlatform, UpdateOffer};
pub use meter::SpeedMeter;
pub use policy::{evaluate, plan, Channel, CheckPlan, PlanInput, Postponed, SkipReason, UpdateState, Verdict};
pub const DEFAULT_ENDPOINT: &str; // https://github.com/Reeperk/Forge/releases/latest/download/latest.json
pub const BETA_ENDPOINT: &str;    // https://github.com/Reeperk/Forge/releases/download/beta/latest-beta.json
pub const CHECK_INTERVAL_SECS: u64; // one day
pub fn parse_version(text: &str) -> Result<semver::Version> { … }
pub fn format_size(bytes: u64) -> String { … }
```

## Used by

- IPC: `updates_check`, `updates_respond`, `updates_status`, `updates_clear_skipped`, and the
  update step of the splash (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/updates.rs`, `app/src-tauri/src/startup.rs`)
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/updates`, `app/ui/src/splash`

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: none
- External: `serde`, `serde_json`, `thiserror`, `semver`, `reqwest`

## Tests

5 source files; 26 unit tests. The feed tests run against a local HTTP server on `127.0.0.1`
(no network access).

```sh
cargo test -p forge-update
```

# forge-vcs

`crates/forge-vcs` — Forge IDE version control: drives the git CLI and parses its output.

## Purpose

Forge version control. Drives the `git` command line (no libgit2, no shell) and parses
its machine-readable output into serializable types for the UI.

Paths in and out are relative to the *workspace* root, which may be a subdirectory of the
repository; `Repo` converts them to and from repository paths.

The parsers and the three-way merge (`merge`) are pure and also build for WebAssembly
(`default-features = false`); running git needs the default `git` feature.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `blame.rs` | Parser for `git blame --porcelain`. |
| `branch.rs` | Branches and tags from `git for-each-ref`, plus recently checked out branches from the reflog. |
| `changelists.rs` | `Changelists`: the changelist model of the Commit tool window (lists, active list, file → list, moved hunks → list): `sync` with the status, `create`/`edit`/`delete`/`set_active`/`ensure`, `move_files`, `move_hunks`, `normalize_file`, `view`. Pure (also WebAssembly). |
| `cmd.rs` | Running the `git` executable. No shell is involved: arguments are passed as-is, so paths with spaces or quotes need no escaping on any platform. |
| `diff.rs` | Parser for unified diffs as printed by `git diff`. |
| `history.rs` | File, folder and selection history: `FileRevision`, `BlockRevision`, `HistoryQuery` and the parsers of `git log -z --name-status` and `git log -L` output. Pure. |
| `hunks.rs` | Change hunks of a file against its committed version for partial commits: `change_hunks` (stable ids from base position and content), `apply_hunks` (base plus the included hunks). Pure. |
| `log.rs` | Commit history: parser for a NUL/RS separated `git log` format, ref decorations and per-commit changed files. |
| `ops.rs` | Options of the Pull, Merge, Rebase, Reset HEAD and Tag dialogs (`PullOptions`, `MergeOptions`, `RebaseOptions`, `ResetMode`, `TagOptions`, `OperationAction`) and the git command lines they stand for; forbidden combinations are rejected. Pure. |
| `patch.rs` | `git diff --binary` patches: split per file (`split_patch`, `join_patch`), apply a file's hunks to its base text (`apply_file_patch`), give foreign unified diffs git headers (`normalize_patch`), make paths project-relative (`strip_path_prefix`) and the Apply Patch preview (`preview_patch`). Pure. |
| `merge.rs` | Three-way merge for the merge window: diff3 chunking of yours/base/theirs (`merge_three_way` → `MergeModel` with `left`/`right`/`both`/`conflict` chunks), word-level "Resolve Simple Conflicts" (`resolve_simple`), `auto_merge`, line separator helpers. Pure. |
| `rebase.rs` | Git Log actions that rewrite history and the interactive rebase: which actions a selection allows with PHPStorm's reasons (`log_action_states` from `SelectionFacts`, protected branch patterns), the initial plan with autosquash (`autosquash`) and the `git-rebase-todo` (`plan_todo`, `render_todo`: messages are applied with `exec` amend steps from blobs, the todo is copied in by `sequence.editor`). Pure. |
| `repo.rs` | `Repo`: every git operation of the IDE, through a `GitExec` (local or remote host). |
| `repo/rewrite.rs` | The Git Log context menu: `log_action_states` (pushed / protected detection via `for-each-ref --contains`), `cherry_pick` (skips empty picks, `-x` for protected commits), `revert_commits`, `undo_commit`, `reword`, `squash_commits`, `drop_commits`, `rebase_plan`, `interactive_rebase` (`git rebase -i --autostash` without an editor), `undo_rewrite`, `commits_patch`, `tree_files`. |
| `repo/conflicts.rs` | Merge conflicts: unmerged files and their sides (`git ls-files -u`), the operation (merge, rebase, cherry-pick, revert, unstash; a rebase only when `git status` confirms it, since `rebase --skip` leaves a stale `REBASE_HEAD`) and pane titles, stage versions `:1:`/`:2:`/`:3:` (`merge_file`), Accept Yours/Theirs (`accept_conflict_side`). Yours is git's `theirs` in a rebase. |
| `repo/ops.rs` | Pull/Merge/Rebase with options (`pull_with`, `merge_with`, `rebase_with`), the operation in progress (`operation_state`, via `REBASE_HEAD`/`MERGE_HEAD`/… and the long status, which also drops a stale `REBASE_HEAD`), Continue/Abort/Skip (`operation_action`), `reset_head`, `tag`, `resolve_commit`, `edit_remote`, stash details (`stash_files`, `stash_file`, `stash_clear`, `stash_branch`). |
| `repo/partial.rs` | Commits with the commit panel's options (`CommitOptions`: amend, sign-off, `--no-verify`, author; `commit_opts`) and partial commits (`commit_files`: the index is saved with `write-tree`, rebuilt from HEAD plus whole files and `hash-object`/`update-index` blobs of the included hunks, committed, then restored), `file_hunks`. |
| `repo/patches.rs` | Create Patch from local changes (`create_patch`, optionally reversed, project-relative) and Apply Patch (`apply_patch`: what fits in one go, the rest with `--3way` so conflicts reach the resolver; base directory via `--directory`). |
| `repo/shelve.rs` | Shelve (`changes_patch` incl. untracked files, then roll back), Unshelve (`git apply`, falling back to `--3way` with conflicts for the resolver; partial by file) and `shelf_file` (before/after for Show Diff). |
| `repo/history.rs` | Show History (`file_history`, `--follow` for files), Show History for Selection (`block_history`, `git log -L`), Annotate Revision (`blame_at`) and Compare with Branch on a folder (`changes_since`). |
| `shelf.rs` | `Shelf`: shelved changelists stored in Forge's per-project data dir (`<id>/changes.json` + `shelved.patch`): list, create, rename, delete, remove files. |
| `status.rs` | Parser for `git status --porcelain=v2 -z --branch`. |

## Main public items

# forge-vim

`crates/forge-vim` — Vim emulation (IdeaVim-style): modes, motions, operators, text objects, registers, ex commands and ~/.ideavimrc parsing (pure, built to WebAssembly).

## Purpose

The engine behind [Vim emulation](docs/guide/user/vim-emulation.md). It is pure Rust so it compiles
to WebAssembly: the editor calls it synchronously for every key press (a keydown handler
must decide on `preventDefault` before it returns), in the desktop app and in browser mode.

- `Vim` holds the global state (options, registers, mappings, macros, search, the
  shortcut handlers) and one buffer per attached editor: a copy of the document, mode,
  caret, marks and pending keys.
- The UI sends each key with a `Sync`: the document changes since the last call (batches
  of CodeMirror changes, UTF-16 offsets), the selection, the visible lines and the indent
  unit. The `Response` carries sequential edits, the new selection, the mode, the pending
  keys, the command line, a message and effects for the UI: undo/redo through the
  editor's history, IDE actions (`:action`, `gd`, `:w`), opening files, clipboard writes,
  scrolling and reloading the rc file. Effects the UI performs asynchronously pause the
  remaining keys of a mapping or macro (`resume`).
- `claims` tells the keymap resolver which keys Vim takes from the IDE keymap in the focused
  editor (plain keys outside Insert mode, `Escape`, and the `Ctrl` shortcuts whose handler is
  Vim in the current mode).

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `engine.rs` | The state machine: typeahead and mappings (with `timeoutlen`), Normal/Visual/Insert/Replace/command-line modes, operators, dot repeat, macros, marks, search, scrolling and responses. |
| `command.rs` | Parsing of Normal and Visual mode commands (`"a2d3w`, `ci"`, `gUU`, `<C-w>v`). |
| `motions.rs` | Word, paragraph, bracket and character motions. |
| `textobj.rs` | `iw aw iW aW`, quotes, brackets (with counts), tags and paragraphs. |
| `ex.rs` | Ex commands with ranges: `:w :q :e :s :g :v :normal :d :y :j :> :< :m :t :sort :set :map :action :registers :marks …`. |
| `rc.rs` | `~/.ideavimrc`: `set`, mappings, `let mapleader`, `sethandler`, `if has('ide')`, `source` inlining, problem reports. |
| `handlers.rs` | The shortcut conflict table (Vim or IDE per `Ctrl` shortcut and mode) and `sethandler`. |
| `keys.rs` | Vim key notation (`<C-r>`, `<leader>`, `<Action>(Id)`) and DOM key events. |
| `pattern.rs` | Vim regular expressions translated to a syntax shared by Rust's `regex` and JavaScript (search highlights), and `:s` replacement strings. |
| `registers.rs` | Unnamed, numbered, small delete, named (append), black hole, read-only and clipboard registers. |
| `options.rs` | `:set` options with Vim's abbreviations and `no…`/`inv…`/`…!`/`…?`/`…+=`. |
| `buffer.rs` | The document copy: lines, character classes, UTF-16 conversion. |

## Main public items

```rust
pub use engine::{Change, Effect, Handle, Response, SelRange, Sync, Viewport, Vim};
pub use handlers::{HandlerOverride, HandlerRow};
pub use keys::DomKey;
pub use rc::RcReport;
```

## Used by

- Browser mode and the desktop UI: `forge-wasm` (`vim.rs`: `vim_attach`, `vim_key`,
  `vim_timeout`, `vim_configure`, `vim_load_rc`, `vim_handlers`, …); `keymap_handle_key` asks
  `claims` before resolving a key in the editor
- IPC: `vim_read_rc` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/vim.rs`, inlines `source` lines with
  `rc::expand_sources`)
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/vim/`

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: none
- External: `regex`, `serde`, `serde_json`

## Tests

```sh
cargo test -p forge-vim
```

Unit tests per module plus behaviour tests in `tests/engine.rs` that type keys into a buffer
with the caret marked as `|` (`check("foo b|ar", "ciwqux<Esc>", "foo qu|x")`).

# forge-vulns

`crates/forge-vulns` — Vulnerable dependency check: a shared vulnerability model, the JSON
reports of each ecosystem's audit tool (composer audit, npm / pnpm / yarn audit, pip-audit,
cargo audit, govulncheck, OWASP dependency-check), what to audit in a project, where
dependencies are declared and the Upgrade quick fix.

## Purpose

Everything the [Vulnerable dependencies](docs/guide/user/vulnerable-dependencies.md) UI shows is
computed here. Forge has no advisory database of its own: each ecosystem's tool does the
lookup and this crate turns its JSON into one model. The crate is pure (no processes, files or
network): the desktop app runs the tools through the project's backend
(`app/src-tauri/src/commands/vulnerabilities.rs`) and browser mode feeds recorded reports of
the demo projects through `forge-wasm`.

The ecosystem parsers it builds on are reused, not copied: `phpforge-composer` reads
`composer audit` and composer.json / composer.lock, `pyforge-lang-python` the requirements
files and pyproject.toml, `goforge-lang-go` go.mod, `webforge-lang-web` the package manager
of package.json and `forge-jsonschema` the positions in package.json.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `model.rs` | `Vulnerability` (ecosystem, package, installed version, advisory id and aliases, severity, title, affected range, fixed version, URL, `via` direct dependencies, `reachable`), `Notice` (abandoned, unmaintained, yanked), `Findings`, `Severity` with its editor severity, version comparison and the fixed version of an affected range or patched list. |
| `cvss.rs` | CVSS 3.0 / 3.1 base scores from a vector, for advisories without a rating (cargo audit). |
| `parse/` | One module per report: `composer` (through `phpforge_composer::audit`), `npm` (npm 7+ `auditReportVersion: 2`, the npm 6 format of pnpm and Yarn 2/3, Yarn 1 NDJSON, Yarn 4 trees), `pip` (pip-audit), `cargo` (cargo audit with warnings), `go` (the govulncheck message stream), `depcheck` (dependency-check JSON with Maven coordinates from package URLs). |
| `tool.rs` | `Tool` (id, label, executable, arguments, install hint), `detect` (which audits a project's root needs, with the lock file, the files to annotate and why one is blocked) and `cache_key` (FNV-1a over the tool and its input files). |
| `declare.rs` | Declarations with name and constraint positions in composer.json, composer.lock, package.json, requirements files, pyproject.toml (PEP 621, dependency groups, Poetry), Cargo.toml (tables, inline tables, renames, workspaces), go.mod (plus `go` / `toolchain` for the standard library), pom.xml and Gradle scripts; `upgraded_constraint` keeps the constraint's style. |
| `problems.rs` | The Vulnerable Dependencies problems of a file (direct packages with `Upgrade`, transitive ones on the dependency that pulls them in, notices) and `upgrade` (the edited text). |
| `report.rs` | `TargetResult` (status ok / blocked / missing / failed), `from_output` (a run's stdout and stderr, tolerant of the tools' error exit codes), `fill_installed` (installed versions from composer.lock / package-lock.json) and `CacheEntry`. |
| `text.rs` | Byte offsets ↔ 0-based lines and UTF-16 columns. |

## Used by

- IPC: `vulnerabilities_check`, `vulnerabilities_problems`, `vulnerabilities_upgrade`,
  `vulnerabilities_install_command` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/vulnerabilities.rs`; the
  results are cached in `<cache dir>/forge/vulnerabilities/<project>/`)
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/vulnerabilities/` (and Composer | Audit in `features/composer`)
- Browser mode: built into `forge-wasm` (`vulnerabilities.rs`), used by
  `app/ui/src/mock/vulnerabilitiesMock.ts`

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: forge-jsonschema, phpforge-composer, pyforge-lang-python, goforge-lang-go,
  webforge-lang-web (without its `fs` feature)
- External: `serde`, `serde_json`

## Tests

Unit tests for every module, plus `tests/reports.rs` with output recorded from each tool in
`tests/fixtures/` (composer audit, npm audit with and without a lock file, pnpm audit, Yarn 1
and Yarn 4, pip-audit, cargo audit, govulncheck, dependency-check). No test runs a tool or
needs network.

```sh
cargo test -p forge-vulns
```

# forge-wasm

`crates/forge-wasm` — WebAssembly build of Forge's pure Rust logic for the browser-mode UI.

## Purpose

WebAssembly bridge for the browser-mode UI.

Forge's rule is "Rust computes, TypeScript renders". In the desktop app the UI calls Rust
through Tauri IPC; in browser mode (`pnpm dev`, screenshots, tests) the same Rust code runs
as WebAssembly so mocks never re-implement logic in TypeScript.

Only **pure** crates belong here (no file system, processes, network or tokio). Each area
adds a module that wraps its crate with `#[wasm_bindgen]` functions taking and returning
JSON strings, mirroring the matching IPC command:

```rust
#[wasm_bindgen]
pub fn keymap_resolve(request_json: &str) -> String { … }
```

Rebuild the bundle with `pnpm --dir app/ui wasm` (output: `app/ui/src/wasm/pkg`).

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `cli_tools.rs` | Command Line Tool Support (`phpforge-cli-tools`), mirroring the `cli_tools_*` commands: the effective tools from the demo files and settings, parsing of recorded `list --format=json` output, completion and the command line of a console input. |
| `ai_editor.rs` | AI in the editor (`forge_ai_editor`) for the browser-mode mock: the fake provider's canned answers go through the same post-processing, prompts, proposals and `.aiignore` policy as the desktop app's `ai_inline_complete`, `ai_action` and `ai_explain`. |
| `agents.rs` | Agent CLIs (`forge_agent_cli`) for the browser-mode agent mock: the built-in agents' profiles (what `agent_list` reports besides detection) and the stream parsers, so the mock replays recorded CLI output through the same Rust code as the desktop app. |
| `containers.rs` | Services tool window (`forge-containers`) for the browser-mode mock: the mock keeps a fake Docker daemon as Engine API JSON, compose files and a kubeconfig as text, and asks Rust for the models, the tree, the details pane, the gutter markers, command lines and pull progress, like the desktop app's hub. |
| `editing.rs` | Editor actions (`forge-editing`): postfix templates and their expansion, Complete Current Statement and Cyclic Expand Word, mirroring the `editor_postfix_*`, `editor_complete_statement` and `editor_expand_word` commands. |

# forge-window

`crates/forge-window` — Forge window chrome: desktop detection, title bar button layouts and dialog window geometry (pure, also built to WebAssembly).

## Purpose

Window chrome for Forge's own (undecorated) windows.

- `desktop`: which OS and desktop environment Forge runs on, read from the target OS and
  environment variables (`XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP`, `DESKTOP_SESSION`, …).
- `chrome`: the title bar style and button layout for the setting
  `appearance.windowControls` (`auto | windows | macos | gnome | kde | linux | native`),
  including GNOME's `button-layout` and KDE's `kwinrc` button order.
- `geometry`: where a dialog window opens (centered on its parent, or where the user left
  it) and the remembered size and position of every dialog.
- `projects`: the registry of running project windows (one Forge instance each, oldest
  first), Next / Previous Project Window with wrap-around, pruning of instances that no longer
  answer, and the `forge-window <token> info|focus` control lines between instances.
- `reveal`: the commands that show a file in the system file manager (Explorer's `/select,`,
  `open -R`, the freedesktop `FileManager1.ShowItems` D-Bus call with `xdg-open` as fallback)
  and the file manager's name for Select In….

The crate is pure (no file system, processes or windowing): the Tauri shell reads the
environment and files and passes them in, and the browser-mode UI runs the same code as
WebAssembly.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `chrome.rs` | Title bar style and button layout for `appearance.windowControls`. |
| `desktop.rs` | Operating system and desktop environment detection. |
| `geometry.rs` | Where dialog windows open and the geometry Forge remembers for each dialog. |
| `projects.rs` | The project window registry and the control protocol between Forge instances. |
| `reveal.rs` | Commands that reveal a file in Explorer, Finder or the Linux file manager. |

## Main public items

```rust
pub use chrome::{…};
pub use desktop::{detect_desktop, Desktop, Os};
pub use geometry::{place_dialog, DialogStates, Rect, Size};
pub use projects::{control_line, parse_control_line, ControlRequest, ProjectWindowEntry, ProjectWindowInfo, ProjectWindows};
pub use reveal::{file_manager_name, reveal_commands, RevealCommand};
pub fn dialog_label(id: &str) -> Option<String> { … }
pub fn dialog_id(label: &str) -> Option<&str> { … }
```

## Used by

- IPC: `window_chrome`, `reveal_in_file_manager`, `dialog_window_open`, `dialog_window_close`, `dialog_window_message` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/window.rs`); `project_windows_list`, `project_window_focus`, `project_window_cycle`, `project_window_open` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/project_windows.rs`)
- UI: `app/ui/src/shell/window`
- Browser mode: built into `forge-wasm`

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: none
- External: `serde`, `serde_json`

## Tests

6 source files, about 1400 lines; 30 unit tests.

```sh
cargo test -p forge-window
```

# javaforge-build

`packs/javaforge/build` — JavaForge: Maven and Gradle builds (detection from the build files, wrappers, modules, lifecycle goals and tasks, JaCoCo, command lines, sync models, dependency trees, Gradle DSL and pom.xml completion, outdated dependencies; pure, also built to WebAssembly).

## Purpose

JavaForge's Maven and Gradle support, like IntelliJ IDEA's build tool integration. Pure Rust:
the caller hands in file names and texts, so the desktop backend, the remote agent and the
browser mode (WebAssembly) share it.

- `detect` reads a build (`BuildProject`): the tool, its wrapper (`mvnw`, `gradlew`), the
  Kotlin or Groovy DSL, modules (`settings.gradle` `include`, `pom.xml` `<modules>`), JaCoCo,
  the test frameworks the build depends on, the Java release, Gradle's `application` main class,
  Spring Boot and custom tasks.
- `goals` lists Maven lifecycle phases and plugin goals, or Gradle tasks by group, for the
  Gradle / Maven tool windows.
- `command` builds command lines: goals and tasks (Gradle `:module:task`, Maven `-pl module
  -am`), Build Project (`classes testClasses`, `test-compile`) and test runs (Gradle `cleanTest
  test --tests`, Maven Surefire `test -Dtest=` with `-Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false`)
  with their JUnit XML report folders and JaCoCo reports; Maven profiles (`-Pdev,!prod`) and
  Skip Tests; Application runs through Gradle (`forgeRun` of `GRADLE_RUN_INIT_SCRIPT`) and the
  sync command lines.
- `model` is the Gradle / Maven tool window's model (`BuildModel`: projects, tasks, Maven
  plugins and profiles, dependency trees, source sets with their `java` / `groovy` / `kotlin` /
  `scala` / `resources` folders: `conventional_source_sets` of the applied plugins, Gradle's
  `sourceSets` after a sync): `static_model` from the build files,
  `GRADLE_INIT_SCRIPT` (`forgeModel` writes projects, tasks and resolved dependencies as JSON)
  with `parse_gradle_model`, `parse_maven_tree` for `mvn dependency:tree` (plain and `[INFO]`
  output) and `merge`.
- `wrapper` reads and updates `gradle-wrapper.properties` and compares
  `distributionSha256Sum` with the published checksum (`Checksum`).
- `dsl` completes Gradle Kotlin / Groovy DSL scripts from a hand-written model of the common
  blocks and in `pom.xml`; `request` says what Maven Central must answer (coordinates,
  versions), `complete` builds the items (`forge_jsonschema::CompletionOut`).
- `deps` finds declared dependencies with the place of their version (Maven properties
  resolved) and the "newer version available" markers; `version` orders Maven versions
  (qualifiers, variants like `-jre` / `-android`).
- `central` has Maven Central's search and `maven-metadata.xml` URLs and parsers; `net`
  (feature `net`, desktop only) downloads them with a cache in `<cache>/forge/maven-central`
  and asks services.gradle.org for releases and SHA-256 sums.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `central.rs` | `search_query`, `search_url`, `parse_search` → `Artifact`, `metadata_url`, `parse_metadata` → `Versions`. |
| `command.rs` | `ExecOptions` (wrapper, executable, build folder, offline, profiles, skip tests), `executable`, `goals_command`, `build_project_command`, `TestFilter` and `test_command` → `TestRun`, `GRADLE_RUN_INIT_SCRIPT`, `GradleAppRun` and `gradle_application_command`, `gradle_sync_command`, `maven_sync_command`. |
| `deps.rs` | `FileKind`, `Declared`, `declarations`, `versioned_coordinates`, `OutdatedMarker` and `outdated`. |

# javaforge-fw-spring

`packs/javaforge/fw-spring` — JavaForge: Spring Boot and Jakarta EE (Java / Kotlin declaration
scanner, beans and injection points, Spring MVC and JAX-RS endpoints, JPA entities,
application.properties / application.yml assistance from spring-configuration-metadata.json and
the dependency jars, the Spring Boot run configuration, actuator client and run dashboard; pure,
also built to WebAssembly).

## Purpose

The logic of the plugin `forge.spring`; see [Spring Boot and Jakarta EE](docs/guide/user/spring.md).
Everything is static analysis of the texts the caller hands in: the application is never
started to find beans or endpoints. Two features add I/O for the desktop: `jars` (reading the
dependency jars as zip files) and `net` (a plain HTTP/1.1 client for the actuator on
localhost). Without them the crate builds to WebAssembly.

- `scan` lexes Java and Kotlin (comments, text blocks, raw strings, string templates, backtick
  names) and reads package, imports, classes (kind, supertypes with type arguments, enum
  constants), constructors (Kotlin primary constructors with `val` / `var` properties),
  methods, fields and parameters with their annotations **and annotation arguments** (string
  literals, concatenations, constants, class literals, arrays), doc comments, literal
  defaults and string constants (also `API + "/stock"` across files). Half-typed code still
  yields the declarations around it.
- `model` builds the project model: beans (stereotypes and custom meta-annotated ones, `@Bean`
  methods, Spring Data repositories, `@ConfigurationProperties`, CDI scopes, EJB, JAX-RS
  resources, `@Produces`), injection points (constructors, Lombok's required-args fields,
  `@Autowired` / `@Inject` / `@Resource` fields and setters, `@Bean` parameters) matched by
  type and supertypes with qualifiers, `@Primary` and name fallback; Spring MVC endpoints with
  class prefixes, methods, media types and parameters, JAX-RS endpoints below the
  `@ApplicationPath`; JPA entities with columns, ids and relations linked to their
  repositories; `@ConfigurationProperties` classes turned into metadata; the APIs in use
  (`jakarta.*`, `javax.*`, Spring); profiles; configuration values per profile; and the gutter
  markers of a file. `Project` keeps the scanned files so an edited file is scanned again on its
  own.
- `config` reads `application*.properties` / `application*.yml` (documents, lists, block
  scalars, quoted keys, continuation lines) into dotted keys with byte ranges, finds where the
  cursor is (a key being typed with its YAML parent path, or a value), and implements relaxed
  binding (`canonical`).
- `metadata` holds `spring-configuration-metadata.json` (properties, groups, hints, deprecations)
  plus enum constants; `assist` completes keys (nested YAML insertion) and values (booleans,
  enums, hints, profiles) with Markdown documentation, inspects unknown / deprecated keys and
  invalid values (with the replacement text of the quick fix), hovers and navigates to
  `@ConfigurationProperties`.
- `jars` (feature `jars`) finds the jars of the synced coordinates in `~/.m2/repository` and
  Gradle's `modules-2/files-2.1` cache (or Spring Boot's own jars of the build's version, else
  the newest cached), reads their metadata files and the enum constants of property types from
  class files (`class_enum_constants`).
- `run` turns the `spring-boot` configuration into an Application run (profiles, colored
  output, `--key=value` overrides, actuator exposure) and follows the console (`Observed`:
  port, context path, server, profiles, PID, startup time, failures, Spring Boot version).
- `actuator` parses `/actuator/health`, `/beans` and `/mappings` (Spring Boot 2 and 3, MVC and
  WebFlux); with `net`, `probe` reads them from `127.0.0.1` (chunked and length-delimited
  bodies, 503 health).
- `dashboard` builds the Services nodes and details of the run dashboard; `views` merges the
  model with a running application's beans and mappings and writes "Open in HTTP Client"
  requests.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `scan.rs` | `parse(path, text) -> SourceFile`, `Lang`, `ClassInfo`, `Callable`, `Field`, `Param`, `Annotation`, `AnnArg`, `Val`, `TypeRef`, `resolve_constants`. |
| `model.rs` | `analyze(files) -> Model`, `Project`, `Bean`, `Injection`, `Endpoint`, `Entity`, `ConfigClass`, `Application`, `Api`, `gutter(model, path) -> Marker[]`, `setting(model, key, profiles)`, `injected_type`, `join_paths`. |
| `config.rs` | `config_file`, `Format`, `parse`, `Entry`, `place_at`, `Place`, `canonical`, `kebab`. |
| `metadata.rs` | `Metadata`, `Property`, `Hint`, `Group`, `Deprecation`, `short_type`. |
| `assist.rs` | `complete`, `inspect`, `hover`, `goto`, `documentation`, `Context`, `Completion`, `Problem`, `Hover`. |
| `jars.rs` | `Caches`, `Coordinate`, `jars_for`, `jar_metadata`, `load`, `enum_constants`, `class_enum_constants` (feature `jars`). |
| `run.rs` | `TYPE`, `launch`, `Launch`, `profiles`, `overrides`, `Observed`, `strip_ansi`. |
| `actuator.rs` | `parse_health`, `parse_beans`, `parse_mappings`, `Snapshot`; `get`, `probe` (feature `net`). |
| `dashboard.rs` | `DashboardApp`, `tree`, `details`, `node_id`, `app_name`. |
| `views.rs` | `EndpointRow`, `BeanRow`, `endpoint_rows`, `bean_rows`, `http_request`. |

## Used by

- The app: `commands/spring.rs` (the `spring_*` IPC commands: model cache, jar metadata cache,
  run tracking and actuator probes) and `commands/run.rs` (Spring Boot runs become Application
  runs; their output goes to the dashboard's observer).
- [`forge-wasm`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-wasm.md): `spring_overview`, `spring_gutter`, `spring_config`,
  `spring_http_request`, `spring_launch`, `spring_observe`, `spring_dashboard` for the browser
  mode (`?project=spring`).
- [`forge-project`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-project.md) detects the `spring-boot` and `jakarta-ee` frameworks
  that activate the plugin.

12 source files; unit tests on inline Java / Kotlin / YAML / properties fixtures, a fake
metadata JSON, jars and class files written by the tests, and a local mock HTTP server for the
actuator (no network).

# javaforge-jdk

`packs/javaforge/jdk` — JavaForge: JDK detection and Eclipse Temurin downloads.

## Purpose

JavaForge's JDKs, like IntelliJ IDEA's SDK table.

- `detect` finds the JDKs on the machine: `JAVA_HOME`, `java` on `PATH` (symlinks resolved),
  `/usr/lib/jvm`, `/usr/java`, `/opt/java` (Linux), `/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines` and
  `~/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines` plus Homebrew (macOS), `Program Files` vendor folders and
  the registry (`reg query`, Windows), SDKMAN!, asdf, jabba, Gradle toolchains (`~/.gradle/jdks`),
  IntelliJ's `~/.jdks` and Forge's downloads (`<data dir>/forge/jdks`). macOS bundles
  (`Contents/Home`) and folders with one JDK inside are followed; a JRE (no `javac`) is skipped;
  the same JDK reached twice is listed once. `pick` chooses the JDK of a minimum release
  (JDT LS) or a preferred one.
- `release` reads a JDK's `release` file (`JAVA_VERSION`, `IMPLEMENTOR`, …): the feature
  release (`1.8.0_412` → 8) and the vendor (`Eclipse Temurin`, `Azul Zulu`, …).
- `adoptium` downloads Eclipse Temurin: the Adoptium API names the latest build of a feature
  release for this platform with its SHA-256; the archive is verified, unpacked into a staging
  folder and renamed into `<data dir>/forge/jdks/<release>`.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `adoptium.rs` | `AvailableReleases`, `Platform`, `assets_url`, `parse_assets`, `available_releases`, `download`. |
| `detect.rs` | `Jdk`, `DetectEnv` (`system()`), `detect`, `inspect`, `pick`, `parse_registry`, `system_roots`. |
| `release.rs` | `ReleaseInfo`, `parse_release`, `major_of`, `vendor_name`. |

## Main public items

```rust
pub use detect::{detect, inspect, pick, DetectEnv, Jdk};
pub fn default_jdks_dir() -> Option<PathBuf>;
pub fn java_executable(home: &str, windows: bool) -> String;
```

## Used by

- The app (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/java.rs`: `java_jdks`, `java_jdk_inspect`,
  `java_jdk_releases`, `java_jdk_download`, the JDK of JDT LS, runs and `JAVA_HOME`).

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: [`forge-langservers`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-langservers.md) (`managed::Http`, `archive`, `Event`)
- External: `serde`, `serde_json`, `dirs`

## Tests

5 source files, about 1140 lines; 9 tests with fixture JDK folders and a local HTTP server (no
network). `tests/jdtls_smoke.rs` is an ignored end-to-end test against the real JDT LS,
java-debug and, if needed, a Temurin download:


# javaforge-minecraft

`packs/javaforge/minecraft` — JavaForge: Minecraft plugins and mods (the New Project generators for Paper, Purpur, Folia, Spigot, Bukkit, Velocity and BungeeCord plugins and Fabric and NeoForge mods with pinned version tables, project detection, plugin.yml / paper-plugin.yml / velocity-plugin.json / bungee.yml main class checks and navigation, fabric.mod.json and mixin class checks and navigation, neoforge.mods.toml completion, event handler gutter markers; pure, also built to WebAssembly).

## Purpose

The logic of the Minecraft Development plugin (`forge.minecraft`) and of the New Project
wizard's Minecraft Plugin and Minecraft Mod generators. Pure Rust: the app reads files and fetches metadata, this
crate decides. See [Minecraft plugins](docs/guide/user/minecraft.md).

- `versions` is the pinned table: Minecraft versions with their Java release, the rules for
  versions outside the table, each platform's repositories and API coordinates
  (`api_spec`), lower bounds (Purpur 1.18, Folia 1.20, `paper-plugin.yml` 1.20.6), the plugin
  versions of generated builds (run-paper, Shadow, Kotlin, Maven plugins) and the parsing of
  paper-api's `maven-metadata.xml` for "Refresh versions".
- `generate` validates the wizard's `Options` (`resolve` → `Project`: names, package, main
  class, descriptor, Java release) and writes the files: Gradle Kotlin / Groovy DSL or Maven
  builds, the descriptor, `.gitignore`, README and the shared "Run Paper Server"
  configuration. `sources` holds the Java and Kotlin templates of the main class, `/hello`
  command and join listener per API flavor (Paper, `paper-plugin.yml` with Brigadier,
  Spigot / Bukkit, Velocity, BungeeCord).
- `detect` recognizes a Minecraft plugin from build texts (API artifact, Minecraft version,
  run-paper).
- `descriptor` finds the `main` entry of a descriptor (UTF-16 offsets), checks it against the
  module's sources and resolves Go to Declaration.
- `markers` scans Java / Kotlin sources for `@EventHandler` / `@Subscribe` methods (with the
  event type) and `JavaPlugin` main classes.
- `mods` holds the mod side: `mods::versions` (the pinned table per Minecraft version: Java,
  Fabric API, Yarn, NeoForge, Parchment; Fabric Loader, Loom, ModDevGradle, Fabric Language
  Kotlin; the daemon JVM file; `resolve_versions`, `mod_version_choices`, and the parsers of
  Fabric's meta API, the Fabric API / NeoForge / plugin `maven-metadata.xml` and NeoForge's
  version scheme), `mods::generate` (`ModOptions` → `ModProject` → files: Gradle build,
  `gradle.properties`, `fabric.mod.json` or `neoforge.mods.toml`, sources from
  `mods::sources` with Mojang or Yarn names per version, assets, PNG textures from
  `mods::png`, run configurations), `mods::editor` (a tolerant JSON scanner, entrypoint and
  mixin references with checks and Go to Declaration), `mods::toml` (`neoforge.mods.toml`
  completion) and `detect_mod` (Loom, ModDevGradle, NeoGradle, ForgeGradle, Quilt Loom).
- `net` (feature `net`, desktop only) fetches the Minecraft versions from Paper's repository
  and, with `refresh_mods`, the mod versions (Fabric meta, Fabric API, Loom, NeoForge,
  ModDevGradle); it is only called when the user clicks Refresh.

# javaforge-android

`packs/javaforge/android` — JavaForge: Android basics (Gradle Android modules, AndroidManifest.xml, the Android SDK location, adb devices and emulator AVDs, Android App run command lines, Logcat parsing, filtering and stack trace links; pure, also built to WebAssembly).

## Purpose

The Android plugin's logic (`forge.android`). Pure Rust (no file system, processes or
devices): the app runs adb and the emulator and hands their output to this crate. See
[Android](docs/guide/user/android.md).

- `gradle` recognizes Android modules in build files (AGP plugin ids, version catalog aliases,
  `apply plugin:`; `namespace`, `applicationId`, SDK levels, Kotlin Android) and the AGP version
  (`gradle/libs.versions.toml`, plugin versions, buildscript class paths).
- `manifest` reads `AndroidManifest.xml` with a tolerant scanner (package, `uses-sdk`, label,
  activities and aliases, the `MAIN` / `LAUNCHER` activity), qualifies class names with the
  package or namespace and lists AGP's merged manifest paths.
- `sdk` finds the SDK (setting, `ANDROID_HOME`, `ANDROID_SDK_ROOT`, `local.properties`
  `sdk.dir` with Java properties escapes, the platform's default folder) and its tools; the
  hint shown without one (the SDK is never downloaded).
- `adb` parses `adb devices -l` (states such as `unauthorized` and `no permissions`, model,
  product, transport id, USB port), `emulator -list-avds`, `emu avd name` and `ps`.
- `run` builds the Android App run: `:<module>:assemble<Variant>`, the default APK path of a
  variant (flavors too), `adb install -r -t` and `am start -n` (or `monkey` without an
  activity), chained into one `sh -c` / `cmd /c` command line that echoes each step.
- `logcat` parses `threadtime` lines (also `,year`), tracks the packages of processes (`ps`,
  `Start proc`), marks stack traces and links frames to project sources, implements Android
  Studio's query language (`Query`) and keeps a ring buffer (`Logcat`) that returns filtered
  views.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `gradle.rs` | `android_module`, `AndroidModule`, `ModuleKind`, `plugin_kind`, `agp_version`. |
| `manifest.rs` | `parse`, `Manifest`, `Activity`, `qualify`, `merged_manifest_candidates`, `capitalize`. |
| `sdk.rs` | `locate`, `SdkEnv`, `SdkLocation`, `local_properties_sdk_dir`, `default_sdk_dir`, `adb_path`, `emulator_path`, `NO_SDK_HINT`. |
| `adb.rs` | `parse_devices`, `Device`, `parse_avds`, `parse_avd_name`, `parse_ps`. |
| `run.rs` | `AppRun`, `steps`, `chain`, `assemble_task`, `default_apk`. |
| `logcat.rs` | `parse_line`, `LogEntry`, `Level`, `FrameLink`, `frame`, `resolve`, `Query`, `Logcat`, `LogcatView`, `stream_args`, `ps_args`. |

## Main public items

```rust

```

## Used by

  `android_emulator_start`, the `android_logcat_*` stream and view, Android App command
  lines). [`forge-wasm`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-wasm.md): `android_adb`, `android_module`,
  `android_app_command`, `android_logcat_view` for the browser mode.

## Dependencies

- External: `serde`, `serde_json`, `regex-lite`

## Tests

# javaforge-lang-groovy

`packs/javaforge/lang-groovy` — JavaForge: Groovy basics (tolerant source scanner, scripts and main classes, Spock specification discovery and commands for the shared test runner, Groovy script command lines with groovy or through Gradle, Groovy SDK lookup; pure, also built to WebAssembly).

## Purpose

The Groovy plugin's logic (`forge.groovy`). Pure Rust (no file system or processes). See
[Groovy and Scala](docs/guide/user/groovy-scala.md).

- `source` tokenizes Groovy (comments, `'…'`, `"…"`, triple-quoted strings with their text,
  shebang lines) with brace depths and scans package, imports, classes / interfaces / traits /
  enums with binary names and supertypes, methods (also string-named Spock features, with the
  Spock block labels of their bodies, annotations and `static`) and whether the file has
  top-level statements (a script). Half-typed code and slashy strings are tolerated.
- `spock` finds specifications (`extends Specification`, `spock.lang.*`, or a base spec in a file
  importing Spock) and their features (string names or methods with blocks; fixtures excluded;
  `@Ignore` / `@PendingFeature`, data-driven `where:`).
- `tests` is the shared test runner's provider `SpockTests` (type `spock`): gutter targets,
  Rerun Failed Tests (`Class#feature`) and commands through JavaForge's
  `javaforge_lang_java::tests::build_command` with `language = groovy` (Gradle `--tests`,
  Surefire `-Dtest=`, `src/test/groovy` location rules, JaCoCo).
- `launch` lists what runs in a file (`runnable`: script, `main` methods), builds Groovy Script
  command lines (`groovy` with `JAVA_OPTS`, or Gradle with the `GRADLE_INIT_SCRIPT` task
  `forgeRunGroovy` running `groovy.ui.GroovyMain` on the main source set), finds Groovy SDK
  candidates (GROOVY_HOME, SDKMAN!) and parses `groovy --version`.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `source.rs` | `parse(text) -> GroovyFile { package, imports, types, script }`, `TypeDecl`, `Method`, `SPOCK_LABELS`. |
| `spock.rs` | `specs`, `specs_of`, `Spec`, `Feature`. |
| `tests.rs` | `SpockTests` (`TestFrameworkProvider`), `SPOCK`. |
| `launch.rs` | `runnable`, `Runnable`, `MainMethod`, `Runner`, `ScriptRun`, `script_command`, `GRADLE_INIT_SCRIPT`, `gradle_applies_groovy`, `groovy_candidates`, `launcher_in`, `parse_version`. |

## Main public items

```rust
pub use launch::{runnable, Runnable};
pub use spock::{specs, Spec};
pub use tests::SpockTests;
```

## Used by

- The app: `RunState` registers `SpockTests` (`commands/run.rs`); `commands/groovy.rs`
  (`groovy_status`, `groovy_runnable`, Groovy Script command lines) and `commands/java.rs`
  (Spock runs are prepared like JUnit). [`forge-wasm`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-wasm.md): `groovy_runnable`,
  `groovy_script_command` and the test registry of the browser mode.

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: [`forge-output`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-output.md), [`forge-runtools`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-runtools.md), [`forge-testing`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-testing.md), [`javaforge-lang-java`](docs/guide/developer/crates/javaforge-lang-java.md)

# javaforge-lang-scala

`packs/javaforge/lang-scala` — JavaForge: Scala basics (tolerant source scanner, main objects, sbt builds read from build.sbt and from sbt's output, sbt command lines, ScalaTest and MUnit discovery and commands for the shared test runner, the Metals launch and its Coursier install; pure, also built to WebAssembly).

## Purpose

The Scala plugin's logic (`forge.scala`). Pure Rust (no file system or processes); code
intelligence comes from Metals through `forge-lsp`. See [Groovy and Scala](docs/guide/user/groovy-scala.md).

- `source` tokenizes Scala (nested comments, strings, triple-quoted strings, character
  literals, backtick identifiers) and scans packages (also chained clauses), imports, objects /
  classes / traits / enums with fully qualified names and parents, `def main(args:
  Array[String])`, `extends App` and Scala 3 `@main` methods (`main_objects`), for braces and
  Scala 3's indentation syntax.
- `suites` finds ScalaTest suites (FunSuite, FlatSpec with `it should`, WordSpec clauses,
  FunSpec `describe` / `it`, FreeSpec `-`, PropSpec, async styles) and MUnit suites
  (`munit.FunSuite`, `CatsEffectSuite`, `ScalaCheckSuite`) with the full test names the
  frameworks report (`A Cart when empty should have no items`).
- `tests` is the shared test runner's providers `ScalaTests::scalatest()` / `munit()` (types
  `scalatest`, `munit`): gutter targets, Rerun Failed Tests (suites) and `sbt testOnly`
  commands (`-z` for ScalaTest test names, a glob for MUnit) reading the JUnit XML of
  `target/test-reports`.
- `sbt` reads builds statically (`static_build`: projects, folders, `dependsOn`, `aggregate`,
  names, Scala versions, `libraryDependencies` with `%%` / configurations, string `val`s and
  setting sequences, `project/build.properties`, `project/plugins.sbt`), parses an import's
  output (`parse_sync` of `projects` and `show scalaVersion baseDirectory
  libraryDependencies`), merges both and builds command lines (`task_command`, `scoped_task`:
  `core/test`, `~core/compile`, `-J` VM options).
- `metals` holds the pinned Metals version, the Coursier `bootstrap` arguments, the
  initialization options and workspace settings.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `source.rs` | `parse(text) -> ScalaFile`, `Template`, `main_objects`, `MainObject`. |
| `suites.rs` | `suites`, `suites_of`, `Suite`, `SuiteTest`, `Framework`. |
| `tests.rs` | `ScalaTests` (`TestFrameworkProvider`), `SCALATEST`, `MUNIT`, `project_dir_of`. |
| `sbt.rs` | `SbtBuild`, `SbtProject`, `SbtDependency`, `TASKS`, `static_build`, `parse_build_properties`, `parse_sync`, `merge`, `SYNC_COMMANDS`, `sync_args`, `task_command`, `scoped_task`, `split_tasks`. |
| `metals.rs` | `METALS_VERSION`, `SERVER_ID`, `coordinates`, `bootstrap_args`, `initialization_options`, `settings`, `version_of_install`. |

## Main public items

```rust
pub use sbt::{SbtBuild, SbtProject};
pub use source::{main_objects, MainObject};
pub use tests::ScalaTests;
```

## Used by

- The app: `RunState` registers both `ScalaTests` (`commands/run.rs`); `commands/scala.rs`
  (Metals registration and install, the sbt model and import, sbt Task command lines, test
  preparation). [`forge-wasm`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-wasm.md): `scala_main_objects`, `scala_sbt_build`,
  `scala_command_line` and the test registry of the browser mode.

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: [`forge-output`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-output.md), [`forge-runtools`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-runtools.md), [`forge-testing`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-testing.md)
- External: `serde`, `serde_json`, `regex-lite`

## Tests

6 source files, about 2100 lines; 11 unit tests on fixtures (`tests/fixtures`: a multi-project
`build.sbt`, `build.properties`, recorded sbt output, ScalaTest and MUnit suites; no network,
no sbt).

# javaforge-lang-java

`packs/javaforge/lang-java` — JavaForge: Java language support (structural source scanner, main methods, JUnit 5/4/3 and TestNG discovery and commands for the shared test runner, application command lines, Eclipse JDT LS launch configuration; pure, also built to WebAssembly).

## Purpose

JavaForge's Java language support. Pure Rust (no file system or processes); code intelligence
itself comes from Eclipse JDT LS through `forge-lsp`.

- `source` scans a Java file: package, imports, types (classes, interfaces, enums, records,
  annotation types, nested types with binary names such as `com.acme.Outer$Inner`) and their
  methods with annotations, modifiers, return types and parameters. It skips comments, strings,
  text blocks and method bodies and tolerates half-typed code.
- `discovery` finds `main` methods for the Run gutter (`public static void main(String[])`,
  Java 25 instance mains and compact source files) and tests: JUnit 5 (`@Test`,
  `@ParameterizedTest`, `@RepeatedTest`, `@TestFactory`, `@TestTemplate`, `@Nested`), JUnit 4,
  JUnit 3 `TestCase` subclasses and TestNG (method and class level `@Test`), chosen by imports.
- `tests` is the shared test runner's provider (`JavaTests::junit()`, `JavaTests::testng()`):
  gutter targets with temporary configurations, Rerun Failed Tests (`Class#method` lists) and
  commands through `javaforge-build` with `TestReport::JUnitFile`, `JUnitFlavor::Java`, the
  build's report folders (`TestCommand::report_dirs`), location rules from the source root and
  JaCoCo coverage with its own rules (main sources). With the option `runner = junit` ("Run
  tests using: IntelliJ IDEA") JUnit runs on the JUnit Platform Console Launcher instead, on
  the class path the backend resolved (`resolvedClasspath`, `launcherJar`, `reportsDir`).
  `build_command` also serves KotlinForge (`language = kotlin`) and Spock
  (`language = groovy`: `src/<set>/groovy/` roots, `JUnitFlavor::Kotlin` names with spaces,
  locations renamed to `.groovy`).
- `launch` builds Application command lines (`java` with VM options, `-p` / `-cp`, `-m`, the
  JDWP agent of debug runs), the debug arguments of Gradle (`--debug-jvm`) and Surefire, and
  `junit_console_command` (`java -jar junit-platform-console-standalone.jar execute
  --select-… --reports-dir …`).
- `jdtls` describes how JDT LS starts: the command line (read-only installation, OSGi
  configuration and `-data` in the cache dir), `initializationOptions` (java-debug bundle,
  extended client capabilities) and the `java.*` settings (JDKs as runtimes, Gradle / Maven
  import, hot code replace), plus the JDT LS and java-debug commands Forge sends.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `discovery.rs` | `main_methods`, `discover_tests`, `Framework`, `TestDiscovery`, `source_root`. |
| `jdtls.rs` | `JdtlsSetup` (`args`, `settings`, `initialization_options`), `Runtime`, `execution_environment`, `config_folder`, `commands`. |
| `launch.rs` | `AppLaunch`, `application_command`, `jdwp_listen`, `remote_jvm_arguments`, `build_output_classpath`, `build_tool_debug_args`, `JUnitSelector`, `junit_console_command`, `DEBUG_PORT_ENV`. |
| `source.rs` | The tolerant scanner: `parse(text) -> JavaFile { package, imports, types, top_level_methods }`. |
| `tests.rs` | `JavaTests` (`TestFrameworkProvider`) and `module_of_source_root`. |

## Main public items

```rust
pub use discovery::{discover_tests, main_methods, Framework, MainMethod, TestDiscovery};
pub use tests::JavaTests;
```

## Used by

- The app: `RunState` registers `JavaTests` (`commands/run.rs`); `commands/java.rs` builds
  JDT LS, Application and debug runs with it. [`forge-wasm`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-wasm.md): `java_main_methods`,
  `java_command_line` and the test registry of the browser mode.

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: [`forge-output`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-output.md), [`forge-runtools`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-runtools.md), [`forge-testing`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-testing.md), [`javaforge-build`](docs/guide/developer/crates/javaforge-build.md)
- External: `serde`, `serde_json`

# kotlinforge-lang-kotlin

`packs/kotlinforge/lang-kotlin` — KotlinForge: Kotlin language support (structural source scanner, main functions, JUnit 5 and Kotest discovery and commands for the shared test runner, Kotlin/JVM and script command lines, kotlin-lsp launch, ktlint and detekt reports, coroutine dumps; pure, also built to WebAssembly).

## Purpose

KotlinForge's Kotlin language support. Pure Rust (no file system or processes); code
intelligence itself comes from kotlin-lsp (or kotlin-language-server) through `forge-lsp`. See
[KotlinForge](docs/guide/user/kotlin.md).

- `source` tokenizes Kotlin (nested block comments, string templates, raw strings, backtick
  names) and scans package, imports, `@file:` annotations, classes, interfaces, objects,
  companion objects and enums (with JVM binary names such as `com.acme.Cart$Companion`),
  functions with annotations, modifiers, parameters and receivers, `init` blocks and the
  argument ranges of supertype constructors. It tolerates half-typed code.
- `discovery` finds `main` functions (top-level → the file facade `MainKt` or `@file:JvmName`;
  `@JvmStatic` mains in objects and companions) and JUnit 5 / `kotlin.test`, JUnit 4 and TestNG
  tests with backtick names and `@Nested inner class`es.
- `kotest` reads Kotest specs (FunSpec, StringSpec, DescribeSpec, BehaviorSpec) from the
  constructor lambda and `init` blocks into tests and containers with their paths
  (`totals -- applies the discount`).
- `tests` is the shared test runner's provider `KotlinTests` (type `kotest`): gutter targets,
  Rerun Failed Tests (the failed specs) and commands through JavaForge's
  `javaforge_lang_java::tests::build_command` with Kotest's filter variables and
  `JUnitFlavor::Kotlin`; JUnit tests in `.kt` files become `junit` / `testng` configurations
  with `language = kotlin`.
- `launch` builds Kotlin/JVM runs (Gradle with an init script adding `forgeRunKotlin`, Maven
  `exec:java`, `kotlinc` then `java -cp`) and Kotlin scripts (`kotlin` / `kotlinc -script`;
  Gradle build scripts are refused).
- `lsp` describes how kotlin-lsp (`bin/intellij-server --stdio`) and kotlin-language-server
  start: arguments, `JAVA_HOME`, JVM options, initialization options.
- `lint` parses ktlint's JSON and Checkstyle reports and detekt's SARIF and Checkstyle reports
  into `LintProblem`s, and builds their command lines (ktlint on stdin, detekt with the project's
  configuration and baseline).
- `coroutines` holds the debugger expressions of the Coroutines view and parses what they return
  (the `DebugProbes` text dump or the coroutine info list) into `CoroutineDump`.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `source.rs` | `tokenize`, `parse(text) -> KotlinFile { package, imports, file_annotations, classes, functions }`, `facade_name`, `skip_balanced`. |
| `discovery.rs` | `main_functions`, `MainFunction`, `discover_tests`, `KotlinTestDiscovery`. |
| `kotest.rs` | `discover_specs`, `KotestSpec`, `KotestTest`, `SpecStyle`. |
| `tests.rs` | `KotlinTests` (`TestFrameworkProvider`), `KOTEST`, `FILTER_SPECS_ENV`, `FILTER_TESTS_ENV`. |
| `launch.rs` | `KotlinApp`, `Runner`, `application_command`, `ScriptRun`, `script_command`, `is_runnable_script`, `GRADLE_INIT_SCRIPT`. |
| `lsp.rs` | `Server`, `KotlinServerSetup`, `launcher_path`. |
| `lint.rs` | `LintProblem`, `parse_ktlint_json`, `parse_sarif`, `parse_checkstyle`, `ktlint_args`, `detekt_args`, `detekt_config_files`, `gradle_plugin`. |
| `coroutines.rs` | `DUMP_EXPRESSION`, `INFO_EXPRESSION`, `parse_dump`, `CoroutineDump`, `Coroutine`. |

## Main public items

```rust

```

## Used by

- The app: `RunState` registers `KotlinTests` (`commands/run.rs`); `commands/kotlin.rs` builds
  the language server config, Kotlin runs, ktlint / detekt runs and the debugger plan with it.
  [`forge-wasm`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-wasm.md): `kotlin_main_functions`, `kotlin_command_line`,
  `kotlin_lint_report`, `kotlin_coroutines` and the test registry of the browser mode.

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: [`forge-output`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-output.md), [`forge-runtools`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-runtools.md), [`forge-testing`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-testing.md), [`javaforge-build`](docs/guide/developer/crates/javaforge-build.md), [`javaforge-lang-java`](docs/guide/developer/crates/javaforge-lang-java.md)

# luaforge-lang-lua

`packs/luaforge/lang-lua` — LuaForge: Lua language support (lexer, structural parser, EmmyLua/LuaLS annotations, project index, require resolution, hover, navigation; pure, also built to WebAssembly).

## Purpose

LuaForge language pack: Lua 5.1–5.4 and LuaJIT support. Pure Rust (no file system or
processes), so the same code backs the desktop app and the browser mode (WebAssembly).

- `lexer` and `parser` index a file into a `model::FileIndex`: locals with their
  scopes, globals, table fields, functions and methods (`M.f`, `M:f`), references,
  `require` calls and the module's `return`.
- `annotations` parses EmmyLua / LuaLS doc comments (`---@class`, `---@field`,
  `---@param`, `---@return`, `---@type`, `---@alias`, …).
- `require` resolves module names through `package.path`-like templates.
- `project::ProjectIndex` holds a workspace's files and resolves values across them
  (Go to Declaration, Search Everywhere).
- `hover` renders documentation as the `forge-markdown` AST, `structure` builds the
  Structure tool window and `run` finds main chunks for gutter run icons.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `annotations.rs` | EmmyLua / LuaLS annotations (`---@class`, `---@field`, `---@param`, `---@return`, `---@type`, `---@alias`, `---@deprecated`, `---@see`) and the Markdown description of a doc comment block. |
| `hover.rs` | Hover documentation from the index and EmmyLua/LuaLS annotations, as the Markdown AST of `forge-markdown` (the same `HoverDoc` the UI renders for language server hovers). |
| `lexer.rs` | Lua 5.1–5.4 / LuaJIT lexer. Error tolerant: unterminated strings and comments end at the end of the line or file, unknown characters become one-character operators. |
| `model.rs` | What the parser extracts from one Lua file. |
| `offsets.rs` | Offset conversion. The parser works in UTF-8 byte offsets; the UI (CodeMirror / JS strings) uses UTF-16 code units. Convert at the IPC boundary. |
| `parser.rs` | Structural Lua parser: a tolerant recursive-descent pass over the tokens that records declarations (locals, parameters, globals, fields, functions and methods) with their scopes, name and field references, `require` calls, the module's `return` value and the doc comments attached to each statement. |
| `project.rs` | The project index: every Lua file of a workspace, with lightweight type resolution across files (locals, globals, table fields, `require`d modules, `---@class` / `---@type` / `---@param` / `---@return` annotations), Go to Declaration and symbol search for Search Everywhere. |
| `require.rs` | `require("a.b")` resolution through `package.path`-like templates relative to the project root (`?.lua`, `?/init.lua`, `lua/?.lua`, …), extended by the `lua.requirePaths` setting and the `runtime.path` of a `.luarc.json`. |
| `run.rs` | Gutter run icons (▶) for main chunks: scripts that do not return a module table, and the `main.lua` of a LÖVE game. |
| `structure.rs` | The Structure tool window (Alt+7) of a Lua file: classes with their fields and methods, module tables with their functions, top-level functions and variables. |

## Main public items

```rust
pub use project::{IndexStats, Location, ProjectIndex, SearchKind, SymbolHit, SymbolKind};
```

## Used by

- IPC: `lua_index_workspace`, `lua_files_changed`, `lua_search_symbols`, `lua_file_structure`, `lua_hover`, `lua_goto`, `lua_run_markers`, `lua_format` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/lua.rs`)
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/lua`
- Browser mode: built into `forge-wasm`

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: [`forge-fuzzy`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-fuzzy.md), [`forge-markdown`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-markdown.md)
- External: `serde`, `serde_json`

## Tests

11 source files, about 4516 lines; 34 unit tests.

```sh
cargo test -p luaforge-lang-lua
```

# pyforge-lang-python

`packs/pyforge/lang-python` — PyForge: Python language support that does not need a language
server. Pure Rust (no file system or processes), so the same code backs the desktop app and the
browser mode (WebAssembly, `crates/forge-wasm/src/python.rs`).

## Purpose

- `pep440` parses and normalizes versions (`1.0RC1` = `1.0rc1`, `1.0-1` = `1.0.post1`), orders
  them like pip and matches specifier sets (`~=`, `==1.4.*`, `!=`, `<`, `>` with the pre- and
  post-release exclusions, `===`).
- `pep508` parses dependency specifications (name, extras, specifiers, `@ url`, markers) with
  byte ranges, and normalizes names (PEP 503).
- `deps` reads the dependencies of `requirements*.txt` (options, `-r` includes, line
  continuations, comments, `--hash`) and `pyproject.toml` (PEP 621, PEP 735 groups, Poetry
  tables with `^` / `~` converted to PEP 440) with the position of each name, and edits the
  files for "Add requirement".
- `imports` finds the import statements of a file (strings and comments skipped, `try:`
  blocks marked) and knows the standard library and module → distribution names.
- `inspections` reports unsatisfied requirements and undeclared imports with quick fixes.
- `completion` finds the name / version context in dependency files; `run` builds the
  arguments of the Python run configuration and finds `__main__` guards.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `completion.rs` | Completion contexts in dependency files: a package name or a version after an operator, in `requirements.txt` lines and in the dependency strings of pyproject.toml; final releases sorted before pre-releases. |
| `deps.rs` | Declared dependencies of `requirements*.txt` and `pyproject.toml` with their positions (0-based lines, UTF-16 columns), Poetry constraint conversion and the "Add requirement" edits. |
| `imports.rs` | Import statements, `STDLIB` (Python 3.8–3.13) and `KNOWN_DISTRIBUTIONS` (`yaml` → `PyYAML`, `PIL` → `Pillow`, …). |
| `inspections.rs` | `check_dep_file` ("Package requirement 'X' is not satisfied") and `check_imports` ("Package containing module 'x' is not listed in the project requirements") with `Fix`es. |
| `pep440.rs` | `Version`, `Specifier`, `SpecifierSet` (`contains`, `best`). |
| `pep508.rs` | `Requirement`, `parse`, `normalize`, `is_name`. |
| `run.rs` | `arguments` of a script / module run, `run_markers`, `module_of`. |

## Used by

- IPC: `python_inspect`, `python_add_requirement`, `python_complete`, `python_run_markers`, `python_dependencies`, the Python run configuration (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/python.rs`)
- [`pyforge-interpreters`](docs/guide/developer/crates/pyforge-interpreters.md), [`pyforge-packages`](docs/guide/developer/crates/pyforge-packages.md)
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/python`
- Browser mode: built into `forge-wasm`

## Dependencies

- External: `serde`, `serde_json`, `toml`

## Tests

8 source files, about 2970 lines; 24 unit tests.

```sh
cargo test -p pyforge-lang-python
```

# pyforge-interpreters

`packs/pyforge/interpreters` — PyForge: Python interpreters (Settings | Project | Python
Interpreter, the status bar widget and its popup).

## Purpose

- `model` describes an interpreter (`EnvKind`: system, pyenv, venv, virtualenv, uv, Poetry,
  conda, Pipenv, Hatch, Docker, Docker Compose, SSH, WSL) and how it is stored in the
  `objects` settings `python.interpreters` / `python.projectInterpreters`;
  `python.interpreter` selects one by name or is a local path. `PythonInterpreter::label` is
  the status bar text (`Python 3.12 (shop-api)`). Remote kinds run through the PHP
  interpreters' command lines and path mappings: `wrap_target` turns the interpreter into a
  `phpforge_interpreters::PhpInterpreter` whose program is `python`.
- `probe` parses `python --version`, the probe script's JSON, `pyvenv.cfg`, `conda-meta` file
  names, `py -0p`, `conda env list --json` and the one-path answers of `poetry env info -p`,
  `pipenv --venv` and friends.
- `detect` (not in WebAssembly) finds the project's environments and the machine's Pythons
  (see the [user guide](docs/guide/user/python.md#python-interpreter)); versions come from metadata,
  only system Pythons are run. `SearchEnv` and the `version_of` / `run_tool` callbacks make it
  testable with fixture folders and fake executables.
- `create` plans the commands of a new environment (venv, uv, Poetry, conda) and the
  dependency install.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `create.rs` | `NewEnvironment`, `ProjectFiles`, `plan` → `Step`s, `python_in`. |
| `detect.rs` | `SearchEnv::system`, `detect`, `version_of`, `run_with_timeout`. |
| `model.rs` | `EnvKind`, `PythonInterpreter`, `InterpreterSet` (`resolve`: names, ids and local paths). |
| `probe.rs` | Parsers and `PROBE_SCRIPT`. |

## Used by

- IPC: `python_interpreter_current`, `python_interpreters_detect`, `python_interpreter_info`, `python_environment_plan` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/python.rs`)
- [`pyforge-packages`](docs/guide/developer/crates/pyforge-packages.md)
- Browser mode: `python_interpreter_label`, `python_environment_plan` in `forge-wasm`

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: `phpforge-interpreters` (`packs/phpforge/interpreters`), [`pyforge-lang-python`](docs/guide/developer/crates/pyforge-lang-python.md)
- External: `serde`, `serde_json`, `dirs`

# pyforge-packages

`packs/pyforge/packages` — PyForge: the Python Packages tool window, "Install requirement"
quick fixes and completion in dependency files.

## Purpose

- `listing` holds the `importlib.metadata` script that lists an environment's distributions
  with their top-level modules (it works without pip), and parses its JSON (and `pip list
  --format=json`).
- `manager` chooses pip, uv, Poetry or Pipenv for an environment and builds the install,
  uninstall and upgrade command lines.
- `pypi` parses PyPI's JSON API (latest version, summary, licence, required Python, home page,
  releases without yanked ones) and its search page.
- `net` (feature `net`, desktop only) is the PyPI client: requests through the system proxy,
  answers cached in `<cache dir>/forge/pypi` (12 hours for packages, 1 hour for searches) with
  the stale copy used when PyPI cannot be reached.

## Modules

| --- | --- |
| `listing.rs` | `LIST_SCRIPT`, `parse`, `parse_pip_list`. |
| `manager.rs` | `Manager`, `Action`, `choose`, `command`. |
| `net.rs` | `Pypi` (`package`, `search`, `cached`). |
| `pypi.rs` | `PackageInfo`, `SearchHit`, `parse_json`, `parse_search`, URLs. |
| `testserver.rs` | A tiny HTTP server on localhost for the tests (no network). |

## Used by

- IPC: `python_packages_list`, `python_packages_command`, `python_packages_latest`, `python_packages_search`, `python_package_info`, `python_complete` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/python.rs`)
- Browser mode: `python_packages_command` in `forge-wasm`

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: [`pyforge-lang-python`](docs/guide/developer/crates/pyforge-lang-python.md), [`pyforge-interpreters`](docs/guide/developer/crates/pyforge-interpreters.md)
- External: `serde`, `serde_json`; with `net`: `reqwest` (rustls), `tokio`, `dirs`

# rustforge-lang-rust

`packs/rustforge/lang-rust` — RustForge's Rust and Cargo support. Pure Rust (no I/O), shared
by the desktop backend and the WebAssembly build of browser mode.

## Purpose

- `metadata`: a `CargoWorkspace` from `cargo metadata --format-version 1`: members, targets
  (lib, bin, test, bench, example, build script, proc macro), features with their defaults,
  direct dependencies and a dependency tree per member from the `resolve` graph (packages
  seen before are `repeated`, like `cargo tree`'s `(*)`); `module_path` / `crate_of` give the
  crate and module of a source file.
- `toolchain`: `rustup toolchain list -v`, `rustup show active-toolchain` (default,
  `rust-toolchain.toml`, directory override, `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN`), `rust-toolchain(.toml)`,
  `rustc -vV` and `rustup component list --installed`.
- `scan`: a small Rust lexer (strings, raw strings, chars, lifetimes, nested comments) and
  brace tracking: `fn main`, `#[test]` / `#[<runtime>::test]`, `#[bench]`, test modules and
  doctests named like rustdoc (`cart::Cart::total`, the line of the fence).
- `context`: `CargoContext` (cargo, toolchain, nightly, test runner and format, installed
  plugins, environment, features, workspace members and files), handed to the provider
  through `CommandContext.settings["rust.context"]`; `location_rules` map libtest's
  `<crate>::<module>` locations to files, deepest modules first.
- `command`: the "Cargo" run configuration (any cargo command with package, target,
  features, profile, target triple and toolchain, the user's own options winning), Cargo
  tool window actions and `fn main` run targets.
- `provider`: `CargoTestProvider` for the manifest's `cargo-test` framework: discovery keyed
  `<file>::<libtest name>`, `cargo test` (libtest JSON on nightly, plain output otherwise),
  `cargo bench`, `cargo test --doc`, `cargo nextest run --message-format libtest-json`,
  `cargo llvm-cov --lcov` for coverage, Rerun Failed Tests by exact names; `debug_test`
  builds a test binary for the debugger (`cargo test --no-run --message-format json`).
- `messages`: cargo's JSON messages — executables (`compiler-artifact`), rustc and Clippy
  diagnostics as `RustProblem`s with their suggestions as fixes, build failures.
- `analyzer`: rust-analyzer's configuration (check on save with Clippy, features, target,
  build scripts, proc macros; off in untrusted projects).
- `format`: rustfmt arguments (edition, `--config-path`) and the config files `cargo fmt`
  would find.
- `debug`: rustc's pretty printers for LLDB (`initCommands`) and GDB (adapter arguments).

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `metadata.rs` | `parse_metadata`, `CargoWorkspace`, `CargoPackage`, `CargoTarget`, `DependencyNode`, `module_path`, `crate_of`. |

| `analyzer.rs` | `AnalyzerSettings`. |
| `format.rs` | `config_candidates`, `rustfmt_args`. |
| `debug.rs` | `PrettyPrinters`. |

# rustforge-toolchain

`packs/rustforge/toolchain` — RustForge on the user's machine.

## Purpose

- `detect`: `RustStatus` of a project folder — rustup's toolchains, the active one and why,
  a standalone `rustc` without rustup, `rustc -vV`, the sysroot, the standard library sources
  (`rust-src`), installed components, the tools Forge uses (rust-analyzer through
  `rustup which`, Forge's download or the `PATH`; rustfmt; Clippy) and cargo plugins
  (cargo-nextest, cargo-llvm-cov), and rustc's pretty-printer files. Programs run through a
  `Runner` with `RUSTUP_AUTO_INSTALL=0`, so detection never installs anything.
- `install`: command lines for `rustup toolchain install`, `rustup component add` and
  `cargo install --locked` of cargo plugins (names validated; the UI asks first).
- `analyzer`: the rust-analyzer download — the pinned release (`PINNED_RELEASE`), the asset
  of the platform (`rust-analyzer-<target>.gz`, `.zip` on Windows), its SHA-256 digest from
  the GitHub release API, unpacked into `<data dir>/forge/langservers/rust-analyzer`.
- `gdb`: `RustGdbAdapter`, the `rust-gdb` debug adapter: the Debugger plugin's GDB
  (`gdb -i dap`) with rustc's pretty printers loaded before the program.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |

| `install.rs` | `toolchain`, `component`, `cargo_plugin`. |
| `analyzer.rs` | `install`, `installed`, `asset_name`, `default_dir`, `PINNED_RELEASE`. |
| `gdb.rs` | `RustGdbAdapter`, `ADAPTER`. |

## Used by

- IPC: `app/src-tauri/src/commands/rust.rs` (`rust_status`, `rust_install_command`,
  `rust_analyzer_download`, `rust_debug_request`, `sync_debug`).

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: [`rustforge-lang-rust`](docs/guide/developer/crates/rustforge-lang-rust.md),
  [`forge-langservers`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-langservers.md), [`forge-dap`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-dap.md),
  [`forge-plugin-api`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-plugin-api.md)
- External: `serde`, `serde_json`, `dirs`, `tokio`, `flate2`

## Tests

Detection runs against recorded rustup and rustc output in temporary folders; the download
is tested with a local HTTP server (`forge_langservers::managed::testserver`); the GDB
adapter against the Debugger plugin's GDB contribution. An ignored smoke test detects this
machine's toolchains.

```sh
cargo test -p rustforge-toolchain
```
