# rubyforge-lang-ruby

`packs/rubyforge/lang-ruby` — RubyForge's Ruby language support, in the style of RubyMine.
Pure Rust (no I/O), shared by the desktop backend and the WebAssembly build of browser mode.

## Purpose

- `version`: the Ruby a project asks for — `.ruby-version`, `.tool-versions`,
  `mise.toml` / `.mise.toml`, the Gemfile's `ruby "3.3.6"` or `ruby file: ".ruby-version"`, in
  that order — version parts, engines (`jruby-9.4`) and matching (`3.3` matches `3.3.6`).
- `gemfile`: a tolerant Gemfile scanner (sources, `ruby`, `gemspec`, `gem` with requirements,
  groups from blocks and options, platforms, `require: false`, `path:` / `git:` / `github:`)
  and the Gemfile.lock sections (`GEM`, `GIT`, `PATH` specs with dependencies, `PLATFORMS`,
  `DEPENDENCIES`, `RUBY VERSION`, `BUNDLED WITH`); `bundle` merges both into `Bundle` (direct
  and transitive gems with groups, missing gems).
- `rake`: `rake --tasks --all` output (tasks, arguments, descriptions), `rake --where`
  locations, and `scan_rakefile` for `desc` / `task` / `namespace` and the tasks of
  Bundler's gem tasks, `RSpec::Core::RakeTask`, `Rake::TestTask`, `Minitest::TestTask` and
  `RuboCop::RakeTask` without running Rake.
- `discovery`: RSpec groups and examples with their full descriptions, Minitest test classes,
  `def test_*` methods, ActiveSupport `test "…"` blocks and Minitest::Spec blocks
  (`test_0001_<description>`), nested by indentation.
- `provider`: `RubyTests`, the `forge-testing` provider of the `rspec` and `minitest`
  manifest frameworks — gutter targets keyed like the test tree's results, `rspec
  file:line … --format json --out <report dir>/rspec.json` and `ruby -Ilib -Itest <file> -v
  -n <filter>` (or a loader for folders) through `bundle exec`, Rerun Failed Tests.
- `command`: Ruby script and Rake configurations, `rake --tasks`, Bundler actions, `gem
  install`, the IRB console and `rdbg --open --host 127.0.0.1 --port ${port} --command -- …`.
- `rubocop`: `rubocop --format json --stdin <path>` arguments, the JSON report as
  `RubyProblem`s (0-based positions, RuboCop's levels as Forge's), autocorrect arguments
  (`-a` / `-A` with `--stderr`) and the corrected source.
- `context`: `RubyContext` (interpreter, `bundle`, `use_bundler`, gem executables,
  environment, the bundle's gems), handed to the provider as `CommandContext.settings["ruby.context"]`.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `version.rs` | `requested_version`, `parse_ruby_version`, `parse_tool_versions`, `parse_mise_toml`, `parse_gemfile_ruby`, `matches`, `compare`, `engine`. |
| `gemfile.rs` | `parse_gemfile`, `parse_lockfile`, `bundle`, `Gemfile`, `Lockfile`, `Bundle`, `BundleGem`. |
| `rake.rs` | `parse_tasks`, `merge_locations`, `scan_rakefile`, `RakeTask`. |
| `discovery.rs` | `discover_rspec`, `discover_minitest`, `is_spec_file`, `is_test_file`, `RubyTest`. |
| `provider.rs` | `RubyTests`, `register`, `rspec_command`, `minitest_command`, `RSPEC`, `MINITEST`. |
| `command.rs` | `script_command`, `rake_command`, `rake_tasks_command`, `bundler_action`, `gem_install`, `irb_command`, `rdbg_command`, `RUBY`, `RAKE`. |
| `rubocop.rs` | `check_args`, `autocorrect_args`, `parse_report`, `corrected_source`, `RubyProblem`. |
| `context.rs` | `RubyContext`, `RubyCommand`, `CONTEXT_KEY`. |

## Used by

  `ruby_command_line`, `ruby_action_command`, `ruby_script_entry`, `ruby_rubocop_report`,
  `ruby_requested_version`) and the test registry of `testing.rs`.
- [`rubyforge-sdk`](docs/guide/developer/crates/rubyforge-sdk.md).

## Dependencies

  [`forge-testing`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-testing.md)
- External: `serde`, `serde_json`

# rubyforge-fw-rails

`packs/rubyforge/fw-rails` — the analysis behind the [Ruby on Rails](docs/guide/user/rails.md)
plugin, in the style of RubyMine. Pure Rust (files in, data out): the desktop backend hands it
the project's files read in one round trip (`commands::rails::project`), browser mode the demo
files through WebAssembly. Nothing of the application runs; `bin/rails routes` and `bin/rails
generate` output (trusted projects only) is passed in as text.

## Purpose

- `source`: a forgiving Ruby scanner — UTF-16 line/column positions, comments, logical lines
  (calls continued with `,`, `\` or open brackets, `=begin`, heredocs), tokens (symbols,
  strings, `%w[]` / `%i[]`, hash keys, `=>`, constants) and call arguments (`Args`:
  positional values, options, `do` blocks, `redirect(…)`).
- `inflect`: ActiveSupport's plural and singular rules with irregular and uncountable words,
  `camelize`, `underscore`, `tableize`, `classify`.
- `routes`: `config/routes.rb` as `bin/rails routes` prints it — `resources` / `resource`
  (options, nesting, `member` / `collection`, `on:`), `namespace`, `scope`, `controller`,
  verbs and `match … via:`, `root`, `mount`, `concern` / `concerns`, `draw`; Rails' names
  (a path's name on its first route, `_index` for uncountable resources) and sample paths;
  `parse_rails_routes` reads the command's table.
- `app`: controllers and mailers with their public actions, views and partials,
  `render` / `layout` references and their files, models (table, `self.table_name`, STI,
  `table_name_prefix`, associations, scopes) linked to their columns.
- `schema`: tables from `db/schema.rb`, then the migrations newer than its version
  (`create_table`, `t.<type>`, `t.references`, `t.timestamps`, `add_column`,
  `remove_column`, `rename_column`, `add_reference`, `change_table`, `rename_table`,
  `drop_table`), with the migrations of each table.
- `yaml`: the YAML of locale files and database.yml (block maps and sequences, scalars, block
  scalars, flow lists, anchors, aliases, `<<:` merges) with key positions.
- `database`: database.yml environments and multi-database entries, ERB-lite for `ENV[…]` /
  `ENV.fetch`, `url:` parsing and Forge's driver per adapter.
- `i18n`: the catalogue of `config/locales/**/*.yml` (plural forms, missing locales), the
  default locale and `t(…)` / `I18n.t(…)` / `translate(…)` calls with lazy lookup.
- `hotwire`: Stimulus controllers (identifier from the path, targets, values, classes,
  outlets, methods), `data-*` attributes of HTML and `data: { … }` hashes, Turbo frame ids.
- `generators`, `command`: built-in and project generators, `bin/rails generate` output,
  and the command lines of `server`, `console`, `dbconsole`, `generate` / `destroy` and
  `routes` from a `RubyContext` (`ruby bin/rails …`, else `bundle exec rails …`).
- `editor`: `goto`, `complete` and `marks` (gutter marks, problems, translation folds) on an
  editor's text, with UTF-16 offsets.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `lib.rs` | `Project`, `Options`, `RailsInfo`, `Location`, `wanted`, `is_rails_app`, `gemfile_has_rails`, `rails_version`, `EXTENSIONS`, `FILE_NAMES`. |
| `source.rs` | `LineIndex`, `utf16_to_byte`, `byte_to_utf16`, `logical_lines`, `tokens`, `call_args`, `string_around`, `word_at`. |
| `inflect.rs` | `pluralize`, `singularize`, `camelize`, `underscore`, `tableize`, `classify`. |
| `routes.rs` | `parse_routes`, `parse_rails_routes`, `sample_path`, `Route`. |
| `app.rs` | `controller`, `view`, `model`, `link_models`, `render_refs`, `resolve_render`, `Controller`, `View`, `Model`. |
| `schema.rs` | `tables`, `schema_version`, `migration_version`, `Table`, `Column`. |
| `yaml.rs` | `parse`, `Value`, `Entry`. |
| `database.rs` | `parse`, `render_erb`, `driver`, `DatabaseConfig`. |
| `i18n.rs` | `Catalog`, `default_locale`, `refs`, `lazy_scope`, `TRef`. |
| `hotwire.rs` | `controller`, `identifier`, `stimulus_refs`, `data_attributes`, `frame_refs`, `TURBO_HELPERS`. |
| `generators.rs` | `built_in`, `project_generators`, `parse_generate_output`, `Generator`. |
| `command.rs` | `server_command`, `console_command`, `dbconsole_command`, `generate_command`, `routes_command`, `generators_command`, `RAILS`. |
| `editor.rs` | `goto`, `complete`, `marks`, `enclosing_def`, `Completions`, `FileMarks`. |

Tests run on the `blog` fixture application in `tests/fixtures/blog` (also the browser demo,
`app/ui/src/mock/demoRailsProject.ts`, generated from it).

## Used by

- IPC: `app/src-tauri/src/commands/rails.rs` (`rails_*` commands) and `run.rs` (the `rails`
  run configuration).
- WebAssembly: `crates/forge-wasm/src/rails.rs` (`rails_project`, `rails_goto`,
  `rails_complete`, `rails_marks`, `rails_generators`, `rails_command`).
- Go to Related for Rails files lives in `forge-codeintel` (`related.rs`), project detection
  (`rails`) in `forge-project`.

# rubyforge-sdk

`packs/rubyforge/sdk` — RubyForge on the user's machine.

## Purpose

- `detect`: `RubyStatus` of a project — the interpreters of version managers (rbenv with
  `RBENV_ROOT`, rvm with its gem sets, chruby, asdf with `ASDF_DATA_DIR`, mise with
  `MISE_DATA_DIR`, frum, rv) read from their folders, and of Homebrew, RubyInstaller and the
  `PATH` (shims skipped, symlinks resolved) asked for their version with the interpreter only
  (`ruby -e …`, through a `Runner`); `choose` (the setting, the requested version, the

  with the user's own RubyGems (nothing bundled or downloaded by Forge itself), the installed
  executable and its launch environment (`GEM_PATH`).

  (`localfs`, `nonstop` unless Stop on entry) and asks `forge-dap` to send breakpoints after

# goforge-lang-go

`packs/goforge/lang-go` — GoForge: everything about Go that needs no I/O. The desktop
backend and the WebAssembly build of browser mode share it.

## Purpose

- `scan`: a tolerant Go tokenizer (identifiers, decoded string literals, punctuation, lines).
- `gomod`: `go.mod` (`module`, `go`, `toolchain`, `godebug`, `require`, `replace`, `exclude`,
  `retract`, `tool`, `ignore`, single lines and blocks, `// indirect`) and `go.work` (`go`,
  `toolchain`, `use`, `replace`) with positions (UTF-16 columns), problems and the completion
  context at an offset (directive, module path, version of a module, Go version).
- `version`: module versions (semver, pseudo-versions, `+incompatible`), ordering, the latest
  release, proxy `@v/list` answers and module path escaping (`!a` for `A`).
- `discovery`: `TestXxx`, `BenchmarkXxx`, `FuzzXxx` and `ExampleXxx` functions and literal
  subtests / sub-benchmarks (`t.Run("name", func(t *testing.T) {…})`, any depth) with
  `go test`'s names.
- `provider`: `GoTestProvider`, the `forge-testing` provider of the manifest's `go-test`
  framework: gutter targets keyed `<package folder>::<name>`, `go test -json` command lines per
  scope (all, directory, file, test, pattern) and kind (tests, benchmarks, fuzzing), coverage
  (`-coverprofile`, Go coverprofile), profiles (`-cpuprofile`, …), Rerun Failed Tests, `-C`
  for modules in sub folders and location rules from import paths to project paths;
  `debug_test` gives Delve the test binary flags of a configuration.
- `build`: Go Build configurations (`go run` / `go build -o`, package / directory / files,
  tags, Go tool arguments) and module commands (`go mod tidy|download|verify`,
  `go work sync`, `go get`, `go install`).
- `generate`: `//go:generate` directives and `go generate -run '^<directive>$' file.go`.
- `lint`: `go vet -json` and golangci-lint JSON (v1 `--out-format=json`, v2
  `--output.json.path=stdout`) as `GoProblem`s of project files.
- `env`: `GoContext` (SDK, GOPATH, GOFLAGS, build tags, environment, modules), handed to the
  provider through `CommandContext.settings["go.context"]`, and `go env -json`.

# goforge-sdk

`packs/goforge/sdk` — GoForge on the user's machine: SDKs, tools and the module proxy.

## Purpose

- `detect`: Go SDKs found without running anything — the `go` on the `PATH` (symlinks
  resolved), `GOROOT`, `/usr/local/go`, `/usr/lib/go`, `/usr/lib/golang`, `/opt/go`, Snap,
  Homebrew, `Program Files\Go`, `~/sdk/go*`, `~/go/go*` and `<data dir>/forge/go-sdks` —
  newest first, the version from the SDK's `VERSION` file.
- `download`: the release list of `go.dev/dl/?mode=json`, the archive of a stable release for
  the platform, and the install: download, SHA-256 check against the list, unpack
  (`forge_langservers::managed::archive`, `go/` stripped) into a staging folder renamed to
  `<data dir>/forge/go-sdks/go<version>`. Only called after the user agreed.
- `tools`: gopls, Delve, goimports and golangci-lint — the setting with the user's path, the
  lookup order (Forge's `GOBIN`, `GOBIN`, `GOPATH/bin`, the SDK's `bin`, `PATH`), and the
  pinned `go install <module>@<version>` per SDK version (Delve 1.27.2 for Go 1.25+, 1.25.2
  before; gopls 0.23.0 / 0.20.0; goimports 0.30.0). golangci-lint (GPL-3.0) is never installed.
- `proxy`: `ModuleProxy` (module versions from `<proxy>/<escaped>/@v/list`, `@latest` for
  untagged modules), cached 12 hours in `<cache dir>/forge/go-proxy` with the stale copy used
  offline; `proxy_from_goproxy`; `cached_modules` (module paths in the module cache).

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |

# goforge-delve

`packs/goforge/delve` — GoForge's debugger on [forge-dap](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-dap.md).

## Purpose

- `DelveAdapter` implements `DebugAdapterDescriptor` for the adapter type `go`: each session
  starts `dlv dap --listen=127.0.0.1:<port>` in the package's folder (Delve runs `go build`
  there) with the project's environment and the SDK's `bin` first on the `PATH`, and connects
  to it. The built program goes to `<temp>/forge-delve`, never into the project.
- Requests: `launch` with `mode: debug` (Go Build), `mode: test` (Go Test), `mode: core`
  (core dumps); `attach` with `mode: local` (Attach to Process) and `mode: remote` (a running
  `dlv --headless --accept-multiclient` server, Go Remote configurations, `substitutePath`).
- `request(cfg, env, go, root)` builds the `LaunchRequest` of a `go-build`, `go-test` or
  `go-remote` configuration (program, arguments, working directory, environment,
  `buildFlags`, test binary flags from `goforge_lang_go::debug_test`).

## Used by

- `app/src-tauri/src/commands/go.rs`: `sync_debug` registers the adapter while `forge.go` is
  enabled (called by `commands/dap.rs`), `go_debug_request`, `go_delve_status`.
- UI: the `delve` debug launcher in `app/ui/src/features/go/index.tsx`.

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: [`forge-dap`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-dap.md), [`forge-runtools`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-runtools.md),
  [`goforge-lang-go`](docs/guide/developer/crates/goforge-lang-go.md)
- External: `serde`, `serde_json`

## Tests

Unit tests for every mode. `tests/delve_smoke.rs` (ignored) debugs a small Go program with a
real Delve and Go toolchain: breakpoint, stack, variables.

```sh
cargo test -p goforge-delve
FORGE_DLV=$(go env GOPATH)/bin/dlv cargo test -p goforge-delve -- --ignored
```

# goforge-pprof

`packs/goforge/pprof` — the data of the Profiler tool window.

## Purpose

- `proto`: the protobuf wire format (varints, length-delimited fields, packed repeated
  numbers, fixed 32/64-bit fields skipped), reading and writing. No protobuf library is
  needed for `profile.proto`'s few messages.
- `profile`: `decode` reads a profile, gzip compressed (`flate2`) or not: sample types,
  samples (location ids, leaf first, and values), locations with their inlined lines,
  functions, the string table, period and duration; frames are interned.
- `view`: `view(profile, sample_index, options)` for one sample type — the top list (flat and
  cumulative per function, sorted like `pprof -top`), the top-down call tree merged by
  function, with nodes below `min_fraction` pruned. The UI draws the flame graph from the tree.
- `builder`: `ProfileBuilder` writes profiles (tests) and `demo_profile` is the CPU profile of
  the browser-mode demo.

## Used by

- IPC: `pprof_open` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/go.rs`).
- Browser mode: `crates/forge-wasm/src/go.rs` (`pprof_view`).
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/go/ProfilerView.tsx` (the views themselves are shared:
  `app/ui/src/features/profiler/callTree.tsx`).
- [cforge-analyzers](docs/guide/developer/crates/cforge-analyzers.md): `perf script` output becomes a `Profile`, so perf
  profiles get the same views.

## Dependencies

- External: `serde`, `flate2` (MIT / Apache-2.0)

## Tests

`tests/fixtures/` holds a CPU and a memory profile written by `go test -cpuprofile` /
`-memprofile`; the views of a known built profile are checked value by value.

```sh
cargo test -p goforge-pprof
```

# cforge-toolchains

`packs/cforge/toolchains` — CForge: the toolchains of Settings | Build, Execution,
Deployment | Toolchains, like CLion's. A toolchain is a C and C++ compiler with CMake, a build
tool (Ninja, Make) and a debugger (GDB or LLDB).

## Purpose

- `version`: `gcc -v` / `clang -v` (target, thread model, installed dir, vendor such as
  `Ubuntu`, `MSYS2 project`, `Arm GNU Toolchain 13.3.Rel1`), Apple Clang, MSVC's `cl` banner
  and the first line of `--version` of CMake, Ninja, Make, GDB, LLDB and clang-format;
  `at_least` / `version_key` compare versions.
- `vswhere`: `vswhere -format json` installations (newest first), the newest MSVC tool set in
  `VC\Tools\MSVC`, `cl.exe` for a host / target architecture, `vcvarsall.bat` and the CMake and
  Ninja that Visual Studio bundles.
- `detect`: the toolchains of a machine — the system GCC and Clang, versioned compilers
  (`gcc-14`), cross compilers `<triple>-gcc` (with `<triple>-gdb` or `gdb-multiarch`; Debian's
  host aliases are skipped), MinGW-w64 folders on Windows and Visual Studio — with their
  problems ("GDB 12.1 has no DAP server", "No build tool"), the user's toolchains from the
  setting `cpp.toolchains` (`ToolchainEntry`, empty fields detected) and the CMake variables a
  toolchain sets (`CMAKE_C_COMPILER`, `CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER`, `CMAKE_MAKE_PROGRAM`).

Everything detection does to the machine goes through the `Probe` trait (`SystemProbe` for
the real one), so the tests describe Linux and Windows machines with a fake.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `version.rs` | `parse_compiler`, `parse_tool_version`, `CompilerInfo`, `CompilerFamily`, `at_least`, `version_key`. |
| `vswhere.rs` | `parse`, `VsInstallation`, `newest_toolset`, `msvc_paths`, `VSWHERE_ARGS`. |
| `detect.rs` | `detect`, `all`, `from_entry`, `which`, `cmake_variables`, `Toolchain`, `ToolchainEntry`, `Probe`, `SystemProbe`. |

## Used by

- IPC: `app/src-tauri/src/commands/cpp.rs` (`cpp_toolchains`, `cpp_toolchain_inspect`, the
  configure command, the debugger and coverage tools of a profile).

## Dependencies

- External: `serde`, `serde_json`

## Tests

Unit tests with fixtures recorded on Ubuntu 24.04 (`gcc -v`, `clang -v`, `cmake --version`,
`ninja --version`, `make --version`, `gdb --version`, `lldb --version`,
`clang-format --version`) and documented-format samples (MinGW, `arm-none-eabi-gcc`, Apple
Clang, the `cl` banner, `vswhere` JSON) in `tests/fixtures/`.

```sh
cargo test -p cforge-toolchains
```

# cforge-cmake

`packs/cforge/cmake` — CForge: everything about CMake that needs no I/O. The desktop backend
reads files and runs CMake; this crate decides. The WebAssembly build of browser mode shares
it.

## Purpose

- `presets`: `CMakePresets.json` and `CMakeUserPresets.json` (which includes the project
  file) with `include` files (cycles reported), configure, build and test presets,
  `inherits` (depth first, the first parent that sets a field wins; cache variables and
  environments merge, `null` unsets), `condition`s (`const`, `equals`, `notEquals`,
  `inList`, `notInList`, `matches`, `anyOf`, `allOf`, `not`) and macros (`${sourceDir}`,
  `${sourceParentDir}`, `${sourceDirName}`, `${presetName}`, `${generator}`,
  `${hostSystemName}`, `${fileDir}`, `${dollar}`, `${pathListSep}`, `$env{}`, `$penv{}`).
- `profile`: CMake profiles (`Profile`; the setting `cmake.profiles` holds `ProfileEntry`
  tables) with CLion's defaults (a Debug profile, `cmake-build-<name>`), preset profiles, and
  the command lines of configure (`-S`, `-B`, `-G`, `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE`, the toolchain's
  variables, `CMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS`, options; `--preset=<name>` for presets), build,
  rebuild (`--clean-first`), clean and CTest's location.
- `fileapi`: the stateful client query (`.cmake/api/v1/query/client-forge/query.json`:
  `codemodel` 2, `toolchains` 1, `cmakeFiles` 1) and the reply: the newest index, the
  client's responses, configurations, projects, targets (kind, artifacts, sources with their
  language, dependencies, the `CMakeLists.txt` line that defines them from the backtrace
  graph), compilers and the project's CMake files.
- `log`: `CMake Error/Warning/Deprecation Warning/Warning (dev) at file:line (command):` blocks
  and `in file` / one-line `CMake Error:` messages of a configure, and whether it failed.
- `complete`: completion of CMake commands (signatures), the keywords of the command the
  caret is in, and `${VARIABLES}`.
- `sanitizers`: a profile's sanitizers (`address`, `undefined`, `thread`, `memory`, `leak`;
  `ProfileEntry.sanitizers`) as `-fsanitize=…` compiler and linker flags appended to the
  flags the options set, the combinations compilers reject (`Profile.sanitizerError`) and
  the runtime options of runs (`UBSAN_OPTIONS`, `ASAN_OPTIONS`).
- `packages`: vcpkg manifest mode (`vcpkg.json` dependencies, the root from the setting,
  `VCPKG_ROOT` or `VCPKG_INSTALLATION_ROOT`, its toolchain file, port completion in
  `vcpkg.json`) and Conan 2 (`conan install . -of <build> -s build_type=… --build=missing`,
  where `conan_toolchain.cmake` is generated). `ConfigureContext.package_toolchain` becomes
  `-DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE` unless the profile sets its own.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `presets.rs` | `load`, `Presets`, `RawPreset`, `ResolvedConfigure`, `ResolvedBuild`, `MacroContext`, `expand`, `condition_holds`. |
| `profile.rs` | `Profile`, `ProfileEntry`, `profiles`, `configure_command`, `build_command`, `BuildAction`, `Command`, `ConfigureContext`, `split_args`, `ctest_next_to`, `build_dir_of`. |
| `fileapi.rs` | `query_json`, `parse_reply`, `CMakeModel`, `Configuration`, `Target`, `TargetKind`, `Source`, `Location`, `QUERY_DIR`, `REPLY_DIR`. |
| `log.rs` | `parse_log`, `failed`, `ConfigureMessage`, `Severity`. |
| `complete.rs` | `complete`, `COMMANDS`, `VARIABLES`, `Completion`. |
| `sanitizers.rs` | `SANITIZERS`, `parse_list`, `conflict`, `compile_flags`, `link_flags`, `run_env`, `cmake_definitions`. |
| `packages.rs` | `PackageManagers`, `vcpkg_dependencies`, `vcpkg_root`, `vcpkg_toolchain`, `complete_vcpkg`, `conan_install_command`, `conan_toolchain_candidates`. |

## Used by

- IPC: `app/src-tauri/src/commands/cpp.rs` (`cmake_*`), `commands/cpp_tools.rs`
  (`cpp_packages`, `cpp_vcpkg_complete`, `cpp_conan_install_command`).
- [cforge-lang-cpp](docs/guide/developer/crates/cforge-lang-cpp.md) (command type, argument splitting).
- Browser mode: `crates/forge-wasm/src/cpp.rs`.

## Dependencies

- External: `serde`, `serde_json`

## Tests

configuring a small project with Ninja (paths replaced by `/home/dev/shapes`);
`tests/fixtures/cmake-configure-*.txt` are recorded configure logs with errors and warnings.

```sh

```

# cforge-lang-cpp

`packs/cforge/lang-cpp` — CForge: everything about C and C++ that needs no I/O. The desktop
backend and the WebAssembly build of browser mode share it.

## Purpose

- `diagnostics`: compiler and linker messages of a build — GCC and Clang
  (`file:line:col: error: …` with `[-Wflag]` codes; source excerpts and `In function`
  context skipped; notes attached to their message), MSVC (`file(line,col): error C2065: …`,
  `link.exe` `LNK` errors), GNU `ld` (`file.cpp:(.text+0x9): undefined reference …`), `lld`
  and Apple's `ld` — and `project_path`, which makes paths project-relative (relative paths
  resolve against the build folder).
- `compdb`: `compile_commands.json` (`command` strings split like a shell, or `arguments`),
  standards, include folders, a summary and `--query-driver` globs.
- `discovery`: GoogleTest (`TEST`, `TEST_F`, `TEST_P`, `TYPED_TEST`, `TYPED_TEST_P`) and
  Catch2 (`TEST_CASE`, `TEST_CASE_METHOD`, `SCENARIO`, `TEMPLATE_TEST_CASE`, nested `SECTION`,
  `GIVEN` / `WHEN` / `THEN` with Catch2's prefixes, tags) with a tokenizer that skips comments
  and reads string and raw string literals; the included header decides the framework.
- `provider`: `CppTests`, the `forge-testing` providers of `gtest`, `catch2` and `ctest`
  (replacing the manifest's declarations): gutter targets keyed like the test tree,
  command lines per scope (`--gtest_filter` for tests, suites, parameterized and typed tests;
  Catch2 test specs with escaping and `-c` sections; `ctest -R/-L/-j`), JUnit reports, Rerun
  Failed Tests and Run with Coverage (`LLVM_PROFILE_FILE` and a `CoverageCollect` for the
  backend). The executable comes from a `CppContext` (build folder, CTest, executable targets
  with their sources) in `CommandContext.settings["cpp.context"]`; `debug_command` gives the
  debugger a test's program and filter.
- `coverage`: gcov's JSON (`gcov --json-format --stdout`) to LCOV (project files only, counts
  of several objects added, branches and functions), the `llvm-profdata merge` and `llvm-cov
  export -format=lcov` command lines, and the tools that belong to a compiler
  (`g++-14` → `gcov-14`).
- `tools`: clangd's arguments (`--compile-commands-dir`, `--background-index`,
  `--clang-tidy`, `--header-insertion`, `--completion-style`, `--query-driver`), its version,
  clang-format's arguments (`--assume-filename`, `--style=file`, `--fallback-style`) and the
  debug setup with STL renderers (GDB `-iex` commands that register libstdc++'s printers,
  LLDB `initCommands`), with the folders where GCC keeps its printers.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `diagnostics.rs` | `parse_build_output`, `project_path`, `BuildProblem`, `Severity`. |
| `compdb.rs` | `parse`, `summary`, `query_drivers`, `entry_for`, `CompileCommand`. |
| `discovery.rs` | `discover`, `included_framework`, `CppTest`, `Discovered`, `Framework`, `Kind`. |
| `provider.rs` | `CppTests`, `register`, `CppContext`, `ContextTarget`, `debug_command`, `gtest_test_filter`, `catch2_escape`, `is_cpp_source`. |
| `coverage.rs` | `gcov_json_to_lcov`, `gcov_command`, `llvm_merge_command`, `llvm_export_command`, `llvm_profile_env`, `tool_next_to`. |
| `tools.rs` | `clangd_args`, `ClangdOptions`, `clangd_version`, `clang_format_args`, `debug_setup`, `printer_dir_candidates`. |

## Used by

- IPC: `app/src-tauri/src/commands/cpp.rs`, `commands/run.rs` (the providers in
  `RunState.tests`, CMake Application command lines), `commands/testing.rs` (coverage).
- Browser mode: `crates/forge-wasm/src/cpp.rs` and `testing.rs`.

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: [`forge-output`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-output.md), [`forge-runtools`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-runtools.md),
  [`forge-testing`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-testing.md), [`cforge-cmake`](docs/guide/developer/crates/cforge-cmake.md)
- External: `serde`, `serde_json`

## Tests

Unit tests per module with recorded fixtures in `tests/fixtures/`: GCC 13 and Clang 18 errors,
a GNU `ld` error, a failed Ninja build, CTest's `--output-junit` report and console output,


# cforge-analyzers

`packs/cforge/analyzers` — CForge's dynamic analysis results, parsed without I/O. The desktop
backend collects run output, reads Valgrind's XML file and runs `perf script`; this crate turns
the text into the models the Run tool window and the Profiler show. The WebAssembly build of
browser mode shares it.

## Purpose

- `sanitizer`: `==pid==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: …`, `WARNING: ThreadSanitizer: …`,
  `WARNING: MemorySanitizer: …`, LeakSanitizer's `detected memory leaks` (one report per
  `Direct leak` / `Indirect leak`) and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer's `file:line:col: runtime
  error: …` lines. Each `SanitizerReport` has the sanitizer, its kind, the headline, titled
  stacks (access, allocation, free, previous access, thread creation), extra lines and the
  `SUMMARY`. Frames are parsed from ASan's `#n 0xaddr in func file:line:col (module+0x…)`
  and TSan's `#n func file:line (module+0x…)` forms (`(BuildId: …)` dropped).
- `valgrind`: Memcheck's XML (protocol 4, `--xml=yes`): errors with `kind`, `what` /
  `xwhat`, the stacks (`auxwhat` titles the stack after it), `errorcounts`, leak records
  sorted by size and the leak summary added up (definitely / indirectly / possibly lost,
  still reachable). Truncated files (a killed run) are read as far as they go.
- `perf`: `perf record -g -o <file> [-F n] [--call-graph mode] -- program` and
  `perf script -F comm,pid,tid,time,period,event,ip,sym,dso,srcline`; the script output (one
  call stack per sample, leaf first, `srcline` lines) becomes a `goforge_pprof::Profile`
  (sample types `samples` and the event, `cpu` in nanoseconds for `cpu-clock` /
  `task-clock`), so `goforge_pprof::view` computes the method list, call tree and flame graph
  shared with GoForge.
- `frames`: `StackFrame` / `Stack` and `project_path` (absolute paths below the root,
  relative ones in the project or the build folder; toolchain, C library and sanitizer runtime
  files never), `resolve_stacks` (the first project frame is the location).
- `xml`: a small tree on quick-xml, also used for CMSIS-SVD files by
  [cforge-embedded](docs/guide/developer/crates/cforge-embedded.md).
- `valgrind_args`: the Memcheck command line (`--tool=memcheck --xml=yes --xml-file=…`,
  `--leak-check=full` unless the options set it).

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `sanitizer.rs` | `parse`, `resolve`, `SanitizerReport`, `Sanitizer`. |
| `valgrind.rs` | `parse`, `resolve`, `ValgrindReport`, `ValgrindError`, `LeakSummary`, `Leaked`. |
| `perf.rs` | `record_args`, `script_args`, `RecordOptions`, `parse`, `open`. |
| `frames.rs` | `StackFrame`, `Stack`, `project_path`, `resolve_stacks`. |
| `xml.rs` | `parse`, `Element`. |

## Used by

- IPC: `app/src-tauri/src/commands/cpp_tools.rs` (the sanitizer observer of C/C++ runs,
  `RunRequest.nativeTool`, `cpp_sanitizer_reports`, `cpp_valgrind_open`).
- [cforge-embedded](docs/guide/developer/crates/cforge-embedded.md) (`xml`).
- Browser mode: `crates/forge-wasm/src/cpp_tools.rs`.

## Dependencies

- Internal: [goforge-pprof](docs/guide/developer/crates/goforge-pprof.md)
- External: `serde`, `quick-xml`

## Tests

Unit tests on recorded fixtures in `tests/fixtures/`: AddressSanitizer (heap-buffer-overflow,
heap-use-after-free, leaks), ThreadSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer reports of GCC 13,
a MemorySanitizer report, Memcheck XML of Valgrind 3.22 and `perf script` output.
`tests/smoke.rs` (ignored) compiles a program in a temporary folder and runs the real
Valgrind: `cargo test -p cforge-analyzers --test smoke -- --ignored`.

# cforge-embedded

`packs/cforge/embedded` — CForge's embedded development support without I/O: it reads
project files and builds command lines; the desktop backend starts them and reads memory
through the debugger. The WebAssembly build of browser mode shares it.

## Purpose

- `platformio`: `platformio.ini` (sections, multi-line values, `;` comments, `[env]`
  defaults, `extends` chains with loop detection, `${section.key}` / `${this.key}`
  interpolation, `default_envs`) into `PioProject` / `PioEnv` (platform, board, frameworks,
  every resolved option, the section's line), and the task commands (`pio run -e <env> -t
  upload|clean|compiledb`, `pio test`, `pio device monitor`).
- `espidf`: detection (`sdkconfig`, `idf_component.yml`, the IDF's `project.cmake`), the
  chip target of `sdkconfig`, and `idf.py build|flash|monitor|menuconfig|fullclean` with
  `IDF_PATH`, its Python, the serial port and baud rate.
- `zephyr`: detection (`west.yml`, `prj.conf` with `find_package(Zephyr)`), the board of a
  build's `CMakeCache.txt`, boards an application defines in `boards/`, and `west build -b
  <board> -d <dir> -p auto|always <app>`, `west flash`, `west debug`.
- `openocd`: `openocd -f <cfg>… -c "gdb_port N"` (the GDB server), `-c "program {<elf>} verify
  reset exit"` (flashing), the ready line and GDB's `target remote` address.
- `svd`: CMSIS-SVD (`device` → `peripherals` with `derivedFrom` → `registers` / nested
  `cluster`s with `dim` arrays → `fields` with `bitOffset`/`bitWidth`, `bitRange` or
  `lsb`/`msb`, `dim` and `enumeratedValues`), with size, access and reset value inherited from
  the device and peripheral; `read_ranges` (adjacent readable registers; write-only ones and
  those with a `readAction` are skipped) and `decode` (little-endian register values and
  field values with their enumerated names).
- `detect`: which of PlatformIO, ESP-IDF and Zephyr a project uses (`EmbeddedKinds`).

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `platformio.rs` | `parse`, `list`, `PioProject`, `PioEnv`, `PioTask`, `task_command`. |
| `espidf.rs` | `detect`, `target`, `IdfAction`, `IdfSetup`, `command`. |
| `zephyr.rs` | `detect`, `board_of_cache`, `local_boards`, `WestAction`, `command`. |
| `openocd.rs` | `OpenOcdSetup`, `server_command`, `program_command`, `is_ready_line`, `gdb_target`. |
| `svd.rs` | `parse`, `number`, `Device`, `Peripheral`, `Register`, `Field`, `read_ranges`, `decode`, `RegisterValue`, `DeviceSummary`. |
| `lib.rs` | `ToolCommand`, `EmbeddedKinds`, `detect`. |

## Used by

- IPC: `app/src-tauri/src/commands/embedded.rs` (`embedded_info`, `pio_command`,
  `idf_command`, `west_command`, `cpp_embedded_launch`, `cpp_svd_peripherals`,
  `cpp_svd_read`).
- Browser mode: `crates/forge-wasm/src/cpp_tools.rs`.

## Dependencies

- Internal: [cforge-analyzers](docs/guide/developer/crates/cforge-analyzers.md) (`xml`)
- External: `serde`

## Tests

Unit tests per module; fixtures `tests/fixtures/platformio.ini` (defaults, `extends`,
interpolation, multi-line values) and `tests/fixtures/stm32f4-mini.svd` (a trimmed STM32F401
description with `derivedFrom`, register and field arrays, a cluster and enumerated values).

# dotnetforge-lang-dotnet

`packs/dotnetforge/lang-dotnet` — DotNetForge's .NET logic. Pure Rust (no I/O), shared by the
desktop backend and the WebAssembly build of browser mode.

## Purpose

- Read solutions and projects the way Rider shows them before a design-time build: `.sln`
  and `.slnx` (projects, solution folders, configurations), MSBuild project files with the
  nearest `Directory.Build.props` / `Directory.Packages.props` (properties with `$(…)`
  references, simple conditions, target frameworks, output type, references, package
  references with central versions and `VersionOverride`, F# compile order), and
  `launchSettings.json` profiles.
- `global.json` and the SDK the dotnet host picks (`rollForward` policies), `dotnet
  --list-sdks` / `--list-runtimes`, install hints per platform.
- MSBuild / compiler output as problems (C#, F#, VB, NuGet, MSBuild, `[project]` suffixes,
  each problem once) with the built outputs and the summary.
- A tolerant C# / F# scanner for xUnit, NUnit and MSTest tests and `Main` methods, and the
  `dotnet-test` provider of the shared test runner (`DotnetTests`): discovery, `dotnet test`
  with `FullyQualifiedName` filters and a TRX logger, Rerun Failed Tests, location rules from
  test classes to files.
- Command lines: build / rebuild / clean / restore / test / pack / publish / watch,
  ".NET Project" runs (`dotnet run` / `dotnet watch` with launch profiles), the debug build,
  `dotnet add|remove package`, `dotnet new` with `dotnet sln add`, `dotnet format`.
- `dotnet new list` tables, NuGet v3 service index / search / versions, NuGet SemVer
  comparison and upgrades, `dotnet format` JSON reports and EditorConfig lookup, the Roslyn
  server's arguments, `solution/open` and settings.
- Web and cloud projects, on a small C# tokenizer (`csharp.rs`: names, punctuation and string
  values, attributes, argument lists): ASP.NET Core endpoints (minimal APIs with `MapGroup`
  route groups, `WithName`, `RequireAuthorization`; controllers with `[Route]`, `[Http*]`,
  `[controller]` / `[action]` tokens, `~/` routes, `[Area]`; Blazor `@page`; Razor Pages
  routes from their path) with their parameters and `.http` requests; Blazor components with
  `[Parameter]`s from `@code` blocks and code-behind; EF Core projects, DbContexts with
  DbSets, migrations, `dotnet ef` command lines and their JSON / text output; Aspire AppHosts
  and their resources, the dashboard URL in the AppHost's output; multi-stage Dockerfiles and
  the ".NET Docker" command lines; `dotnet watch` Hot Reload events; user secrets paths and
  adding a `UserSecretsId` to a project file.

# dotnetforge-gamedev

`packs/dotnetforge/gamedev` — DotNetForge: Unity and Godot in the style of Rider. See
[Unity and Godot](docs/guide/user/unity-godot.md).

## Purpose

The logic of the Unity (`forge.unity`) and Godot (`forge.godot`) plugins. The file system
and the process list come in as data or functions, so everything is tested with fixtures and
fakes; `app/src-tauri/src/commands/gamedev.rs` wires it to IPC.

### Unity (`unity`)

- `project`: `ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt` (`m_EditorVersion`, the revision),
  `Packages/manifest.json`, the IDE packages that write project files, the Test Framework,
  the bridge package (embedded or in the manifest, update available), the root `.sln` /
  `.csproj` files, `Library/EditorInstance.json` (the editor's pid).
- `editors`: Unity Hub folders per OS, `secondaryInstallPath.json`, manually located editors
  (`editors-v2.json`, `editors.json`), Settings' editor; `match_editor` picks the exact
  version, else the newest of the same `major.minor`. `version_key` orders Unity versions
  (`a` < `b` < `f` < `p`).
- `package`: the bridge package (`dev.forge.unity`, C# in `unity-package/`, embedded with
  `include_str!`), its install plan below `Packages/dev.forge.unity`, version checks.
- `bridge`: protocol 1 (see [Unity editor bridge protocol](docs/guide/developer/unity-bridge-protocol.md)):
  `Library/ForgeBridge.json`, messages, console message locations (compiler messages, stack
  frames), and `BridgeClient` (tokio): handshake, commands with acknowledgements, events until
  `Disconnected`.
- `commands`: Start Unity (`-projectPath`), project files in batch mode (`-executeMethod`
  of the bridge or the Rider package).
- `test_runner`: the `unity-test` provider of `forge-testing`: NUnit / `[UnityTest]`
  discovery (DotNetForge's C# scanner), `-runTests -testPlatform -testResults -testFilter`,
  location rules from the test classes, Rerun Failed Tests, the refusal while an editor has
  the project open. Results: `forge_output::formats::nunit`.
- `processes`: Unity editors in a process list (`-projectPath`, the editor instance's pid)
  and their Mono debugger port (`56000 + pid % 1000`).

### Godot (`godot`)

- `project`: `project.godot` (multi-line values, `PackedStringArray`, autoloads, `[dotnet]`),
  scenes, `res://` paths.
- `executable`: Settings, `GODOT4` / `GODOT`, `PATH` names, Flatpak, macOS apps, downloaded
  `Godot_v4…` executables (also inside extracted .NET folders); .NET builds first for C#
  projects; `godot --version` parsing.
- `commands`: the `godot` run configuration (`--path`, scene, `--headless`, options,
  arguments after `--`), the editor (`--editor`), `dotnet build` before C# debugging.
- `lsp`: the GDScript server config (`tcp://host:6005`, see `forge_lsp::launch`) and a port
  probe.
- `dap`: `GodotAdapter`, a `forge_dap::DebugAdapterDescriptor` that connects to the editor's
  debug adapter (6006) and sends `launch` (`project`, `scene`, `playArgs`) or `attach`.
- `gdunit`: the `gdunit4` provider: `GdUnitTestSuite` discovery, GdUnit4's command line
  (`-a`, `-rd`), suite location rules, reruns by suite. The app reads GdUnit4's
  `report_<n>/results.xml` below the report folder.

## Tests

Unit tests per module; `tests/bridge.rs` (a fake Unity peer), `tests/godot_editor.rs` (a fake
GDScript language server and a fake Godot debug adapter on loopback, driven through
`forge-lsp` and `forge-dap`). No Unity, Godot or network is needed.

# pyforge-frameworks

`packs/pyforge/frameworks` — PyForge's web framework support (plugins `forge.python-web`,
`forge.django`, `forge.flask`, `forge.fastapi`, `forge.celery`, see
[Django, Flask, FastAPI and Celery](docs/guide/user/python-web-frameworks.md)). Pure: files in,
data out; the desktop app (`commands/python_web.rs`) and the WebAssembly build
(`crates/forge-wasm/src/python_web.rs`) share it. Nothing of the project runs.

## Purpose

- `source`: a forgiving token scanner — logical lines (brackets and `\` continuations
  joined, comments dropped), names, operators and string literals with the byte range of
  their content, call arguments, decorators, definitions and assignments. The scanner of
  `pyforge-testing` keeps only line text; navigation needs the offsets of string literals.
- `modules`: source roots (`""`, `src`, the folders of `manage.py`), module ↔ file, the
  names a file imports (relative imports included), so `views.index` resolves to its `def`.
- `detect`: frameworks from `requirements*.txt`, `pyproject.toml`, `Pipfile` and imports
  (Django also needs `manage.py`); `FLASK_APP` (also `module:create_app()`), the uvicorn app
  (`module:attr`, `--app-dir src`) and the Celery `-A` app.
- `django`: the settings module (setting, `manage.py`, a `settings.py` next to `urls.py`),
  `INSTALLED_APPS`, `ROOT_URLCONF`, `TEMPLATES` (`DIRS` from `BASE_DIR`, `APP_DIRS`, Jinja2)
  through `from .base import *`; URL patterns from `path` / `re_path` / `url` through
  `include()` with namespaces; models and fields; `manage.py` commands (built in, the
  project's `management/commands`, parsing `help --commands`).
- `flask`, `fastapi`: routes, blueprints and their registration prefixes; path operations
  of apps and `APIRouter`s with nested `include_router` prefixes.
- `celery`: `@shared_task` / `@app.task` functions and their registered names.
- `templates`: template folders and names, references in Python and templates, Go to
  Declaration, completion, gutter marks and the unresolved template / URL name inspections.
- `run`: `django-server`, `django-manage`, `flask-server`, `fastapi`, `celery-worker` and
  `celery-beat` as Python runs (target, arguments, environment, working directory, port).

## Tests

Unit tests per module with fixture projects (`tests/fixtures/django`), no network:
`cargo test -p pyforge-frameworks`.

# pyforge-jupyter

`packs/pyforge/jupyter` — PyForge's Jupyter support (plugin `forge.jupyter`, see
[Jupyter notebooks](docs/guide/user/jupyter.md)). The default build is pure and also compiled to
WebAssembly (`crates/forge-wasm/src/jupyter.rs`); the desktop app (`commands/jupyter.rs`)
adds the features `runtime` (kernels) and `keychain` (server tokens).

## Purpose

- `nbformat`: `.ipynb` (nbformat 4.x) into a `Notebook` (cells with joined texts, typed
  outputs, metadata, the cell's `origin` in the file) and back. `serialize` merges the editor's
  model into the original JSON: unchanged cells and outputs keep their raw JSON, changed
  fields keep the original's form (string or list of lines), new cells and outputs are written
  like Jupyter writes them (sorted keys, lines). The indent, compact one-line files, `\u`
  escapes of non-ASCII text and the final line break are detected and kept; key order is read into the
  crate's own ordered JSON values (`ordered`), so serde_json's `preserve_order` stays off for
  the workspace. nbformat 3 and older are refused.
- `output`: stream, `execute_result`, `display_data` and error outputs with MIME bundles
  (texts joined, JSON types as JSON) and `render`, the representation the editor shows:
  console lines from `forge-output` (ANSI, `\r`, file links), sanitized HTML, data URLs for
  images (SVG sanitized), JSON, Markdown or a DataFrame, chosen by JupyterLab's MIME order.
- `html`: a small tokenizer with `sanitize_html` (allowlist of elements and attributes,
  http(s)/mailto links, `data:image` sources, CSS without `url()`), `sanitize_svg` (scripts,
  event handlers, `foreignObject`, doctypes and external references removed) and `tables`.
- `dataframe`: pandas' HTML (index names, MultiIndex columns and rows through colspan /
  rowspan, the "N rows × M columns" footer), Table Schema JSON
  (`application/vnd.dataresource+json`) and the helper's View as DataFrame JSON into one
  `DataFrame`; `query` sorts (numeric-aware, `forge_viewers::sort_order`), filters and pages.
- `diff`: notebook diffs. Cells are paired by id, or by a patience alignment of their sources
  with neighbouring removed and added cells as changed cells; sources and outputs (as text,
  images as size and hash) get separate line diffs (`similar`).
- `protocol`: messages, HMAC-SHA256 signing and constant-time checks, the ZeroMQ frames
  (`<IDS|MSG>`), the WebSocket JSON form, connection files, `KernelEvent`s of iopub and shell
  messages and `user_expressions` replies.
- `runtime`: `kernel` (DEALER sockets for shell and control, SUB for iopub with the pure-Rust
  `zeromq` crate, MIT; five free ports from [`forge-ports`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-ports.md) and private
  connection files), `server` (REST `/api/kernels`, `/api/kernelspecs` and the kernel
  WebSocket with `tokio-tungstenite`) and
  `session` (runs cells and reports `SessionEvent`s per cell id with rendered outputs; waits
  for both the reply and the idle status; Variables, children and View as DataFrame through
  the helper `forge_jupyter.py` and `user_expressions`; interrupt with `interrupt_request`).
- `keychain`: Jupyter server tokens in the OS keychain (service `forge-jupyter`).

## Tests

Unit tests per module, fixture notebooks in `tests/fixtures` (written by Python's `json.dumps`
exactly as Jupyter writes them, plus an nbformat 4.2 file with another style) that round-trip
byte for byte, and `tests/fake_kernel.rs`: the session against an in-process fake kernel on
127.0.0.1 that checks every signature (a wrong key gets no answers). No network:
`cargo test -p pyforge-jupyter --features runtime`. `tests/ipykernel_smoke.rs` runs a real
ipykernel (ignored; `FORGE_JUPYTER_PYTHON=/path/to/python … -- --ignored`).

# pyforge-testing

`packs/pyforge/testing` — PyForge's tests, debugger, console and profiler support (the
`forge.python-tools` plugin, see [PyForge](docs/guide/user/python.md)). Pure, so the desktop app
and the WebAssembly build share it.

## Purpose

- `source` scans Python source without a parser: logical lines (brackets, continuations and
  triple-quoted strings joined, comments removed) and the classes and functions they declare
  with decorators, bases and nesting.
- `discover` finds pytest tests (`test_*.py` / `*_test.py`, `test*` functions, `Test*`
  classes without `__init__`), `unittest.TestCase` cases in any module and the ids of
  `@pytest.mark.parametrize` cases, and turns them into gutter targets with temporary
  `pytest` / `unittest` configurations (`config`). `detect` tells whether the project uses
  pytest or tox from its files and picks a file's runner (`python.testing.runner`).
- `command` builds the interpreter arguments: `-m pytest` with a scope, `--junitxml` (or
  `--report-log`) and pytest-cov's Cobertura report; Forge's unittest runner
  (`helpers/forge_unittest.py`, TeamCity messages, sent inline as base64 with `-c`; with
  `--coverage-xml` it measures with coverage.py and writes a Cobertura report);
  `-m tox -e …`; `-m debugpy --listen … --wait-for-client`; `-m cProfile -o …`; the console
  (`helpers/forge_console.py`). Report paths are made relative to the working directory, so
  they stay valid where interpreters and run targets map the project.
- `rerun` turns failed tests into pytest node ids or unittest ids, with the classes read from
  the files. `tox` reads `tox.ini`, `setup.cfg`, `tox.toml` and `pyproject.toml` environments
  (generative names expanded).
- `pstats` reads cProfile's `.pstats` files (the `marshal` subset they use) into hot spots and
  a call tree; `pstats::write` writes them (tests, the browser demo).
- `console` separates the console helper's replies (`\x1e` + JSON lines) from the user's
  output and builds its requests.
- `provider` registers the three runners as a `forge_testing::TestFrameworkProvider`.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `source.rs` | `logical_lines`, `declarations` (`Def`, `Decorator`), `split_top_level`, `bracket_contents`. |
| `discover.rs` | `scan` (`Scan`, `Item`, `Case`), `test_file`, `parametrize_cases`, `Runner`. |
| `config.rs` | The `pytest`, `unittest` and `tox` types, their options and builders. |
| `detect.rs` | `detect` (`ProjectTesting`), `choose_runner`. |
| `command.rs` | `pytest`, `unittest`, `tox`, `build`, `debugpy_args`, `profile_args`, `console`, `inline_script`, `relative_to`. |
| `rerun.rs` | `rerun_failed`. |
| `tox.rs` | `environments`, `from_ini`, `from_toml`, `expand` (`ToxEnv`). |
| `pstats.rs` | `parse`, `unmarshal`, `Profile` (`hot_spots`, `call_tree`, `view`, `map_files`), `write`. |
| `console.rs` | `Splitter`, `Piece`, `request`. |
| `provider.rs` | `PythonTestFrameworks`. |

## Used by

- IPC: `run_start` / `run_command_line` for the `python`, `pytest`, `unittest` and `tox`
  types, `test_discover` and `test_rerun_failed` for Python files, `python_testing_detect`,
  `python_tox_environments`, `python_debugpy_status`, `python_debug_plan`,
  `python_console_*`, `python_profiles`, `python_profile_view`, `python_profile_open`,
  `python_profile_delete` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/python_tools.rs`)
- Browser mode: `python_test_discover`, `python_testing_detect`, `python_rerun_failed`,
  `python_test_command`, `python_tox_environments`, `python_demo_profile` and the test
  registry of `testing_discover` in `forge-wasm`
- Output: the tox parser lives in [`forge-output`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-output.md) (`TestReport::Tox`)

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: [`forge-testing`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-testing.md), [`forge-output`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-output.md), [`forge-runtools`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-runtools.md)
- External: `serde`, `serde_json`, `toml`

Unit tests for discovery (functions, classes, nesting, parametrize ids), detection, command


# phpforge-builtin-lsp

`packs/phpforge/builtin-lsp` — PHPForge: the built-in PHP language server
[php-lsp](https://github.com/stdimnet/php-lsp), run by the Forge binary and the remote agent in
a hidden `--php-lsp --stdio` mode.

## Purpose

php-lsp is a pure-Rust PHP language server under MIT OR Apache-2.0, a drop-in for Intelephense
(same CLI flags, `intelephense.*` settings, diagnostics and formatting) with its premium
features free. It is Forge's only PHP language server and is linked into Forge, so users
install nothing. It is a cargo git dependency pinned to one revision
(`rev = "7011d4c1e1b4f27ad8ded67b55ae4fabcd92ef09"`); its embedded JetBrains phpstorm-stubs
(Apache-2.0) and the js-beautify port (MIT) are listed in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.

The server runs in a **separate process** for crash isolation: `forge` (and
`forge-remote-agent`) call `main_hook` first thing in `main`. With `--php-lsp` as the first
argument it runs `php_lsp::run_stdio()` and exits, before Tauri, logging or the agent runtime
start. Otherwise it announces the executable to `phpforge-lang-php`
(`lsp::register_builtin_server`), whose `server_config` then starts `<current exe> --php-lsp
--stdio` through forge-lsp like any other server. Transport, restarts, Safe Mode, remote
projects (the agent runs its own copy on the host) and the Language Servers UI work unchanged.

`run_stdio` runs the server on a thread with a 64 MB stack (`SERVER_STACK`) and sets
`RUST_MIN_STACK` to 16 MB (`WORKER_STACK`) for php-lsp's own threads, unless the environment
sets it. php-lsp's parser and type inference recurse over the syntax tree; the main thread of a
Windows program has a 1 MB stack (8 MB on Linux), and long expression chains overflowed it there,
which killed the server.

The in-process `php_lsp::Embedded` was not used: a server bug would take the IDE down, and the
LSP client would need a second, in-memory transport.

## Public items

| Item | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `FLAG` | `"--php-lsp"`, the first argument of the hidden mode. |
| `VERSION`, `REVISION`, `version_label()` | php-lsp's version and pinned commit, `"0.1.0 (7011d4c)"` (`VERSION` is `php_lsp::VERSION`; a test checks the pinned commit against `Cargo.lock`). |
| `main_hook(args)` | Runs the server in the hidden mode (`--version` prints the version) and returns the exit code; otherwise registers the built-in server and returns `None`. |
| `is_server_mode`, `server_args`, `run_stdio`, `register` | The pieces of `main_hook`. |

## Dependencies

`php-lsp` (git, pinned), `phpforge-lang-php`. It brings `lsp-types` 0.97 and `rowan` 0.17
next to forge-lsp's `lsp-types` 0.95 and tree-sitter-based crates; the server talks to Forge only
through JSON-RPC, so the versions never meet.

## Tests

- Unit tests: the hidden-mode arguments and the pinned version against `Cargo.lock`.
- `tests/server.rs` starts the test host `phpforge-builtin-lsp-host` (`tests/support/host.rs`,
  never shipped) through forge-lsp's `LspClient` with the configuration Forge builds from its
  PHP settings, on a small project in a temporary folder: initialize (capabilities), hover,
  cross-file definition, completion (also on CRLF text), diagnostics, formatting and rename,
  with a root from `std::fs::canonicalize` (a verbatim `\\?\C:\…` path on Windows). The test
  host is a GUI-subsystem program on Windows, like a release build of Forge. A second test opens
  a file with a 3000-part concatenation chain (deep syntax tree) and expects the server to
  survive.
- The tests also run as a Windows build: `cargo xwin test --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc -p
  phpforge-builtin-lsp --no-run`, then run `target/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/debug/deps/server-*.exe`
  under Wine or on Windows.

# phpforge-quality-tools

`packs/phpforge/quality-tools` — PHPForge: PHP quality tools (PHPStan, Psalm, PHP CS Fixer,
PHP_CodeSniffer, PHP Mess Detector, Laravel Pint, Rector): configurations, command lines,
parsing of their JSON reports with path mapping, and unified diffs.

## Purpose

Everything [PHP Quality Tools](docs/guide/user/php-quality-tools.md) computes. The crate is pure
(no processes or files): the app (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/php_quality_tools.rs`) runs the
command lines through the project backend, directly or wrapped by the tool's PHP interpreter
(`phpforge-interpreters`), and hands the output back to the parsers.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `model.rs` | `QualityTool` (ids, labels, `vendor/bin` candidates, phpcbf as phpcs's fixer, the configuration files each tool finds, which tools read unsaved text), `ToolConfig` from the `php.tools.<id>.*` settings (inspection, interpreter, path, phpcbf path, configuration file, level/ruleset, options, timeout, `SeverityChoice`), `split_args` (shell-like option splitting). |
| `command.rs` | `check_args(cfg, config, input)` for `Input::Files`, `Input::Stdin` (phpcs `--stdin-path=<file> -`, PHP CS Fixer `-`) and `Input::TempCopy` (PHPStan `--tmp-file … --instead-of …`); `fix_args` and `FixMode` (phpcbf: stdin → stdout, PHP CS Fixer / Rector: dry-run diff, Pint: in place); `in_place_args` (Actions on Save); `parse_version`. |

Severities follow the tools (PHPMD priorities, Psalm info as weak warnings, fixers' hunks as weak warnings) unless the configuration overrides them. |
| `problem.rs` | `Problem`, `Severity`, `PathContext` (reported paths relative to the tool's working directory, mapped back from the interpreter with `forge_runtargets::Mapper`, stdin and temporary copy aliases, made relative to the project root). |
| `diff.rs` | Unified diff hunks: `parse`, `apply` (hunks searched near their place, CRLF kept, `ApplyError` when the text changed), `Hunk::changed_lines`. |
| `lib.rs` | Re-exports, `CheckTrigger` and `tools_to_run` (which tools check unsaved text). |

## Main public items

```rust
pub fn fix_args(cfg: &ToolConfig, config: Option<&str>, file: &str, text: &str) -> ToolArgs;
pub fn parse_report(tool: QualityTool, stdout: &str, ctx: &PathContext, severity: SeverityChoice) -> Result<Report, String>;
pub fn tools_to_run(configs: &[ToolConfig], trigger: CheckTrigger, temp_copies: bool) -> Vec<QualityTool>;
pub mod diff; // parse, apply
```

## Used by

# phpforge-test-frameworks

`packs/phpforge/test-frameworks` — PHPForge: PHP test frameworks (PHPUnit, Pest, Codeception,
Behat, PHPSpec): settings and detection, run configuration command lines, test discovery for
gutter icons, Gherkin and Behat step definitions, Rerun Failed Tests.

## Purpose

Everything [PHP test frameworks](docs/guide/user/test-frameworks.md) computes. The crate is pure
(no processes, files or network) and builds to WebAssembly for browser mode; the app runs the
tests through the project backend and the PHP interpreter, and the results are parsed by
[`forge-output`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-output.md) (TeamCity messages and JUnit reports). The frameworks
register on the shared test runner as one provider (`PhpTestFrameworks`, see
[`forge-testing`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-testing.md)), so discovery, Rerun Failed Tests and Run with Coverage
go through the same registry as every other pack's frameworks; the discovery types
(`TestFile`, `TestTarget`, `TargetKind`, `FailedTest`) are `forge-testing`'s.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `frameworks.rs` | `Framework` (ids, labels, Composer packages, `vendor/bin` scripts, configuration files), `FrameworkConfig` (Settings \| PHP \| Test Frameworks: interpreter, Composer autoloader or path, configuration and bootstrap files) and its codec for the `php.testFrameworks` objects setting; `detect` (composer.json, `vendor/bin`, configuration files, `tests/Pest.php`), `effective` (configured first, then detected frameworks without an entry) and `resolve` (the entry of an interpreter, else Local). |
| `command.rs` | `build`: the arguments after `php` of Pest (`--teamcity`, `--filter` with the description and Pest's method name, dataset rows), Codeception (suite, file, `file:method`, groups, environments, `--xml` into the report folder), Behat (`--format=progress --out=std --format=junit --out=<dir>`, `file:line`, profile) and PHPSpec (`run --format=junit`, `file:line`, bootstrap) configurations, with the `TestReport` and `JUnitFlavor` of their results; `phpunit_defaults` fills a PHPUnit configuration's executable, configuration and bootstrap from the settings. |
| `discover.rs` | `discover(path, text)`: the tests of a file with their temporary configurations and result keys — PHPUnit classes and methods, Pest `test()` / `it()` / `describe()` calls (nested describes named `` `a` → it b `` like Pest) and inline dataset rows, Codeception Cest/Cept files and methods and `Codeception\Test\Unit` classes, Behat features, scenarios and example rows, PHPSpec specs and `it_*` / `its_*` examples; `target_at` for Run Context Configuration; `pest_evaluable` (Pest's `Str::evaluable`). |
| `gherkin.rs` | `parse`: features, background, scenarios and outlines with tags, steps (`Given`, `When`, `Then`, `And`, `But`, `*`) and example rows (1-based lines, doc strings skipped); `split_step`. |
| `steps.rs` | Behat step definitions from doc comments (`@Given …`) and attributes (`#[Given('…')]`, `#[\Behat\Step\Then("…")]`); `pattern_regex` (delimited regular expressions with flags, turnip `:placeholders`, optional `(s)` and `word/other` alternatives); `step_at` (a step's text, outline placeholders replaced by the first example row) and `step_targets`. |
| `rerun.rs` | `rerun_failed`: PHPUnit / Pest `--filter`, Codeception `-g failed`, Behat `--rerun`, PHPSpec the failed spec file. |
| `provider.rs` | `PhpTestFrameworks`: the `forge_testing::TestFrameworkProvider` of the five types (commands stay with the PHP interpreter path of the backend); `coverage_plan`: Run with Coverage of every type — the driver (`CoverageDriver`: Auto `XDEBUG_MODE=coverage`, Xdebug `-dxdebug.mode=coverage -dpcov.enabled=0`, PCOV `-dpcov.enabled=1`), PHPUnit / Pest `--coverage-clover` with `--path-coverage` and `--coverage-xml` (per-test), Codeception `--coverage-xml=` / `--coverage-phpunit=`, Behat and PHPSpec the Clover file their coverage extension's YAML configuration names (`clover_target`). |

# phpforge-composer

`packs/phpforge/composer` — PHPForge: Composer support (version constraints, composer.json/lock analysis, Packagist metadata, outdated packages, audit advisories, completion).

## Purpose

Everything the [Composer](docs/guide/user/composer.md) UI shows is computed here. The crate is pure
and builds to WebAssembly for browser mode; the `net` feature (desktop app only) adds the
Packagist client and the composer.phar download.

- Composer's version and constraint semantics: `^`, `~`, wildcards, ranges, `||`, hyphen
  ranges, `@dev`/`@beta` stability flags, branches and aliases, the recommended constraint of
  `composer require`.
- composer.json requirements with their source ranges, installed packages from composer.lock or
  installed.json, outdated markers with Composer's statuses, `composer audit` reports (which
  [forge-vulns](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-vulns.md) adapts to the shared vulnerability model).
- Packagist's Composer 2 metadata (minified version lists) and search results; completion and
  hover in `require` / `require-dev` built on `forge_jsonschema::complete::json_cursor`.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `version.rs` | Versions (`v1.2.3`, `2.0.0-RC1`, `1.x-dev`, `dev-main`), normalized and ordered like Composer (`dev < alpha < beta < RC < stable < patch`), stability. |
| `constraint.rs` | Constraint parsing and matching (`Constraint::matches`, `allows` with a minimum stability, `latest_allowed`) and `recommended(version)` (`^2.1`, `^0.4.2`, `^3.0@beta`). |
| `lock.rs` | Installed packages from composer.lock (`packages`, `packages-dev`) and vendor/composer/installed.json (Composer 1 and 2 formats). |
| `manifest.rs` | Requirements of composer.json with byte ranges, platform packages, package name validation, lock file entries and UTF-16 / line-column offsets. |
| `packagist.rs` | Packagist p2 metadata (minified lists expanded, `__unset`), search results, URLs. |
| `outdated.rs` | Outdated markers (installed vs latest, `semver-safe-update` / `update-possible`, the constraint for the update) and `composer outdated --format=json`. |
| `audit.rs` | `composer audit --format=json` (advisories as arrays or index-keyed objects, abandoned packages); forge-vulns places them in composer.json and composer.lock. |
| `complete.rs` | Completion of package names and versions and the package hover, in two steps (`request` / `hover_target`, then `items` / `hover` with the fetched data). |
| `net.rs` (`net`) | `Packagist`: metadata and search cached in `<cache dir>/forge/packagist` with a time to live and a stale fallback offline; `download_phar` (getcomposer.org, SHA-256 checked, into `<data dir>/forge/composer`). |

## Used by

- IPC: `composer_project`, `composer_markers`, `composer_complete`, `composer_hover`,
  `composer_search`, `composer_package`, `composer_download_phar`
  (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/composer.rs`); `php_composer_outdated` (through
  phpforge-lang-php)
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/composer/`
- Vulnerable dependency check: [forge-vulns](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-vulns.md) (`composer audit`, declarations)
- Browser mode: built into `forge-wasm` (`composer.rs`)

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: forge-jsonschema
- External: `serde`, `serde_json`; with `net`: `reqwest`, `sha2`, `tokio`, `dirs`

## Tests

10 source files, about 2800 lines; 28 unit tests. Network tests talk to a local fake server
(`testserver.rs`), never to Packagist.

```sh

```

# phpforge-dql

`packs/phpforge/dql` — PHPForge: Doctrine DQL tokenizer, parser, highlighting, completion and diagnostics, and DQL sites in PHP source (pure, also built to WebAssembly).

## Purpose

Doctrine DQL for PHPForge, without I/O so it also runs as WebAssembly in browser mode.

- `model`: entity mapping metadata (filled by `phpforge-orm-doctrine`).
- `dql`: tokenizer, parser, semantic highlighting, completion and diagnostics.
- `site`: DQL inside PHP strings (`createQuery()`, QueryBuilder calls) and the
  source-level functions over a `site::SiteFinder`; `lexical` is a finder without a
  PHP parser, `editor` the same functions with UTF-16 offsets.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `dql/lexer.rs` | DQL tokenizer. Path expressions (`o.customer.email`) are single identifier tokens; `super::highlight` splits them into alias and field parts. |
| `dql/mod.rs` | DQL: parsing (identification variables and their entities), semantic highlighting, completion and diagnostics against the project's entity mappings. |
| `editor.rs` | The site functions with editor offsets (UTF-16 code units, as JavaScript strings and CodeMirror count), as the IPC commands and the browser mock expose them. |
| `lexical.rs` | A `SiteFinder` without a PHP parser, for browser mode (WebAssembly cannot run the tree-sitter grammar): string literals are found lexically, the call around them by walking back to its `(`, and QueryBuilder aliases are read from the whole file. |
| `model.rs` | Entity mapping metadata as the DQL functions need it. `phpforge-orm-doctrine` fills it from PHP attributes, annotations, XML and YAML; browser mode passes it in as JSON. |
| `site.rs` | DQL inside PHP code: a `Site` is one DQL text assembled from the string literals of a call argument (`createQuery('…')`, QueryBuilder fragments like `->andWhere('o.status = :s')`) with a mapping back to source offsets. |

## Used by

- IPC: `doctrine_complete`, `doctrine_goto`, `doctrine_diagnostics`, `doctrine_highlight` (through phpforge-orm-doctrine)
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/doctrine/editor.ts`
- Browser mode: built into `forge-wasm`

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: none
- External: `regex-lite`, `serde`, `serde_json`

## Tests

7 source files, about 2329 lines; 14 unit tests.

```sh
cargo test -p phpforge-dql
```

# phpforge-fw-laravel

`packs/phpforge/fw-laravel` — PHPForge: Laravel support (routes, views, Blade components, config/env, Eloquent, translations, artisan).

## Purpose

PHPForge Laravel support, built on the PHP pack's tree-sitter parser.

`Laravel::load` analyses a project statically:
- `routes`: `routes/*.php` (groups, prefixes, names, middleware, resources) or the
  output of `php artisan route:list --json`;
- `views`: view names, Blade components (anonymous, class based, Livewire) and custom
  Blade directives;
- `config`: `config()` and `env()` keys;
- `eloquent`: models with columns from migrations, `$fillable`, casts, relations,
  scopes and accessors;
- `translations`: `__()` keys from PHP and JSON language files.

On top of that, `complete` offers completion, Go to Declaration and gutter markers
for an editor buffer, and `artisan` lists and builds artisan commands.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `artisan.rs` | Artisan commands: the list from `php artisan list --format=json` (with a built-in fallback when PHP is not available), command line splitting, and running commands with streamed output. |
| `complete.rs` | Editor services for PHP and Blade buffers: completion of route names, views, config and env keys, translations, columns, relations, model properties, scopes, components and custom directives; Go to Declaration for the same; gutter markers for routed controller methods, route definitions and `view()` calls. |
| `config.rs` | `config('app.name')` keys from `config/*.php` and `env('APP_NAME')` keys from `.env` files. |
| `context.rs` | What the caret is on, found lexically so it works while the code is being typed (`route('orders.\|` has no closing quote yet): a string argument of a call, a property access, a Blade component tag or a Blade directive. |
| `eloquent.rs` | Eloquent models: table columns from migrations, `$fillable`, casts, relations (with the related model), local scopes, accessors and `@property` docblocks. |
| `php.rs` | Small helpers over the tree-sitter PHP syntax tree: literal values, call arguments and returned arrays. Laravel's configuration lives in plain PHP arrays and fluent calls, so static evaluation of these few shapes covers routes, config, translations and models. |
| `project.rs` | Project layout: Laravel version, PSR-4 autoloading, file helpers and locations. |
| `routes.rs` | Routes: static parsing of `routes/*.php` (verbs, `match`, `resource`, `view`, `redirect`, groups with prefix/name/middleware/controller, included route files) and the JSON output of `php artisan route:list --json`. |
| `translations.rs` | Translation keys for `__()`, `trans()`, `trans_choice()` and `@lang`: grouped PHP files (`lang/en/messages.php` → `messages.welcome`) and JSON files (`lang/de.json`). |
| `views.rs` | Views and Blade components: `view('orders.show')` names, anonymous components in `resources/views/components`, class components in `app/View/Components`, Livewire components and custom directives registered with `Blade::directive` / `Blade::if`. |

## Main public items

```rust

pub use eloquent::{Model, ModelAttribute, Relation, Scope};
pub use project::{Location, Psr4};

pub use translations::Translation;
pub use views::{Component, CustomDirective, View};
pub struct Laravel { … }
pub struct LaravelInfo { … }
pub use project::is_laravel;

```

## Used by

- IPC: `laravel_detect`, `laravel_routes`, `laravel_complete`, `laravel_goto`, `laravel_gutter` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/laravel.rs`); `artisan::builtin_commands` is the fallback list of the Command Line Tools Console (`command_line_tools.rs`, see [phpforge-cli-tools](docs/guide/developer/crates/phpforge-cli-tools.md))
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/laravel`

- External: `serde`, `serde_json`, `thiserror`, `tracing`, `tree-sitter`, `walkdir`

# phpforge-fw-symfony

`packs/phpforge/fw-symfony` — PHPForge: Symfony support (service container, routes, Twig templates, console commands).

## Purpose

PHPForge Symfony plugin: everything the IDE knows about a Symfony application.

- `container` reads `config/services.yaml` (explicit services, aliases, `_defaults` and
  autowired `resource:` directories) and, when present, the compiled container XML in
  `var/cache/<env>/`, which also lists the services and parameters of all bundles.
- `routes` collects routes from `#[Route]` attributes, legacy `@Route` annotations and
  YAML route files.
- `twig` lists templates, Twig tags/filters/functions/tests (core, Symfony bridge and
  project extensions) and which controller renders which template.
- `console` finds console commands and builds `bin/console` command lines.
- `complete` answers completion and Go to Declaration for route names, service ids,
  templates, parameters and Twig syntax; `gutter` computes the editor gutter marks.

`scan` builds a `Snapshot` of a project once; the IDE caches it and rescans when files
change.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `complete.rs` | Completion and Go to Declaration for Symfony references in PHP, Twig and YAML files: route names (`generateUrl`, `redirectToRoute`, Twig `path()`/`url()`), templates (`render()`, `{% extends %}`), service ids (`@id`, `#[Autowire(service:)]`, `$container->get()`), parameters (`%name%`, `getParameter()`) and Twig tags, filters, functions and tests. |
| `console.rs` | Console commands: the application's own (`#[AsCommand]`, `$defaultName`, `setName()`) plus the common framework and bundle commands, and the `bin/console` command line. |
| `container.rs` | The service container: services and parameters from `config/services*.yaml` (including `resource:` directories registered with autowiring) and from the compiled container XML Symfony dumps to `var/cache/<env>/` in debug mode. |
| `gutter.rs` | Editor gutter marks, like the Symfony plugin's line markers: routes on controller actions, "go to template" next to `render()` calls, "rendered by" on Twig templates and a run marker on console commands. |
| `routes.rs` | Routes from `#[Route]` attributes, legacy `@Route` annotations and YAML route files (`config/routes.yaml`, `config/routes/*.yaml`), including import prefixes. |
| `strings.rs` | String literal helpers shared by completion, navigation and the gutter: find the quoted string around a cursor and the call it is an argument of (`generateUrl('\|')`). |
| `twig.rs` | Twig: templates, the tags/filters/functions/tests available in templates (Twig core, the Symfony bridge and the project's own extensions) and which controllers render which template. |

## Main public items

```rust
pub use complete::{CompletionItem, CompletionKind, CompletionList};
pub use console::ConsoleCommand;
pub use container::{Parameter, Service, ServiceSource};
pub use routes::{Route, RouteSource};
pub use twig::{Template, TwigSymbol, TwigSymbolKind};
pub struct Location { … }
pub struct Config { … }
pub struct SymfonyInfo { … }
pub struct PhpFile { … }
pub struct Snapshot { … }
pub fn is_symfony_project(root: &Path) -> bool { … }
pub fn framework_version(root: &Path) -> Option<String> { … }
pub fn line_col(text: &str, offset: usize) -> (u32, u32) { … }
pub fn index_php_files(root: &Path, dir: &str) -> Vec<PhpFile> { … }
pub fn scan(root: &Path, config: &Config) -> Snapshot { … }
```

## Used by

# phpforge-fw-wordpress

`packs/phpforge/fw-wordpress` — PHPForge: WordPress support (hook index, hook completion and
navigation, gutter marks, hook usages, Yoda condition hints, plugin/theme detection, WP-CLI and
stubs lookup). Pure Rust without system dependencies, so the browser mode runs the same code
through WebAssembly.

## Purpose

What the IDE knows about a WordPress site, plugin or theme. `scan` (a folder) or `scan_files`
(in-memory files) builds a `Snapshot`: the detection (`WordPressInfo`) and the hook index.
`api::answer` answers the IDE's queries on it with UTF-16 offsets; the desktop app runs it
next to the project's files (`forge_backend::frameworks`, `FrameworkCall::WordPress`), the
browser mode through `forge-wasm` (`wordpress_query`).

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `lexer.rs` | A small, error tolerant PHP tokenizer (inline HTML, comments, strings, heredocs, operators), plus argument splitting of calls. |
| `hooks.rs` | Hook references of a file: registrations (`add_action`, `add_filter`), invocations (`do_action`, `apply_filters`, `_ref_array`, `_deprecated`), removals and checks, with callback, priority and the source line. Dynamic names (`"save_post_{$post->post_type}"`, concatenations) become patterns; `pattern_matches` matches a static name against one. Also function and method declarations. |
| `index.rs` | `HookIndex`: the project's hooks and functions (`vendor/`, `node_modules/`, `uploads/` skipped), the WordPress stubs' functions, `related` (registrations ↔ invocations), `usages` and the per-hook summary (`hooks`). Editor queries overlay the unsaved buffer. |
| `editor.rs` | Hook name completion (`hook_context` is text based, so it works while typing), Go to Declaration (hook ↔ hook, callback → function, WordPress function → stubs), gutter marks and Find Usages with the tree the Find tool window renders (`forge_codeintel::usages`). |
| `core.rs` | Frequently used WordPress core hooks with Forge's own one-line summaries, for projects without WordPress core. |
| `yoda.rs` | "Use Yoda condition" hints of the WordPress Coding Standards with the swapped comparison as quick-fix. |
| `detect.rs` | Site / Composer install / `wp-content` / plugin / theme detection, the plugin and theme headers, WP-CLI (`vendor/bin/wp`, `wp-cli.phar`, `wp` on PATH) and the installed stubs (`vendor/php-stubs/wordpress-stubs`). |
| `api.rs` | `Query` (`detect`, `refresh`, `hooks`, `complete`, `goto`, `gutter`, `usages`, `inspect`) and `answer`. |

## Main public items

```rust
pub struct Location { … }
pub struct Snapshot { pub info: Option<WordPressInfo>, pub index: HookIndex }
pub fn scan(root: &Path) -> Snapshot { … }
pub fn scan_files(files: &HashMap<String, String>) -> Snapshot { … }
pub fn api::answer(snap: &Snapshot, query: api::Query) -> serde_json::Value { … }
pub fn hooks::scan(path: &str, src: &str) -> Vec<HookRef> { … }
pub fn hooks::pattern_matches(pattern: &str, name: &str) -> bool { … }
pub fn yoda::hints(src: &str) -> Vec<YodaHint> { … }
pub fn detect::detect(probe: &dyn Probe, which: &dyn Fn(&str) -> Option<String>) -> Option<WordPressInfo> { … }
```

## Used by

- IPC: `wordpress_detect`, `wordpress_refresh`, `wordpress_hooks`, `wordpress_complete`, `wordpress_goto`, `wordpress_gutter`, `wordpress_usages`, `wordpress_inspect` (`app/src-tauri/src/commands/wordpress.rs`)
- Backend: `forge_backend::frameworks` (`FrameworkCall::WordPress`, cached snapshot)
- UI: `app/ui/src/features/wordpress`
- Browser mode: `crates/forge-wasm/src/wordpress.rs` (`wordpress_query`) over the `?project=wordpress` demo

## Dependencies

- Workspace crates: [`forge-codeintel`](docs/guide/developer/crates/forge-codeintel.md)
- External: `serde`, `serde_json`

## Tests

8 source files; unit tests for the lexer, hook extraction and patterns, the index, completion,
navigation, gutter marks, usages, Yoda hints, detection and the API.

# phpforge-fw-cms

`packs/phpforge/fw-cms` — PHPForge: Drupal, Joomla and Shopware basics (detection, Drupal hook
completion, implementations and hook docs). Pure Rust, shared with the browser mode via
WebAssembly.

## Purpose

The `forge.cms` plugin is one plugin for three CMS because each part is small: detection with
version and console, and Drupal's hooks. File types and template languages come from the
plugin manifest (`.module` & co. as PHP) and the editor (Shopware's `sw_*` Twig tags).
`scan` / `scan_files` build a `Snapshot` (the detected CMS, Drupal extensions from their
`.info.yml`, `hook_…` functions of the project's `*.api.php` files); `api::answer` answers the
IDE's queries with UTF-16 offsets.

## Modules

| Module | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `detect.rs` | Drupal (composer packages, `core/lib/Drupal.php`, a module's `.info.yml`), Joomla (`joomla.xml`, an extension manifest) and Shopware 5 / 6 (composer packages, plugin type, `engine/Shopware`) with version, kind (site or extension) and console (`vendor/bin/drush`, `drush`, `bin/console`). |
| `drupal_hooks.rs` | The bundled list of core hooks: names and parameters from Drupal's API, summaries written for Forge; placeholders (`FORM_ID`, `ENTITY_TYPE`, `HOOK`, `N`) match implementation names. |
| `drupal.rs` | The extension a file belongs to, completion of `<module>_<hook>` after `function`, the implementations of a file (gutter marks) and the hook docs (the `*.api.php` declaration, else api.drupal.org). |
| `api.rs` | `Query` (`detect`, `refresh`, `complete`, `goto`, `gutter`) and `answer`. |

## Main public items

```rust
pub fn drupal_hooks::hook_for(suffix: &str) -> Option<&(&str, &str, &str)> { … }
```
